Resurrection refers to the re-uniting of soul and body at the end of ages. It is the return of all the dead in to life at the end of the world. It marks the start of eternal ‘life’ after the second coming of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. Resurrection also denotes the final removal of the consequences of Adam’s sin (human disobedience). This mystery represents all what is at stake in our spiritual journey on earth. We believe in the authentic apostolic Gospel to be genuine candidates of the Kingdom of God, which would be revealed at the end of the ages. We take part in sacramental rituals implementing two among the five pillars of mysteries (Mystery of Baptism and Mystery of Holy Eucharist) for the same reason. The essence of Christianity is the life we have after death. We don’t dare to sacrifice our everlasting life in heaven for “a moment of happiness” on earth which transgresses God’s commandments. We believe and proclaim that all the dead humans will rise up for glory or demise. We believe the way we do and perform good deeds to be genuine candidates of God’s grace for a glorious resurrection.

So, when a person dies, he faces two opportunities of places where he lives with soul, and we decide one of the two when we are still alive before we die. This means that if we do righteous deeds, we will go to paradise. If we sin, we go to hell. So first, until the second coming, if a person is a sinner, his soul will go to hell, and if his deeds are good, he will go to paradise. After the second coming, the soul of the righteous will be sent to the kingdom of heaven, and the soul of the sinner will be sent to the fire of hell.

The second coming of Jesus Christ will be as lightning as it’s said: “For as lightning that comes from the east is visible even in the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.” (Matthew 24:27). He will be seen with great power and authority: “They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky, with power and great glory” (Matthew 24:30-31). “For the Son of Man is going to come in his Father’s glory with his angels, and then he will reward each person according to what he has done” ((Matthew 16:27 Luke 17:28-30 Luke 21:34-36 Matthew 25:1-12 Luke 12:37-38 John 14:1-3 Luke 12:40 Mark 8:38).

The lord said “For as the lightening cometh out of the east, and shines even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.” (Mathew 24:27) Church scholars rightly note that the moment of our physical death on earth, even before judgement day, is our “final day”. We don’t have the chance to have the faith and deeds for salvation after departure. Hence, our final day is our judgement day and there is no point to speculate about the “final day of the world” while our final day comes without being noticed.

Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ was crucified and died to save the human race in order to bring us back to our original inheritance in heaven.  Paradise is a place of temporary happiness where the righteous will stay.

(Part 12 Continues)👇

On Friday, while our Lord was being crucified, the thief on the right, Fyatawi Zeyman, saw our Lord performing 3 miracles in heaven and 4 on earth, and believed that He was truly God. 👉🏾👉🏾👉🏾 About #Betrothal

Dear and respected members who follow the orthodox education and spiritual service that we convey on the John's Repentance website; Based on the title mentioned in above, we have sent you the following important lesson, so we entrust you to read and learn from it.

Betrothal/Engagement:- means choosing, preparing. Betrothal is a time of togetherness between the two couples before marriage, and it is a time of hope leading to marriage.

Engagement

Engagement is a journey of purpose, courtship, and preparation that you embark on together for a successful marriage life. This is a way for us to start with consent; and wait for the holy marriage and the blessings it will bring us to a great chapter of responsibility. Thus, since betrothal is not a permanent relationship or marriage, matters that happen after marriage should not be done during betrothal. Instead, it is a time to gather our scattered conscience and help each other with a holy purpose.

Things To Do during Engagement

- Religious Unity: Since religion is the primary issue in the life of a Christian betrothed; and most importantly, since marriage is a journey to salvation, religious unity should be the main selection criterion.

- Staying Virgin - Betrothal with virginity and virginity with betrothal have an inseparable basic combination. The Orthodox Church emphatically teaches that both men and women have a Christian responsibility to maintain chastity until the day of their marriage, and in other word, it is a sin to lose virginity before marriage.

- Pray - Praying and asking for God's will to be worthy of holy marriage

- Not extending the engagement period - Unless there is a special reason, it is preferable that it is not less than six months and not more than two years.

   - Getting married in the church system : agreeing to perform their marriage in the church system based on one intention and purpose; Apart from this, if both or one of them are not on the same path, having different thoughts and objectives, their destination will be different. Besides, marriage is not a way of abandoning, but a path of righteousness where you walk together with each other and support each other. Moreover , the covenant of marriage is said to be valid when its basis is confirmed by the sacraments in the true Church order. it is the secret of coming to unity from duality. Otherwise, they will be called two, not one.

- Trust - If we face the interference and rumors of friends and third parties , instead of fighting, it is better to carefully investigate and openly discuss and come to a common position to save our relationship. The secret to a long marriage is tolerance and open communication.

- Courtship - that is, narrowing down the differences of opinion or thinking between them, bringing them to a common point of view, correcting if there are ethical deficiencies, and facilitating the conditions for filling religious deficiencies with the fathers of the Church.

- Christian Morality - Emphasizing love, forgiveness, patience, honesty, compassion, respect, and humility. A person who feels responsible is of great importance to our continued life together; In addition, there should be mutual goals based on future interests and balanced love and affection on both sides. Not only do we expect these Christian behaviors from our fiancee, but they are values that we should practice together, not by blaming, but by showing compassion.

- Economy - establishing the ability to overcome daily life mutually; 

- Relative: Confirming that there is no marriage relationship and spiritual relationship between their close relatives

- Father of penitence: meeting the father of penitence regularly and being helped by education, advice and prayer.


(Part 2 continues )👇

Dear and respected members who follow the orthodox education and spiritual service that we convey on the John's Repentance website; Based on the question mentioned in above, we have sent you the following reply lesson, so we entrust you to read and learn from it.

✍Answer:

text:
Paradise, as we understand from its name, means a place that is unique, pleasant and satisfying to the spirit, restful, special, and naturally blessed with unique natural grace. This is what we call Paradise, and  it was given to Adam to inherit.
 
Today, when we see a place where plants and birds abound, where the whole earth is full of flowers,  we are amazed and we call the place a "Paradise". 
 
When God gave Paradise to our father Adam and our mother Eve, there was no suffering, no pain, no hunger and thirst for water, no going up and down, no tiredness in work; They lived happily for a thousand years, and if they were lucky, after a thousand years, God renewed their nature, and they would have lived for a thousand years.
 
In the midst of that, after God appointed them to rule over everything, to lead, to enjoy everything, without depriving them of anything except from the tree of knowledge which was in the middle of Paradise. So, when we think about heaven or the tree of knowledge, what we ask should not be  research questions like what kind of wood is it? Where did it grow? or What does it look like? Our dear member, Paradise is an independent, holy land or world. Apart from this, it is not Religion to think about how far Paradise is from this earth by the measure of holy angels, or how far it is from this world we live in.

In Noah's time, the ark was given to Noah until the flood passes or dries up, so that Noah would not be destroyed by the flood. The ship being on Mount Ararat, there was something that the scholars or the fathers fathers have researched about how close the ship's direction indicator was to heaven. 
 
Because it is the Holy Spirit who explains everything to them, our fathers have documented it's direction and distance from this world. If you, our inquirer, have in-depth knowledge of religion or holy books and have asked for research, contact us at our address and we will discuss it in detail.
 
But with such a question, since not everyone has the same spiritual knowledge, it is better to explain it as a generalization  that in paradise  our father Adam and our mother Eve glorified it as a child, and God's grace was abundant for them. Today, it is known how much pain and suffering we go through to get what we need for food, but it was not like that for them. In that paradise, God made Adam the king and made all the animals to live in subjection to him, that is what we call paradise. But then the grace of childhood that Adam received from God was stripped/taken away from him due to sin he committed, he was expelled from Paradise and its door was closed to him.
 
God ordered him to inform them that God is the creator and Adam is a creature, that there is a ruler and a subject, and that he is a creature that lives in law and order. He said, "Don't eat this, you will die." This is a law, an order. It was forbidden to eat from that tree because its nature brought death to Adam. Just as we are accused of breaking the law by doing what we are forbidden to do, we will be destroyed, if we become law breakers, 

(Continues )👇

Dear members of John's Repentance service, In order to provide you with the answers to all the previous questions regarding adultery, we have sent "part one" as follows, and we will send the rest of the parts in the following days, so please stay tuned!
Question #1: What is adultery and why is it a major sin

text:
Sexual intercourse that is not between a husband and a wife, meaning that is outside of marriage, which is fornication, is called adultery. But the intercourse committed by a couple who is legally married is not fornication, not adultery.

Adultery is one of the main sins that God hates and despises.  That is why our enemy, Satan, the devil, in order to make us fall apart from the Creator and deprive us of our sacred sonship, forcibly puts us into his trap and pushes us to execute and practice/normalize this hateful sin. Therefore, it is important to understand that the main function of adultery is to replace the law of God with the law of the devil, which means to replace our eternal life with eternal death. Like a dead person was with us yesterday and is not by our side today, a person who commits adultery is taken by death. 

When people collaborate in sin, the destruction is brought not only to oneself, but also to the country and the earth. As we know, the main sins of the people of Noah's days were fornication and adultery. Because of those who have no law, who jump as they please without a bridle, who had generally thrown away all their beingness and out of the sin of man, the earth and all the creatures on the earth have perished in the punishment of the burning plague and wrath sent from God. The main cause of this scourge was the sin of adultery.

👉👉👉

text.text: Question #2: What are the types of adultery?

text:
1. To pour seed upon the earth, burning with carnal lust and passion; (Genesis 38:6-11)
 2. Sexual relations with the earth and/or stones (Leviticus 20:15)
 3. Sexual relations with plants and with animals (Leviticus 20:15)
 4. Sexual relations with our relatives who are close to us in the flesh; (Leviticus 18:6 and 17)
 5. Man with man;  (Genesis 19:9) (Genesis 19:22)
 6. Woman to woman;  (Leviticus 20:15)
 7. Adultery committed by a woman and a man who is outside of the marriage (Leviticus 23:17)
 8. With oneself);  (1 Cor 6:18)
 9. Indulging in drinking, materialism, and other carnal thoughts;  (1 Cor 6:13)
 10. Idolship;  (Acts 21:25)
 11. It is also adultery to coveting food, a brother, his wealth, his strength, his wife 

In this day and age, which type of adultery is tempting everyone from the youth to the old?  Unable to bear the sensuality and burning with the idea of ​​adultery, men and women behind closed doors tempt and/or satisfy themselves, pouring their seeds. This is called adultery with oneself. This type of fornication is outside the natural order, so it is a greater sin than those who commit physical fornication. In fact, the idea of ​​homosexuality starts from this and thus it is connected with the spirit of homosexuality. Fornication with oneself, man with man, woman with woman... it is even hard to speak and say the terms. This type of sin is a new philosophy of sin brought by people who are led by the spirit of Satan. Unfortunately, many beginning from young age are falling and under temptation of this, knowingly or unknowingly.

 👉👉👉

text.text: Question #3: What is the cause of falling into adultery?

text: The thing is, after we boldly commit all these sins by thinking of the temporary benefits and feelings we get for our flesh, the excuses we give is saying that Satan misled us. But Satan, whom we hold responsible, has never, and will never, take accountability. Indeed, Satan sees our desire and

us to execute his desire by exploiting our weaknesses.

text.text: Beloved and respected members who follow the orthodox education and spiritual service that we convey on John's Repentance page, we send you this writing about the great lent by Bishop Serapion of the Coptic Orthodox Church so you may read and understand to get the blessings of this fast.

text:
Great Lent is considered the holiest fast since our Lord Jesus Christ Himself had fasted it.
Therefore, during Great Lent we follow the example set by our Lord Jesus Christ, Who fasted on our behalf forty days and forty nights (Matt. 4: 2). Also during Holy Week, which comes after the 40 days, we live the Passion of Christ day-by-day and hour-by-hour. Because of the significance and holiness of Great Lent, the Church designated a week of preparation to precede the 40 days. The Church is teaching us to prepare for Great Lent in a spiritual manner. We fast to prepare ourselves for the 40 holy days. In fact, the preparatory week is not the only fast which the Church designated to get us ready for Great Lent and Holy Week. Two weeks prior to Great Lent there is Jonah’s Fast, also known as Nineveh’s Fast. It is a short fast, only three days, and it is a fast of repentance. During this fast, we live with Jonah his fasting and repentance in the whale’s belly. We also live with the Ninevites their fasting and repentance. Just as the fasting accompanied by repentance saved Jonah and the Ninevites from perdition, also our fasting accompanied by repentance will save us from eternal destruction and death due to sin. Great Lent is an Apostolic Fast:

It is mentioned in the Didskalia (chapter 18) the following: "Great Lent should be honored before Holy Week. It starts on the Monday following the Saturday and is completed on the Friday preceding Holy Week. After it, you must pay great attention to Holy Week and fast it with fear and piety." In Canon 69 from the Canons of our Fathers the Apostles, the following is mentioned: "Any bishop, priest, deacon, reader, or chanter who does not fast Great Lent or Wednesdays and Fridays shall be excommunicated, unless he has a physical ailment. As for a lay person, he shall be excluded."

Great Lent is an Ascetical Fast:
The Church teaches us to fast until sunset. Fish is not allowed during this period. Also married couples should refrain from physical relations to give themselves time for fasting and prayer (1 Cor. 7: 5). We would like to emphasize the importance of the period of strict abstention during fasting. It is refraining from eating and drinking for a period of time, followed by eating vegetarian food.

Some people practice fasting by abstaining from meat and they eat vegetarian food, disregarding the period of strict abstention. These people should actually be regarded as vegetarians and not as fasting. A vegetarian eats only vegetarian food, but is not considered a fasting person. True fasting must be accompanied by abstention from food and drink until sunset as designated by the Church. However, due to variations in people’s physical and spiritual abilities, the Church gave the father of confession the authority to designate to his children the length of their strict abstinence. He determines what is suitable for their spiritual benefit according to the nature of their work, as well as their physical ability to endure fasting.

Great Lent is a Period of Prayer:
The period of Great Lent is distinctive for its many Liturgies. They become the spiritual treasure for the fasting person to help him throughout the rest of the year. In addition to the Divine Liturgy on Sundays, which have specific readings, hymns, and tunes, the Church also arranged special readings for the daily Liturgies during Great Lent. Also, during the weekdays, there are special hymns.
The Church celebrates the Divine Liturgy almost daily during Great Lent. It is preferred that these Liturgies start late in the day to offer those fasting the opportunity to practice strict abstinence.

It is not permitted to have the Divine Liturgy on weekdays early in the morning, since we pray the hours until the Compline Prayer. How can we pray the psalms of the Complin Prayer at 5:00 A.M.? Also, having an early morning Liturgy means there will not be abstention from food, since we can not abstain from food following the Divine Liturgy.

The proper time to end the Divine Liturgy during the weekdays of Great Lent is at sunset. Due to the inability of the elderly and the sick, it is permitted to have it end earlier, but not before noon. That way everyone may receive the blessing of Holy Communion, while benefiting from abstention. We hope that the fathers of confession will take great care in guiding their children as to the importance of strict abstinence and how to struggle to keep it for as long as they can.

text.text: Great Lent is a Period of Repentance:

text:
Fasting without repentance and changing one’s life becomes useless. Unless the fasting person changes his life during fasting, he will only be hungry and exhausted without gaining anything else. Therefore, the Church constantly reminds us of the importance of repentance during fasting. Before Great Lent, we fast Jonah’s Fast and we live the story of Jonah and the Ninevites’ repentance. During the third Sunday of Lent, the Holy Church offers us the Gospel reading of the Prodigal Son as a model of repentance, which requires an awakening, confession of sins, leaving the place of sin, and returning to the Heavenly Father with confidence in His mercies and acceptance. This parable reveals to us the depth of God’s love for sinners and how He accepts them no matter how horrendous their sin is. Our Lord Jesus Christ said, "the one who comes to Me I will by no means cast out." (John 6: 37) Christ "has come to save that which was lost." (Matt. 18:11) God desires that all men be saved and come to the knowledge of truth (1Tim. 2:4). Christ is the True Physician who is needed by those who are ill by sin. He did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance (Mark 2: 17). Repentance is a result of divine action; it is the Spirit of God, Who moves the hearts of sinners to repent.

It is written in the Holy Bible, "For it is God who works in you both to will and do for His good pleasure." (Phil. 2: 13) God’s pleasure is in the return of a sinner so that he will not die in his sin. When God sees his sinful child returning to Him, He has compassion and goes to him, kissing him, and welcomes his return by saying, "It is right that we should make merry and be glad." (Luke 15: 32) The return of a sinner and his repentance results in joy to God, as well as all those in heaven, because, "there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine just persons who need no repentance." (Luke 15: 7)

During Great Lent, we praise God for His many mercies. The Doxology of Great Lent presents to us a magnificent hymn in praising God on His mercies, as well as asking for His mercies. The first Doxology of the Sundays of Great Lent starts with the following:

I will praise you, O Lord, for your mercies are forever. From generation to generation, my mouth shall declare Your truth.

In this beautiful doxology, we praise God for His mercies. Then the chanter remembers his many sins and transgressions by saying, " My sins are heavy over my head." As his sins are revealed in front of him, he then remembers the stories of those who repented and were accepted by God, so he won’t lose hope. Therefore, he remembers the publican, the adulteress, and the thief and asks God to make him like any one of them.

Again, he recalls God’s attributes by saying, "I know You are good, kind and merciful. Remember me in Your mercy forever." God does not wish the death of a sinner but that he should return and live. Then the chanter remembers his sins once again and says: “I have sinned, O Jesus, my Lord, I have sinned, O Jesus, my God, O my King, do not count the sins I have committed.”

(Continues)👇

text:
(Continued) 👆

He asks for God’s mercies and not to be punished like Sodom and Gomorrah, but to have mercy on him like the Ninevites. The chanter ends his praise by saying: “But absolve and forgive My many transgressions As good and lover of mankind Have mercy on us according to Your great mercy.”

This doxology is beautiful poetry, through which the human soul expresses her feelings resulting from the heaviness of her sins. At the same time, she shows her great hope in our kind and merciful Lord, Who is happy with the return and repentance of the sinner. Yet, He punishes the unrepentant sinners. Therefore, repentance is the means by which we enjoy God’s great mercies.

text.text: Great Lent is a Period for Doing Mercy:

text:
The Church reminds us of the importance of doing merciful acts during fasting. Therefore, during Great Lent we chant together praising those who have mercy on the poor. The Holy Bible teaches us that the fasting which is accepted by God is the one in which we do acts of mercy to others. "Is this not the fast that I have chosen: to loose the bonds of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, to let the oppressed go free, and that you break every yoke? Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and that you bring to your house the poor who are cast out; when you see the naked, that you cover him, and not hide yourself from you own flesh?"

Fasting is a beautiful period to do good deeds by helping the poor, feeding the hungry, visiting the sick, and taking care of the needs of others. The person who fasts by not yielding to the needs of the flesh, will feel the needs of others and his heart will be moved to serve them. Also, the asceticism of fasting teaches us to care for the heavenly and not be concerned with the earthly. Thus it becomes easy to forsake our material possessions and offer them to the needy.

text.text: Great Lent is a Period of Reconciliation with Others:

text:
Fasting is an act of worship presented to God, and God does not accept the offering and worship of a person who quarrels with others. Instead, He asks him to go and make peace with his brother before coming to worship and present offerings in front of God’ altar. Fasting is an appropriate time to evaluate our relationship with others. As we ask God to forgive us our sins, we must also forgive those who have sinned against us.

May God grant us a blessed fast by which we can grow in a life of prayer, asceticism, and repentance. May we always increase in doing acts of mercy and living in peace with one another.

and his Responsibility 

👉Question: What does the father of repentance mean? What is expected of a repentant father? What about his authority?
 
All our beloved and respected members who follow the orthodox education and spiritual service that we convey on the website of John's Repentance; Based on the above-mentioned question, we have sent you an important lesson that will help you to lead your spiritual life with knowledge, and to constantly grow under the guidance of a repentant father  by getting the appropriate service from them, and we entrust you all to read and use it.
 
✍Answer
A Father of penitence is one's closest advisor in spiritual and physical life.

text: In Sirac 6-6, it says: "Let many people be your friends, and let one of many be your counsel, and let your counsel be one with your heart." This means that although the believers may have many priests to teach them about religion and morals, one of them should be the teacher to whom they confess their repentance.

text.text: The Father of pennance is to whom we confess our sins.

text: When we confess our sins to the priest, we are confessing and honoring God. As Joshua said, "

text.text: My son, give, I pray thee, glory to the LORD God of Israel, and make confession unto him; and tell me now what you have done; hide it not from me.”

text: Joshua 7-19 shows us that confessing sins to a priest is giving glory to God. After accepting the confession, the priests say "May God release you" and not "I have released you". Even if we confess our sins in front of our father of confession, the one who hears and forgives our sins is God, but the system is carried out through our spiritual father whom God The Son Himself has appointed over us. "And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven." (Matthew 16:19)

text.text: A father of penance is a shepherd who teaches the children basic religion, monitors the overall change of the children, and cares about his sheep.

text: Our Lord Jesus Christ, to save us  - crucified on a cross, died and was buried, rose from the dead on the third day, appeared to the apostles after the resurrection and taught them : - "Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? text.text: Are we justified by works or by faith?

Beloved and respected, all our members who follow the orthodox education that we convey on John's Repentance page; Based on the topic mentioned above, we have sent you the important lesson below, so we entrust you all to read and learn from it.

text:
Wherever there is a law, there is justice and condemnation, for those who keep the law are justified and those who transgress the law are condemned. The message of the prophet Isaiah confirms this reality "If you are willing and obedient, You shall eat the good of the land; But if you refuse and rebel, You shall be devoured by the sword”; For the mouth of the Lord has spoken" (Isa. 1:19-20). Of course, the foundation of righteousness is faith. Good work is a roof and a wall. A foundation alone is not called a house, and faith without conduct is worthless. Just as a wall and a roof cannot stand without a foundation, doing good deeds without faith is like building a house on sand.

Everyone knows that there is a spiritual law in him, and that is conscience. Man does good by his natural moral knowledge or by his conscience. This indicates that there is one supreme God who rewards both the righteous and the wicked according to their deeds and judges impartially. To explain this, Saint Paul wrote the following; "for when Gentiles, who do not have the law, by nature do the things in the law, these, although not having the law, are a law to themselves, who show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and between themselves,
thoughts accusing or else excusing

profit, my brethren, if someone says he has faith but does not have works? Can faith save him?" "If a brother or sister is naked and destitute of daily food, and one of you says to them, “Depart in peace, be warmed and filled,” but you do not give them the things which are needed for the body, what

profit? Thus also faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead" James 2:14-17 reveals. Saint John Chrysostom, the Archbishop of Constantinople, says, "A building cannot stand and be seen without a foundation, and a Christian cannot be called a Christian without conduct" (Essay on John Chrysostom, Essay 9). Just as a tree that doesn't bear good fruit is cut down, if we do not do good because we have faith that is not manifested by works, then we are worthless. He said, "If your righteousness exceeds that of the nations, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven."

Because the Lord is perfect in all His works, "Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me" as we have in Matthew 11:29. Feeding the hungry, sympathizing and comforting the bereaved, welcoming guests, giving one to another, visiting the sick, preaching the gospel to the prisoner, and living in love are hallmarks of Christian ethics Matthew 25:15-30.

As it is said, "You are the salt of the earth". We have had enough of those whose lives are left with pharisaical leaven and are swayed by the original identity, revenge, malice and deceit, greed and impurity, adultery, and worshiping idols. we must get rid of the temptations of the flesh and return to a good identity (Matthew 5:11).

(Continues) 👇

👉🏾👉🏾👉🏾 Advice on #general #life #challenge
 
👉Question 1: How does one avoid fearing failure and worrying too much about the future?
 
Answer 1st: The solution is to make God our power. Man falls when he is separated from God. Not doing what God says 'Do', and doing what God says 'Don't do' is a sin. When we say 'fall', we mean fall into sin. For example, he says don't kill, "killing is falling", don't steal, "stealing is falling", don't lie, he says "lying is falling", live in love, don't fight, he says "fighting is falling", so if this is the case, then doing what God likes will not lead to failure.
 
A person who lives with God will do what God wants him to do. A person who does what God loves will not be found in failure, nor will he fail. So the solution is to not worry and to avoid failure. "It is possible for all who believe" (Mark 9:23). A person who lives with God can do everything, even if he falls into sin, he will rise in repentance, he will control himself, and manage.
 
Therefore, our fathers neither worry nor get upset about useless things. Because of this, sin did not fall upon  them, and even if it fell upon them, they repented. Therefore, even if we are separated from God by sin, we must repent, do the work that God loves, persevere in religion, be strong, fast and pray, because these are our spiritual weapons, we are expected to hold and carry them out.
 
Matthew chapter 17 verse 21 tells us, "Without fasting and prayer, an evil spirit will not come out." Therefore, it is the evil spirit that lives with us and makes us do things that God does not like. This can be avoided only when we are equipped with spiritual armor. What we call spiritual armor is fasting, prayer, prostration, almsgiving, etc. as we mentioned above.

Some people believe that they can handle any challenge on their own; But self-confidence does not exempt from suffering; The best thing is to believe and hope in God.

Living in God's hope makes us have full faith in Him. With God on our side, each of us can reach beyond our imagination. Therefore, our hope depends on the strength of our faith in our God. Hope is the stepping stone to move forward in life, the foundation of our life and the beginning of our happiness. For if we live in hope, we will pass into eternal life.

Prophet David said, "Who is my hope now? Isn't it God?" he said, even if we are in trouble, we should believe that God will get us out of trouble. It is mentioned in the Bible that the prophet lived hoping and relying on God when his enemies were many. And God did not hand him over to his enemies. (1 Sam. 16-31)
 
In general, It is possible to avoid over-anxiety by doing what God loves, putting God first in all things, fearing God, and obeying His orders, practicing trust and hope.  

The Bible says, "Do not worry about what we will eat, what we will drink, what we will wear. Who among you is anxious and can add a cubit to his height?" Who says I should be longer or shorter? He said that no one can, so we shouldn't worry, we shouldn't disturb ourselves, if we are with God, if we repent whenever we fall into sin, if we receive His holy body and holy blood, we are good. "Our biggest solution is to live with God."

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always. 

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.
Amen.

©John's Repentance 

Follow our Telegram group every day and share it with your friends https://t.me/orthodoxQnAs.

Question 2: What are the ways we can deal with difficult situations in our lives? Thank you
 
✍  Answer 2

text:
. Our forefathers, because of their religion, faced all the difficult issues that separate them from God, they were steadfast and strong. Even if they were told  'deny your religion, bow down to an idol', they said we will not compromise on our religion. By way of punishment for saying so, as the scriptures tell us, they were thrown into the fire, but the fire did not harm them, they were thrown to the lions and the lions did not eat them. This is because God protected them through the steadfastness of their faith. What made them so is their steadfastness in religion, which means, "It is possible for everyone who believes." It is possible for everyone who says, 'It will be possible for me.'
 
For example, Elijah believed and prayed to God to hold the rain for three years, because the people did not know God, they were people who  worshiped idols, so he prayed to God to hold the rain so their eyes can open up and see the glory of God. Jacob described it in chapter 5 of his message: Elijah is a man like us, he gets sick just like we get sick, but he prayed to God that it wouldn't rain and the rain was prevented. Later, he asked God to make it rain again, and it rained, it was his religion that made it so.
Religion and morals are very important. A believer must respect God's commandments and put his faith into practice. "

text.text: And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it should obey you.

text:
(Luk 17:5-6) And this was done by "Abraham the Syrian".
 
Therefore, a religious person should not have anything to fear or worry about, there are no difficult things for him. Abraham the Syrian destroyed the mountain with his religion. God's prophet Elijah stopped the rain, God's prophet Moses parted the Eritrean sea, God's prophet Joshua stopped the sun, our righteous father Abune Aregawi was placed on a dragon with the strength of his faith and morals, Father Samuel Zewaldba was commuting on a lion.
 
Therefore, the answer is morality, and religion.

text.text: Morality means fasting, prayer, prostration, almsgiving, humility, love, etc. I

text:
n general, it is doing all the things that God loves. In the same way, not doing things that God doesn't like is called spiritual work, it is called a manifestation of religion. If we do this, nothing difficult can happen to us.

Another thing we need to understand is that the duty of a Christian is always to live in hope, not despair. As the apostle St. Paul said, "

text.text: Stand firm in the religion you have learned,"
we are expected to live steadfastly in faith in God. We must live in hope, believing that God, who saved us, sacrificed his only son and paid the price for us on the cross

text:
. (Col. 2:7)
 
People may experience a lot of suffering and pain while living in this world. Our lives will be full of trials. If we look at the story of Job, when his wealth and possessions were lost, when all his children died and his whole body was struck by disease, he trusted God and lived patiently, but did not give up hope. It is said, "Job was tested like gold in fire." God spoke to Job in the cloud. After that he cured him of all his diseases. He blessed all his wealth and made it twice as much as before and gave him blessed children, servant men and women. (Job 1:21)
 
(Continues)👇

text: This service is the English version of our Amharic service

The purpose of this service is to bridge the language barrier that many face when trying to learn about the faith and bring the success we had with the Amharic program to a whole new set of audience. 

We provide 24/7 Q&A support, lessons on the major feasts, lessons on the teachings of the church, a medium where fellow Orthodox can connect, discuss and encourage one onother. Members can ask publicly on Telegram or privately on Facebook, Telegram or using our email address. 

We also provide spiritual support over phone by assisting in a number of ways. 

We post everyday at 11:30pm EST on Telegram and have presence in other social medias as well:

(click English for language)

The intended audience for our service is anyone age 16 and up. This is a very safe space where people ask about anything and everything which is why we have an age restriction. However we do not have a faith restriction: anyone who wants to learn about the faith is welcome. They can ask questions, read what we post, call us and use the service to help them in their spiritual journey. 

Our service is not common and the best way to understand the value we offer is to experience it by asking questions, reading regularly, inviting friends, communicating with your fellow brothes and sisters, calling us for spiritual support, staying fully engaged and

You may also share hyms, icons, news and so forth that you think is super useful to your Orthodox brothers and sisters as long as it doesn't have a link.

You can search through content using this method: 

Say you want to read about marriage, then you search

and all the answers and lessons that have 'marriage' as their topic will show up. If you want to read a lesson, you choose the ones that has 3 hands (👉🏾👉🏾👉🏾) whereas if you want Q&A, you choose the ones thtat have 1 hand only (👉🏾). 

Say you want to search all the content that have both 'repentance' and 'fornication' in the topic, then you search:

and you will get all the relevant results. 

Clicking the highlighted text above will also take you to those topics.

This service has the blessings of Abune Ermias (Bishop) which can be seen in some of our YouTube videos (in Amharic), is mainly lead by Like Hiruyan Tserse Abebe (Priest, church Scholar and head of the EOTC's public relations department), Aba Wolde Giorgis (Monk), Memeher Simur Getenet (priest and Church scholar)

Although the above are the major personals in the service, there are numerous others who serve day and night as volunteers.

Although the Church that has initiated this service is the EOTC, we sometimes reference and allow you to post material from any Orthodox Church, eastern and oriental.   

It is the order of God that His people first be served and thus we have done for the past three years with the Amharic service. By the will of God we are now providing the service in English so everyone can learn about the true faith regardless of their background. Hence we urge you to spread awareness of this service and be a reason for the salvation of your friends, family and even coworkers. Do not hide God's talent in the ground (The Parable of the Talents Matthew 25:14-30)

text.text:
👉Question: Does marital status determine whether to receive Holy Communion? For example, if we are single, married, what if our partner is not willing? Or what should I do if my fiance refuses to marry me in the sacrament?

✍Answer

text:
: One of the sacrements of the New Testament is Christ's holy flesh and His precious blood. We have said that the special gift of the Holy Spirit that we have been blessed with since the birth of a boy on the 40th day and the birth of a girl on the 80th day is the food of eternal life. To separate from this is to die although we seem alive simply because we breath. Our body: If we lose  food for a few days or even for few hours for some people, it is definitely not possible to stay alive. This is one of the common weaknesses of the body where we lose our fleshly existence. Likewise, if the soul loses Christ's holy flesh and precious blood, it dies and has no life. It means that we have killed it. Therefore, in order to eat this eternal life, to drink that gives eternal life, we should learn what kind of system and what kind of spiritual preparation we should follow. We are commanded by God to live a Christian life, of which the Holy Eucharist is the foundation. Any teaching that keeps us away by threatening and exaggerating for other reasons is false teaching and should be avoided. 

Apostle St. Paul said that if we eat and drink the ultimate food of the soul without preparation and understanding, it will be a debt to us. This means that it is necessary to always have a life prepared for repentance and to accept those who are counselors in the affairs of our souls, the fathers of the church whom God has appointed as our servants and shepherds. In other words, we are commanded to always receive with repentance, so that we do not make this mistake that St. Paul wrote about (so that we do not receive without deserving or understanding this), but there is no occasion where we are commanded to depart from this mystery, not even for a single day.

Therefore, for those who are said to be before marriage, as we mentioned above, we should realize that we should continue to accept what we received in our childhood, that started from the time of Christianity,  until the end of our lives. But we should do this without committing any shame or sin as that is the only thing which keeps us away from the Holy Communion. Everyone knows what sin or shame is that keeps us away from the Holy Communion, even a child knows. There is no one who does not know the type of sin from the smallest to the highest level of sin. Murder, adultery, adultery, all these seeming sins can keep you away from the sacrament. But through repentant and reprimanded, you can continue the communion by repenting and being mentored and taught by their penitent father. 

Back to the question, it is to say that we should do this throughout our life, and it is not a matter of martial status. Both the male and female start participating in this sacrement at the time of their baptism and actively participate alone until they reach maturity age. After that, the man chooses someone who resembles him in his spiritual life and the woman chooses someone who resembles her in her spiritual life and they get married and continue with the Holy Communion together. Even those who are not married in the Holy Communion, without having this opportunity, come to repentance and they, too, can continue their holy purpose that they have abandoned. Because the Church has made a system for us, it has reconciliation for all from her creator.

To be continued 👇

text:
(Continued part)👆👇.
 
In general, the sacrament does not depend on the state of marriage; After all, the Holy Church has never commanded us to stay away from the Holy Communion for a single day until marriage. This is an attitude that some people have brought by habit, or even counselors and teachers have been absorbed in the people's system, not God's system; and we need to understand that it is not the correct teaching of the Church. Besides, it is not an honor for us to continue to be a father of repentance for people living far from the Holy Communion, but a great shame. Why? The first and foremost task of a penitent father is to teach his penitent children, equip them for penance and Holy Communion, and watch over them to live steadfastly in this spiritual life. But as we can see what is happening in practice, does everyone who is a Christian receive the Holy flesh and the precious blood of Christ?  Not really.
 
On the other hand although it is not comparable with our faith, when we see other faith institutions around the world who claim to be in Christianity, even those who do not believe in partaking fekm His holy flesh and precious blood do not leave without receiving 'in rememberence' each time they come to their church, never. Our church, however, does not consider the Holy Communion as a memorial, and not do not take this mystery simply or boldly. Rather, we receive it believing that it is the real holy flesh and his noble blood that our Creator shed for us through all that suffering on Friday; and we accept it in the fear of God . This is Christian ethics. As Christian ethics, we correct our wrongdoing and accept it through a life of repentance. So, the only thing that may keeps us far from the Holy Communion before and during marriage is our own sin.

So the answer to the question is that if there is a time when we are different from Holy Communion, the biggest thing is our own reason. Thi may be, either we didn't get real lesson of the Orthodox Church; Or that we are not willing to repent for what we committed a sin; Or that we have not decided to stop that sin. But, in general, there is no time to deprive us the Holy Communion except in this way.

(to be continued)

text.text: Beloved and respected, all our members who follow the orthodox education that we convey on John's Repentance page; Based on the topic mentioned above, we have sent you the important lesson below, so we entrust you all to read and learn from it.
I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever, and the bread that I give for the life of the world is my body." (John 6:51)

text: This word speaks of the body of Christ in which eternal life is found. And this flesh was obtained from the Virgin Mary. The Gospel of John begins as follows: "

text.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God... and the Word became flesh"

text:
(John 1:1 and 14). When he said, "The Word became flesh," he is actually confirming that the Son of God came down from the heavens to save the fallen Adam, took the flesh from the Virgin Mary's body, and the soul from her soul, and appeared as a man. This is God who became man. Because, in the Old Testament (before God appeared in the flesh), God asked Adam, "Where are you, Adam?" / Gen. 3:10/ After making him tell his whereabouts, He gave him a promise of salvation, "I will be born from your grandson and save you" (Klemenitus).

Later, when the time came, the angel Gabriel was sent to the Virgin Mary and said to her, "

text.text: Behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son, and you will call his name Jesus, and he will be great."

text: He is also called the son of the innocent. (Luke 1:1-3) Holding this word, when we refer back what Isaiah said in his prophecy, "...

text.text: therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign, behold, a virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and she will call his name Immanuel."

text:
He says. (Isaiah 7:14)

The Lord Jesus also taught extensively about Bread from Heaven (John 6: 22-59). His teachings of ‘Bread from Heaven’ are the basis for Mystery of Holy Eucharist. St John the Evangelist summarized this as follows: “

text.text: Most assuredly, I say to you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you have no life in you. Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day. For My flesh is food indeed, and My blood is drink indeed. He who eats My flesh and drinks My blood abides in Me, and I in him.”

text:
(John 6:53-56). This eternal word remains to be the core theology of mystery of Holy Eucharist.

Jesus Christ, when he taught about his holy body and his precious blood, which was begotten from the Virgin Mary, united and given to the world for salvation, he said, "

text.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man, and drink his blood, ye have no life in you.

text:
" (John 6:53).
All those who eat and drink the flesh and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, who was crucified on Friday to save us, will inherit the kingdom.

text.text: The holy body and the noble blood given to the world for salvation is from the Virgin Mary. This is why we call her the cause of salvation (sign of salvation) in our teaching about the Virgin Mary.

text: Also, the prophet Isaiah said, '

text.text: Lord God will give you a sign', then using a connecting word "behold", he continued saying a virgin will conceive and give birth to a son,

text: God has revealed to the house of David that the sign for the revelation of the Messiah and the salvation of mankind is a virgin and that she will conceive as a virgin. Later, when the prophecy was fulfilled while angel Gabriel was sent from God "
," the evangelist Lukas wrote in connection with the words of the prophet Isaiah, "

-  Before incarnation, there were two natures and two persons. Divinity and Humanity. The Divine nature, God the Son, is one nature with the Father and the Holy Spirit. He is also one of the three persons of God. He is present everywhere, is eternal, knows everything, and can do everything. On the other aspect was Humanity, the Human nature. Humanity is a combination of Flesh/body (Soil, Air, Fire, Water) and rational Soul (Think, Speak, Immortal). The human nature has limited knowledge and power. We believe that God the Son perfectly united with body and soul from St Virgin Mary. A prominent church scholar, St Cyril (Kyrillos) explained this biblical fact saying “starting from incarnation, there is only one person Jesus Christ. Whatever belongs to Divinity, is an attribute of His humanity and whatever belongs to humanity is an attribute of His Divinity.”
 
Based on Orthodox teachings, incarnation is from two Persons to one Person; and from two natures to one united nature. From two Persons to one Person means Divine Person and Human united in to one hypostasis, Jesus Christ – He is both perfectly Divine and perfectly Human. Similarly, from two natures to one nature means Divine nature and Human nature perfectly united in to one united nature.

text: My life has been polluted by sins and I wanted to repent. But I was very afraid of falling into the same sin again, so I thought before I repent, I should try to overcome the sin that challenges me. If I win, then I will repent and cleanse myself of the past. What do you advise me about this?

: Among the ways of salvation that Satan fights against, there is no better than repentance, because repentance destroys all the edifices of sin that the enemy, the devil, has built to destroy the lives of Christians, making it not exist by God's grace. Because of this, he tries to prevent us from repentance, and even if we were to repent, he will never stop doing his best to prevent it from happening sooner than later. Among the obstacles to repentance that the enemy, the devil, uses to keep people in sin or prolong the time for repentance:

1.

: They can be sudden challenges or opportunities, but they disable us from repenting by creating obstacles.

2.

text.text: To convince the sinner that he is better by comparing himself with those who have sinned more than him and that he does not need repentance

text:
, but holiness should not be compared to a sinful life.

3.

text.text: Being guided by environmental influences due to the weakness

text:
. Saint Paul said, "Do not be conformed to this world." Romans 12:2 A small fish swims in a stormy sea. A Christian should withstand such temptations and live a spiritual life.

4.

: The devil does not fight us directly to prevent us from repenting, but he delays us from repenting by suppressing various hidden temptations and reasons. One of the dangers of procrastination is changing the heart prepared for repentance and destroying the opportunity for repentance. If sin is not crushed immediately and continues, it will take root and become an addiction, and then it can destroy the regret and desire for repentance.

5.

:  Before we fall into sin, Satan makes us sin by thinking of God's goodness and forgiveness, and after we sin, he reminds us of God's judgment and cruelty and discourages us from repenting.

6.

text.text: By making the repentant think that he is not a sinner, that he is justified by self-admiration

text:
.  A man cannot change what he thinks is good unless he believes that his own life is corrupted by sin. If there is no spiritual change in his life, he will not think about repentance. He does not repent, so he does not examine himself.

7.

: According to Saint Isaac, if there is no God-fearing, there is no repentance. Sometimes, some people take out "GOD-fearing" from their hearts in excuse of love. At this time, they become careless about their penitential life and fall into sin. Because of sin, they lose the love of God that leads them to repentance.

In general, it is not appropriate to live as a slave of sin or to fight without repenting but fighting with and winning the devil, falling and getting up in repentance. Joshua son of Sirak told his son that if he wanted to serve God, he should prepare himself for the challenges he would face. Satan is jealous of our spiritual work when it comes to our fasting and repentance. He fights to prevent us from accepting the value of our labor. He will prepare every trap so that we will fall. He tells us that you will not leave us until we surrender. But as St. Peter told us, "Your partner the devil prowls around like a roaring lion looking for someone to devour. Knowing that your brothers in the world have received all that suffering, resist him steadfastly in faith (1 Peter 5:89), we should remember this advice and fight, not give up or run away in fear."

In the work that a person does, while controlling his body and humbly contributing the good, he is given the repentance which he discards the evil work day by day with. "Not even heaven is clean before God, let alone a man who drinks sin like water." Job 15:15.

(Continues)👇

(Continued) 👆

Since it is impossible for a person to be free from sin, repentance is done in the morning and in the evening if needed, but it is not delayed so we don't accumulate sin. The righteousness or sin that a person does every day is written in God's record. If we repent for our sin to our father of confession and wash it with tears of repentance, it will be destroyed. Today, we give the pitty excuse that we are ashamed to tell the priest, but we don't know when we will be taken away. We will be taken away suddenly and may hear the word " go away from me" on judgment day. Because if we die while we are in sin and not repenting, we will suffer in the after life. Therefore, we must realize that living in sin while being subject to sin is a shame for the soul.

In addition to this, not only will we lose the death of our soul by not repenting, but even when we live on earth, our fasting and prayers will not be fruitful without repentance. Fasting or any spiritual service is a practice period where we try to get closer to God. Sin pushes us out of this life. Therefore, in order to get closer to God, one should quickly remove sin through repentance. During fasting, just as the body is forbidden from food, the soul is also forbidden from all earthly and worldly desires. For this we return to God through repentance; And God will return to us. "Behold, the hand of God is not shortened from saving, nor his ear deaf from hearing, but your iniquity has separated between you and your God, and your sin has hidden his face from you." (Isa 59:1:2) Therefore, food served on a beautiful and polished table will make me happy, fasting and prayer done with repentance and a clean and polished body will bring reward. Since it is impossible for a person to be free from sin, repentance is done in the morning and in the evening if needed, but it is not delayed so we don't accumulate sin. text:

To sum up, to live in sin is death and slavery. Sin takes away from us peace, rest, tranquility, understanding. It also causes stress. It keeps us away from the grace and fruits of the Holy Spirit. It takes away from God's sonship, from the protection of the Trinity, from life, from love, from the goodness and virtues of God. Sin will also take us to eternal death. There are ups and downs in the journey of life. The crutch that help us stand up again is repentance. Repentance is like being born again or being regenerated every time. Anyone who commits sins every now and then adds diseases to old age. The Christianity of a person who does not repent is useless and his sins will be many. A person who repents and frequently examines himself for his soul with his confession father is like a healthy and peaceful person because he always asks a doctor for help.

So our questioner, thinking about running away from repentance and fighting sin is like making a plan to widen the door for sin or extending the date for repentance, so we recommend that this is not appropriate. Instead, as our Lord Jesus Christ told us, "if your burden is heavy, come to me", because he called us to help us from our burden, we must repent and fight to be freed from sin by taking down our burden continuously. God is our power to be able to do what we think we cannot do. It is said to draw near to God and he will draw near to you (Jas 4:8). 👉Question: If two adults got married outside of the church but are Orthodox Christians, are they still able to take Holy Communion now? Or do they need to first take Communion together?

✍Answer

text: Our family, first, it is important to note that any Christian should not be far from the Holy Communion throuh out his/her life once after he/she become child of God in the 40th  and 80th  day of birth; as  they are  baptized and sealed by Holy Communion and entered the gate point of Christianity since then.

text.text: When we come to the question, about marriage:-

text:
Marriage is a great mystery: Because it is a a secret of unity between the divine and the flesh. As our Lord said, they become one flesh. The main cause of this is about the three party involved in marriage: The couple and God! If there is anyone missing, it is not considered marriage. Marriage is an event where by Our flesh becomes His flesh and our blood His blood . It is a secret to the couple sealed in the sacred sacrament. All of this is when marriage is fulfilled in his holy flesh and the glorious blood, This is the time we receive invisible grace in visible service. "Together in the flesh: "thness," thy bones of my bones, and Flesh of My Flesh "(Gen. 2:23). This is a truth realized by this mystery. More than physical unity, we find the unity and love of the spirit. In general, marriage is mystery because the brides will change from physical unity to spiritual unity.
 
Therefore, in short,  marriage is unity of two opposite sexes, which is true and Christian marriage fulfilled in the sacrament. Because of physical unity, we will grow up to the unity and love of the spirit, and our Lord Jesus Christ will be our spiritual support. So,  any other than this Church system,  it is the Gentiles, not a Christian marriage.
 
So our dear member, If you first receive the sacrament upon marriage ceremony, it is not a must to receive together after then; rather they can go alone at their own convinient times and receive Holy couminion alone. Also, when it is convinent time for both, they can also go together and receive individually like others. The main point is that they have to receive it once being together.
 
But,  knowingly or unknowingly , if they were already married out of the Church system,  they must first repent and receive Holy Communion together by the guidance and assistance of their repetance father. This is a special occation where by they will also be dressed an Honor's garment (Caba) and sit  at a special place. All this will be arranged by the assistance of their repetance father.  So, they celebrate this first day in a different spiritual system. After this, they can receive anytime at their convinient time individually at  regular basis. They can also go together when it is convinient time for both. The point is once they receive together, they can  receive Holy Communion individually; at heir convinience. 
 
But if they have not received the Holy Communion before (being together); they cannot then receive individually, or one of them can not receive alone. If the problem is that one of them refusing or not wanting to receive, then he/she will be given series of spiritual lesson and advice through the father of repentance. Then if he/she agreed on it,  they will receive together. And then, they can continue to receive in a regular basis individually. But , if incase, the problem can not be solved, with a series of advise given by the spiritual fathers, then we need to give more try until the end even by involving more Church Scholars and closer families whom he/she can listen. If it still becomes beyond our capacity and if we are sure that all exaustive trial is done ,, then since it is a matter of soul ,a final solution will be given. The solution of the problem will be  recommended by their father of repetance and the final decision on it will be made by the couples mutually or individually .

About the Holy Communion, its Origin and the ceremony

text:
According to the canon of our Church, the Holy Eucharist (Qurban) is one of the seven sacraments of the Church. Qurban is a Surist and Greek (Arabic) word that means blessing, gift of money, knowledge, labor and time. In the Old Testament, the blood of animals offered by the Israelites for their sins and for the glory of God was called a sacrifice.
 
In the Old Testament era, the blood of animals offered by the Israelites for their sins and for the glory of God was called 'sacrifice', 'communion'.

text.text: But in the New Testament, communion or sacrifice means the faithful (true) sacrifice that God offered as an offering to reconcile himself with mankind. Therefore, the sacrament means the perfect body and blood of our God, Jesus Christ, our Savior, the Lamb of God.
It is our God, our Savior, Jesus Christ, who founded the sacrament of the Holy Communion

text: . And the day he started the system is the eve of the crucifixion on Thursday. When our savior established this great system and secret, only his twelve disciples were with him, and he did not reveal it to all the people who were following him as before. This is the reason why the Church still presents it with a veil and honor. When our Lord was sacrificed on the cross, in order to cover Him, the sun was dark the moon was covered with blood and the stars dropped down like withered fruit like chilies .

text.text: Even the angels of heaven dare not touch the sacrifice, for this is given only to the priests.
The Holy Communion is called a mystery

text: . Our Lord Jesus Christ took the bread, blessed it, consecrated it, and gave it to his disciples, saying, "This is my flesh." Therefore, it is a great mystery that the bread is changed into the flesh of God the Son  (the flesh of God) and the wine is the blood of God the Son  (blood of God), that is why it is called the mystery. (Matthew 26:26, Mark 14:22) Even today, the priests prepare the bread only from pure wheat, and they prepare the wine only from pure grapes or raisins.

text.text: When the priest blesses the bread into the flesh of God and the wine into the blood of God, the authority of the priest, the word of God, and through the action of the Holy Spirit transform the bread into the flesh of God the Son (the flesh of God) and the wine into the flesh of God the Son (the flesh of God). This makes the Holy Communion a mystery because it is hidden from the unbeliever, which is visible only to believers with the eyes of faith. In addition, visible service is given the secret of invisible grace
Major Points that we need to understand before receiving Holy Communion
We must believe without doubt that the bread and wine are changed into the body and blood of Jesus Christ.

text:

According to the canon of our Church, the Holy Eucharist (Qurban) is one of the seven sacraments of the Church. Qurban is a Surist and Greek (Arabic) word that means blessing, gift of money, knowledge, labor and time. In the Old Testament, the blood of animals offered by the Israelites for their sins and for the glory of God was called a sacrifice.
 
In the Old Testament era, the blood of animals offered by the Israelites for their sins and for the glory of God was called 'sacrifice', 'communion'.
 
But in the New Testament, communion or sacrifice means the faithful (true) sacrifice that God offered as an offering to reconcile himself with mankind. Therefore, the sacrament means the perfect body and blood of our God, Jesus Christ, our Savior, the Lamb of God.

It is our God, our Savior, Jesus Christ, who founded the sacrament of the Holy Communion. And the day he started the system is the eve of the crucifixion on Thursday. When our savior established this great system and secret, only his twelve disciples were with him, and he did not reveal it to all the people who were following him as before. This is the reason why the Church still presents it with a veil and honor. When our Lord was sacrificed on the cross, in order to cover Him, the sun was dark the moon was covered with blood and the stars dropped down like withered fruit like chilies . Even the angels of heaven dare not touch the sacrifice, for this is given only to the priests.
 
The Holy Communion is called a mystery. Our Lord Jesus Christ took the bread, blessed it, consecrated it, and gave it to his disciples, saying, "This is my flesh." Therefore, it is a great mystery that the bread is changed into the flesh of God the Son  (the flesh of God) and the wine is the blood of God the Son  (blood of God), that is why it is called the mystery. (Matthew 26:26, Mark 14:22) Even today, the priests prepare the bread only from pure wheat, and they prepare the wine only from pure grapes or raisins. When the priest blesses the bread into the flesh of God and the wine into the blood of God, the authority of the priest, the word of God, and through the action of the Holy Spirit transform the bread into the flesh of God the Son (the flesh of God) and the wine into the flesh of God the Son (the flesh of God). This makes the Holy Communion a mystery because it is hidden from the unbeliever, which is visible only to believers with the eyes of faith. In addition, visible service is given the secret of invisible grace.

- We must believe without doubt that the bread and wine are changed into the body and blood of Jesus Christ. "And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body..this is my blood, drink. (Matthew 26:26)

text.text: Respected and beloved John's repentant website members, who follow the Orthodox lesson and spiritual counsel  which we serve to provide in a daily basis; It is to be recalled that, we sent a series of sections on the basic points on the subject. Today, we have sent you the next part as follows, so we entrust you all to read and learn from it.

text:
1.       A person who is not present when the Liturgy begins or who doesn't follow it thoroughly by being present for the whole service is not allowed to receive the Eucharist. Likewise, a priest cannot serve in Liturgy if he isn't present before it starts. Therefore, when we plan to receive the Eucharist, we should make sure to arrive at the church before the Liturgy begins.

2.       It is necessary to focus our thoughts on the Liturgy, approach in fear of God, and most importantly, we should approach in an absolute belief to get salvation for our body and soul in the Holy Eucharist

3.       If you know the prayer to be prayed when you receive Holy Communion, you should say it in heart, or else, we should approach it in the fear of God by thinking repeatedly in our hearts that this is the flesh and blood of Christ. In the same way, when receiving it, you should say 'Amen' once on the body and twice on the blood. (Mass Apostles)

4.       According to the order of the Church, from the bishops to the deacons, to the faithful, everyone receives the Holy Communion in line according to their rank.

5.       Once after receiving the Holy flesh and blood of Jesus Christ, you should drink Holy water. This holy water is served right there for those who received Eucharist, and it represents the water that flowed from our Lord's right side while he was pierced by a spear as he was on the cross.  Then, you should cover your mouth because it helps to remember that we shouldn't discuss earthly things before we eat something (Fit Men 13 Krista 65).

6.       If possible, it is preferable for the receiver of Holy Communion to be accompanied by someone.  But this is not an obligation or a law written by the church, but from the point of view of having someone by his side to help facilitating things so that he does not face challenges. 

8.       Those who do not believe and didn't take lesson about the Holy Communion are forbidden to receive it. So, it is necessary to monitor and control this.  (Ft Men 23 Rasub 44) They should first get a lesson from their church teachers or from their father of repetance about the Mystrery of communion in advance and believe that the sacrament they receive is the flesh and blood of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

9.       If a penitent person falls ill with a fatal illness before completing the period of penance, he is not prevented from receiving the Eucharist. On the other hand, a person who is in the canon of penance cannot receive Holy Communion without finishing the canon he received, unless he is in a life-threatening illness.
 
10.   A person who is tormented by a demon, a sick person, is not prevented from receiving Holy Eucharist. (Ft Men 13)

text.text: The precautions a Christian should take on the day he receives Holy Communion, and the Christian life he should have in his future life:

text:
1.       On the day a Christian receives Holy Communion, he should not wash his body with water, he should not take off his clothes and be naked, he should not draw blood from his body.
 
2.        He should not do hard work that can cause fluid (sweat) on our body, he should not walk a long way (because this is also considered work).
 
3.       Even if we live in a married life, it is necessary to abstain from sexual intercourse 3 days before receiving Holy Communion and 2 days after receiving Holy Communion. 
 
4.       He should not eat too much, drink intoxicating drinks that disturb what we have eaten and drunk.
 
5.       On the day we received Holy Communion, it is forbidden to cut nails, shave hair, bow and kneel, spit, bathe in water, and change clothes before the end of the day. (Liturgy No. 166) We can change our cloths at the evening after 6:00pm, as it is considered as the next day.

6.       if a person experiences nose bleeding , vomit, bodily bleeding, wounds, and a gnat that enters his mouth by Being careless or due to not taking appropriate care on the day of receiving the Holy Communion,  he should tell this to his penitent  father and  he should repent. And he cannot receive the Holy Communion again without performing his penance.  
 
7.       It is forbidden to go to Court and argue on the day you receive Holy Communion. (Council of Nicaea) In general, one should not go to a public place where there is an argument, argue with someone, talk with hard words, do work that provokes anger, and such other things after communion on that day.
 

8.       Before we receive Holy Communion, we should ask for forgiveness and be cleared of our sins of enmitity and revenge through repetance; and promise not to return back on it. So, now after receiving Holy Communion, we should refreain by far from argument, dispute and grudge. We should  be more committed to stay back from being offended, rebuked, or quarreled with. Even if it happens being out of control, we should ask for forgiveness, let go of grudges, repent and accept it as it should be. Be it from your family or social life, you should stay away from this type of situation as much as possible and spend everything patiently so that you don't have ideas that bring resentment and quarrels. We should live in love with everyone.
 
9.       After receiving Holy Communion, we should refrain from any sinful activity, such as adultery, murder, theft, gossip, addiction, fraud, lying, and the like. 
 
10.   After receiving Holy Communion, it is appropriate to listen to the word of God, go to church regularly, pray, fast, prostrate, and generally live a spiritual life and Christian behavior.

11.   It is necessary for us to have a regular prayer program in our personal life. Because the main spiritual struggle that we can do is through prayer so that Satan does not fight and deprive us of the blessings we have received through the Holy Communion.
 
12.   In general, it is appropriate to know that when we live bounded by the Holy Communion, it is never appropriate to go to a place that is contrary to spiritual life and to associate with a situation that exposes us to sin. We should fight against all the evil temptations and sin.

(Continues) 👇🏾

3.       Even if we live in a married life, it is necessary to abstain from sexual intercourse 3 days before receiving Holy Communion and 2 days after receiving Holy Communion. 
 
4.       He should not eat too much, drink intoxicating drinks that disturb what we have eaten and drunk.
 
5.       On the day we received Holy Communion, it is forbidden to cut nails, shave hair, bow and kneel, spit, bathe in water, and change clothes before the end of the day. (Liturgy No. 166) We can change our cloths at the evening after 6:00pm, as it is considered as the next day.

6.       if a person experiences nose bleeding , vomit, bodily bleeding, wounds, and a gnat that enters his mouth by Being careless or due to not taking appropriate care on the day of receiving the Holy Communion,  he should tell this to his penitent  father and  he should repent. 7.       It is forbidden to go to Court and argue on the day you receive Holy Communion. 8.       Before we receive Holy Communion, we should ask for forgiveness and be cleared of our sins of enmitity and revenge through repetance; and promise not to return back on it. So, now after receiving Holy Communion, we should refreain by far from argument, dispute and grudge. We should  be more committed to stay back from being offended, rebuked, or quarreled with. Even if it happens being out of control, we should ask for forgiveness, let go of grudges, repent and accept it as it should be. Be it from your family or social life, you should stay away from this type of situation as much as possible and spend everything patiently so that you don't have ideas that bring resentment and quarrels. We should live in love with everyone.
 
9.       After receiving Holy Communion, we should refrain from any sinful activity, such as adultery, murder, theft, gossip, addiction, fraud, lying, and the like. 
 
10.   After receiving Holy Communion, it is appropriate to listen to the word of God, go to church regularly, pray, fast, prostrate, and generally live a spiritual life and Christian behavior.

11.   It is necessary for us to have a regular prayer program in our personal life. Because the main spiritual struggle that we can do is through prayer so that Satan does not fight and deprive us of the blessings we have received through the Holy Communion.
 
12.   In general, it is appropriate to know that when we live bounded by the Holy Communion, it is never appropriate to go to a place that is contrary to spiritual life and to associate with a situation that exposes us to sin. We should fight against all the evil temptations and sin.

text.text: The Precautions and Christian Life a Believer Should Follow Before and After Receiving Holy Communion.

text:
Holy Communion signifies a commitment to follow the Orthodox Church's teachings, which should inspire us to perform good works and acts of charity. It is not a reward, but a means to receive God's grace. Preparation through confession and repentance is crucial before partaking. Holy Communion symbolizes the union between the believer and Christ, affirming our commitment to His teachings.

The main reason why we should approach Holy Communion with spiritual diligence is not because the Son of God, His holy body, or His precious blood can be defiled by anything else, but rather because we are united with His flesh and blood. We must always strive to live in a manner that avoids the obstacles that Satan, who is jealous of our salvation, places in our way to tempt us and lead us into sin. In order to save ourselves from sin, we must participate in the holy ceremony of receiving the flesh and blood of Christ, which we take for our eternal salvation. We must spend our lives in faith and conduct, doing righteous works. Christian vigilance is necessary because Satan often throws subtle obstacles in our way.

If we stumble and fall into sin after receiving Holy Communion, we must repent and confess our sins to the priest. We should stop receiving Holy Communion for the time being, complete our penance, and seek advice and guidance from the priest before resuming Holy Communion. Once we begin to receive Holy Communion, we should avoid sins and offenses that would prevent us from approaching it. If we commit a sin that should not be repeated after receiving Holy Communion, we have dishonored this great sacrament and must repent and work to strengthen our spiritual purpose.

We should not take repentance lightly or assume that we can continue to repeat the same offense. We must strive to control our thoughts and emotions, live steadfastly in morals and faith, and quickly repent if we fall into sin. We must constantly strive to strengthen our spiritual purpose in order not to be separated from the Holy Communion.

In addition, there are certain rituals and beliefs that may be common in some places but are not in accordance with the Church's canon and tradition. When we encounter doubt or confusion, we should seek guidance from the Church fathers, teachers, and scholars to clarify the true teachings of the Church. We should not be led astray by beliefs or practices that are outside of the Church's system. As St. Paul advised Timothy, "Avoid godless chatter, because those who indulge in it will become more and more ungodly" (2 Timothy 2:16).
