Question፦ Hello father, what can I do to stop my adultery with women?

Answer፦

text:
Dear member if John's Repentance service, It is indeed a matter of great consequence that you bring before us, for the act of adultery is a sin that profoundly afflicts both individual souls and societies at large. A sin not only of the flesh, but one of dissatisfaction and desire for novelty, it is a significant challenge that must be grappled with, not just for the individuals involved, but for the community as a whole. As we know from the teachings of our Lord Jesus Christ in Matthew 12:39, he condemned the adulterous and wayward generation, hinting at a spiritual restlessness and discontent that undergirds the act of adultery itself.

We must understand that adultery has many faces. It is not confined merely to the illicit relations between a man and a woman. Indeed, it stretches to a fundamental restlessness and desire for constant change. It is a yearning for more and for new, a persistent dissatisfaction with the present moment and circumstances. This adulterous attitude stretches beyond mere romantic relationships and seeps into every aspect of life.

Adultery, then, is the act of desiring more than what is given to us by God. It is the refusal to accept and be content with what we have, to honour and cherish what God has bestowed upon us. It is a revolt against the divine will and order, which dictates that a man is meant for one woman and vice versa.

Moreover, the act of infidelity extends beyond the marital bed. It extends to all relations outside the institution of holy matrimony - it is the indulgence in sexual acts before marriage, self-gratification, homosexuality, and even worshipping false gods. The sin of Israel against their idols, for example, is a form of spiritual adultery. To stray from the path that our God has illuminated for us and to follow another is to commit spiritual adultery.

What, then, is the remedy for such a condition? It lies in combating the very tendencies that give rise to adultery. If we are prone to seeking the new and untried, we must strive to remain content with what we have, adhering to the teachings of God. Recognizing the harm and destructiveness of adultery is the first step towards redemption. This harm can manifest itself in various ways, whether it is through consuming inappropriate media, participating in illicit activities, or allowing our thoughts to wander into immoral territories.

The antidote lies in understanding the gravity of the sin and recognizing its consequences. As we see in Genesis 19, those who indulged in debauchery and adultery in the time of Lot were consumed by divine fire, while those who stayed true to God's commandments were saved. Understanding the potential for destruction that adultery harbors, we can then arm ourselves with the strength and resolve to resist such temptations.

Fasting, prostrating, praying, repenting, participating actively in the Church, and engaging with the Word of God are key practices that can fortify us against this sin. These acts of devotion help foster a spiritual mindset that is resistant to the allure of adultery. Furthermore, we can find solace and strength in the lives and stories of those who remained chaste and virtuous, for these stories bear testament to the possibility of a virtuous life.

Ultimately, the path to redemption from this sin lies in following in the footsteps of our spiritual ancestors, who triumphed over such temptations and remained true to their faith. We must strive to cultivate a steadfastness of spirit, resisting the allure of novelty and change and finding contentment in the divine order that God has set before us.

text.text:
Thus, may God, our loving Father, imbue us with the strength and fortitude of our spiritual forefathers to resist the destructive lure of adultery. For it is in His power and mercy that we find our salvation.

© John's Repentance

Question፦ Hello my fathers, how should spiritual courtship be? I am very hesitant on having a girlfriend because if I do, I'll spend a lot of time on the phone and this will affect my spiritual life. And I become ashamed of going to church, my prayers aren't even very authentic. Please advise me?

Answer፦

text:
Dear member, Your question is a deeply important one, an echo of the struggle that youth face in the realm of spirituality and technology today. Modernity and its offerings have brought us closer to the brink of not just convenience, but also possible spiritual calamity. Technology, while possessing many advantages, can act as an Achilles' heel in our pursuit of righteousness.

Just as the law, culture, and tradition once curtailed our potential missteps, we now find that technology, unconstrained by these boundaries, offers numerous opportunities for sinful deeds even as we sit alone, or among a crowd, with a phone in our hand. Thus, your apprehension about fostering relationships through these mediums is both valid and wise.

Indeed, in the realm of friendships and courtship, the digital world poses a challenge. It may offer an illusion of connection, an impression of love, yet the risks of transgressions are manifold. Conversations held in the sanctuary of technology, where both parties are physically distant, can lead to misunderstanding, misdeeds, and regrettable outcomes. Herein lies the paradox of technology - it has the potential for both good and harm.

(Continues)👇🏾

text:
👆🏾

Yet, despite this turbulent sea of modern possibilities, we must remember that the finding of a good spouse is not impossible. While the process requires vigilance, prayer, and patience, it is attainable. The success of one among a hundred should not discourage you, but inspire you, knowing that the effort you put in to find a partner who strengthens your spirituality, is worthwhile.

Unfortunately, the trials and tribulations of this search can sometimes distance us from our Church, disrupt our peace of mind, hinder our prayers, and obstruct our service to God. It is a difficult paradox to navigate - the pursuit of a Godly union often making us feel more removed from God Himself.

This predicament that you, and many others, find yourselves in reflects the inherent imperfection of our human condition. Even in our quest for what seems good and desirable, we stumble and err. This is particularly difficult for those striving to live a Christian life, for we are intimately aware of our wrongdoings and live under the shadow of guilt. Each mistake feels like a sharp, chastising word from God Himself.

However, remember this: It is the duty of conscience to blame us when we err, but it is also our privilege as God's children to seek His forgiveness and guidance. Before you embark on your journey of seeking a life partner, immerse yourself in prayer. Ask God to light your path, to guide your steps, and to reveal the right woman to you.

This journey is not solely about your wisdom or educational attainment. It is about discerning God's will and finding a spouse who complements your spiritual journey. The path is fraught with distractions and temptations. Do not let your gaze linger on the superficial, for it can lead to the 'fornication of the eyes', 'fornication of thought', and ultimately 'fornication of action'.

Seek counsel and advice, for it can offer much-needed guidance. Lean on God's wisdom to help navigate this complex terrain. This plea is not one to be taken lightly, for falling into sin and straying from God is a perilous journey that the devil is all too eager to encourage.

However, remember, no matter the mistakes made yesterday, today offers a new opportunity to approach God and admit, "I have sinned." We should never shy away from God due to our guilt and shame. To distance oneself from our merciful Father is a grave error, for it is He who forgives, renews, and revives us in our spiritual destruction.

God, the sanctifier of the saints, corrects us not to condemn us, but to draw us back to his holy path. In Him, we find our path, our strength, and ultimately, our salvation. Remember this and approach your spiritual courtship with the fear of God, the love of His commandments, and trust in His wisdom.

Question፦ Can a pregnant women confess/repent? I ask that because it may be hard for her to do the prostrations that the priests usually ask us to do.

Answer፦

text:
Answering from an Orthodox perspective, it is important to bear in mind the overarching emphasis our Church places on love, mercy, and the sanctity of human life. Pregnancy is a time of unique grace and responsibility, carrying and nurturing within oneself a life created in the divine image. It is a period where women should receive exceptional care, guidance, and protection. 

Now, as to the question of repentance during pregnancy, we must remember that God's forgiveness is not confined by physical gestures or actions, such as prostrations. Rather, true repentance begins in the heart and mind. When a person feels genuine remorse for their sins and seeks God's mercy, the journey towards reconciliation with the divine begins. Prostrations, kneeling, fasting, and the like are valuable aids on this journey, but they are not its essence. The essence is contrition and a sincere desire to turn away from sinful patterns. Thus, pregnant women, as well as all others who for one reason or another cannot perform certain acts of penance, can fully partake in the sacrament of confession and receive absolution for their sins.

If there exists any particular sin that the woman feels particularly burdened by during her pregnancy, it should not remain unspoken out of fear of physical restrictions. Our faith holds life and its preservation as paramount, and it does not demand that a pregnant woman risk her health or that of her unborn child to perform certain acts of penance. What is required is the sincerity of the heart and the genuine intention to rectify one's ways, rather than any physical demonstration of penitence.

Moreover, if any transgressions were committed before the woman discovered her pregnancy, she should bring them to light post-delivery. In the interim period, she should seek the counsel of wise and pious elders, stay constant in prayer, and try to lead a righteous life, nurturing the life within her with love and care. God, who is the ultimate source of wisdom and mercy, knows our intentions, our fears, and our struggles. 

While it is true that Orthodox canon permits certain exemptions for pregnant and nursing women, such as being excused from fasting or performing strenuous acts of prayer, it does not exclude them from spiritual engagement entirely. They are encouraged to maintain a strong prayer life and remain connected with their spiritual fathers for guidance and support.

Lastly, regarding a pregnant woman's participation in communal prayer, the Church recommends a balanced approach. While it's true that faith, not the quantity of prayers or their location, is the ultimate path to salvation, the Church also acknowledges the benefit of community and mutual prayer. A pregnant woman may pray at home, and if she chooses to partake in communal prayer, she should do so in a manner that does not compromise her health or wellbeing. After giving birth, the Church community should extend its arms in love and care, ensuring that the mother and child are enveloped in spiritual blessings and God's grace.

In sum, the Orthodox Church teaches us to prioritize the sanctity of life and the health of the mother and child during pregnancy. True repentance and reconciliation with God begins in the heart, and not in the physical acts associated with penance. While physical restrictions may prevent pregnant women from participating in some traditional acts of penance, they are not precluded from confessing their sins, seeking God's mercy, or participating in communal prayers in a manner that respects their physical condition.

text.text: Beloved members of John's Repentance service, today is the annual feast the St. Michael. Hence we send you this writing so you may read and partake form the Archangel's blessings.

text:
The Archangel St. Michael is highly revered in the Orthodox Church, celebrated for his dedicated service to God and his pivotal role as a protector, intercessor, and warrior against the forces of evil. His presence in biblical narratives and miraculous interventions mark him as a significant figure not just in the spiritual realm, but also in the lives of the faithful.

St. Michael, whose name means “Who is like God”, is the leader of the heavenly hosts and always stands before God's throne, advocating for humanity. This idea is reinforced in the Book of Joshua, where St. Michael appears as the commander of the Lord's army, showing his leadership and divine authority. His steadfast support of the saints and martyrs, offering strength and resilience, further showcases his commitment to God's people.

The church celebrates his feast on the 12th of each month, with two major feasts held on the 12th of Hator/Hidär (November 21st) and on the 12th of Paona/Sëné (June 19th). Celebrating St. Michael through these feasts is a testament to his influence and importance. Traditional practices such as offering alms and holding festivals in his name serve to honor and remember him, reflecting the deeply ingrained respect and love for St. Michael among the faithful.

Miracles are often associated with St. Michael, reinforcing his role as an active, divine participant in human affairs. The story of Dorotheus and Theopista provides a powerful example of this, as St. Michael aids this pious family in their time of need, miraculously providing for them as they honor him with a feast.

The Archangel Michael is often depicted in church iconography in a soldier's attire, symbolizing his role as the commander of the heavenly army. The spear he holds signifies his victory over Satan, as described in the book of Revelation, where he triumphs in the war in heaven, expelling the devil.

St. Michael is also recognized as the angel of the Resurrection, as cited in the Gospel of Matthew. His protective role extends to entire communities, where he is considered the guardian of monasteries, with many churches worldwide built in his honor. His widespread veneration is also reflected in the many people named after him, demonstrating the depth of his impact on the faithful.

St. Michael's humility, despite his grandeur, is evident in the epistle of Jude, where he disputes with the devil over Moses' body, showing restraint and respect for divine authority. He is also known to assist other archangels, such as Gabriel, in their missions.

Finally, as we celebrate the Annual Feast of Archangel Saint Michael, we are reminded of his role in leading the Israelites out of Egypt and guiding them through their journey, as described in the book of Exodus. He is revered as a protector and intercessor, helping those enslaved by sin, advocating for love, harmony, and peace among the faithful. 

To incorporate these lessons into our lives, we are encouraged to emulate St. Michael's humility, strength, and unwavering loyalty to God. Just as he intercedes for humanity, we too should advocate for one another in love and solidarity. And just as he battles the forces of evil, we should strive to resist sin and promote peace and harmony in our lives. As we honor St. Michael, we can draw inspiration from his divine example and aspire to reflect these virtues in our own lives.

The concept of repentance is not limited to the New Testament but is also present in the Old Testament, where the prophets called on the Israelites to repent and turn away from their wicked ways.

Repentance is a process that involves acknowledging one's sins, seeking forgiveness, and committing to change. It requires a humble heart and a willingness to confess one's wrongdoing. In the New Testament, John the Baptist urged the people to "repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand" (Matthew 3:2). The Apostle Peter also encouraged his listeners to repent and be baptized for the forgiveness of their sins (Acts 2:38).

The prophet Jeremiah also called on the people of Israel to repent and turn back to God (Jeremiah 3:12-13).

It is through repentance that Christians can experience God's grace and mercy and draw closer to Him. As the Apostle Paul wrote, "Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation and leaves no regret, but worldly sorrow brings death" (2 Corinthians 7:10).

Accordingly, we will look through the ten ranks that the saints can achieve through struggle and inheritance. The ten spiritual pillars are the steps or ladders on which a person can grow step by step to reach any of these ten spiritual levels or titles. Ten is the number of fullness. It is a symbol of something whole; and we find this numbering in many stories in the Bible, various books, and   history dictionaries. Spirituality means living in the world of the soul, not worrying about what passes and perishes. 

Therefore, it means that when a person grows in his spirituality, everything else that passes and disappears does not bother him except for the matter of the soul.
A person grows physically, mentally, financially …jn the same way, , there is also spiritual growth which goes gradually. As a baby does not become an adult all at once, it is also not possible to grow spiritually at once or to be perfect soon. Therefore,  gradually practice in a continued manner is important to reach the life of our holy fathers. It it is said "Think of your leaders who have told you the word of God, and look at the fruit of their lives and imitate them in faith. Heb 13:7.

In the parable of the farmer and the seed taught by our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, he said, "And another seed fell on good ground, and one yielded a hundred, and one sixty, and one thirty fruits." /Mathew 13:8/ The seed is God's word, and the good soil is Christians who listen to God's word and bear fruit, religion and food. 1 Cor 3:9 It means that according to their work, they will bear 30, 60, 100/ /thirty, sixty, hundred/ fruits or they will get different honors and powers. The ranks of saints are determined by the extent of their legacy of struggle during their lifetime. In the scriptures, it is repeatedly mentioned that God will reward each person according to his work. / Psalm 51:12; Proverbs 14:12; Matthew 16:17; Romans 2:6; Rev. 10:12/.
 
The Ten Spiritual Ranks (Titles) are as follows.

They are divided into three parts of levels /honers:-  called "purity of body, purity of soul, purity of heart".
 
 
1 'ጽማዌ' (Ignorance to worldly matters)

text.text:
the Covenant of Mercy 

Dear members of John's Repentance service, today is the monthly feast of our Lady the Virgin Mary, which is named Covenant of Mercy (ኪዳነ ምህረት). Today we celebrate the Theotokos, who formed an ineffable Covenant of Mercy with the Almighty. We hence send you a lesson on the Theotokos so you can read and participate in the blessings of this day.

text:
Let us delve into sacred scripture, for in the Psalm of David, chapter 89 verse 3, it was proclaimed: “I have made a covenant with my chosen one.” The Virgin Mary, the unblemished Mother of God, stood as a sentinel of ceaseless prayer upon the hallowed grounds of Golgotha where the precious body of her Son once laid. For fifteen years after our Lord's ascension, she devoted herself, with the ardor of a thousand suns, to the intercession for the salvation of our souls.

Oh, what wondrous tales do the ancient tongues whisper of that fateful day, the sixteenth of February, when the celestial host descended! Led by our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the holy angels carried the Virgin to the very heavens. She beheld with her immaculate eyes the dwelling places of the prophets and the saints. Her heart overflowed with joy and she magnified the Lord.

But lo, her heart was soon to be stricken with sorrow. The angels showed her the abyss of despair, where the souls of the hapless were enveloped in the shadow of eternal flame. Wretched and forlorn, they cried out. The Virgin's heart, pure as the driven snow, wept for them.

Returning to the sacred earth, near the tomb of her beloved Son, the Virgin implored the Saviour. Her plea was as the sweetest hymn, a balm to the Heavens. She spoke, “By the manger wherein You were cradled, by the swaddling cloth that embraced You, by the very steps I took by Your side through our sojourn, I beseech You, O Lord, hearken to the humble entreaties of Your handmaiden."

Our Lady sought grace for those who hold her dear, who serve in the temples, who clothe themselves in her honor, who tend to the afflicted, who nourish the hungry, and console the mourning. For these acts of kindness render joy unto her heart, and in turn, may they be blessed with graces unimaginable, with glories unseen and unheard by human senses.

Our Lord Jesus Christ, in His infinite mercy, responded, “As surely as I took on flesh to fulfill the yearnings of your heart, everything you ask shall be granted. I, Emmanuel, do solemnly swear, that My covenant shall never be shattered.”

Thus, my brethren, let us be inspired to lives of piety and charity. Our Lady, who gave birth to God in her chaste womb, she, who remains steadfast as a rock, calls us into her fellowship. How magnificent are the fruits of her womb, and oh, how exalted are those who partake in them!

Through these sacred teachings, we are brought closer to salvation. May the Virgin Mary's intercessions be a refuge, and her boundless love guide us through the tempests of this earthly sojourn.

text.text:
May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every language that He has created, today and always.

May the blessings of the Holy Mother of God, the Virgin, and the Cross be upon us. Amen.

text.text:
Question: Does God listen to prayers? Why are some so successful and other not? Why is it that no matter how much they cry/pray, they're not successful?  

Answer:

text:
In the shadowed halls of the deepest reflections of the human spirit, there resounds a question, both ancient and profound, that beckons the attention of the earnest seeker. With hearts aflutter and souls yearning for the embrace of the divine, we mortals oft implore, "Does the Lord, in His majesty, hearken unto our prayers?" This question, akin to the ceaseless murmur of waves upon the shore, is as ancient as the lament of fallen Adam.

Let us, in humble obedience and trembling reverence, glean wisdom from the Holy Scriptures. For the sacred Word proclaims in Matthew 7:7, "Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you." Lo! How merciful is the Almighty, whose ears are ever attuned to the suppliant's cry!

Yet, we must fathom the depth and breadth of prayer. Forsooth, it is a tapestry woven of thanksgiving and supplication. As we thank our Lord for the blessings showered upon us, we beseech His grace for fortitude in our travails. When, in the freshness of morn, we speak, "Blessed be Thy Name, O Lord, for driving back the dark and bathing us in Thy radiant light," we tender our gratitude whilst praying for His blessings to rain down upon the day.

Let us heed the words of our Savior in Matthew 6:9-13, where He taught us to pray, “Our Father.” Behold the tenderness of His exhortation, for our entreaties ascend not to a distant and indifferent sovereign, but to our heavenly Father. As a father shows compassion to his children, so the Lord shows compassion to those who fear Him.

But, brothers and sisters in Christ, let it not be forgotten that the sincerity of heart is a crucial vessel for our prayers. For the Scriptures implore us to forgive, that we may be forgiven, and to harbor love in the sanctuary of our hearts. Many a prayer is cast asunder for it is borne upon the tainted winds of rancor, whilst those anointed with love find refuge in the embrace of the Almighty.

Contemplate the prayers of Moses, the friend of God. When he pleaded before the Lord, the Red Sea turned into walls and the mountains fled. These marvels were fruits borne out of humility and unyielding faith.

Likewise, let us invoke the blessed mother Yostina, whose pious supplications were received by the Almighty, as chronicled in the sacred text, Sanksar. Truly, the fulfillment of prayers rests not upon the whims of the Lord, but upon the sincerity and purity with which they are offered.

The fathers of old, in their wisdom, declared that prayers, pure and untainted by worldly malice, find favor in the eyes of the Lord. It is not that the Almighty does not hear, but that our prayers are oftentimes like seeds sown amongst thorns; they grow but bear no fruit. text:
The Eucharist, the most sacred of sacraments, as the divine banquet; whereon the Lord’s table is adorned with the Manna from Heaven, the Holy Body, and the Precious Blood of our Saviour. In regularly partaking of this divine sustenance, we are called to a renewal of faith, the forging of an ineffable bond with the Divine, and the fortification of our spirit.

First, let our eyes gaze upon the sanctity of purity and cleanliness as prerequisites to partake of this sacred offering. To approach the table of the Lord, we must be clad in the radiant vestments of repentance and humility. Like the Bride awaiting the Bridegroom, our souls must be pure, ready to receive Him who is the Word made flesh.

As one imbibes the Precious Blood, like a vine, he must draw nourishment from it. For, the Scripture doth proclaim, "I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman. Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me." (John 15:1-5). In communion, we become one with Christ, and our souls entwine with His, like branches to the vine, drawing sustenance for the bearing of good fruits.

But let us also cast our gaze upon the Cross. In this sacrament, the boundless love of God is made manifest, through His Son’s supreme sacrifice. How unfathomable is the love that God hath for us, that He should send His only begotten Son to partake in suffering and death so that we might be free! The blood that was shed at Calvary cries out for our redemption, and in partaking of this Blood, we plead with God for His mercy, forgiveness, and grace.

Moreover, bribed members, consider that in the Eucharist, our sins, though confessed and repented for, are washed anew. For the Body and Blood of Christ hold the power to cleanse us of sins that may have slipped from our memory or have been hidden by the deceit of the Evil One. Through this sacrament, our souls are cleansed from the stains of iniquity, and we are rendered more worthy to stand before the throne of God.

By regularly receiving the Holy Eucharist, we are endowed with the grace to face the tribulations of this world. Christ proclaimed, “In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world” (John 16:33). Through His triumph over death, sin, and Satan, we too are made conquerors. He beckons us to join Him in victory and sit beside Him on His glorious throne (Revelation 3:21).

Let us, therefore, beloved of Christ, clothe ourselves not merely in garments of fabric but in the Holy Spirit. Let our speech, our deeds, and our hearts reflect the Divine grace that has been bestowed upon us through the Eucharist. May it serve as our armor, our sustenance, and our solace. And may we strive always to abide in Him, as He abides in us.

And so, beloved members, let us march forward with renewed vigor and ardor, shedding sloth and worldly concerns. Let the seekers of wisdom come, as the Scripture urges, “Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled. Forsake the foolish, and live; and go in the way of understanding” (Proverbs 9:5-6). With every breath and every heartbeat, let us draw nearer to our Saviour, partaking of His Body and Blood, until the day we are called home to be with Him eternally.

May the blessings of the Holy Mother of God, the Virgin, and the Cross be upon us. Amen.

text.text: Dear members of John's Repentance service, today is the monthly feast if St. Gabriel and so we send you the bellow writing so you can partake of this day's blessings.

text:
Gabriel, whose name from yonder Heavens is an incantation unto itself, embodies the clarion voice of the Lord, signifying “Strength of God.” This celestial herald, with the countenance of a thousand suns and wings unfurled across the firmament, was chosen amongst the angelic throng for a divine purpose. 'Twas on a blessed Sunday, when the stars bowed in silence, that Gabriel defied the darkness of deceit that dared to tarnish God's creation. In this eternal struggle, his palm was seared with purifying flame, a testament to his unyielding devotion.

Thereupon, the Almighty, in His boundless wisdom, did elect Gabriel as the messenger, to deliver tidings of great portent to the Virgin Mary. “Hail, thou that art highly favored, the Lord is with thee,” did Gabriel proclaim, as celestial light cascaded upon Mary, the blessed among women. Thus, the Annunciation was etched into the tapestry of time, woven with the golden threads of divine decree.

The echoes of yore bring forth the tale of Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, brave souls cast into a furnace of fury by Nebuchadnezzar, whose hubris did defy the Heavens. Clad in innocence, their spirits unyielding to despair, they turned their gaze to the Heavens, invoking the intercession of their Creator. Lo, Gabriel descended upon this fiery crucible, his countenance casting shadows upon the raging inferno. His voice, like the murmur of a gentle stream, infused courage into their hearts, as his celestial aura extinguished the flames.

Mighty Gabriel, clad in resplendence, waved his staff and parted the roaring fire, evoking the parting of the Red Sea by Moses through God's grace. The sacred triumvirate, singing praises, tread through the embers unscathed. “Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers,” their voices harmonized with the heavenly choirs, a chorus of salvation.

King Nebuchadnezzar beheld this divine spectacle in awe, as the fourth figure within the inferno appeared likened unto a Son of God. His heart, once stone, became flesh, and he cried out in jubilation, acknowledging the sovereignty of the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.

Ye humble souls, take heed, for in the hour of our lamentation and tribulation, if we call upon the Holy Archangel Gabriel with hearts unburdened by sin, he shall arrive with divine swiftness. His presence is as a fortress, impregnable and steadfast. However, should we tread the path of iniquity, his countenance remains beyond our grasp, for his devotion is eternally to the Holy Name.

Therefore, let us be emboldened by Psalm 91:11, “For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.” Let us be vigilant and steadfast in our faith, calling upon the Archangel Gabriel to shield and guide us through the fires of this earthly sojourn, towards the eternal embrace of the Almighty.

May the blessings of the Holy Archangel Gabriel, protector, and messenger, grace your journey, as you, in sacred steps, walk the path ordained by Heaven’s boundless love.

text:
In the resplendent tapestry of God’s Creation, there exists a luminary surpassing all luminaries, a blessed vessel more sacrosanct than the Cherubim and Seraphim - this, my brethren, is none other than Our Lady, the Theotokos, the Holy Virgin Mary, whom the Creator Himself has chosen as His most hallowed tabernacle. In her, grace, humility, and obedience converge to compose a symphony of Divine Love, where her voice tenderly whispers, “Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.” (Luke 1:38).

It is vital to comprehend the awe and reverence the heavens bear towards the Blessed Virgin. text:
Dear members of John's Repentance spiritual service, today we celebrate the building of the first church - let us venture into the divine tapestry of the first church built in honor of the Holy Mother Saint Mary in Caesarea, Chalcedon. Saint Paul and Saint Barnabas, those stalwart Apostles, were the heralds who sowed the seeds of faith amongst the gentiles. With their hearts aflame, they fervently preached the Good Word. Yet, the believers yearned for a sanctuary to partake in the Holy Communion. The Apostles, led by an unyielding devotion, sought the divine intervention of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ.

Through the ethereal mist of prayer and 'Subae' , a miraculous revelation embraced the Apostles. Summoned from the corners of the earth, they were lifted upon clouds and converged in the land of Philippians, where the Lord bestowed upon them a celestial decree. He ordained that churches in the name of His Holy Mother Mary shall grace the four corners of the world. The trinity of stones, a divine manifestation of the Holy Trinity, took form and were consecrated as the foundation of this sacred abode. 

With renewed clarity, we understand that the measurements – twenty-four cubits in height and twelve cubits in width – symbolize not only the 24 prophets and 24 heavenly priests but also the twelve Apostles. These three stones also epitomize the sacred Arks of the Covenant of Adam, Moses, and Jesus Christ, encompassing the harmony of creation, the Law, and redemption through grace.

With heavenly resplendence, the Lord then anointed Saint Peter as an Archbishop, bestowing upon him the authority to shepherd the faithful across the world. This moment, marked by angelic and earthly acclamation, was sealed with the descent of heavenly bread and the cup. The Holy Communion was performed, sanctifying the Apostles and ordaining them to carry forth the Divine Liturgy.

In this exalted house, the righteous Archbishop Basilios, with a heart full of devotion, sought to venerate the Holy Mother with a portrait. Yet, let this be a reminder of the humility required in service, for the first plate acquired was tainted by a hardened heart. The Holy Mother herself appeared in a vision to Basilios, guiding him to a sacred image, which when placed in the church, emanated healing water and oil, a testament to Her grace and mercy.

Alas, not all who partook of these blessings were deemed worthy, as illustrated by the account of a woman stained by betrayal and bloodshed. Her sins, laid bare before the righteous Basilios, revealed the necessity of repentance and living in accordance with God’s law. She stands as a stark reminder that divine grace is intrinsically bound to the purity of our hearts and our submission to the will of the Almighty.
Let us not forget, dear members, that this blessed day on which the first Church of the Holy Mother Saint Mary was erected is not just a day of joy, but also a day of reflection and commitment. It is a summons from the divine to construct sanctuaries within our own souls, edifices of faith and devotion, to carry forth the unwavering light of our Holy Mother and Savior into the world. As the Apostles were commanded to cease from handy work on this day, so too should we dedicate this day to prayer, to acts of charity, and to the joyful singing of hymns in honor of the Holy Mother

On  june 28th, let us, children of God, celebrate this consecrated day with hearts ablaze with devotion, gratitude, and humility. As we pay homage to the construction of the first Church of the Holy Mother Saint Mary, may we build within our hearts a sanctuary, pure and unwavering, dedicated to the service and love of our Lord and His Holy Mother.

May the divine grace of the Holy Trinity and the Holy Mother Saint Mary guide our steps, and may we, as humble vessels of faith, be eternally bound in their loving embrace. Amen.

text.text: Dear members of John's Repentance page, today is the monthly feast of St. George in the EOTC and so we send you this short writing for you to learn about the life of this great saint and martyr.

text:
St. George is a Christian saint who is widely known for his courage, steadfast faith, and unwavering devotion to God. He was born in 280 A.D. in the city of Capadocia, which was part of the Eastern Empire in Asia Minor. He came from a wealthy and noble Christian family and followed the usual career path of young nobleman by joining the Roman army.

St. George's ability and charm quickly brought him promotion within the army, and eventually, he was made a tribune or an officer in the Imperial Guard by the Emperor. According to one story, he was a friend of Constantine, another officer who later became the first Christian emperor. The legend says that St. George accompanied Constantine to Britain and visited some holy places, including Glastonbury and Caerleon. When he returned to Nicomedia, the capital of the Eastern Empire, he encountered the fierce storm of persecution against Christians.

Diocletian, the emperor at the time, issued a formal edict against Christians on February 23, 303 A.D., which was the feast of Termhlalia. The edict mandated that all churches should be leveled to the ground, all sacred books burned, all Christians who held any honorable rank were to be degraded and deprived of civil rights, and all Christians who were not officials were to be reduced to slavery.

Despite the persecution, St. George boldly stood up for his faith. He pushed his way through the market to read the proclamation in front of the awe-stricken crowd and then deliberately tore down the Imperial edict and threw it away. This act of defiance resulted in his arrest and subsequent encounter with Diocletian.

The Emperor tried to seduce St. George by promising him a higher position in the empire, but St. George remained steadfast in his faith. Diocletian then began to threaten him with unbearable tortures that he would inflict on him. St. George refused to renounce his faith, even in the face of torture, and eventually was imprisoned.

St. George's chastity and suffering are two prominent aspects of his story. Diocletian arranged for a very beautiful woman to spend the night with him in prison to try to debauch him. St. George, who could only look forward to heavenly joy, began to pray and within a short while managed to swing her heart to the Christian faith. She seriously began to inquire about salvation, and by morning she declared that she found her true Bridegroom, Jesus Christ. With great courage, she announced her Christianity to the Emperor and his men and joined the other saintly martyrs.

(Continues)👇🏾

text:
(Continued) 👆🏾

As for his suffering, the tortures that were applied to St. George are too numerous to mention in depth, but it is worth noting his utmost love for Christ. His body was torn by a special instrument that had metallic teeth, and our Lord Jesus rose him after his death, leading to the conversion of many pagans. He was put in active lime, and water was poured on it. Again the Lord returned him back to life. The Emperor became very agitated, imagining that the Saint was using magic. He called his top magician, Athanasius, and requested him to prepare a lethal poison to kill St. George.
The Saint signed over the cup with the sign of the cross before drinking it, and of course, no harm came to him. The Emperor's counselors informed him that St. George's magic was, in fact, contained in the sign of the Cross itself. Another cup was also given to the Saint, but this time with his hands tied behind his back. The Saint signed it by his head, saying: "shall I drink it from here or here or here or here!!!"

As St. George stood before the emperor and his court, he was given one last chance to renounce his Christian faith and offer sacrifice to the idols. The emperor promised him great rewards, honors, and privileges if he would do so. But St. George refused, declaring that he would never deny his Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

In a final act of defiance, the emperor ordered St. George to be beheaded. The saint willingly accepted his fate and went to his death with courage and grace. He is said to have uttered a prayer to God, thanking Him for the privilege of dying for the faith.

text.text:
👉Question: Does marital status determine whether to receive Holy Communion? For example, if we are single, married, what if our partner is not willing? Or what should I do if my fiance refuses to marry me in the sacrament?

✍Answer

text:
: One of the sacrements of the New Testament is Christ's holy flesh and His precious blood. We have said that the special gift of the Holy Spirit that we have been blessed with since the birth of a boy on the 40th day and the birth of a girl on the 80th day is the food of eternal life. To separate from this is to die although we seem alive simply because we breath. Our body: If we lose  food for a few days or even for few hours for some people, it is definitely not possible to stay alive. This is one of the common weaknesses of the body where we lose our fleshly existence. Likewise, if the soul loses Christ's holy flesh and precious blood, it dies and has no life. It means that we have killed it. Therefore, in order to eat this eternal life, to drink that gives eternal life, we should learn what kind of system and what kind of spiritual preparation we should follow. We are commanded by God to live a Christian life, of which the Holy Eucharist is the foundation. Any teaching that keeps us away by threatening and exaggerating for other reasons is false teaching and should be avoided. 

Apostle St. Paul said that if we eat and drink the ultimate food of the soul without preparation and understanding, it will be a debt to us. This means that it is necessary to always have a life prepared for repentance and to accept those who are counselors in the affairs of our souls, the fathers of the church whom God has appointed as our servants and shepherds. In other words, we are commanded to always receive with repentance, so that we do not make this mistake that St. Paul wrote about (so that we do not receive without deserving or understanding this), but there is no occasion where we are commanded to depart from this mystery, not even for a single day.

Therefore, for those who are said to be before marriage, as we mentioned above, we should realize that we should continue to accept what we received in our childhood, that started from the time of Christianity,  until the end of our lives. But we should do this without committing any shame or sin as that is the only thing which keeps us away from the Holy Communion. Everyone knows what sin or shame is that keeps us away from the Holy Communion, even a child knows. There is no one who does not know the type of sin from the smallest to the highest level of sin. Murder, adultery, adultery, all these seeming sins can keep you away from the sacrament. But through repentant and reprimanded, you can continue the communion by repenting and being mentored and taught by their penitent father. 

Back to the question, it is to say that we should do this throughout our life, and it is not a matter of martial status. Both the male and female start participating in this sacrement at the time of their baptism and actively participate alone until they reach maturity age. After that, the man chooses someone who resembles him in his spiritual life and the woman chooses someone who resembles her in her spiritual life and they get married and continue with the Holy Communion together. Even those who are not married in the Holy Communion, without having this opportunity, come to repentance and they, too, can continue their holy purpose that they have abandoned. Because the Church has made a system for us, it has reconciliation for all from her creator.

To be continued 👇

In general, the sacrament does not depend on the state of marriage; After all, the Holy Church has never commanded us to stay away from the Holy Communion for a single day until marriage. This is an attitude that some people have brought by habit, or even counselors and teachers have been absorbed in the people's system, not God's system; and we need to understand that it is not the correct teaching of the Church. Besides, it is not an honor for us to continue to be a father of repentance for people living far from the Holy Communion, but a great shame. Why? The first and foremost task of a penitent father is to teach his penitent children, equip them for penance and Holy Communion, and watch over them to live steadfastly in this spiritual life. But as we can see what is happening in practice, does everyone who is a Christian receive the Holy flesh and the precious blood of Christ?  Not really.
 
On the other hand although it is not comparable with our faith, when we see other faith institutions around the world who claim to be in Christianity, even those who do not believe in partaking fekm His holy flesh and precious blood do not leave without receiving 'in rememberence' each time they come to their church, never. Our church, however, does not consider the Holy Communion as a memorial, and not do not take this mystery simply or boldly. Rather, we receive it believing that it is the real holy flesh and his noble blood that our Creator shed for us through all that suffering on Friday; and we accept it in the fear of God . This is Christian ethics. As Christian ethics, we correct our wrongdoing and accept it through a life of repentance. So, the only thing that may keeps us far from the Holy Communion before and during marriage is our own sin.

So the answer to the question is that if there is a time when we are different from Holy Communion, the biggest thing is our own reason. Thi may be, either we didn't get real lesson of the Orthodox Church; Or that we are not willing to repent for what we committed a sin; Or that we have not decided to stop that sin. But, in general, there is no time to deprive us the Holy Communion except in this way.

(to be continued)

Question: How to develop a deep prayer life and strengthen my spiritual life every day; How can I get closer to God?

Answer:

text:
In the pursuit of a profound prayer life and the strengthening of your spiritual journey, it is crucial to approach this endeavor with unwavering commitment, a sincere heart, and a deep understanding of its significance. Let us delve into several key principles, which can serve as guiding lights on the path to experiencing a deeper connection with God through prayer.

First and foremost, prayer should be recognized as a sacred conversation with the Creator—a transcendent opportunity to engage in a direct dialogue with the Almighty. It is not a mere ritualistic duty or an obligation to be fulfilled mechanically; rather, it is an invitation to commune intimately with the divine. In embracing this understanding, one's love for prayer will flourish, and the recognition of its indispensable role in nurturing spiritual well-being will deepen. Let prayer be seen as the very essence of life itself, for just as a person ceases to breathe without air, one who neglects prayer becomes spiritually lifeless.

To truly enter into the spirit of prayer, it is essential to direct our thoughts and intentions towards God. Begin by expressing heartfelt gratitude for His abundant blessings in your life—recognize the gifts of love, grace, and mercy bestowed upon you. Humbly seek His guidance and assistance in all aspects of your existence, acknowledging your dependence upon Him. Remember the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, who admonished us to "watch and pray so that you will not fall into temptation." Approach prayer with unwavering sincerity, knowing that it strengthens your resolve, deepens your understanding of God's will, and helps you align your life with His divine purpose.

In order to nurture your spiritual life, it is beneficial to establish clear goals in your prayer practice. Take time to reflect upon your purpose and aspirations in your journey as a Christian. Identify areas in need of growth and development, and bring them before God in prayer. Focus your prayers on cultivating virtues such as love, patience, humility, and forgiveness. Seek to deepen your faith, exploring the mysteries of divine truth and opening your heart to receive spiritual illumination. Embrace a spirit of service, praying for opportunities to extend compassion, kindness, and generosity to those in need. By establishing such intentional goals, you infuse your prayers with purpose and align them with your desired spiritual development.

Consistency in prayer is vital. Establish dedicated times each day, free from distractions, to commune with God. Find a peaceful and secluded space where you can withdraw from the noise and busyness of the world, creating an atmosphere conducive to deepening your connection with the divine. By adhering to a regular prayer routine, you establish a rhythm that reinforces your spiritual bond and fosters a sense of discipline in your spiritual life. Whether it be in the early morning, before meals, or before retiring to rest, choose a time that best suits your circumstances and commit to it unwaveringly.

(Continued) 👇

text:
Let us delve into the profound mystery of the incarnation, a cornerstone of our faith. In this divine revelation, we proclaim that the Word, one of the Holy Trinity, assumed perfect humanity to reveal His boundless love and redeem the world. He was born of the Holy Virgin Mary, fulfilling the prophecies of God's love for mankind, who found themselves ensnared in sin, burdened by their fallen nature, and oppressed under the dominion of demons. As the Apostle Paul declares, "But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth his Son, born of woman, born under the law" (Galatians 4:4).

The Word, the invisible Divinity by nature, became visible through the mystical incarnation. The intangible was grasped, the unbeatable was wounded, the immortal experienced death in the flesh, the one who knew no hunger or thirst became hungry and thirsty, and the one without need was satisfied. In this union, the flesh was infused with divinity, and the eternal Word became known as the firstborn, for it merged with the eternal Divinity. As it is written, "Behold, the man has become like one of us" (Genesis 3:22), and thus He was counted as the Son of God the Father and the Son of the Virgin Mary. The Son born of a Virgin is rightfully called the Son of God the Father. Hence, due to this inseparable unity, the Orthodox faith asserts the following teachings regarding the incarnation:

1.

: When the Word becomes flesh, it does not undergo any alteration or modification. Just as the Scriptures affirm, "Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever" (Hebrews 13:8). "With whom there is no variation or shadow due to change" (James 1:17). As the Lord Himself proclaims, "I am the Lord, I do not change" (Malachi 3:6).

2.

The Divinity did not abandon the body after accomplishing the salvation of the world. He did not separate Himself from the flesh, as confirmed in the words of the prophet Jeremiah, "Have I not preserved them in my dwelling?" (Jeremiah 17:16).

3.

The two natures, divine and human, are not blended into one another but exist in a perfect union. Therefore, when it is said that "this is my body," it signifies a complete and indivisible union without any shame.

4.

: The divinity and the flesh remain distinct, without mixing or leaving their respective essences. The Word did not abandon His divinity, nor did the flesh cease to be flesh. Rather, the flesh was divinely glorified, and the Word became flesh, displaying a perfect union.

, the will of the Word, which cannot be violated or augmented, is the same as the will of the flesh. It is a union of two wills without confusion—a perfect harmony of wills. 

Furthermore, our mystical incarnation doctrine asserts that God was born in the flesh of the Virgin Mary, and she is rightly called the Theotokos, the Mother of God, for she gave birth to God in the flesh (Luke 1:35). As the devil, disguised as a serpent, separated mankind from God, the Lord chose a mysterious plan that rendered the crafty wisdom of the devil futile. The mystery through which He accomplished the salvation of the world surpasses the wisdom with which He created it. He chose a virgin and, from her flesh and soul, was born in a humble stable, crucified naked, and thus saved the world.

When we declare that God became man, it does not diminish or increase His divinity. As the Scriptures affirm, "Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever" (Hebrews 13:8). He remains the eternal Lord of all (Psalm 101:27).

text:
In His incarnation, Christ assumed our humanity to become the Redeemer of humankind, to raise the fallen, to seek the lost, and to serve as our perfect example. He came to reveal His immeasurable love, to redeem us from sin and death, and to restore us to life. The Son, born of the Virgin Mary, fasted, was baptized, preached the Gospel, and was crucified on Calvary, giving His life for our salvation. On the third day, He triumphed over death, and after forty days, He ascended into heaven. He will come again, bringing perfection and glory. When He returns, all those who pierced Him will behold His majesty.

The teachings of the Orthodox Tewahedo Church concerning the mystical incarnation elucidate our belief in the unity of the divine and human natures in Christ. Although some may label us as Monophysites, associating our Church with a belief in the mingling or absorption of the natures, our faith is not Monophysite in nature. Such assertions stem from misunderstandings and misinterpretations of the teachings of revered figures like Adeshke, who, despite his devoutness, deviated from the Orthodox understanding of the Trinity. Scholars often recount his teachings as examples of misguided monastic fervor rather than authoritative theological positions.

When the Orthodox Tewahedo Church proclaims "Tewahedo" (Oneness), it signifies the unity of the two natures without one destroying or consuming the other. The unity of their essence is not singular but composite. St. Cyril of Alexandria, a renowned Church Father, unveils the mystery of Christ's incarnation as the mystery of salvation, affirming that before Christ became man, He was God, and when He assumed humanity, He remained fully God.

In contemplating the mystery of the incarnation, we are humbled by the profound love and mercy of God. Through His voluntary self-emptying, the Word became flesh to dwell among us, revealing the path of salvation and offering us the opportunity for eternal communion with Him. Let us meditate on the incarnation, embracing its depth and significance, as we marvel at the infinite wisdom and grace of our Lord Jesus Christ.

text:
Beloved members of John's Repentance spiritual service, 

Today is the annual feast of the birth of Saint John the Baptist. Let us delve into the depth of his life and draw valuable lessons for our spiritual journey.

In the pages of Holy Scripture, the Gospel according to St. Matthew recounts the extraordinary events surrounding the birth and ministry of St. John. As St. Matthew writes, in those days, the voice of St. John the Baptist resounded through the wilderness of Judea, proclaiming with urgency, "The kingdom of heaven is near, repent!" (Matthew 3:2). Such was the resolute conviction with which he preached, invoking the words of the prophet Isaiah, "Prepare the way of the Lord" (Isaiah 40:3).

Now, dear brethren, let us reflect upon the essence of St. John's message. In the New Testament, it is God Himself who, in His infinite mercy, offers true forgiveness of sins. It is He who beckons us to prepare our hearts for this divine forgiveness, directing us to the true Father who possesses the power to absolve all transgressions. St. John, in his ministry, baptized with water for repentance, inviting people to a life of genuine contrition. However, he proclaimed, "But the one who comes after me will baptize you with the Holy Spirit" (Matthew 3:11). He revealed that the Messiah, our Lord Jesus Christ, would restore humanity to the status of God's beloved children, emancipating them from sin's grip.

In the depth of his wisdom, St. John acknowledged his own unworthiness to even bear the shoes of the One who was to come. He declared, "He who comes after me is mightier than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire" (Matthew 3:11). St. John recognized his role as the humble precursor to the One who would effect a profound transformation in the lives of believers. With an evocative metaphor, he compared the Lord to a winnower who would thoroughly cleanse the threshing floor, gathering the wheat into the barn while burning the chaff with unquenchable fire (Matthew 3:12).

Therefore, dear members, let us take heed of St. John's exhortation. Those who stubbornly persist in rebellion and continue in sin, disregarding the counsel, reproof, and truth proclaimed to them, shall face judgment. St. John, the forerunner, exemplified a life of penitence even before the Lord's earthly manifestation. He was born to our father Zacharias and our mother Saint Elizabeth, with the archangel Gabriel foretelling his birth and his divine calling. From his mother's womb, he was destined to live a life of exceptional holiness, preparing the way for the Lord and proclaiming a genuine sermon of repentance. He abstained from worldly pleasures, not even tasting the flavor of meat or wine, choosing instead to sustain himself with a diet of locusts and desert honey.

Furthermore, dear members, contemplate the unique position held by St. John the Baptist. Even before his birth, while he was still in his mother's womb, he received divine revelation concerning the approach of the Virgin Mary, the mother of our Lord. As the blessed Mary entered the presence of St. Elizabeth, the unborn John, filled with the Holy Spirit, leaped for joy, acknowledging the sacredness of the encounter. In awe, St. Elizabeth exclaimed, "How is it that the mother of my Lord should come to me?" (Luke 1:43). Thus, we witness the extraordinary moment when the first apostle, St. John, bearing witness from his mother's womb, testified to the divine nature of Christ. Truly, he was a martyr even before his birth.

text.text: Beloved members, today we gather to commemorate the monthly feast of the conception of the blessed Virgin Mary. Let us delve into the profound significance of this event and may our hearts be enlightened by the wisdom and grace of the Holy Spirit.

text:
In the year 5485 since the creation of the world, fifteen years prior to the dawn of the Year of Mercy, the conception of our Lady took place. It was a time when the world was engulfed in the darkness of sin, and the consequences of human transgression weighed heavily upon all creation. The floodwaters of Noah's time serve as a vivid testimony, for they rose fifteen cubits above the highest mountains, covering the earth and cleansing it from the defilement of wickedness (Genesis 7:19).

Reflect upon the significance of those waters, dear members, for they were a symbol of the pervasive sin that had plagued humanity from the time of our progenitor Adam until the advent of Christ. Just as the floodwaters harmed not only humanity but also every living creature on earth, the sin of Adam affected not only humankind but also the animals and even the celestial beings of heaven.

The holy angels, who dwell in glory and serve as intermediaries between God and man, were exempt from the burden of this sin. However, they refrained from entering into the service of humanity, recognizing that it was through man's agency that this sin had entered the world. It was in this context that the angelic proclamation of peace and salvation to the shepherds on that holy night came to pass (Luke 2:8-12).

Our Lady, the chosen vessel, descended from priestly lineage through her mother and royal lineage through her father. She was a descendant of King David and Solomon, as well as of Aaron the High Priest. Yet, her ancestors, Hannah and Joachim, faced great trials and reproach due to their barrenness. Barrenness was erroneously believed to be a consequence of sin, and thus, they were scorned, reproached, and even prevented from entering the House of God for worship.

However, let us be mindful, dear members, that God's ways are not like those of mortals. In their distress, Hannah and Joachim wept before the Lord, beseeching Him to remove the shame that clung to them. They offered fervent prayers and supplications, joining the chorus of many prophets and saints who had longed for the advent of the Virgin Mary. The culmination of these cries for divine intervention found their fulfillment in the birth of our Lady.

The barrenness that had afflicted Hannah and Joachim, perceived as a consequence of sin, transformed into a vessel for God's divine plan. It was a vessel through which the Virgin Mary, the bearer of heavenly secrets, would enter the world. She appeared in a vision to her mother Hannah, and even before her conception, the fruit of life, the mother of Jesus Christ, the embodiment of righteousness, was foretold by the angel of the good news, Gabriel. 

While still in her mother's womb, our Lady, the fruit of the holy union between Hannah and Joachim, performed extraordinary deeds that testified to her greatness. She bestowed light upon the blind and strength upon weak hands, even before her birth. From the moment of her conception, she exuded sanctity, and her mere presence caused the dead to rise.

Witnessing these events, Satan could not remain silent. Though unaware of the precise timing, he understood that a moment of great significance was upon him. If such miracles occurred even before her birth, what extraordinary wonders would unfold when she came into the world? In his relentless enmity, Satan stirred up the Jews against the parents of our Lady, seeking to torment her even while she resided within the sacred confines of her mother's womb. But the Virgin Mary had already confounded him, even before her birth, by opening the eyes of the blind and causing the mute to speak. Who among God's creation had ever achieved such wonders from the confines of the womb?

text:
👆🏾

From the very beginning, when the angels beheld her on their wings, she was entrusted with the divine guardianship, as proclaimed by the messenger Gabriel, who was appointed to protect her. Recognizing that she did not belong to this world, our Lady departed from her parental home, accompanied by her spiritual kinsfolk and angelic hosts. The Lord, who sought out Adam when he wandered away from his home and lost communion with God, is now reunited with him through his mother. Thus, she embarked on a journey to Mount Lebanon, the revered land where her ancestors had received visions. For she is the promised Bride of Lebanon, foretold to be born in a lion's den beneath the celestial heights of the Lebanese mountains.

Satan, witnessing these divine interventions, persisted in his enmity. He did not rest, for he comprehended that if such wonders could occur before her birth, the magnitude of her impact upon the world after her birth would be unparalleled. He gathered the Jewish armies, instigating hostility against Hannah and Joachim. Even in her mother's womb, the Virgin Mary was not afforded a moment of peace. She had already struck at Satan's core, displaying her profound capabilities. Indeed, as written in the great book, Jeremiah declares, "Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you; before you were born, I sanctified you" (Jeremiah 1:5).

The initial revelation of our Lady to the angels, accompanied by their protective wings, served as a testament to her divine calling. Recognizing that she did not belong to this world, she departed her familial abode, forsaking the transient pleasures of earthly existence. She journeyed to Mount Lebanon, the land of her ancestral visionaries, in fulfillment of the prophecy that proclaimed her as the Bride of Lebanon. The birth of the Virgin Mary, shining more brightly than the sun and surpassing all glory, occurred on a day in May.

On that sacred day, plants blossomed out of season, stones transformed into bread, and the winter months yielded to the approaching season of blessing. It was the time when Christ, the Bread of Life, would grant nourishment to the world, manifesting Himself as the heavenly manna. Indeed, this momentous sign was accompanied by the presence of numerous angelic hosts, descending from heaven to earth, saturating the surroundings with a fragrance indescribable. The tidings of the archangel Gabriel resonated throughout the heavens and spread with exultation, heralding the birth of the Virgin Mary.

Dear members, may the profundity of this Orthodox perspective on the conception of the blessed Virgin Mary touch the depths of your souls. Answer፦

text:
Age does not determine our ability to partake in the Holy Communion. Rather, it is our spiritual readiness and understanding of the sacrament that are of utmost importance. From the moment we are baptized and become children of God, we are invited to partake in the Holy Communion.

It is customary to present infants for Holy Communion forty days after birth for boys and eighty days for girls. This sacrement serves to confirm their status as children of God and members of the Church. From that point forward, there is no separation, departure, or cessation of their life as individuals who belong to God. The continuous participation in Holy Communion sustains our spiritual journey.

When considering age in relation to sin, some refer to the age of Adam for men and the age of Eve for women. This metaphorical understanding implies that individuals reach a level of maturity and responsibility where they are accountable for their actions. However, it is essential to recognize that sin does not discriminate based on age. Sin can be committed at any stage of life, and it is our duty to strive to avoid it.

Rather than focusing solely on age, the primary concern should be cutting off the chain of sin in our lives. It is akin to interrupting a power line or severing a water line. We must make a decisive choice to break the cycle of sin, no matter our age. We should not postpone this decision, waiting until we are older or assuming that age exempts us from sin. Our goal is to sanctify our lives through the sacrament and live in communion with God, thus inheriting eternal life.

Therefore, rather than determining our readiness for Holy Communion based on age, we should take a momentous step to cease habitual sin. There is no fixed system or law that permits sin based on age. The notion that one can indulge in sin while young or wait until old age due to physical limitations is a grave misunderstanding. Such thinking suggests weakness in our commitment to Christianity. God desires the hearts of the youth and children, free from sin. Repentance and forgiveness are available to all, regardless of age.

Considering this perspective, dear member, age alone does not determine when you can approach Holy Communion. We have emphasized the significance of the sacrament on numerous occasions, and we encourage you to explore our teachings and advice available on our social media pages. Our teachings center around the sacrament, and we believe that separation from Holy Communion is a clear indication of our separation from God, which brings great sorrow.

We implore you not to allow any sins to hinder your approach to Holy Communion. Remember that no sin is permissible based on age. God commands us to refrain from sin in every stage of life—during childhood, youth, adulthood, and old age. If we happen to stumble and fall into sin, we must approach with repentance, without shame or fear, and seek forgiveness.

To provide you with comprehensive guidance and support, we recommend engaging with the teachings and advice shared through the John's Repentance website. It is our hope that these resources will serve as a valuable aid on your spiritual journey. We kindly request that you share the provided link with others, extending the opportunity for them to benefit from this invaluable guidance as well.

May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you, guiding you on the path of righteousness and communion with God.

text.text:
and St. P#aul

Dear members of John's Repentance spiritual service, today we comemorate the death of St. Peter and St. Paul. Accordingly, we have prepared a lesson for you to read and participate in the blessings, so we entrust you to read and apply the learnings to your life.

text:
St. Peter, the chief of the apostles, was a simple fisherman hailing from Bete Saida. It was on the day after His baptism that our Lord encountered him and chose him to be His disciple. Prior to that, Peter's brother, Andrew, had been the first to join Jesus. Peter displayed exceptional faith, recognizing Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God, when others were unsure of His identity. Jesus, in turn, praised Peter, declaring him the recipient of the keys to the Kingdom of Heaven.

Empowered by the comforting grace of the Holy Spirit, St. Peter fearlessly ventured into the world, confronting the metaphorical wolves of this world through his preaching. Alongside innumerable miracles performed by his hands, Peter penned three invaluable epistles and collaborated with St. Mark in the translation and writing of the Gospel. His journey eventually led him to the city of Rome, where a significant event unfolded.

In the great playground of Rome, where nobles congregated, St. Peter addressed the people, and astonishingly, four stone pillars present there resounded with a thunderous "Amen." This miraculous occurrence left those who witnessed it in awe and inspired great reverence. Furthermore, a man who had been tormented by a demon for seventy years experienced liberation upon hearing the word proclaimed by those stones. Stirred by this supernatural intervention, a nobleman named Kewstos and his wife, Acrosia, embraced the teachings of St. Peter regarding renunciation of worldly possessions and compassionate care for the poor.

Impressed by their example, they distributed their wealth among the needy, reserving only their daily sustenance. Subsequently, Kewstos received a summons from the king, which caused anxiety due to their depleted funds. Acrosia, however, encouraged him to proceed, assuring him of God's providence. True to her words, Kewstos embarked on the journey and encountered numerous blessings along the way. The king received him with joy and honor, proving the divine favor that accompanies faithful commitment.

Tragedy struck Kewstos and Acrosia's household upon their return, as their two children were found lifeless, having consumed poisoned water. Concealing this devastating news from her husband, Acrosia resorted to various excuses. Yet, through the intercession of St. Peter and the power of his teachings, a heavenly voice proclaimed that the children would be granted new life due to their acceptance of Peter's words. As promised, the resurrected children became fervent adherents to the teachings of St. Peter. One of them, named Clement, revealed extraordinary visions granted to St. Peter after the Lord's ascension.

In these visions, St. Peter beheld the glorious presence of the Immaculate Virgin Mary, the Mother of God. A cloud, resembling an arrow, bore a luminous tent wherein the Holy Virgin sat, surrounded by angels and archangels brandishing flaming spears and swords. St. Peter received divine revelations, understanding the Virgin Mary as the vine and her womb as the pure hall that bore the Lamb of God. The secrets and mysteries unveiled in these visions were impossible for St. Clement to have known otherwise, attesting to their divine authenticity.

text:
The command of our Savior beckoned St. Peter to proclaim the Holy Gospel throughout various lands. Accompanied by St. John, he encountered a remarkable incident in Joppa. Enveloped by a bright cloud, St. Peter witnessed a wide curtain descending, adorned with depictions of animals and birds. From the heavens, a voice called out, instructing Peter to rise and eat. However, Peter hesitated, declaring his unworthiness to consume anything unclean. Thrice, the voice reiterated that what God had made clean should not be considered unclean. This encounter served as a revelation that the Gospel was to be preached not only to the Jews but to the Gentiles as well, broadening the scope of salvation.

St. Peter and St. John then journeyed to the city of Antioch, as commanded by our Lord. There, they encountered opposition and threats, facing the prospect of death. However, trusting in God's providence, they prayed fervently for divine assistance. Their prayers were answered when our Lord Jesus Christ appeared to them, accompanied by cherubim and seraphim. Encouraging them, He declared that He would be with them always, even in the face of martyrdom. He reminded them of His own crucifixion and assured them that the chief of the apostles would share in His suffering.

St. Paul, originally known as Saul, also experienced a remarkable conversion and calling. Previously, Saul had zealously persecuted believers in Christ. However, on the road to Damascus, a blinding light from heaven enveloped him, and he heard the voice of Jesus addressing him. Struck by this divine encounter, Saul became temporarily blind and fasted for three days until Ananias, a disciple of Jesus, visited him. Ananias restored his sight through the power of God, and Saul, now Paul, was baptized and embraced his calling as an apostle.

St. Paul's subsequent missionary journeys, marked by imprisonment, floggings, and countless hardships, exemplify his unwavering commitment to spreading the Gospel. In their travels, he and St. Barnabas encountered resistance and opposition, facing false prophets and the wrath of rulers. However, through their faith and the power of the Holy Spirit, they performed miracles, healed the sick, and raised the dead, leading many to embrace the Christian faith.

The apex of St. Paul's ministry unfolded in Rome, where he preached the Gospel and witnessed numerous conversions. However, the tyrannical Emperor Nero subjected him to persecution and torture. Ultimately, St. Paul met his martyrdom, with his head severed by a swordsman. Yet, a young girl from Nero's own family intercepted his severed head, wrapping it in her cloak. Question፦ My confession father does not answer my calls or my text anymore. They have left us in a country without any priest. They expect us to establish a church without any guidance or help. I am tired and frustrated. 

Answer፦

text:
It is vital, beloved members, to perceive circumstances from your spiritual father's perspective. For if he is truly in the service of the Church, he shall not abandon his flock willingly. The heart of a true priest resonates with the love of a father - a love that parallels the love our Heavenly Father has for us. A true spiritual father protects and nurtures not just the body but the soul, fostering an intimate bond between us and the Divine.

Therefore, let us not hasten to judge or yield to despair. We must remind ourselves that we are all frail beings, subjected to earthly trials and tribulations. There could be myriad reasons, known only to God, for your spiritual father's absence.

Our Savior, in the Gospel of John 10:11, stated: "I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep." God, in His divine wisdom, will assuredly pave the way forward, offering us His sacred guidance. Let us then turn our hearts and prayers towards Him.

The Prophet Saint David, in Psalm 23:1-2, comfortingly reassured us: "The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. He makes me lie down in green pastures." It is God who watches over us, who steadies our course amidst the storms of life. He extends His merciful gaze upon us, proffering His support and shielding us from those who seek our downfall.

Dear member, do not allow weariness to veil your hope. God's divine power is our refuge, our strength when we are weary. When you feel your spirit flagging, remember the words of the Psalmist, in Psalm 121:1-2, "I lift up my eyes to the mountains—where does my help come from? My help comes from the Lord, the Maker of heaven and earth."

Rest assured that God's grace is omnipresent. Let us strive to understand the circumstances of your spiritual father. We are always available to extend our help, should you need it. We have answered your question as much as we understood it but it was not very clear what you're looking to do so please reach out to us with more detail so we can assist further. Let us cast our burdens onto the Lord, for He is our peace, our solace.

May we continually glorify the God of our ancestors, our Father, magnifying His holy name in all we do. Peace be upon us all.
