text.text: The Three Views of the World

text:
The Different Views of the World Concerning Intercession

There are three main views in the world regarding the mystery of intercession:

👉🏾 First, some claim, “There is no such thing as intercession. No one can intercede for another, for every person can approach God directly.”
This belief denies the communion of the saints and rejects the role of intercession revealed throughout Scripture.

👉🏾 Second, others say, “There is intercession, and it is necessary, but the only Intercessor is Christ.”

👉🏾 Third, there are those who say, “There is intercession, but it is the work of the creature, not the work of the Creator.”
This is the teaching of our Holy Orthodox Church. Intercession belongs to the saints, angels, and all the righteous who have been made worthy by God’s grace. They do not act apart from Him, but through His will. Their intercession is not independent of the Creator, but a reflection of His mercy working through His faithful servants.

Thus, our faith upholds that while Christ is the one true Mediator, the saints, by His grace, share in the ministry of intercession praying for us before the throne of the Almighty.

The Protestant View and Its Contradictions Regarding Intercession

The Protestant faith teaches the following about the intercession of saints:
They claim that there is no such thing as a saint set apart from others; all believers are saints. According to this belief, intercession is only possible when people pray for one another while still alive in the flesh.

However, this teaching stands in contradiction to itself. If, as they say, all believers are saints, then what is the meaning of praying for one another? Why would a saint need the prayer of another saint if all possess equal holiness and standing before God? This confusion exposes the weakness of such reasoning.

Furthermore, they argue that no one can pray for another after death—that prayer is only possible if they are physically alive. Yet this denies the power of God, who is the Lord of both the living and the departed. For in Him, “all live” (Luke 20:38). The righteous who have departed from this world are not dead in spirit, but alive in Christ, and their prayers rise continually before His throne.

Therefore, the belief that the saints cease to pray after death contradicts both Scripture and the living faith of the Church, which confesses that those who died in holiness remain alive in the presence of God, interceding for the faithful on earth.

The teaching of intercession is not new, nor is it a human invention. It is a divine truth revealed and practiced since the beginning of sacred history. From the time of the patriarchs under the Law, through the Torah and the writings of the Old Testament, to the era of the Apostles and the Holy Church, intercession has been a living part of the faith. It continues to this very day and will endure until the end of time.

Our Holy Orthodox Church faithfully upholds this teaching, preserving the traditions of the Holy Scriptures, the Apostles, and the early Fathers. It is not a doctrine born of man’s imagination, but one that God Himself approves and delights in. From the founding of Christianity, the intercession of the righteous has been an integral part of the Church’s prayer and life.

Today, however, the question of intercession has become one of the most debated and misunderstood topics throughout the world. Whether in marketplaces, on buses, in offices, schools, homes, or even among families and friends, arguments over intercession divide hearts and scatter unity. Parents are estranged from children, husbands from wives, neighbors from neighbors all because of confusion over this sacred truth.

text.text: The Power of the Saints’ Intercession

text:
The Orthodox Church teaches, with unwavering faith, that the righteous martyrs, the holy angels, and above all, our Lady the Holy Virgin Mary, intercede for us before our Creator. Yet this teaching offends the ears of those who reject the communion of the saints. They see honor to the saints as an insult to God, not understanding that to honor the servants of God is to glorify their Master.

The claim that intercession should be rejected and that no one should seek the prayers of others is not only false but deeply offensive to the Orthodox faithful. It is hypocrisy and betrayal of the ancient faith handed down through the Apostles.

The Churches of Alexandria, Syria, India, and Armenia, which stand among the oldest in the Christian world, have all preserved the belief in the intercession of saints. Their witness proves that this teaching belongs to the earliest and purest form of Christianity.

History itself testifies that the denial of intercession is a recent invention an unfamiliar stream flowing far from the ancient river of truth. The Holy Scriptures warn us clearly:

“Do not be carried away by strange teachings, for Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.” (Hebrews 13:8)

Therefore, let every believer remain steadfast in the faith of the fathers, cherishing the intercession of the saints as a sign of God’s mercy and as the unbroken bond between heaven and earth.

text:
Blessed be God, who in every age reveals the hidden fragrance of His mercy through His saints and His Mother. The time called Zemene Tsege.It is the period in which the Church remembers the fulfillment of ancient prophecy when the barren earth of humanity blossomed through the womb of the Virgin.

👉🏾The holy prophet Joel foretold that “the mountains and hills of Judah shall flow with sweet grass and milk richly.”

✍🏾This prophecy pointed to the time of grace that would come through the Virgin Mary and her Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.

✍🏾When the Blessed Virgin gave birth to Christ, this prophecy was fulfilled in both sweetness and fragrance . "Sweet grass and milk", symbolize the grace that flowed from her pure womb the nourishment of salvation for all creation.

✍🏾In the fullness of time, the same Christ, who took flesh and blood from His Mother, was crucified on the Cross on Good Friday. The Son of Man, who humbled Himself to share our human hunger and thirst, poured forth living water and divine nourishment from His own side. His flesh and blood became the true food and drink of the soul.

✍🏾Through this mystery, the long famine of five thousand five hundred years  the spiritual hunger of mankind came to an end. In Him, the barren earth became fruitful once again, and the sweetness of Joel’s prophecy was fulfilled forever.

text.text: 4.5 The Grace and Silence of Our Lady Mary

text:
👉🏾“Our Lady Mary, your grace is beyond praise and cannot be measured by words. Hasten to catch the little foxes that destroy our vineyard.”

✍🏾The Evangelist Saint Luke writes, “She kept all these things in her heart” (Luke 2:51), showing how wonderful our Lady truly is. She heard the angel’s message that no creature had ever heard and was blessed with a virgin conception and birth that no one had ever seen. For nine months and five days, her womb was filled with praise. She was blessed by the prayers of angels and honored by her Creator, receiving greater grace and glory than all creation, even more than the seraphim and cherubim. Yet, while she lived in this world, she never said, “I saw this” or “I heard that,” but kept everything in her heart.

✍🏾Eve lost her grace by revealing to the devil the secret given only to her and Adam. But our Lady was blessed for keeping everything within her heart.

✍🏾We learn from both Christ and His Mother the virtue of silence and humility. When Pilate and the chief priests questioned Christ, asking, “Where are you from, and what is your teaching?” He remained silent. He only answered when Pilate said, “I have authority to crucify you” (John 19:9; Matthew 27:14).

👉🏾Therefore, we too must follow the example of our Father, Christ, and our Mother, the Virgin Mary keeping peace, silence, and humility in our hearts.

text.text: The Vineyard and the Days of Creation

text:
✍🏾After the author praises our Lady, the wise Solomon says, “Catch the little foxes that destroy our vineyard.” (Song of Songs 2:15)
The vineyard represents the Law, and the keeper of the vineyard prays to the Virgin Mary to protect us from fox-like hypocrites and demons who seek to destroy the vineyard of our hearts.

✍🏾Mary’s mother, Saint Hannah, is likened to the third, fourth, and seventh days of creation. On the third day, when God created plants, flowers, and fruits (Genesis 1:11–13). imagined Saint Hannah as the day Tuesday ,our Lady as the flower, and the Lord whom she bore as the fruit that came from that flower.

On the fourth day (Wednesday), when God created the sun, the moon, and the stars, he imagined Saint Hannah as a day wednesday ,our Lady as the sun, for she bore Christ, the Light of the World.

✍🏾On the seventh day, God rested from all His works. In the same way, through our Lady, all creation finds rest  for she gave birth to the Lord who is the eternal rest of heaven and earth. Through her, the weary find comfort and peace, fulfilling he prise God by saying: “The Sabbath was made for man; He made the Sabbath a rest for humanity.”

text.text: 4.6 The Revelation of the Holy Trinity through Our Lady

text:
✍🏾“In you, in the Jordan and on Mount Tabor, He revealed the mystery of the Trinity to mankind. O Virgin, your light has manifested His wonders and scattered the darkness with His brightness. Through you, God made known His unity and His Trinity in the Jordan and on Mount Tabor.”

✍🏾When the angel Saint Gabriel announced the good news to our Lady, he said, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you” (Luke 1:35).

✍🏾In these words, the mystery of the Holy Trinity was revealed: the sprit of God is called Holy Spirit , the Son is called the Power of the Most High, and the Father is the Most High . Thus, in the Annunciation, the Trinity was revealed through the Virgin Mary. She was united with the Son in the body He took from her, while the Father testified to Him as His beloved Son, saying, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased” (Matthew 3:16–17).,the holy spirit ot help her to be the mother of God.

✍🏾When the Son was baptized in the Jordan, the Father appeared in a cloud and bore witness to Him, while the Holy Spirit descended in the form of a dove. In that moment, the false claim of those who said that God was one person with many names was destroyed. All three Persons appeared together in perfect harmony  the Son in the flesh, the Father in the cloud, and the Holy Spirit in the form of a dove.

✍🏾And again, on Mount Tabor, the Father’s voice was heard in a cloud, saying, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to Him.” (Matthew 17:5)
Thus, both in the Jordan and on Mount Tabor, the divine mystery of the Holy Trinity was revealed through the presence of the Son, the testimony of the Father, and the descent of the Holy Spirit.

text:
✍🏾O Mary, the unfading sunflower neither from highlands nor from lawlands among the thorny Jews, deliver me, who trusts in you, from the evil of my condemnation, so that my trust in you may not be in vain. For you are the custom of mercy.

👉🏾 In the Song of Solomon, it is written: “Like a sunflower of flax among thorns, so are you” (Song of Songs 2:2).

✍🏾 Even though the sunflower is surrounded by thorns, it continues to bloom and bear fruit. Similarly, Our Lady, though living among the wicked Jews who, despite seeing many miracles, did not believe and constantly sought signs, did not allow this to hinder her faith. She continued to flourish spiritually and bore the greatest fruit—Christ.

✍🏾 Abba Tsige Dingle explains that Solomon's prophecy was fulfilled through Our Lady’s bringing forth Christ among the Jews. Reflecting on this, he prays: “ I believe in your motherhood and covenant, save me from evil judgment, for my trust and hope in you are not in vain.”

✍🏾 Mahlete Tsige is a work filled with mystery, power, and a unique beauty. Its full depth can only be appreciated when read in Ge’ez. Even a poem loses some of its spirit when translated, as the nuances, rhythm, and spiritual essence are difficult to convey fully in another language.

✍🏾Fasting without humility is an empty shadow. The true fast is not of the lips or stomach alone, but of the heart. The believer must fast with compassion, give alms to the poor, restrain anger, forgive offenses, and keep the tongue from deceit. Let fasting be united with mercy, prayer, and repentance, that it may ascend as sweet incense before the throne of God.

As the fathers teach: “When you fast, do not fast for vain praise, but that your fasting may be a fasting of mercy, wherein you find help, blessing, and the grace of God.”

text: Dear followers of Orthodox teachings, we greet you with the blessings of God. Today, on the topic of "Mamaled" (Intercede ), we bring you an important teaching that we entrust to each of you to read, reflect upon, and learn from. This lesson is meant to deepen your understanding of the sacred act of praying for one another and the roles of those involved in intercession.

The word “Mamaled”(Intercede) is derived from the Ge’ez verb “Tenbele,Amalede” which means that “to pray for one another.” In its simplest and most concrete sense, intercession is the act of pleading before God on behalf of another’s need: to carry the burden of a brother’s trouble into the presence of the Lord. This is no exotic doctrine; it is the familiar practice of the Church and of every faithful heart that loves its neighbor. Intercession is prayer that stands between the sufferer and God, a bridge of humility and love.

This concept is clear and relevant to all people and societies because it reflects an action we often see and practice in our daily lives caring for others through prayer and support.

text.text: II. The three parties in the economy of intercession

text: From the very definition we see that intercession always involves three distinct persons or parties, each with its own role. Attend to each one and understand their place.

Intercession is a humble and compassionate act that reflects the nature of all created beings. Because of this, there are many who serve as intercessors. In general, these include saints and holy angels, yet Our Lady is regarded as the greatest of all intercessors.

The role of the intercessor is to stand before God on behalf of sinners, offering prayers for mercy and forgiveness in place of their sins.

Saints, while living in the flesh, endure great suffering through fasting, prayer, and penance, not only for their own sake but for the salvation of others. The Scriptures show that some saints were even willing to sacrifice their own eternal reward for the redemption of sinners.

the holy ones, while yet in the body, undergo ascetic labors fasting, unceasing prayer, tears, penance as though they were even bearing their neighbor’s judgments and sufferings. Scripture gives us this wondrous example:  Moses interceded for the people of Israel, saying:

text:
The word “Temalaj” refers to the recipient of the prayers offered by intercessors. In our faith, the sole recipient of all prayers and intercessions is God.

While the saints and angels serve as intercessors, they are not divine. They pray to God, not as God. All intercession ultimately rises to the one God, who exists as the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit three persons in one divine essence.

This divine unity is not divided by the three persons; rather, the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit share one lordship, one power, one glory, one divinity, one kingdom, and one will. Together, they receive the thanksgiving and supplications of all creation those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth and carry out every act of divine mercy and goodness.

There is no hierarchy among the three persons of the Trinity; none is superior or inferior of each other. All are equal in essence, majesty, and authority.

Scripture affirms this truth:

“And I heard every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and in the sea, and all that is in them, saying,
‘To Him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be blessing and honor and glory and power forever and ever.’
And the four living creatures said, ‘Amen,’ and the elders fell down and worshiped.”
(Revelation 5:13–14)

Thus, all intercession whether through saints, angels, or Our Lady finds its fulfillment in God alone, who alone is worthy to hear and answer the prayers of His creation.

text.text: 3.Those Who Are Interceded For(the sinner who receives the prayer)

text:
Those who are prayed for or interceded for also have a part in the work of intercession. Intercessors offer their prayers to God for the salvation of sinners, and though evil spirits exist in opposition, the grace and blessing of intercession are given by God solely for the benefit of sinners.

Those who receive the prayers of intercessors also share in the work of intercession. This participation comes through faith in the intercessor’s prayer, trust in the power of intercession, and a sincere heart that turns away from sin.

However, if a person continues to sin while claiming to rely on intercessors, such faith becomes false. It would make the saints those holy intercessors partners in sin, which is impossible, for they are united with God, the righteous Judge, who cannot take part in wrongdoing.

There are times when God does not accept the intercession of the saints. This happens when a sinner refuses to repent and persists in evil. Scripture provides several clear examples of this truth:

“How long will you mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him from reigning over Israel?”
(1 Samuel 16:1)

“Therefore do not pray for this people, nor lift up a cry or prayer for them, nor make intercession to Me; for I will not hear you. Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? The children gather wood, the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the queen of heaven and to pour out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke Me to anger.”
(Jeremiah 7:16–18)

“Then the Lord said to me, ‘Even if Moses and Samuel stood before Me, My heart would not turn toward this people. Send them out of My sight and let them go.’”
(Jeremiah 15:1)

These passages remind us that intercession is not a substitute for repentance. The mercy of God flows freely through intercessors, but only to those who turn from sin with a contrite heart. Without repentance, even the prayers of the greatest saints cannot avail before the throne of God.

Practical and pastoral consequences

What then should the faithful do, hearing these truths?

Pray for one another: make intercession a daily task. Let the household, the Church, and every faithful person carry the burdens of others before God.

Honor the holy intercessors: respect and seek the prayers of the saints and of the Theotokos, for they stand before God and plead with motherly and fatherly love. Yet place no trust in the intercessor to the point of neglecting repentance.

Repent personally: the one for whom others pray must show forth repentance and a willing heart to abandon sin. Intercession works with repentance; it does not replace it.

Beware presumption: do not sin thinking that another’s prayer will remove all consequence. The lesson warns sharply against such sacrilege; God’s mercy is not a cloak for stubborn lawlessness.

text: Beloved in Christ, grace and peace be multiplied to you from our Lord Jesus Christ. As we reflect upon the sacred memories of the month of Tsige, let us immerse our hearts in the profound truths revealed by the Holy Scriptures and the experiences of our most holy Lady, the Virgin Mary, and her Divine Son, our Redeemer. Today, we contemplate the blessedness of Christians who are persecuted for righteousness, seeking to learn from their example and the warnings that God sets before us through the stories of the righteous and the wicked alike.

text.text: I. The Persecution of Our Lady and Our Lord

text:
During the month of Tsige, we remember the holy suffering of the King of Heaven and Earth, Jesus Christ, who in the tender arms of His Mother, the Blessed Virgin Mary, was exiled with Joseph and Salome for three years and six months of hunger and trial. This exile was not a mere accident of history but the fulfillment of God’s plan for the redemption of mankind.

Christ, the eternal Son of God, voluntarily left the glory of Paradise to bear the sins of Adam and all his descendants. He was the Innocent among the guilty, the Light among darkness. Our Lady, by her endurance of suffering and persecution, teaches us an eternal truth: to be persecuted for righteousness is not disgrace, but honor. The saints, whom God loves, persecution for their faith, for the truth, and for the cause of righteousness.

text.text: II. Christ Teaches the Blessedness of Persecution

text:
The Lord Himself, our Redeemer, gave His followers the Beatitudes as a guiding light:

“Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven” (Matthew 5:10).

Persecution, beloved, is not merely the act of being driven from one country to another. It is a spiritual condition, a life lived as a witness of the truth in every thought, word, and deed. To be persecuted for righteousness is to bear witness to God in a world of falsehood, to stand firm in the face of slander, and to endure humiliation without surrendering to deceit.

The Lord continues, “Blessed are you when men revile you, persecute you, and utter all kinds of evil against you falsely on my account. Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven, for so they persecuted the prophets who were before you” (Matthew 5:11-12). Let these words of Christ encourage the faithful to persevere, knowing that earthly trials are a passage to heavenly glory.

Even as we endure persecution, we must remember that not all suffering is of God’s will. We must distinguish between suffering for righteousness and suffering for sin. As the Apostle Paul warns, “Do not be deceived: God is not mocked. Whatever one sows, that will he also reap” (Galatians 6:7).

When insults, reproach, or false accusations come upon us, let us examine our hearts. If sin has led to our misfortune, let us repent. But if we are persecuted for defending the truth, we must endure with humility and patience, not masking sin as a sacrifice. The month of Tsige, recalling the sufferings of our Lady, reminds us to renew our repentance and strive toward righteousness so that we may truly become heirs of the Kingdom of God.

Witnesses of Christ Who Were Persecuted for Righteousness’ Sake

“Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” Matthew 5:10

Those who suffer for the truth are the true friends of Christ. They have made righteousness the rule of their lives and accepted every trial with patience and love. Their suffering is not loss but glory, for they share in the Cross of the Lord and receive the crown of eternal life.

text:

The story of this month reminds us of three such examples: Herod, who persecuted Christ for fear of losing his throne; Herod’s soldiers, who obeyed evil without conscience; and Kotiba and her family, who judged and mocked the Holy Virgin in her suffering.

text:

In their blindness, They despised the humble Virgin who carried the Lord of Glory in her arms. And behold, divine justice answered their cruelty: they were transformed into monkeys, their beauty turned to shame, and even the dogs of their own house chased them away.

text: Dear followers of Orthodox teachings, we greet you with the blessings of God. Today, on the topic of Intercession, we bring you an important teaching that we entrust to each of you to read, reflect upon, and learn from. This lesson is intended to deepen your understanding, to clarify who we call an intercessor.

Our Holy Church stands as an intercessor before God. As such, she offers prayers of intercession for the whole world. Among these sacred prayers is the supplication: “For rulers and authorities, that they may be granted wisdom and the fear of God.” This prayer, found in the Liturgy of the Word, it's from a command rooted in Holy Scripture.

As the Apostle Paul teaches: “Therefore, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people l for kings and all who are in authority that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in godliness and holiness.” (1 Timothy 2:1).

A Christian, then, does not pray for himself alone. He gives thanks for the mercy shown to him, yet his heart is also moved to pray and give thanks for others. In this way, the faithful distinguish between personal supplication and intercessory prayer two distinct paths of devotion.

Both are essential, both belong to the life of prayer, and together they form one offering before God: the private cry of the soul and the shared voice of the Church. The Holy Church, in her wisdom, does not confuse the two, but upholds each in its proper place.

Thus, intercession is the act of reconciling, presenting, and pleading on behalf of others. It is the prayer that bridges hearts, the offering that binds heaven and earth.

👉🏾

Intercession is the work of created beings; it does not belong to the nature of the Creator. God, in His majesty, is the One to whom intercession is offered not the One who intercedes. Yet among His creatures, He has appointed certain holy ones to perform this sacred ministry.

First among them are the holy angels, whom God has honored and appointed to serve His divine will. These heavenly beings, pure and steadfast, bear the prayers of humankind before the throne of grace.

Next are the holy people, the saints whom God has sanctified through their faith, their struggle, and their steadfast love. Among them shines most brightly our Lady, the Most Holy, the Blessed Virgin Mary, who, through her unique holiness and glory, bears the great service of intercession for all creation.

This sacred work does not belong to sinners, for one weighed down by his own iniquities cannot stand as mediator for others. Rather, the sinner must first labor in repentance, seeking the mercy of God for his own soul. As it is written: “As the old proverb says, ‘From the wicked comes wickedness.’” (1 Samuel 24:13).

Thus, intercession is the labor of the pure the ministry of those whose hearts have been cleansed by grace, whose voices ascend before the Lord as a pleasing incense on behalf of all who call upon His name.

Dear followers of Orthodox teachings, we greet you with the blessings of God. Today, on the topic of Intercession, we bring you an important teaching that we entrust to each of you to read, reflect upon, and learn from. This lesson is intended to deepen your understanding, to clarify who we call an intercessor.

The Holy Church as Intercessor

Our Holy Church stands as an intercessor before God. As such, she offers prayers of intercession for the whole world. Among these sacred prayers is the supplication: “For rulers and authorities, that they may be granted wisdom and the fear of God.” This prayer, found in the Liturgy of the Word, it's from a command rooted in Holy Scripture.

As the Apostle Paul teaches: “Therefore, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people l for kings and all who are in authority that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in godliness and holiness.” (1 Timothy 2:1).

Thus, intercession is the act of reconciling, presenting, and pleading on behalf of others. It is the prayer that bridges hearts, the offering that binds heaven and earth.

👉🏾 Whose Work Is Intercession?

Intercession is the work of created beings; it does not belong to the nature of the Creator. God, in His majesty, is the One to whom intercession is offered not the One who intercedes. Yet among His creatures, He has appointed certain holy ones to perform this sacred ministry.

First among them are the holy angels, whom God has honored and appointed to serve His divine will. These heavenly beings, pure and steadfast, bear the prayers of humankind before the throne of grace.

Next are the holy people, the saints whom God has sanctified through their faith, their struggle, and their steadfast love. Among them shines most brightly our Lady, the Most Holy, the Blessed Virgin Mary, who, through her unique holiness and glory, bears the great service of intercession for all creation.

This sacred work does not belong to sinners, for one weighed down by his own iniquities cannot stand as mediator for others. Rather, the sinner must first labor in repentance, seeking the mercy of God for his own soul. As it is written: “As the old proverb says, ‘From the wicked comes wickedness.’” (1 Samuel 24:13).

Thus, intercession is the labor of the pure the ministry of those whose hearts have been cleansed by grace, whose voices ascend before the Lord as a pleasing incense on behalf of all who call upon His name.

Continues 👇🏾

text:
The necessity of intercession springs from both divine mercy and human weakness. For though all may lift their voices in prayer, not all stand in equal favor before the throne of God. The Lord, who is holy, delights in the prayers of His saints, for their hearts are purified and their lives are adorned with righteousness.

Thus, the intercession of the saints is needed:

First, because God accepts the prayers of His saints more readily than those of sinners. 

Second, because through them our prayers ascend more swiftly to heaven, and our Creator, moved by their faithfulness, performs His goodness upon us. The saints, like fragrant incense, carry our petitions upward; through them the prayers of the Church rise as one harmonious voice before the Almighty.

As it is written in the Book of Enoch, “The righteous who dwell in heaven with one voice give thanks together and make intercession for men.” (Enoch 12:34). They pray not for themselves alone, but for all the children of men, fulfilling the covenant of love entrusted to them by God.

Throughout the Holy Scriptures, we behold examples of this sacred ministry. Many have stood as intercessors before the Lord and have obtained mercy for others.

When our father Abraham journeyed into Gerar, and King Abimelech took Sarah into his house, God appeared to the king in a dream, saying: “Return the man’s wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and you shall live.” (Genesis 20:7).

The Lord commanded that Abraham pray for Abimelech because Abraham was righteous and chosen as His prophet. Through Abraham’s intercession, the punishment that was to fall upon Abimelech was turned aside, and mercy triumphed over judgment.

So too do the saints, by their prayers, intercede for us standing before God on behalf of the faithful, so that we may be spared from the sufferings that our sins deserve. Their voices rise like morning light over a darkened earth, pleading for mercy where there should be wrath.

As the Psalmist testifies: “For the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears are open to their cry.” (Psalm 33:15).

Therefore, beloved, the intercession of the saints is not only an ornament of our faith but its living breath the ceaseless prayer of love that unites the Church on earth with the Church in heaven. Through their prayers, we are upheld; through their love, we are reconciled; and through their holiness, we are reminded of the mercy of God, who delights to save through those who are His friends.

text.text: His Holy Origin and Miraculous Birth

text:
In the land of Nhissa, Egypt, a barren couple, Simon and Aqleas, mourned for thirty years, childless and heavy with longing. But their mourning was turned into joy, for the Lord, who opens barren wombs and remembers His servants, answered their tearful supplication. Aqleas, in her travail of spirit, fell before the Holy Trinity in the temple and lo! a voice from the heights proclaimed: "Receive a son whose glory is greater than the height of heaven."

On Megabit 29 he was conceived; on Tahisas 29 he was born.but in exultation and divine utterance. For the infant, upon his arrival into the world, stood up and proclaimed:

text.text: His Monastic Calling and Angelic Commission

text:
When he was three years old, the angel Saint Gabriel, took him from the monastery where the monks lived and placed him at the gate. When Abba Zemedbirhan heard about this sign, he found the child, took him in, and made him a monk. Abba Zemedbirhan raised him, taught him, and guided him in the monastic life.

After this, he was given the gift of healing. In a single day, he healed thousands of blind and lame people. When the bishops and priests heard about his fame and came to investigate and tax his works, , Saint Gabriel took him and presented him before the Lord.

The Lord said, “Many will be saved from death, the torment of the soul, and hell.” Then he told him, “Go into the forest, live apart from people, with sixty the Anabst and the Anabrt..” they asked, “My Lord, what will they eat and live on?” The Lord replied, “They will live by licking the dust that you have trampled on; that will be their food.”

They entered a secluded monastery and began to live among the Anabst and the Anabrt. When Daniel was cast out by the Anabst, the Anabst followed him like a cat under his feet. 

After living this way for 30 years, the Lord appeared to them in three forms and asked, “What do you want me to do for you?”
First, they asked to pray for the people of the earth. They said, “Have mercy on them.” The Lord brought 3,000 sinners out of hell and led them to paradise.

text.text: His Mission to Ethiopia and Intercessory Sacrifice

text:
He was commanded, "Go to Ethiopia," and Saint Gabriel carried him in a chariot to " Midre Kebd". Afterward, he was taken to Zquwala (Debre kidus), where he prayed for 100 years with a pure heart, pleading for the forgiveness of the sins of the Ethiopian people.

When he was 40 days , an angel appeared to him and said:

"Remember, O Master, and come to me."But he replied:

"If you do not forgive ethiopia, I will not come out of the sea."

He remained in prayer for 100 years, crying out:

"If you do not forgive Ethiopia , I will not come out of the sea."

After this long intercession, the Lord rose and said:

"I will forgive , O Master. Come out of the sea."

After receiving forgiveness, he and the angel descended from the heavens and stood between the earth and the sky for seven years shining like a pillar of light, praying day and night without covering their eyes.

However, Satanstill filled with envycame in the form of a crow and blinded them. After two weeks of prayer, Saint Michael and Saint Gabriel came to their aid and healed them.

From there, they returned to Zquwala, where they saw the Holy Trinity resting under the shade of the elders of the temple. The Trinity said to them:

"We have asked you pby the throne of God. Please sending out us , one by one."

As they departed, they saw the Trinity as three in one, and they fell down in awe. But God lifted them up and said:

"Go to Zquwala and defeat your enemies."

They obeyed, arriving like a flash of lightning, and empowered by the seven archangels they destroyed thousands of demons.

text.text: The Repose of the Righteous Abune Gebre Menfes kidus

text:
The repose of the righteous father, Abune Gebre Menfes Kidus, is commemorated on Megabit 5, which falls during the period of the Great Lent. According to Article 15 of the Book of the Feteha Negest , no feast or celebration is to be held during this sacred time of fasting and repentance. Since the season of Lent is one of mourning and spiritual reflection, drums are not beaten, songs are not sung, and applause is not heard the faithful observe it in solemn silence and contrition.

For this reason, the Feast of the Crucifixion, originally observed on Megabit 27, was moved to Tikimt 27 and the The repose of the righteous father, Abune Gebre Menfes Kidus,celebrated on Tikimt 5. This change has remained part of the Church’s holy tradition.

Our father, the righteous Abune Gebre Menfes Kidus, lived in Ethiopia for 262 years, and after 562 years of spiritual service and divine endurance, he peacefully departed from this world on a Sunday, entrusting his soul to the Lord, who delivers His saints from suffering. The angels carried him in a circle of fire to Jerusalem and laid his blessed body in a holy resting place.

text.text:
May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.

text: Beloved in Christ, children of the Orthodox faith, inheritors of the covenant sealed in blood by prophets, apostles, and martyrs today we meditate on the mystery of those who suffer for righteousness’ sake. For the Lord Himself declared, “Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven” (Matthew 5:10). This divine saying is not a mere comfort for the weary, but a crown of fire placed upon the heads of those who walk the path of truth amid the hatred of the world.

Those who reject the righteous and add sorrow to those who suffer unjustly will face severe punishment in hell and, later, in the eternal fire. Kotiba and her family represent those who despise the righteous, mock the suffering of the innocent, and falsely accuse them just by giving them names that are not theirs. They even intrude upon the lives of the righteous only to increase their pain. Such people will meet a fate worse than that of Kotiba and her family.

✍🏾Christians must understand that in this life we face two paths: either we follow our Lord, who shares the blessing of persecution with our Holy Mother and makes us heirs of the Kingdom of Heaven, or we imitate the wicked Herod, who separates himself from the blessings of the saints and becomes a child of hell. The pursuit of righteousness is not an option but a daily calling for every believer.

✍🏾As our Lord taught us in the Holy Gospel, “Behold, the Kingdom of God is within you” (Luke 17:21). Just as persecution for righteousness’ sake surrounds us, so does the opportunity to live righteously. We must grow in wisdom, patience, and endurance so that we may inherit the Kingdom of God with those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake.

✍🏾Let us be careful not to join the company of the wicked who persecute the righteous, for their end is destruction. Instead, let us walk with those who suffer for truth and holiness, that we may share in their eternal reward.

text.text: Persecution: A Transition to the Kingdom of Heaven

text:
The Holy Scriptures teach us that when we suffer for righteousness in this earthly life according to our strength, our trials and persecutions will one day come to an end. Earthly suffering is temporary; but through it, we are led toward the eternal Kingdom of Heaven.

✍🏾One of the early fathers who wrote about the life of the Virgin Mary is the beloved Evangelist Saint John, who received our Lady as his mother on behalf of all humanity (John 19:26; Revelation 12:1).

✍🏾Saint John, because of his steadfast witness to the truth and his defense of the faith, was exiled and imprisoned by earthly rulers on the island of Patmos. Yet this righteous and holy apostle understood that persecution is not destruction but transition a passage to the Kingdom of Heaven. He did not grieve for himself, nor did he despair in his exile. Rather, he was sorrowful only because he could not continue preaching the Gospel as the other apostles did.

The Lord, who never forsakes those who serve Him, revealed to John the mysteries of Heaven while he prayed on the island. From that revelation, Saint John wrote the sacred book we now call The Revelation (Apocalypse). His physical persecution did not hinder him from entering into divine mysteries and receiving heavenly visions. Instead, it became his gateway to the eternal Kingdom.

text.text: The Mystery of Exile and Deliverance

text:
✍🏾In Revelation 12:6, Saint John speaks of the exile of our Lady and, symbolically, of the Church:

“And the woman fled into the wilderness, to a place prepared by God, that she should be stayed there for a thousand two hundred and sixty days.”

This number 1260 days, or 42 months, or three years and six months represents the length of the Virgin’s exile.

✍🏾As our Holy Fathers explain, the fact that these days are numbered shows that the sufferings of the righteous are temporary and measurable. Persecution and hardship for the sake of God will pass away, but the heavenly reward is eternal and without end. The same symbolic number 42 appears again in the lives of the saints who endured trials before receiving glory.

✍🏾The exile of Israel, recorded in the Book of Exodus, lasted forty-two years. Those who pleased God among them entered the land of Canaan after their trials, while their persecutors Pharaoh and his army perished in judgment.

✍🏾The prophet Elijah was also exiled for forty-two months, fleeing from the wicked rulers Ahab and Jezebel because he proclaimed the word of God and defended the poor. Elijah’s suffering ended with his glorious ascent to heaven, but his persecutors died in disgrace, their memory erased from among the living.

✍🏾Likewise, our Lady the Virgin Mary and her beloved Son, the Lord Jesus Christ, endured exile and persecution under Herod’s cruelty. Yet after Herod’s death, they returned safely to Nazareth in Galilee. The persecutor died in torment.

✍🏾Therefore, as members of God’s family, we must also become faithful witnesses of truth. When the time comes for us to stand for righteousness, we should accept persecution and suffering with joy, just as our holy fathers did.

✍🏾For persecution is not merely a burden it is a sacred transition, a path that leads us from the trials of earth to the everlasting peace of heaven.

text.text: The End of Our Lady’s Persecution and Her Return to Galilee

text:
On the 6th day of hidar each year, at the end of the month of Tsige, we remember the moment when Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, together with her beloved Son, Saint Joseph the Righteous, and Saint Salome, found rest after their persecution and suffering at the hands of Herod. They rested in a place called Debre Kusqam.

As the Evangelist Saint Matthew records:

“When Herod died, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, saying, ‘Rise, take the Child and His mother, and go to the land of Israel, for those who sought the Child’s life are dead.’”(Matthew 2:20)

We therefore remember that the elderly Joseph returned from exile in Egypt with the Holy Virgin Mary whom Salome faithfully assisted and with her beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.

✍🏾 The day of Our Lady’s persecution and the end of her exile was known to God with absolute certainty. Yet, as we see in the lives of the saints, when one persecution ends, another often follows. Their lives are a ladder of glory, upon which they ascend from one trial to another, and from glory to glory.

✍🏾 Each hardship they overcome brings them closer to divine perfection. There is endless grace for those who conquer persecution through faith. When the saints triumph over the devil’s assaults, even the angels in heaven rejoice, for Satan is defeated by their endurance.

The Mother of God, the Holy Virgin Mary, never displeased God during her persecution. By her patience and prayer, she overcame the evil one. Her beloved Son, Jesus Christ, rested her in Debre qusquam, which symbolizes the Kingdom of Heaven. Although Debre Kusqam is not itself a heavenly place, it is a model of divine rest a reflection of the eternal peace promised to the faithful.

After this blessed rest, Our Lady experienced four of her five great sorrows, continuing to bear witness through her suffering and obedience.

The End of Our Lady’s Persecution and Her Return to Galilee

On the 6th day of hidar each year, at the end of the month of Tsige, we remember the moment when Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, together with her beloved Son, Saint Joseph the Righteous, and Saint Salome, found rest after their persecution and suffering at the hands of Herod. They rested in a place called Debre Kusqam.

As the Evangelist Saint Matthew records:

“When Herod died, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, saying, ‘Rise, take the Child and His mother, and go to the land of Israel, for those who sought the Child’s life are dead.’”(Matthew 2:20)

We therefore remember that the elderly Joseph returned from exile in Egypt with the Holy Virgin Mary whom Salome faithfully assisted and with her beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.

✍🏾 The day of Our Lady’s persecution and the end of her exile was known to God with absolute certainty. Yet, as we see in the lives of the saints, when one persecution ends, another often follows. Their lives are a ladder of glory, upon which they ascend from one trial to another, and from glory to glory.

✍🏾 Each hardship they overcome brings them closer to divine perfection. There is endless grace for those who conquer persecution through faith. When the saints triumph over the devil’s assaults, even the angels in heaven rejoice, for Satan is defeated by their endurance.

The Mother of God, the Holy Virgin Mary, never displeased God during her persecution. By her patience and prayer, she overcame the evil one. Her beloved Son, Jesus Christ, rested her in Debre qusquam, which symbolizes the Kingdom of Heaven. Although Debre Kusqam is not itself a heavenly place, it is a model of divine rest a reflection of the eternal peace promised to the faithful.

After this blessed rest, Our Lady experienced four of her five great sorrows, continuing to bear witness through her suffering and obedience.

text:
The great lesson we learn from her holy life is this: in our Christian journey, when one trial ends, we must prepare ourselves for another. We should never become proud or self-justifying after passing through one hardship, for the path to heaven is lifelong perseverance.

The apostles themselves warned us of this truth, saying,

“It is through much labor and tribulation that we must enter the Kingdom of God.” (Acts 14:22)

Therefore, we must guard ourselves against the false teachings of hypocrites who mock the holy matter of salvation. Our faith rests not in comfort but in endurance. We have a faithful God who will grant us entry into the heavenly Jerusalem, the holy city of Debre Kusqam (Mekane Ereft), which we long for and hope to inherit.

✍🏾 When our Holy Virgin Mary endured three years and six months of persecution and hardship with her beloved Son, the power and protection of the Most High never departed from her. The holy angels who assisted her throughout her trials also glorified her with songs of praise.

That is why our Church proclaims:

“The power of the Most High surrounded her with wondrous splendor, clothing her in divine light."

This divine protection revealed in the life of Our Lady is also granted to all who believe in Christ, who suffer for His Name, and who remain steadfast in the true faith He has entrusted to us.

May our Lord and God separate us from the Herodians those who persecute truth and unite us with the Christians who suffer for righteousness. May He count us among those who stand firm in faith and receive the incorruptible crown.

Let us pray that through the intercession of the Holy Virgin Mary, the Apostle John, and all the saints who endured suffering for truth, we may find strength to persevere until the end.

“Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.” (Matthew 5:10)

Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ,
we greet you in the name of our Lord and Savior, who has called us to holiness and to the fellowship of His saints. Today, with hearts full of faith, we continue our reflection on the sacred mystery of the intercession of the saints, learning why God reveals His divine will to His chosen friends and how their prayers become a light for the world.

“The desire of the righteous is only good, but the expectation of the wicked is destruction.”
(Proverbs 11:23)

(Proverbs 12:5)

Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ,
we greet you in the name of our Lord and Savior, who has called us to holiness and to the fellowship of His saints. Today, with hearts full of faith, we continue our reflection on the sacred mystery of the intercession of the saints, learning why God reveals His divine will to His chosen friends and how their prayers become a light for the world.

The Necessity of Intercession

✍🏾 The intercession of the saints is necessary because through them our prayers reach God more quickly. The saints are God’s beloved friends, and our Creator accepts their prayers with special favor especially the prayers of His holy Mother, the Virgin Mary. Through their prayers, God acts with mercy, heals our troubles, and grants relief to His people.

The Holy Scriptures testify that the prayers of the righteous are far more acceptable than the prayers of the wicked:

“The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears are open unto their cry.”
(Psalm 33:13–20; Proverbs 10:24)

The Power of the Saints’ Prayers

✍🏾 The prayers of the saints are pleasing to God because their hearts are pure. They have cleansed themselves from hatred, revenge, and sin. They do not ask for things contrary to God’s will but pray with full faith, trusting that He will hear them.

The Scriptures explain this truth clearly:

“The desire of the righteous is only good, but the expectation of the wicked is destruction.”
(Proverbs 11:23)

“The thoughts of the righteous are right, but the counsel of the wicked is deceit.”
(Proverbs 12:5)

When the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to the Lord asking that her sons might sit at His right and left hand in His Kingdom, Jesus answered,

“You do not know what you are asking.”
(Matthew 20:20–22)

And He also said,

(Mark 11:24)

✍🏾 The saints and holy angels rejoice greatly whenever sinners receive forgiveness. When God’s beloved Mother and His holy friends plead for mercy on behalf of sinners, the Lord gladly hears and answers their prayers in order to honor them.

“There will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance... there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents.”
(Luke 15:7, 10)

“Whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give it to you... Ask and you will receive, that your joy may be full.”
(John 16:23–24)

Intercession as a Divine Honor

✍🏾 The intercession of the saints is not a limitation of God’s glory but a revelation of His mercy and honor toward His faithful servants. God Himself has, at times, led humanity through the intercession of His chosen ones. Before bringing judgment upon people, He often revealed His will to His friends, such as:

👉🏾The coming flood revealed to Noah

👉🏾The destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah revealed to Abraham

👉🏾The sin of Nineveh revealed to Jonah

👉🏾The captivity and destruction of Israel revealed to the prophets

Why God Reveals His Will to the Saints

✍🏾 God reveals these mysteries to His saints for several holy reasons:

1. To teach and counsel the people—turning them from active sin to active righteousness, from idolatry to the true worship of God through repentance, and to rebuke and discipline the disobedient with the divine authority granted to them (Deuteronomy 14:27; Acts 5:5).

2. To intercede for the people’s sins—pleading for God’s mercy and appealing for His patience in the face of His righteous wrath.

3. To be living examples of holiness—not only through their words and teachings but also by shining as lights in a darkened world through the purity and faithfulness of their lives.

Continues 👇🏾

✍🏾 The Scriptures clearly command all Christians to pray for one another:

“Pray for one another, that you may be healed.”
(James 5:16)

The prayer of Abune Zebesemaat, taught by our holy father Medhane Alem, also emphasizes praying not only for ourselves but for others showing that intercession is central to Christian prayer.

Saint Paul likewise urges:

“I exhort that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people, for kings and all who are in authority... This is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior, who desires all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.”
(1 Timothy 2:1–4)

“Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.”
(Philippians 4:6)

The Prophet Isaiah lamented:

“He saw that there was no one, and was appalled that there was no intercessor.”
(Isaiah 59:16)

Our Lord Himself commanded:

“Love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who persecute you, that you may be children of your Father in heaven.”
(Matthew 5:43–47)

text.text: The Superiority of the Saints’ Intercession

text: ✍🏾 While intercession is a duty for all believers, the Scriptures clearly show that the intercession of the saints is superior, more honorable, and brings quicker answers from God. Consider the following examples:

When the Holy Trinity appeared to Abraham, they said, “Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?” Because of Abraham’s pleading, God spared Lot from destruction, though Sodom and Gomorrah perished for their sins.
When Lot prayed, the Lord said, “Behold, I have accepted your request in this matter; I will not destroy the city you have spoken of.” The angels spared the city on account of Lot’s faithfulness.

Beloved children of the Light,
Grace and peace be multiplied to you in the name of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. Today we bring to you a holy teaching filled with divine wisdom a reflection on those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake, whose reward is none other than the kingdom of heaven itself. Let us open our hearts to this mystery, that we may understand the blessing hidden in suffering and the glory that follows the cross.

Our Lord teaches in the Gospel of Matthew:

“Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.”

Righteousness refers to truth, integrity, and honesty. It is the good and virtuous work that flows from faith in God and brings honor and glory to Him. In the original Gë'ëz ( Ele Yiseddu), the word translated as “persecuted” literally means “those who suffer” or “those who are mistreated.” Thus, “persecuted for righteousness’ sake” describes all who suffer because they uphold the truth, speak the truth, stand for justice, perform good deeds, or earnestly seek the truth.

✍🏾 There is only one true righteousness: Jesus Christ. He is the source and author of righteousness (Jeremiah 23:6; 2 Corinthians 5:21). Therefore, those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake are those who suffer for believing in and following Christ, for obeying His commandments, for preaching His Word, or for serving Him faithfully.

The Apostle Paul also teaches this truth:

"You know the persecutions that happened to me at Antioch, at Iconium, and at Lystra, which I endured; but out of them all, the Lord delivered me. Indeed, all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will be persecuted." (2 Timothy 3:11-12)

This reminds us that persecution is not a sign of failure, but a confirmation that we are walking in the way of Christ, living righteously, and upholding the truth in a world that often opposes it.

✍🏾

text.text: Blessed Are Those Who Suffer for Righteousness’ Sake

text:
Therefore, those who suffer for the sake of the true Christ are noble, honored, and blessed; the kingdom of heaven belongs to them. As Saint John the Baptist explained, our Lord did not mention merely those who are causes the suffering  the main focus is the purpose ‘for righteousness’ sake’ not the identity of the persecutors. 

As long as the persecution comes with the intention of righteousness, whether from Gentiles, heretics, believers, or unbelievers, the reward is the kingdom of heaven. Rather, one who rebukes others and suffers for the sins of fellow believers will receive the blessing, as Saint John the Baptist promised

✍🏾 The phrase “for righteousness’ sake” is profound, as it distinguishes a martyr from a criminal. Though the external punishment may appear the same, the purpose makes all the difference:

The martyr suffers for righteousness, upholding the truth and the will of God.

The criminal suffers as punishment for wrongdoing.

The martyr will receive eternal reward, while the thief has no hope of blessing unless he repents.

text.text: The Cross and the Martyrdom of Christ

text: Our Lord was crucified for the truth, while the two thieves were crucified as punishment for their crimes. Although all three were condemned to die, the purpose of our Lord’s crucifixion was to save humanity. Through His cross, He reconciled mankind to God. Therefore, the cross became a symbol of judgment and mercy. To the faithful sinner who said, “Lord, remember me when You come into Your kingdom” acknowledging his sin and repentance our Lord replied, “Today you will be with me in paradise” (Luke 23:42-43).

✍🏾 The Christian life is a life of trials, suffering, and struggle, not a life of earthly pleasure and wealth. Our Lord taught that the path of righteousness is difficult:

"Narrow is the gate and narrow the way that leads to life, and few there are who find it" (Matthew 7:14).

And regarding the challenges of following Him, He said:

"Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven" (Matthew 5:10).

✍🏾 The true spiritual life is not comfort on earth but a life of sacrifice and endurance. That is why our Lord instructed His disciples:

"If anyone desires to come after Me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Me" (Matthew 16:24).

The apostles, who learned from Him and followed Him faithfully, also taught:

"We must through many tribulations enter the kingdom of God" (Acts 14:22).

They set an example for us by enduring suffering with faith and perseverance.

✍🏾 The saints who left everything behind, bore the cross, and served Christ faithfully are called witnesses of righteousness. Our righteous father, Tekle Haymanot, is one such witness. He was called the “New Apostle” for spreading the Gospel in Ethiopia. In honor of his devotion, church elders sing:

"You preached the Gospel of God, you were a witness to righteousness, and you were called the plant of religion."

Righteousness is obtained by combining true faith with good works. It is not enough to have faith alone; faith must be active and expressed through righteous deeds. The Apostle James explains this clearly:

"My brothers, what does it profit a man if he says he has faith but does not have works? Can faith save him? Faith by itself is dead… Was not our father Abraham justified by works when he offered Isaac his son on the altar? You see that faith worked with his works, and by works faith was perfected. Scripture says, ‘Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,’ and he was called the friend of God. Likewise, was not Rahab of old justified by works when she received the spies and sent them out another way? For as the body apart from the spirit is dead, so also faith apart from works is dead.” (James 2:14-26)

This shows that righteousness is found in the combination of faith and good works.

Our Lord also taught the importance of righteousness in His Gospel:

“Seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you” (Matthew 6:33).

“Except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no wise enter into the kingdom of heaven” (Matthew 5:20).

“John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him; and you, when you saw it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe” (Matthew 21:32).


Regarding the work of the Holy Spirit, our Lord taught:

"When He comes, He will convict the world of sin, righteousness, and judgment: of sin, because they do not believe in Me; of righteousness, because I go to the Father and you will see Me no more; and of judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged" (John 16:8-10).

✍🏾 Saint Peter also emphasizes the Lord’s favor:

"The eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and His ears are open to their prayers, but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil" (1 Peter 3:12).

text:
👉🏾The Apostle Paul also taught deeply about righteousness, saying:

✍🏾"For by the works of the law no flesh shall be justified in His sight, for by the law comes the knowledge of sin. But now the righteousness of God, apart from the law, is revealed, being witnessed by the Law and the Prophets even the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ, to all and upon all who believe. For there is no difference: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, being justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God set forth to be a propitiation through faith in His blood, to demonstrate His righteousness because in His forbearance God had passed over the sins that were previously committed to demonstrate at the present time His righteousness, that He might be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus." (Romans 3:20–26)

👉🏾Saint Paul explains that “justified by grace” does not mean that good works are unnecessary, as some may think. Rather, it means that salvation is a free gift of God, given through faith in Christ’s redemptive work. Since neither Jews nor Gentiles possessed works capable of justifying them before God, both were saved without distinction not by the works of the law, but through faith in the redeeming grace of Christ.

Our Lord Himself affirmed that righteousness must be lived out through faithful action. In His teaching about the final judgment, He said:

✍🏾"When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, then He will sit upon His glorious throne. All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats. He will set the sheep on His right hand, and the goats on His left. Then the King will say to those on His right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry and you gave Me food, I was thirsty and you gave Me drink, I was a stranger and you took Me in, I was naked and you clothed Me, I was sick and you visited Me, I was in prison and you came to Me.’ Then the righteous will answer Him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You drink?’” (Matthew 25:31–36)

This powerful passage shows clearly that righteousness is not achieved by faith alone, but also by Conduct . True righteousness is the living expression of faith through works that please God feeding the hungry, comforting the suffering, and serving others in love.

Therefore, beloved, take courage! Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake. Endure, suffer, labor, and persevere not for earthly gain, but for the heavenly kingdom, for eternal joy in Christ, for the honor of God, and for the glory of the Virgin Mother and the precious Cross.

text:
Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ,
we greet you in the name of our Lord and Savior, who has called us to holiness and to the fellowship of His saints. Today, with hearts full of faith, we continue our reflection on the sacred mystery of the intercession of the saints, learning why God reveals His divine will to His chosen friends and how their prayers become a light for the world.

we read that God was angry with Abimelech, the king of Gerar, because he took Sarah, the wife of Abraham, into his house. The Lord said to Abimelech,
“I also kept you from sinning against Me; therefore, I did not allow you to touch her. Now then, return the man’s wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and you shall live. But if you do not return her, know for certain that you shall surely die, you and all who belong to you.”

Abimelech, trembling at the word of the Lord, obeyed His command and returned Sarah to her husband. Then Abraham prayed to God, and the Lord heard his prayer. God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his servants, for the Lord had closed all the wombs in Abimelech’s household because of Sarah, the wife of Abraham.

✍🏾 From this, we understand that the prayer of a righteous man has great power before God. Even though Abimelech was a king, his deliverance and the healing of his house depended upon the prayer of Abraham, the friend of God. Thus, Scripture teaches us that God Himself honors the intercession of His saints, for through their prayers, mercy triumphs over judgment.

, when the people of Israel turned away from God and worshipped the golden calf, the Lord said to Moses,
“I have seen this people, and behold, it is a stiff-necked people. Now therefore let Me alone, that My wrath may burn hot against them, and I may consume them; and I will make of you a great nation.”

Yet God, who needs no counsel from man, could have destroyed them without speaking to Moses. The phrase “Let Me alone” The phrase ‘Let Me alone, that I may destroy them’ essentially means ‘Do not intercede for them”but Moses, moved by compassion and faith, stood before the Creator and pleaded for mercy. text: Beloved children in Christ,Grace and peace be multiplied to you from our Lord Jesus Christ. Today we turn our hearts to the teaching of our Savior, who said, “Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven” (Matthew 5:10). Let us carefully consider what this Beatitude reveals to us about suffering, exile, and the ways in which the faithful are tested for the sake of holiness.

text.text: This Beatitude is Also Interpreted as Exile

text:
✍🏾Although this eighth Beatitude primarily speaks about suffering for righteousness (persecution), some Church scholars also understand it in relation to exile. Yet, they emphasize that persecution itself is a form of suffering a kind of martyrdom that may appear in different ways.

Persecution, therefore, can be divided into two main types:

👉🏾 Physical persecution

👉🏾 Spiritual persecution

✍🏾 Physical persecution refers to being forced to flee or move from one’s physical place of residence to another. It involves a literal change of location from one home, region, or even country to another due to faith, danger, or other pressures.

✍🏾Spiritual persecution refers to an inner or mental displacement a movement from one’s former beliefs, goals, or way of life to another. This occurs without any physical relocation but involves a deep transformation or struggle within the soul.

In some cases, persecution can be both physical and spiritual, where the believer suffers both outwardly in body and inwardly in spirit for the sake of righteousness.

text.text: The Fourf Persecution from the Perspective of Righteousness

text: From the viewpoint of righteousness, persecution can be understood in four distinct categories. Each reveals a mystery of the Christian journey how the soul moves between the world and God, between obedience and rebellion, between faith and apostasy.

For Righteousness – The Spiritual Migration from the World to God

This is the persecution for righteousness, which takes place in the spirit. It is the inward struggle of a soul that turns away from the world and sets its course toward God. It is not fought with swords or prisons, but within the heart the battle between the flesh and the spirit, between pride and humility, between self-love and divine love.
This persecution is the foundation of Christianity.

Because of Righteousness Suffering for Living in the Truth

The second persecution is because of righteousness the suffering that comes upon those who follow the path of truth. It is the persecution endured by the apostles and early Christians, who believed in Christ and proclaimed His Gospel to the nations.They were reviled, imprisoned, beaten, and slain because they refused to deny the Lord. Throughout the history of the Church, countless believers have shared this same cross, enduring scorn, exile, and death for the sake of their faith.

text:
For the Sake of Righteousness The Pursuit and Service of Holiness

The third persecution is for the sake of righteousness the suffering borne by those who seek to obtain, teach, or learn righteousness:

To seek righteousness to strive after holiness through repentance, fasting, and prayer, resisting temptation and renouncing sin.

To preach righteousness to proclaim truth to a world that prefers lies, facing misunderstanding,  and rejection for teaching what is just.

To learn righteousness to grow in divine wisdom and knowledge, persevering through trials, fatigue, and spiritual opposition.

Many saints endured persecution in these ways they suffered in their quest to serve Christ faithfully, to instruct others, and to remain steadfast in repentance.
As our Lord promised: “Everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or lands for My name’s sake will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.” (Matthew 19:29)

From Righteousness  The Fall from Light to Darkness

The fourth is the persecution from righteousness the soul’s exile from holiness into sin and death. This is not the persecution endured by the faithful, but the suffering of those who turn away from God after having known His truth.
It is the torment of Judas, who betrayed his Lord for silver, and of Demas. Their anguish was not for righteousness but from it the bitter harvest of apostasy, where the soul finds no peace because it has abandoned the source of life.
“The first two exoduses in the history of creation were exoduses from righteousness.”

text.text: 1. The First Exile: The Fall of Satan

text: The first exile was the casting down of Satan from the world of angels into the abyss. Once radiant among the hosts of heaven, he grew proud and rebelled against his Creator.

text.text: 2. The Second Exile: The Fall of Man

text:
The second exile was the expulsion of mankind from paradise to the earth, caused by the deceit of that same fallen spirit. Adam and Eve, clothed in innocence, broke the divine command and were driven from Eden, exiled to a land of labor and death. Yet even in judgment, God wove mercy.

The great Abba Hiriakos, in the Liturgy of Mary, spoke of this tender mystery:

“You are Adam’s hope when he was exiled from paradise.”

These words honor the Holy Virgin Mary as the comfort and redemption of fallen humanity. For through her obedience, the hope that Adam lost was restored; the gate of paradise, once shut, began to open again through her Son.

Our father Abraham, too, knew exile not as punishment, but as obedience. God called him from his homeland in Ur of the Chaldeans, saying, “Go from your country to the land that I will show you” (Genesis 12:1). In faith, he left all behind and journeyed to Canaan, and later to Gerar (Genesis 20:1). His wandering was holy; it was the pilgrimage of faith seeking righteousness.

For the Sake of Righteousness The Pursuit and Service of Holiness

The third persecution is for the sake of righteousness the suffering borne by those who seek to obtain, teach, or learn righteousness:

To seek righteousness to strive after holiness through repentance, fasting, and prayer, resisting temptation and renouncing sin.

To preach righteousness to proclaim truth to a world that prefers lies, facing misunderstanding,  and rejection for teaching what is just.

To learn righteousness to grow in divine wisdom and knowledge, persevering through trials, fatigue, and spiritual opposition.

Many saints endured persecution in these ways they suffered in their quest to serve Christ faithfully, to instruct others, and to remain steadfast in repentance.
As our Lord promised: “Everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or lands for My name’s sake will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.” (Matthew 19:29)

From Righteousness  The Fall from Light to Darkness

The fourth is the persecution from righteousness the soul’s exile from holiness into sin and death. This is not the persecution endured by the faithful, but the suffering of those who turn away from God after having known His truth.
It is the torment of Judas, who betrayed his Lord for silver, and of Demas. Their anguish was not for righteousness but from it the bitter harvest of apostasy, where the soul finds no peace because it has abandoned the source of life.

text.text: The Exile of the Lord: The Blessed Flight to Egypt

text:
Even our Lord Himself entered into exile, sanctifying the path of all who suffer displacement. When Herod sought to destroy the Christ Child, an angel spoke to Joseph in a dream: “Arise, take the young child and His mother, and flee into Egypt.” Thus the Holy Family became strangers in a foreign land.

Abba Tsige Dengel, in the Lamentations of the Virgin, spoke of this mystery in reverent words:

“Jesus, the Hope of the Exiled, the Comfort of the Wandering.”

Christ’s journey from Bethlehem to Egypt was not a sign of weakness, but of divine mercy. By His exile, He blessed ours transforming the pain of displacement into a path of salvation. For as He entered Egypt, He entered the heart of every exile, making our wanderings holy and our suffering redemptive.


Saint Matthew writes of the persecution of our Lord Jesus Christ while He was yet in His mother’s arms:

“And when they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, take the Child and His Mother, and flee into Egypt, and stay there until I bring you word; for Herod seeks the Child to destroy Him. Then Joseph arose, took the Child and His Mother by night, and departed into Egypt, and remained there until the death of Herod. This was to fulfill what was spoken by the prophet, Out of Egypt have I called My Son.”

When Herod saw that he had been deceived by the wise men, he became enraged and ordered the slaughter of all male children in Bethlehem two years old and under.

Then was fulfilled the word of Jeremiah the prophet:

“A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and refusing to be comforted, because they are no more.”
(Matthew 2:13–18)

text.text: The Church carries the cross of suffering

text:
for suffering and the Church are inseparable. From her very foundation she has been persecuted, and even now she walks the same path. The road to righteousness, both now and in the age to come, must pass through tribulation.

The early Christians and apostles were persecuted by kings and rulers. Saint Luke records:

“On that day a great persecution arose against the Church in Jerusalem, and all except the apostles were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria. Devout men buried Stephen and made great lamentation over him. But Saul began to destroy the Church, entering house after house; he dragged off men and women and put them in prison. Those who were scattered went about preaching the word.”
(Acts 8:1–4)

The saints and the witness of suffering

text:
The saints who believed in God and set an example of faith endured the same suffering. Saint Paul speaks of them, saying:

“Saint Paul writes:

“What more shall I say? For time would fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets  who through faith subdued kingdoms, worked righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions, quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in battle, and put foreign armies to flight. Women received their dead raised to life again. Others were tortured, not accepting deliverance, that they might obtain a better resurrection. Others suffered mockings and scourgings, and even chains and imprisonment. They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, they were slain with the sword. They went about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, afflicted, mistreated wandering in deserts and mountains, in dens and caves of the earth of whom the world was not worthy.”
(Hebrews 11:32–38)

This passage speaks of those who were exiled and afflicted for righteousness’ sake men and women whose faith made them strangers in the world, yet heirs of a kingdom that cannot be shaken. Their suffering was not defeat but testimony, and through their endurance the glory of righteousness was revealed.

The apostles themselves fought this good fight and taught us to do the same. Paul exhorted Timothy, saying:

“Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, to which you were called… keep the commandment without spot or reproach until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ, which He will display in His own time the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and Lord of lords.”
(1 Timothy 6:12–15)

When our Lord carried His cross toward Calvary, He said to the women who wept for Him,

“If they do these things when the wood is green, what will happen when it is dry?”
(Luke 23:31)

By this He meant that if such suffering was laid upon the sinless Son of God, how much more will His followers endure who are themselves frail and sinful. Therefore, He told them to weep not for Him, but for themselves and their children.

Thus, the Christian life is not separated from suffering; it is purified by it. To endure trials for righteousness is to imitate Christ Himself, for through the cross we are made worthy of His glory.
