text:
Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ said,“Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.” (Matthew 5:4)

In these divine words, mourning does not mean despair, but the holy sorrow that springs from repentance and love for God. The tears of a penitent heart are precious before the Lord. They wash away sin, soften the soul, and open the gate of mercy.

Throughout Scripture, we see how holy men and women wept not from hopelessness, but from a longing to be united again with God. Their tears became prayers, their sorrow turned to joy, and their repentance became a light to the generations that followed.

text.text: 1. The Sinful Woman Who Wept Before Christ

text: Saint Mary (

) stood behind our Lord at His feet, weeping, and began to wash His feet with her tears. She wiped them with her hair, kissed His feet, and anointed them with precious ointment (Luke 7:38). Through her sincere repentance, her many sins were forgiven.

As written in the Gospel of Luke, one of the Pharisees invited our Lord Jesus Christ to dine with him. While He sat at the table, a woman known in the city as a sinner entered the house. When she saw the Lord, she brought an alabaster jar of perfume and, with deep sorrow, began to wash His feet with her tears and wipe them with her hair.

The Pharisee, seeing this, judged her in his heart, thinking, “If this man were truly a prophet, He would know who this woman is.” But the Lord, knowing his thoughts, said to him, “Simon, I have something to say to you.” Then He spoke a parable:

“There was a certain creditor who had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii and the other fifty. When they could not repay, he forgave them both. Which of them will love him more?” Simon replied, “The one who was forgiven more.” Jesus said, “You have judged rightly.”

Then He turned toward the woman and said, “Do you see this woman? I came into your house; you gave Me no water for My feet, but she has washed My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair. You did not greet Me with a kiss, but she has not ceased to kiss My feet. You did not anoint My head with oil, but she has anointed My feet with perfume. Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But to whom little is forgiven, the same loves little.”

And He said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”

text:
Saint Peter, the apostle chosen by our Lord, was strong in words but weak in the moment of trial. Before the rooster crowed, he denied his Master three times. Yet, when the Lord turned and looked at him, Peter’s heart broke, and he went out and wept bitterly. Those tears became his repentance, and through them, he was forgiven.

As written in the Gospel of Luke, the Lord said to him, “Simon, Simon, behold, Satan has demanded to have you, that he may sift you like wheat; but I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail; and when you have returned, strengthen your brothers.” Peter, full of confidence, answered, “Lord, I am ready to go with you both to prison and to death.” But the Lord told him, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied me three times.”

Later, when Jesus was taken to the high priest’s house, Peter followed Him from a distance. In the courtyard, as he sat among those warming themselves by the fire, a servant woman saw him and said, “This man also was with Him.” Peter denied it, saying, “Woman, I do not know Him.” Soon after, another said, “You also are one of them.” But Peter replied, “Man, I am not.” About an hour later, another insisted, “Surely this man also was with Him, for he is a Galilean.” Peter said, “Man, I do not know what you are saying.”

At that moment, while he was still speaking, the rooster crowed. The Lord turned and looked upon Peter, and Peter remembered the words of his Master. His heart was pierced with sorrow, and he went out and wept bitterly.

The tears of Saint Peter were not of despair, but of deep repentance and love. His denial became the doorway to humility. Though he fell in weakness, he rose again through repentance and was strengthened by grace. From that moment, Peter became a true shepherd, feeding the flock of Christ with a heart purified by tears.

text.text: 3. The Tears of Saint John the Evangelist

text:
John the Evangelist, called the Beloved of God, was one of the few disciples who faithfully followed our Lord to the Cross. In His great wisdom, our Lord entrusted the care of His mother, the Virgin Mary, to John, saying, “Woman, behold your son!” and to John, “Behold your mother!” From that hour, John took her into his own home, showing his obedience, humility, and love (John 19:25–27). The evangelist wept until the day of his death, remembering the suffering of the Son of God, and his tears reflected a heart deeply united with Christ’s sorrow.

He is called the “Face of Sorrow” because he witnessed the suffering of the Lord and his heart was pierced with compassion. In his vision, he saw: “I saw in the right hand of Him who sat on the throne a scroll written within and on the back, sealed with seven seals. And I saw a strong angel proclaiming with a loud voice, ‘Who is worthy to open the scroll and break its seals?’ And no one in heaven, on earth, or under the earth was able to open the scroll or look inside it. I wept much because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or look inside it. Then one of the elders said to me, ‘Do not weep! Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed to open the scroll and its seven seals’” (Revelation 5:1–5).

Through John’s example, we learn that true discipleship involves compassion, steadfast faith, and loving responsibility. His tears remind us that mourning before God is not weakness but a holy act of prayer and repentance. Though sorrow may touch the faithful deeply, God’s mercy and triumph bring hope, restoration, and the assurance that His plan prevails. John teaches us to embrace sorrow with faith, to serve faithfully, and to trust in the victory of Christ, the Lion of Judah.

text: Beloved in Christ,As we reflect on the mysteries of God’s kingdom, we are reminded that the holy angels play a vital role in our spiritual lives. They are not distant beings but ministers sent by God to intercede on our behalf. Today, let us learn from the Scriptures how the angels intercede for God’s people, offering us comfort, guidance, and hope.

text.text: The Intercession of Angels: A Biblical Perspective

text:
The intercession of angels is presented in a mysterious and symbolic way in the Bible. Here are some clear and explicit evidences from Scripture:

✍🏾

The Bible says in 2 Corinthians 5:18:

"He has given us the ministry of reconciliation."

This shows that angels, like humans called to serve, are also ministers. The Scriptures explain this further:

👉🏾 “He makes his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire” (Psalm 103:4).

Additionally, Hebrews 1:14 says:

👉🏾 “Are they not all ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation?”

This demonstrates that angels act as ministers and mediators, particularly in spiritual matters such as reconciliation.

👉🏾 Incense symbolizes prayer.
Psalm 141:2 says:
"Let my prayer be set before you as incense."

Revelation 8:3 further illustrates this:

👉🏾 “Another angel came and stood at the altar, holding a golden censer; much incense was given to him, so that he might add it to the prayers of all the saints on the golden altar before the throne.”

From this verse, we understand that angels represent the prayers of the faithful. They carry our prayers to God, which is the very essence of intercession. In other words, an angel conveying our prayers to God shows us that angels act as intermediaries, presenting our petitions before Him.

text.text: The Intercession of Angels in the Babylonian Captivity

text:
During the Israelites’ captivity in Babylon, the angel of the Lord made a clear plea on their behalf. This is recorded in the Scriptures:

👉🏾 “And the angel of the Lord answered and said, O Lord God of hosts, how long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, with which thou hast had indignation these seventy years?” (Zechariah 1:12)

Here, the angel pleads for God’s mercy on His people.

👉🏾 “And the Lord answered the angel that talked with me with good and comforting words.” (Zechariah 1:13)

What does this “good and comforting word” mean? It points to mercy. The angel could not receive true comfort until God’s mercy was assured. And indeed, the Lord revealed His response through the angel:

👉🏾 “Therefore thus says the Lord: I will return to Jerusalem with mercy; my house will be built in it, and a line will be stretched out over Jerusalem,” says the Lord of hosts. “And you shall say, ‘Thus says the Lord of hosts: My cities shall again be satisfied with good; and the Lord will again comfort Zion and choose Jerusalem.’” (Zechariah 1:16–17)

The angel’s role was to convey God’s message to the people: “Proclaim this: ‘Thus says the Lord of hosts…’”


Therefore, in the Orthodox Tewahedo understanding, the holy angels are truly our intercessors. They carry our prayers before God, ask for mercy, and participate in the ministry of reconciliation, reminding us of God’s loving care and the unseen help that surrounds every faithful believer.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings ,we greet you with the peace and blessing of God. Today, based on the above-mentioned topic, we have prepared this important teaching and encourage you to read and learn from it with devotion

✍🏾
The phrase Negere Mariam (ነገረ ማርያም) is derived from two words:

— meaning “to speak,” “to declare,” or “to reveal.” It refers to a divine revelation or a sacred teaching.

👉🏾

- the name of our Holy Mother, the Virgin Mary.

Therefore, Negere Mariam means “The Revelation (or Story) of Mary.” It is a spiritual teaching through which we learn the mystery that God willingly revealed to humankind through our Mother, the Holy Virgin Mary.

The teaching concerning our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, is vast and profound. It cannot be contained within one message, Just as it is impossible to measure or finish the Nile River with a spoon, it is also impossible to complete the teaching about our Holy Mother, the Virgin Mary.Therefore, in this lesson, we will highlight only three main points:

✍🏾

text.text: The Genealogy of the Holy Virgin Mary

text:
God is holy itself, and every person, place, or thing in which He dwells becomes holy.

Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, is called holy because she was found worthy to be the dwelling place of God. She is counted among the saints whom God made pure, and therefore, she is rightfully called Holy Mary

The name Mary is believed to be derived from the Hebrew word Mariham, which means “the mother of many.”

Just as Abraham means “the father of many nations” (Genesis 17:5), so also Mary is “the mother of many,” for through her, all who believe in Christ become children of God.

In the teachings of our Church Fathers, the name Mary has several deep meanings:

text.text: a. The Way to the Kingdom of Heaven

text: Mary is called the Way to the Kingdom of Heaven because through her, the Savior of the world was born. All the descendants of Adam were reconciled and returned to their former glory through Jesus Christ, who took flesh and blood from her. Without faith in her intercession, it is impossible to enter the Kingdom of Heaven.

Our Lady’s parents were once despised by people because of their barrenness, yet her birth brought them honor, grace, and joy. In the fullness of time, she became the grace and wealth of all believers who recognize her intercession and believe in her promise.

As the Lord said on the Cross, “Behold your mother” (John 19:27), she became the spiritual mother of all the faithful.Abba Hiriakos praises her in the Holy Liturgy, saying:

“When Adam was expelled from Paradise, you were his hope.”

Through her, Adam, who was separated from God’s grace and subjected to the devil, regained grace and became the treasure of the Holy Spirit.

text.text: c. Perfect in Body and Soul

text: Since God is perfect in His divine nature, He chose the Virgin Mary in His divine wisdom to be the vessel of the Incarnation. Therefore, He made her perfect pure in body and perfect in soul  to become the Mother of the Word made flesh.

text.text: d. Above All Creatures and Below the Creator

text:
God placed the Virgin Mary above all angels and saints. The angels were exalted by grace, but Mary was exalted not only by grace and mercy, but also because God the Son took flesh, blood, and soul from her.

That is why the Archangel Gabriel said,

“Blessed are you among women” (Luke 1:28).

Hence, the Virgin Mary is greater than all created beings, standing above all creatures yet beneath the Creator.

As a household has a mother and father, all Christians who believe in Christ have the Virgin Mary as their spiritual Mother. Her Son Emmanuel is the Head of the household of believers, and she is the Mother who nurtures all who follow Him.

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings, we greet you with the peace and blessings of God.Today, based on the above-mentioned topic, we bring you this important lesson. We ask you all to read it carefully and learn from the examples of the saints and prophets who wept before God.

✍🏾

text.text: Our Lord Jesus Christ and His Tears

text:
In his Gospel, Saint John records the death of Lazarus:

“When Mary came to Jesus and saw Him, she fell at His feet and said, ‘Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.’ When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, He was deeply moved in spirit and troubled. ‘Where have you laid him?’ He asked. They said, ‘Lord, come and see.’ And Jesus wept.”(John 11:32–35)

✍🏾 Jesus wept to show His full humanity perfect in both soul and body. He wept with Mary and the mourners to teach us that God comforts those who grieve. He wept to show that those who sow in the Spirit must also sow in sorrow. And yet, He also revealed His divinity by raising Lazarus, showing that He is God, the source of life.

✍🏾 Our Lord and Savior also taught that we should not only mourn our own sins but the sins of others. When He approached the city of Jerusalem, He wept over it. The Evangelist Luke writes:

“As He drew near, He saw the city and wept over it, saying, ‘If you had known, even you, on this day, the things that make for your peace but now they are hidden from your eyes. For the days will come upon you when your enemies will build a rampart around you, surround you, and close you in on every side. They will dash you and your children to the ground, and they will not leave in you one stone upon another, because you did not know the time of your visitation.’”
(Luke 19:41–44)

Through this, our Lord gave us a living example of righteous mourning how it is fitting to weep for the sins of His people.

✍🏾The Apostle Paul also reminds us that while our Lord was in the flesh, He offered prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears for all humanity:

“In the days of His flesh, He offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears to the One who could save Him from death, and He was heard because of His reverent submission. Although He was a Son, He learned obedience through what He suffered; and being made perfect, He became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him, called by God a high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.”(Hebrews 5:7–10)

If He, who was without sin, wept for our sins, how much more ought we, who have sinned against Him, to weep for our own sins and turn to Him in true repentance?

✍🏾

The Prophet Joel encourages us:

“Now, therefore,” says the Lord, “turn to Me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning.”(Joel 2:12)

We are called to turn from our sins with genuine sorrow and heartfelt repentance.

The wise Solomon also teaches the value of mourning and humility:

“It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting, for that is the end of all men, and the living shall lay it to heart. Sorrow is better than laughter, for a sad countenance makes the heart wise.”
(Ecclesiastes 7:2–3)

Those who weep for their sins on earth and fail to repent will face sorrow in heaven. Our Lord warned:

“The Son of Man will send forth His angels, and they will gather out of His kingdom all things that cause sin and all who practice iniquity, and will cast them into the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”(Matthew13:41–42)

Dear followers of the Orthodox faith  we greet you with the peace of God. Today we present to you an important teaching for your spiritual growth on the topic of the intercession of our Holy Virgin Mary. May all who read and learn from it be strengthened in faith and understanding.

✍🏾

The word intercession means supplication or pleading on behalf of another.

It is a prayer offered by one person for the sake of another. In the Orthodox Church, one of the main forms of prayer is intercessory prayer a prayer made for the benefit of another soul.
(Source: Desta Tekle Weld, p. 775)

For example, when a person offends or wrongs a friend, he may be too ashamed or afraid to approach that friend directly. Out of reverence and humility, he sends another someone trusted and loved by the offended person to reconcile him.

In the same way, we sinners, having offended God through our sins, approach Him through the intercession of His beloved saints. We ask them to plead for mercy on our behalf. Above all, we seek the intercession of Our Lady, the Blessed Virgin Mary, the Mother of God, who has the highest favor before Him.

✍🏾

There are three parts involved in the mystery of intercession:

1. The Intercessor (The one who prays for another)

2. The Interceded (The one who receives the prayers)

3.The Beneficiary (The sinner who asks for intercession)

Intercession is an act of humility and love. It reflects the compassionate nature of the saints. The righteous stand before God, continually praying for the salvation of the world.
Through their prayers, our Lord Jesus Christ grants mercy and forgiveness to those who repent.

The saints’ intercession often involves a willingness to give their own lives for the sake of sinners:

“And Moses returned to the Lord and said, ‘Alas, this people has sinned a great sin, and have made for themselves gods of gold. Yet now, if You will forgive their sin but if not, blot me, I pray, out of Your book which You have written.’”
(Exodus 32:31–32)

Likewise, King David prayed for his people:

“Did I not command the people to be numbered? I am the one who has sinned and done evil; but what have these sheep done? O Lord my God, let Your hand be on me and my father’s house, but not on Your people.”(1 Chronicles 21:17)

In the New Testament, the Apostle Paul expressed the same deep love:

“For I could wish that I myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh.”(Romans 9:1–3)

From these examples, we learn that the saints intercede with sacrificial love, standing before God on behalf of humanity.

✍🏾

The one who receives intercession is God Himself the Creator of all things, “by whom all things were made.”(John 1:3)

He is one God in three persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit one Lordship, one power, one glory, one divine will.
It is this one God who hears the prayers of His saints and fulfills His will through their intercession.

When we say that the saints intercede, we do not mean that they are more merciful than God or that He is unwilling to forgive.
God’s mercy is infinite, and the intercession of the saints is a revelation of that very mercy. Their prayers manifest the depth of God’s compassion toward creation.

✍🏾

Those who benefit from intercession are we sinners, living on earth, confessing our sins and seeking forgiveness.
However, to receive the fruit of intercession, repentance is necessary.

The Israelites, when they were in Babylonian captivity, said to the prophet Jeremiah:

“May the Lord be a true and faithful witness between us if we do not do all that the Lord your God sends you to tell us. Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the Lord our  God.”(Jeremiah 42:2–6)

This shows that repentance and obedience are required for intercession to bear fruit.

text.text: Intercession as a Gift from God

text:
The ability to intercede is itself a divine gift.
God chose and appointed His saints as intercessors for humanity.
This is shown in His words to Abimelech concerning Abraham:

“Now therefore, restore the man’s wife; for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for you, and you shall live.”(Genesis 20:7)

Thus, the saints are instruments of God’s mercy, and through their prayers, we receive grace and forgiveness.

✍🏾

text.text: The Intercession of the Holy Virgin Mary

text:
Among all the saints, the intercession of the Blessed Virgin Mary holds a unique and exalted place.
She is the Mother of God (Theotokos), full of grace, chosen before all ages to bear the Word of Life.

Because of her purity, humility, and divine motherhood, she continually stands before her Son, praying for the salvation of the world.
Her intercession is powerful because it springs from perfect love and obedience to God.

As the Church teaches:

“Through the intercession of our Lady, the gates of mercy are opened;

through her prayers, sinners are reconciled with their Creator.”

Intercession is a sacred mystery that reveals both the humility of the saints and the mercy of God.
We are called to honor the saints, seek their prayers, and imitate their faith and love.

Above all, let us remember the constant and motherly intercession of the Holy Virgin Mary, who pleads unceasingly for all who call upon her name with faith and repentance.

May her intercession guide us toward repentance, mercy, and eternal life in Christ our God.
Amen.

Because of her purity, humility, and divine motherhood, she continually stands before her Son, praying for the salvation of the world.
Her intercession is powerful because it springs from perfect love and obedience to God.

As the Church teaches:

“Through the intercession of our Lady, the gates of mercy are opened;

through her prayers, sinners are reconciled with their Creator.”

Conclusion

Intercession is a sacred mystery that reveals both the humility of the saints and the mercy of God.
We are called to honor the saints, seek their prayers, and imitate their faith and love.

Above all, let us remember the constant and motherly intercession of the Holy Virgin Mary, who pleads unceasingly for all who call upon her name with faith and repentance.

May her intercession guide us toward repentance, mercy, and eternal life in Christ our God.
Amen.

The Geʿez word for alms means gift, offering, or act of mercy.
As a Christian virtue, almsgiving must be done with faith and humility.

There are two main forms of almsgiving:

👉🏾Monetary offerings given in the Church.

👉🏾Material aid such as food, clothing, or shelter provided to those in need.

As faithful Christians, we are called to:

👉🏾Feed the hungry,

👉🏾Give drink to the thirsty,

👉🏾Clothe the naked, and

👉🏾Comfort the afflicted.

👉🏾 God gives with those who give,

👉🏾 He receives with those who receive,

👉🏾 Through both giving and receiving,

👉🏾 Compassion and understanding are established among people.

Wealth is given to the rich not for pride, but so that they may extend help to those who are less fortunate. In this way, God uses one person’s abundance to heal another’s need, teaching humanity to share in divine love.

✍🏾 Blatten Geta Hiruy Welde silase explains almsgiving in this way:

“almsgiving means giving money for daily food and yearly clothing to the needy; it also includes giving counsel to those who lack wisdom and offering education to those in need. This too is charity.”(Goha tsibah, p. 24)

Thus, true almsgiving is not limited to money or possessions. It is every act of love, guidance, and knowledge given freely for the sake of another, with faith that God Himself is present in both the giver and the receiver.

When you give to a person in need, you are giving directly to God.

✍🏾 “He who is kind to the poor lends to the Lord, and He will reward him for what he has done.”
— Proverbs 19

✍🏾

Almsgiving is a holy trust that the wise place in the hands of God.
When you give to the poor, you are not losing, but entrusting your gift to the Lord, who will surely repay in due time.

True almsgiving is not only about money.It includes every act of help and mercy:

👉🏾Strengthening the weak with your strength,

👉🏾Guiding the ignorant with your knowledge,

👉🏾Supporting the needy with your skills.

👉🏾Such deeds are all forms of almsgiving before God.

The Holy Scriptures repeat the command to care for the poor:

“You shall open wide your hand to your poor brother, for the poor will never cease from the land.” Deuteronomy 15:11

“If your brother becomes poor and weak, support him as a stranger and a sojourner.” Leviticus 25:35

The Most High, through His prophets, declared that He loves almsgiving more than sacrifice.

“Is not this the fast that I have chosen to share your bread with the hungry, to bring the poor to your house, and to clothe the naked when you see them?” Isaiah 58:6–7

Even Saint John the Baptist taught that repentance must bear fruit through almsgiving:

“He who has two tunics should share with the one who has none, and he who has food should do likewise.” Luke 3:11

✍🏾

A true Christian gives not from ownership, but from stewardship.
Everything we have is from God, and we give from what belongs to Him.

Almsgiving is a pillar of Christian life, a key that opens mercy.
But many hearts are bound by the love of money, which the Apostle calls the root of all evil.

We often think almsgiving means dropping a few coins into a stranger’s hand, yet real almsgiving flows from faith and compassion.

Our Lord warns that the act must be free from hypocrisy and vain praise.Those who give to be seen by men already have their reward on earth.

text:
The one who listens to the cry of the poor and answers with mercy will find mercy when in need.
Almsgiving becomes a shelter in the day of trouble.

“Blessed is he who considers the poor; the Lord will deliver him in the day of trouble.” - Psalm 41:1–2

“Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it.” Ecclesiastes 11:1

✍🏾

How can one throw bread upon water and find it again?
This is the mystery of faith.

Casting your bread upon the waters means giving your alms to those in need.

Finding it after many days means receiving your eternal reward in the Kingdom of Heaven.

So, give your alms quietly, without display or boasting.
Do not give to be seen or praised.
As it is written:

“When your brother becomes poor, strengthen him.” Leviticus 25:35
“You shall not harden your heart nor shut your hand from your poor brother.” - Deuteronomy 15:7

✍🏾

He who gives in secret will be rewarded openly by God.
Almsgiving purifies sin, opens the gates of mercy, and brings grace both in this world and the next.
Every coin, every meal, every act of kindness given in the fear of God becomes a prayer rising to heaven.

✍🏾

Those who fail to give alms  or give carelessly and without compassion  will lose many blessings. In the end, they will face punishment just as those who refuse to give at all.

One of the sins that draws a curse upon a person is the lack of mercy toward the poor.

👉🏾The Prophet teaches

“He who does not remember to give alms sends misfortune upon himself and upon the poor.”

To ignore the suffering of the needy is to close one’s heart to God Himself.

By giving alms, a person imitates the action of his Creator, who gives freely and continually to all His creatures.

✍🏾A person who is capable of working should not depend on others’ charity. Instead, he should strive with his own hands and help others when possible.

👉🏾Almsgiving is not weakness; it is participation in God’s mercy.

👉🏾Almsgiving saves from evil.

👉🏾It atones for sins.
Just as water extinguishes fire, so alms extinguish sin.

This teaching has been preserved from the ancient fathers of the Church, for mercy toward others calls down mercy from heaven.

👉🏾Saint Yohannes Afewerk reminds the faithful:

“You who say, ‘I have given many times, it is enough’ do you not eat morning and evening? Then give morning and evening also! Do you not see that the poor are like yourself?”

True almsgiving is continual, like daily bread. Compassion is not to be rationed.

Almsgiving is given so that, by doing good to others, we may receive good things from God.

“Give, and it will be given to you.”Matthew 10:8
“God loves a cheerful giver.” - 2 Corinthians 9:7–12

Many were saved through the grace of almsgiving.

Even King Manasseh, when afflicted by his enemies, was delivered from their punishment through his acts of mercy.

The holy apostles, following the will and commandments of the Lord, taught the same truth:

“It is more blessed to give than to receive.” - Acts 20:35

Almsgiving must be done with love and sincerity, not as an act of pride or public display.
Saint James warns:

“To him who knows to do good and does not do it, it is sin.” James 4:17

Therefore, let every act of giving spring from the heart.

Not all who give are pleasing to God, for He examines the heart and conscience, not the outward action.

Giving clothes, shoes, or money is not enough if the heart remains proud.

The Lord who “searches the heart and the kidneys” knows whether our deeds are born from compassion or from vanity.

text.text: The Gospel of Matthew warns every believer:

text:
✍🏾“Be careful not to do your alms before men, to be seen by them... When you do your alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing... and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.”  Matthew 6:1–4

This command pierces straight to the heart of human vanity. Almsgiving is not performance; it is communion with God through mercy.

Every Christian act is meant to rise from faith. Without faith, even generosity turns hollow.

When one gives to be seen, the heart divides. Pride takes half, doubt takes the rest, and God receives nothing.

“We must give what we give with all our heart.”

True almsgiving is not measured by amount, but by purity of intention.
If the heart seeks human recognition, the gift becomes contaminated with self-interest.


✍🏾The Lord calls this kind of charity hypocrisy, because it hides pride behind kindness. The world praises such givers; heaven weeps for them.

✍🏾Some people parade their generosity before the cameras and crowds. They announce their gifts to the poor like a trumpet blast.
But Scripture warns:

“Do not blow a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do… that they may be praised by men.”

👉🏾This is not humility,  Their reward ends where the applause stops.

👉🏾The Church teaches that public almsgiving done for praise is like pouring water into sand: it vanishes without fruit.

✍🏾Even those who sincerely wish to help the poor must examine the spirit behind their actions.
If their lives oppose the law of God, their giving becomes a contradiction one hand offers mercy while the other hand sins.

Such people “give to the poor with one hand while breaking the commandments with the other.”

Their act may relieve the body of the needy, but it cannot sanctify the giver.

True almsgiving flows from a life of faith, obedience, and repentance.
It is not a single act of kindness, but a habit of mercy rooted in the Gospel.

The faithful give quietly, pray constantly, and trust that God alone will see and reward.
Such giving does not destroy the giver through pride, but sanctifies both the giver and the receiver.

As the Fathers teach:

“He who gives with love, gives Christ Himself; and he who receives with gratitude, receives Christ.”

If their lives oppose the law of God, their giving becomes a contradiction one hand offers mercy while the other hand sins.

Such people “give to the poor with one hand while breaking the commandments with the other.”

Their act may relieve the body of the needy, but it cannot sanctify the giver.

True almsgiving flows from a life of faith, obedience, and repentance.
It is not a single act of kindness, but a habit of mercy rooted in the Gospel.

The faithful give quietly, pray constantly, and trust that God alone will see and reward.
Such giving does not destroy the giver through pride, but sanctifies both the giver and the receiver.

As the Fathers teach:

“He who gives with love, gives Christ Himself; and he who receives with gratitude, receives Christ.”

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

text:
When the angel Gabriel greeted our Lady, he said,

“Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.” (Luke 1:30)

This means that she was granted honor, favor, and the divine power of intercession.
Therefore, our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, is trusted to intercede for humanity.

She is the pure dove of Noah, preserved by God when the world was destroyed by the flood that punished sin.

Through her purity and obedience, she became the Mother of Mercy, who opens the door of compassion for all who are bound by the chains of sin and seek forgiveness through her intercession.

(From the book “Hail Mary,” Interpretation of the Gospel of Luke)


One of the clearest passages in the Holy Scriptures that reveals the power of our Lady’s intercession is the story of the Wedding at Cana of Galilee, written by the beloved Evangelist Saint John.

At this wedding, our Lord Jesus Christ was present with His Mother and His disciples.

“When the wine ran out, the Mother of Jesus said to Him, ‘They have no wine.’” (John 2:3)

Our compassionate Mother quickly understood the sorrow of the bride and groom.
In the twinkling of an eye, she interceded on their behalf just as the Prophet Isaiah prophesied,

"swift cloud…” (Isaiah 19:1)

👉🏾This “swift cloud” symbolizes the Virgin Mary, who hastens to help those in distress.
At that crucial moment, she arrived as a merciful helper, saving the bride and groom from humiliation.

✍🏾Her intercession moved her Son, our Lord and God, Jesus Christ, to perform His first miracle, turning water into wine thus revealing His divine glory and affirming the power of His Mother’s intercession for all who believe.

✍🏾This prompt and merciful intercession of our Lady is beautifully described by Blessed Abune Gorgorios, who wrote:

“Our Lady, the Virgin Mary, is a compassionate Mother who quickly understands the problems of people and presents them to her Son.”(History of the Ethiopian Church, by His Holiness Abune Gorgorios)

Our Lady, who immediately perceived the need at the wedding, did not approach her Son with pride or command , but with deep humility.

She did not say, “My Son,” nor did she remind Him, “I am Your Mother.”Instead, she simply and humbly said,

“They have no wine.” (John 2:3)

How wonderful is this humility and compassion!Her Son, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, heard her plea, and by His divine power turned the water into wine performing His first miracle at the wedding in Cana.

Through this event, the intercession of our Holy Mother was revealed clearly and widely, teaching all believers that her prayers are powerful and filled with mercy.

Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, has been granted an eternal covenant by God.
Her intercession and maternal care for the faithful have never ceased and will continue forever.

To this day, she stands beside her Son as our ever-present helper and intercessor, praying for mercy upon the world, guiding the repentant, comforting the sorrowful, and leading all who trust in her to the love of her beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox faith  we greet you with the peace of God. Today we present to you an important teaching for your spiritual growth on the topic of "You are misled because you do not know the Scriptures nor the power of God.”(Matthew 22:29).May all who read and learn from it be strengthened in faith and understanding.

✍🏾 Our Lord Jesus Christ said to the Sadducees who denied the resurrection of the dead because they misunderstood the Scriptures 

👉🏾“You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.” (Matthew 22:29)

✍🏾 The Holy Scriptures, together with the teachings of the blessed Fathers and holy scholars, unanimously praise the Virgin Mary as “The Mother of God,” “The Faithful One who gave birth to God,” and “The Mother of our nature.”

✍🏾Whoever truly understands the mystery of the Holy Scriptures will recognize that these praises reveal the divine wisdom through which the Lord accomplished our salvation.

text.text: About the Glory of the Virgin Mary

text:
✍🏾The pure apostolic Gospel that our Holy Church teaches especially concerning the Resurrection and Ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ, which restored the fallen nature of humanity  reveals the goodness of God, the greatness of His gift to mankind, and the depth of His unsearchable grace.

✍🏾Those who lack understanding of the mystery of salvation, and who do not grasp the glory of the Virgin Mary, find it difficult to comprehend that she became the cause and instrument of our salvation the support and comfort of our nature.

✍🏾In their ignorance and pride, some belittle the saving role of our holy Mother, the Virgin Mary, and disregard her divine honor. Yet the Orthodox Tewahedo Church, founded upon apostolic faith, continuously glorifies her and remembers her intercession with gratitude and love.

✍🏾We understand that those who are ignorant of the doctrine of salvation and who do not recognize the glory of the Virgin Mary find it difficult to comprehend that she became the cause and instrument of our salvation.

✍🏾In their ignorance and arrogance, they belittle the holy mystery of our salvation, which was accomplished through the obedience of the Virgin Mary  the foundation and support of our nature.

✍🏾On the other hand, they easily accept and understand how death entered the world through the disobedience of Eve, yet they fail to understand how life entered through the obedience of Mary. They are mistaken and deceived because they do not know the Holy Scriptures.

✍🏾However, our Orthodox Tewahedo Church, which has received the true faith handed down from the Holy Apostles, continually remembers and honors our Lady, the Virgin Mary, as the cause of our salvation in all her prayers and hymns.

✍🏾Just as death came into the world through Eve’s disobedience and transgression of the divine law, life and salvation came into the world through the obedience and faith of our Holy Mother, the Virgin Mary. Therefore, we give thanks to her as the support and foundation of our human nature.

✍🏾 If our people  who struggle to understand the Word of God because they have not received it from a pure and living source would deeply meditate upon the central theme of the Holy Scriptures, which is “the support of our nature” (Christ born of the Virgin), they would surely return to the true faith and righteousness of our fathers.

Dear followers of the Orthodox faith, greetings to you in the name of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. May the peace and mercy of God be with you all. Today, we continue our spiritual lesson on the topic: “Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary Her Intercession. May all who read and reflect on this teaching receive wisdom and spiritual growth.

✍🏾The Covenant of Intercession Granted to the Virgin Mary

God, who made a covenant with His chosen ones, saying, “I have made a covenant with my chosen” (Psalm 89:3), granted a unique and holy covenant to the Virgin Mary a covenant of spiritual motherhood and mercy.

According to the Snksar of Zewereha (Tikimt), God promised that blessings would be given to all who remember her, call upon her name, or even give a cup of cold water to the poor and needy in her honor.

The prophet David, by divine revelation, testified to this covenant, saying:“The queen stands at your right hand, clothed in gold and adorned with splendor.” (Psalm 45:9)

This means that the Holy Virgin stands always at the right hand of her Son, interceding for us with motherly compassion.

✍🏾We, the children of the Church, constantly call upon her with reverence, saying:
“Pure Virgin Mary, the faithful Mother of God, intercessor of mercy for mankind pray for us to your beloved Son, that He may forgive us our sins.”
These words echo the beautiful prayer of Saint Ephrem, found in Wudasie Maryam Ze’arb (The Praise of Mary of Wednesday).

Likewise, Abba Giorgis Ze Gascha prayed:

“O Holy Virgin Mary, I trust in you that you may save me from hidden suffering and from every visible danger in this world, and in the world to come, from the gnashing of teeth and the torment of hell. I do not trust in chariots nor in horses, but in you and your Son.” (Arganon Ze’ehud)

Indeed, the Virgin never abandons those who trust in her intercession.

✍🏾

text.text: The First Miracle through the Intercession of the Virgin

text:
The first miracle that our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ performed through the intercession of His Blessed Mother took place at the wedding in Cana of Galilee, as recorded by the Apostle Saint John in the second chapter of his Gospel.

✍🏾

signifies sweetness or fragrance a fitting description of the mystery of this holy event. In the history of the Church, Cana was one of the districts of Galilee. Though its name might sound ordinary, it became a place of divine glory, for there our Lord, the King of Heaven, revealed His power through the intercession of His Holy Mother.

literally means a sign something that surpasses the laws of nature and the limits of created power. A miracle is an act of God that reveals His divine authority. Every work of God, from the creation of the world to the redemption of mankind, bears the mark of wonder. This is why He is called El Shaddai, the Almighty.

God, in His great love for His creation, also granted His chosen servants the grace to perform miracles for the salvation and strengthening of His people.

In the Old Testament, Moses divided the sea, brought down manna from heaven, and struck the rock to bring forth water. Elijah called down fire from heaven and raised the dead. Truly, the entire Holy Bible is a book of miracles a living testimony to the power and mercy of God.

In the New Testament, our Lord Jesus Christ performed countless miracles and bestowed the gift of miraculous works upon His apostles.

“Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils.” (Matthew 10:8)

“These signs shall follow those who believe.” (Mark 16:17)
The apostles fulfilled these words through the power of the Holy Spirit (Acts 3:6; 5:12; 8:6; 9:33–43; 14:8; 19:11).

text.text: ✍🏾The Miracle at Cana – The Beginning of Christ’s Manifested Works

text:
👉🏾Saint John writes: “This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested His glory.” (John 2:11)

This statement does not imply that Christ had never performed a miracle before, but that it was the first miracle after His public revelation and baptism. According to Church tradition, our Lord was baptized on Tir 11, returned from His fasting on Yekatit 21 and attended the wedding at Cana on Yekatit 25.

👉🏾For liturgical harmony, the Church celebrates the Feast of Cana of Galilee on Tir 12, following the Feast of the Epiphany, to signify the connection between the sanctifying waters of baptism and the sanctifying wine of the miracle.

✍🏾In Cana of Galilee, the bridegroom was Dokim, and the groom’s father was Joachim, the uncle of the Apostle Saint Nathanael. To sanctify this marriage, the Lord Jesus Christ was invited together with His Blessed Mother, the Holy Virgin Mary, and His faithful apostles.

✍🏾Though our Lord and His Mother lived in holiness and abstained from worldly feasting, they attended the wedding out of love and humility—to bless the hosts, to reveal the dignity of marriage, and to manifest the mystery of divine joy within the union of man and woman. Their presence alone made that gathering sacred.

✍🏾When the wedding began, the Lord sat in the middle of the tabernacle, the Virgin at His right hand, Saint John at His left, and the rest of the apostles seated on either side.

As the celebration continued, the food and wine symbols of earthly joy were suddenly depleted. The hosts were distressed.

✍🏾While others panicked, the Holy Virgin ever watchful and filled with mercy perceived their need. The people, knowing her goodness, turned to her with quiet hope, saying among themselves, “intercede for us with God.”
Hearing their silent plea, the Mother of God rose and approached her Son with gentleness and reverence. She did not accuse, command; she merely presented the need of them, saying:
“They have no wine.” (John 2:3)

✍🏾These few words hold deep spiritual meaning. They reveal her compassion, her awareness of human suffering, and her role as intercessor between God and mankind. The Virgin’s heart could not bear to see others fall into shame or distress.

✍🏾The Mystery of the Wine and the Intercession of Our Lady

text:
✍🏾In the mystery of faith, the wine represents love, the Holy Word, and the precious Blood of our Lord. When the Lord said to His mother, “Woman, what have I to do with you? My hour has not yet come,” He was not rejecting her, but speaking in divine wisdom.

✍🏾The Lord waited until the wine jars were completely empty signifying the end of the old covenant and the beginning of the new. It is said that Since Judas had gone out, the Lord waited until he returned, so that he could not present the miracle as a justification for his evil.”

✍🏾When the Lord said, “I will give you wine My holy blood on the hill of Calvary,” He revealed that His true hour of offering had not yet come. Some, misunderstanding this passage, pretend that the Lord belittled His Mother. But this is false. The commandment says, “Honor your father and your mother” (Exodus 20), and our Savior perfectly fulfilled it.

Therefore, when the Holy Virgin the Lady of Light said to the servants, “Do whatever He tells you” (John 2:5), she was showing both faith and obedience. Then the Lord filled the six jars with water and changed them into wine, performing His first miracle. The joy of the feast was restored, and the steward who symbolizes our father Abraham was amazed at the sweetness of the new wine.

In this, the intercession of the Virgin Mary and the power of our Savior were revealed together. Through her faith, mercy was poured out upon the people.


✍🏾

Let us, therefore, honor the great gift we have received through her. Let us cling to her motherly intercession with faith and humility. Through her prayers, may our sins be forgiven, our hearts purified, and our paths guided toward the Kingdom of Heaven.

Dear followers of Orthodox teachings . we greet you in the name of God. Today, we share an important lesson on the blessedness of the meek, and we encourage you to read, reflect, and learn from it.

✍🏾

Who are the meek, and why are they called blessed? Many people misunderstand meekness, thinking it is a sign of weakness, ignorance, or passivity. This is entirely mistaken. In truth, the meek are wise, strong, and full of spiritual understanding.

Meekness is a sign of strength, maturity, and self-control. It manifests in two ways: spiritual meekness and personal meekness.

Spiritual meekness is rooted in the fear of God and the wisdom that comes from Him.

Personal meekness is related to moral competence, emotional maturity, social conduct, and knowledge. It includes patience with others, self-control in difficult times, humility in leadership, listening to others, and accepting when someone has a better idea.

While people who do not believe in God may exhibit personal meekness, our focus here is on spiritual meekness, the meekness that is blessed in the eyes of God.

✍🏾

Our Lord said, “Behold, I send you out as sheep in the midst of wolves; therefore be wise as serpents and harmless as doves” (Matthew 10:16). Spiritual meekness combines wisdom and humility. The Apostle James also teaches, “Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his good conduct his works in the meekness of wisdom” (James 3:13).

He further describes heavenly wisdom: “But the wisdom from above is first pure, then gentle, easy to be entreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without hypocrisy” (James 3:17). Thus, true meekness is a treasure, full of wisdom and spiritual insight.

✍🏾

The meek put God first in all things. They do this out of deep love for God and complete trust in Him. As the wise Solomon said, “In all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will direct your paths” (Proverbs 3:6), the meek place God first in every aspect of their lives. Our Lord also taught, “But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added to you” (Matthew 6:33). The meek prioritize the kingdom of God, trusting that everything else they need will be provided. In this perfect faith, they rely fully on God for all their needs. Jesus Christ said, “Blessed is everyone who does not stumble in Me” (Matthew 11:6; Luke 7:23), showing that His salvation is for those who believe meekly and wholeheartedly in Him.

Dear followers of Orthodox teachings . we greet you in the name of God. Today, we share an important lesson on the blessedness of the meek, and we encourage you to read, reflect, and learn from it.

✍🏾What Is Meekness?

Who are the meek, and why are they called blessed? Many people misunderstand meekness, thinking it is a sign of weakness, ignorance, or passivity. This is entirely mistaken. In truth, the meek are wise, strong, and full of spiritual understanding.

Meekness is a sign of strength, maturity, and self-control. It manifests in two ways: spiritual meekness and personal meekness.

Spiritual meekness is rooted in the fear of God and the wisdom that comes from Him.

Personal meekness is related to moral competence, emotional maturity, social conduct, and knowledge. It includes patience with others, self-control in difficult times, humility in leadership, listening to others, and accepting when someone has a better idea.

While people who do not believe in God may exhibit personal meekness, our focus here is on spiritual meekness, the meekness that is blessed in the eyes of God.

✍🏾The Meek Are Wise

Our Lord said, “Behold, I send you out as sheep in the midst of wolves; therefore be wise as serpents and harmless as doves” (Matthew 10:16). Spiritual meekness combines wisdom and humility. The Apostle James also teaches, “Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his good conduct his works in the meekness of wisdom” (James 3:13).

He further describes heavenly wisdom: “But the wisdom from above is first pure, then gentle, easy to be entreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without hypocrisy” (James 3:17). Thus, true meekness is a treasure, full of wisdom and spiritual insight.

✍🏾Characteristics of the Meek

1. The Meek Put God First:

The meek put God first in all things. They do this out of deep love for God and complete trust in Him. As the wise Solomon said, “In all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will direct your paths” (Proverbs 3:6), the meek place God first in every aspect of their lives. Our Lord also taught, “But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added to you” (Matthew 6:33). The meek prioritize the kingdom of God, trusting that everything else they need will be provided. In this perfect faith, they rely fully on God for all their needs. Jesus Christ said, “Blessed is everyone who does not stumble in Me” (Matthew 11:6; Luke 7:23), showing that His salvation is for those who believe meekly and wholeheartedly in Him.

Continues 👇🏾

text:
They are content because they understand that everything comes from God, and they do not covet what others possess. Saint Paul teaches, “I do not say this because I am in need. I have learned to be content with whatever I have. I know how to be abased, and I know how to abound. In everything and in all circumstances, I have learned both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me” (Philippians 4:11-13). This teaching guides the meek in their daily life, helping them live joyfully, thankful for God’s provision, and free from greed or insatiable desire.

They also follow the wisdom of Saint Paul: “But godliness is great gain when combined with contentment, for we brought nothing into the world, and we cannot carry anything out. If we have food and clothing, we will be content with that” (1 Timothy 6:6-8). Likewise, they live by the principle in Hebrews 13:5: “Keep your life free from the love of money, and be content with what you have, for He Himself has said, ‘I will never leave you nor forsake you’.”

Through such contentment, the meek demonstrate trust in God, simplicity of heart, and freedom from worldly attachment.

✍🏾

When someone wrongs them, the meek do not seek revenge, nor do they demand that God avenge them. Instead, they pray for forgiveness and trust God’s justice. They remember the divine promise: “The Lord will fight for you, and you shall hold your peace” (Exodus 14:14).

Saint Paul teaches: “Do not avenge yourselves, but rather give place to wrath; for it is written, ‘Vengeance is mine; I will repay, says the Lord’” (Romans 12:19). Likewise, Saint Peter instructs: “Do not repay evil for evil or insult for insult. On the contrary, bless, for to this you were called, that you may inherit a blessing” (1 Peter 3:9). The Apostle Paul also writes: “See that no one repays evil for evil to anyone, but always seek to do good to everyone” (1 Thessalonians 5:15).

Our Lord Jesus Christ Himself exemplified meekness in action: “When He was reviled, He did not revile in return; when He suffered, He did not threaten, but entrusted Himself to Him who judges righteously” (1 Peter 2:23).

Through such humility and trust, the meek demonstrate true spiritual strength, leaving justice in God’s hands and responding to evil with goodness.

text:
Dear followers of Orthodox teachings . we greet you in the name of God. Today, we share an important lesson on the blessedness of the meek, and we encourage you to read, reflect, and learn from it.

✍🏾

Out of sincere love, the meek place others before themselves. They are not a burden to anyone, nor do they cause others to stumble, but rather they carry one another’s burdens with patience and compassion. As Saint Paul teaches,

“Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.” (Galatians 6:2)

The meek honor and respect everyone, as it is written,

“Be kindly affectionate to one another with brotherly love; in honor preferring one another.” (Romans 12:10)

Saint Paul also says,

“We who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak, and not to please ourselves. Let each of us please his neighbor for his good, leading to edification.” (Romans 15:1–2)

Thus, the meek seek the good and happiness of others more than their own. In humility, they follow the command:

“Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit, but in humility count others better than yourselves. Let each of you look not only to his own interests, but also to the interests of others.” (Philippians 2:3–4)

Therefore, the meek do not act for their own advantage but strive for the benefit and salvation of their neighbors, fulfilling the perfect law of love taught by Christ.

✍🏾

text.text: The Meek Do Not Seek Earthly Glory

text:
The meek do not seek glory for themselves, but desire that God may be glorified in all they do. They are joyful when others are honored rather than themselves.
As our Lord taught in His Gospel:

“Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted.” (Matthew 23:12)

The meek guard their hearts against vain praise because they know that their true glory is stored up in heaven.
King Solomon also warns,

“It is not good to eat much honey; nor is it glorious to seek one’s own honor.” (Proverbs 25:27)

Our Lord, who is the perfect model of meekness, said:

“I do not accept glory from men.” (John 5:41)

“I do not seek My own glory; there is One who seeks it and judges.” (John 8:50)

“He who speaks on his own seeks his own glory; but he who seeks the glory of the One who sent him is true, and in him there is no unrighteousness.” (John 7:18)
“If I honor Myself, My honor is nothing; it is My Father who honors Me.” (John 8:54)

Thus, the meek glorify God in all things and refuse the empty praise of the world.

✍🏾

Meekness has been seen throughout all times and divine laws:

👉🏾 In the Law of the Heart

👉🏾 In the Law of the Torah

👉🏾 In the Law of the Gospel

In every generation, there have been many meek servants of God. The following examples are mentioned not to list all their righteous works, but to illustrate the spirit of meekness they lived by.

text:
Abel was a shepherd. After some time, he brought an offering to God from the firstborn of his flock and from their fat portions. Scripture says:

“And the Lord respected Abel and his offering, but He did not respect Cain and his offering. And Cain became very angry and killed his brother Abel.” (Genesis 4:1–25)

Abel’s meekness was shown first in offering to God what was pure and worthy. Secondly, he accepted death unjustly without complaint, being killed by his own brother out of envy.

Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ Himself mentioned Abel, saying:

“From the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar, truly I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation.” (Matthew 23:35)

The Apostle Saint Paul also testified to Abel’s meek faith, saying:

“By faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, through which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts; and through it he being dead still speaks.” (Hebrews 11:4)

The Elder Father Abba Hirykos  also compared the Virgin Mary to Abel, saying:

“You are the meekness of Abel, who was unjustly slain.”

✍🏾

Joseph, known for his purity and meekness, shared his dreams with his brothers. Out of jealousy, they threw him into a pit and later sold him into slavery. Yet, Joseph trusted in God and remained meek and faithful.

When tempted by Potiphar’s wife, he refused sin, saying he would not offend God. For this, he was falsely accused and imprisoned. But even there, God was with him. Through divine wisdom, Joseph interpreted Pharaoh’s dream, rose to great power, and saved Egypt from famine.

When his brothers who had sold him came seeking food, Joseph received them with gentleness and forgiveness.
In this, he became a perfect example of meekness, patience, and love.

Meekness is not weakness. It is the strength to remain humble, gentle, and forgiving even when wronged. The meek seek not their own glory but the glory of God. As the Lord Himself said,

“Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.” (Matthew 5:5)

text.text: The Value of Knowing and Living the Truth

text:
Knowing the truth is a precious gift. But what benefit is it to know the truth if one does not live according to it? For those who live by the truth, it brings true freedom and peace of heart (Jeremiah 6:16; Matthew 11:28).

Our Lord Jesus Christ said to the Jews who believed in Him:

“If you abide in My word, you are truly My disciples; and you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.”(John 8:31–32)

Therefore, if we believe that truth frees us from the slavery of sin, we must desire to hear and understand the truth directly from its divine source. Those who love the truth and seek it from God Himself are guided not by emotion, but by knowledge and faith. When the pure truth is revealed, it removes shame, ignorance, and sin, leading the soul to salvation and eternal life (Proverbs 11:9).

Relying on one’s own limited understanding or false teachings from others keeps a person enslaved to error. Indeed, knowledge and identity are closely connected what one believes shapes who one becomes.

True knowledge is only useful when it is put into practice. Therefore, when God reveals the truth, the wise make the right decision and act upon it. Those who accept the truth sincerely also recognize and correct their past mistakes without hesitation.

When the path of righteousness leading to eternal life is made clear, the heart must remain firm and unwaveringvfor the truth concerns eternal salvation.

This teaching reveals the divine truth about the Intercessor and the mystery of intercession for all who desire to walk toward eternal life—those who seek to know the truth from the Holy Bible alone, the one and living Word of God that has no alternative. Whoever learns and lives by this truth is freed from the bondage of sin and walks in the light of salvation.

✍🏾 In the first part of our lesson, we discussed in detail the meaning of the term “intercessor.” To refresh our memory, let us now recall its definition and see how “intercession” is divided according to the Word of God.

✍🏾

The word intercessor (amalaj)comes from the verb to intercede(mamaled), which means “to plead” or “to pray on behalf of another.” The act itself is called intercession. Thus, an intercessor is one who prays, pleads, or reconciles on behalf of others.

However, the word intercession (ማለደ)also carries another meaning “to rise early” or “to get up before dawn.” As it is written:

“And Abimelech rose early in the morning and called all his servants.” (Genesis 20:8)
“And Samuel rose early in the morning to meet Saul.” (1 Samuel 15:12)

Therefore, when the Scripture says, (

in Jeremiah 7:25, it does not refer to supplication, but to the idea of rising early that is, acting before it is too late. Likewise, in Psalm 119 where it says, “My eyes are open to pray, that I may meditate on Your word,” the meaning is to rise early to seek the Word of God, not merely to make a petition.

✍🏾

Although “intercession” generally means to make supplication, not all forms of intercession are the same. According to the Holy Scriptures, intercession is revealed in three primary forms:

1. The Intercession of Christ – Isaiah 53:1–12

2. The Intercession of People in the Flesh – 2 Corinthians 9:14

3. The Intercession of Bribery or False Appeal – Deuteronomy 10:16

The Holy Bible repeatedly and clearly speaks of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ as “He intercedes”. But it is fitting to ask: “Since Christ is God, to whom does He intercede?”

Accepting the Scriptural answer with humility and faith shows spiritual understanding.

text:
Dear faithful followers of the Orthodox teachings , we greet you in the peace and grace of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. Today, by the help of God, we present this important teaching for your reflection and spiritual growth.

✍🏾

When Jesus Christ was incarnate as Lord, He appeared in the flesh and showed humanity how a righteous man should obey his Lord. When He revealed Himself as God, He taught humanity how to worship Him rightly (Matt. 11:28; John 13:13).

✍🏾In this, He revealed that He would clothe humanity with the eternal garment of salvation. Through this act, He disclosed His plan to bring eternal life, to destroy the works of the devil, and to proclaim the good news of salvation to mankind (Gen. 3:15; Isa. 61:10). Christ also promised that He would perform this intercession Himself, without the help of anyone else, for it is His divine work that no one can share or interfere with.

👉🏾The teachings of the Old Testament are a shadow of the salvation that God accomplishes in the New Testament. “These are a shadow of the things to come, but the substance is of Christ” (Colossians 2:17).

✍🏾The message of Genesis 3:8-21 reveals that reconciliation true intercession can only be accomplished by God. As Jeremiah 50:34 states: “Their Redeemer is strong; the Lord of hosts is His name; He will plead their cause thoroughly, to give rest to the earth, and to discomfit the inhabitants of Babylon.” Likewise, the Advocate of our souls, mentioned in 1 John 2:1, is none other than the Lord God Himself.

✍🏾Since God redeems humanity from all sin, and He redeems according to His own will, He is fully for Himself and through Himself. As Scripture says: “For of Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be glory forever!” (Romans 11:36). All intercession and salvation belong to God alone.

text.text: The Word of God in Creation and Salvation

text:
As we read in Genesis, God, who created all things by His Word alone, used the same Word to seek and save humanity, who had fallen into the debt of eternal death (John 1:3). As it is written in Psalm 107:20, “He sent His Word and healed them, and saved them from their destruction” (see also Isa. 55:11-12).

✍🏾 “To save that which was lost” (Matt. 18:11) – In the New Testament, this saving Word was made flesh (John 1:14). When the Word became flesh, He was called the Son of God (Luke 1:35; Rev. 19:13).

👉🏾However, this incarnation was not simply to demonstrate that the Word could become flesh. Rather, as Scripture explains in Hebrews 9:22, “without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.” Therefore, He was called the Lamb of God, destined to be the perfect sacrifice for the forgiveness of sins for all humanity.

God Himself became the intercessor by appearing in the flesh while remaining fully God (1 Tim. 3:16).

✍🏾 As the Apostle Paul clearly wrote:

"God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and has committed to us the word of reconciliation" (2 Cor. 5:19-20).

While it is common for sinners to be reconciled through a human intercessor, God reconciled the world to Himself by His own authority. Therefore, the only intercessor confirmed by Scripture is Jesus Christ.

✍🏾

"It is Christ Jesus who died, rather, who is also raised from the dead, who is at the right hand of God, who also intercedes for us" (Rom. 8:34).

✍🏾 The Holy Word literally describes that He intercedes. It is not a human interpretation or metaphor. Therefore, to believe or say that “He is not an intercessor” or “Christ does not intercede” is to depart from the truth of God’s Word.

Christ gave the apostles the good news the message of reconciliation and entrusted them with the Word of reconciliation. Today, in all their messages, they continue to plead with believers to be reconciled to God (2 Cor. 5:19-20).

As Paul writes in Ephesians 2:14-16:

👉🏾"For He Himself is our peace, who has made both one, having abolished the law of commandments contained in ordinances, and has broken down the middle wall of hostility in His flesh, so as to create in Himself one new man from the two, thus making peace, and to reconcile both to God in one body, having killed the hostility by the cross."

Good news! The wall of hostility has been broken down in His flesh. Since no angel or human could accomplish this, only Christ could break the hostility through His flesh, shed His blood, and offer Himself as the perfect sacrifice for sinners (Matt. 26:26-27).

✍🏾For all descendants of Adam, Christ became the sin offering for humanity. He is the surety, the advocate, the intercessor, and the one who reconciles humanity with God, both on earth and in heaven.

And He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation upon His head; and He put on the garments of vengeance, and He girded Himself with zeal.”

✍🏾The phrase “He put on the garments of vengeance” indicates that God appeared in the flesh (1 Tim. 3:16) to take vengeance on the enemy and defeat sin and death, accomplishing salvation for humanity.

✍🏾

text.text: The Prophetic Symbol – The Bronze Serpent

text:
When Christ spoke of His crucifixion, He referred to the bronze serpent that Moses lifted up in the wilderness:

“As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up.”
(John 3:14)

In the time of Moses, the people sinned against God and were punished with fiery serpents. When they repented, God commanded Moses:

“Make a fiery serpent and set it on a pole, and everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live.”
(Numbers 21:8–9)

This was a divine foreshadowing of Christ’s crucifixion.

✍🏾

text.text: The Bronze Serpent: A Symbol of the Cross

text:
When the Lord of Hosts sent manna from heaven and brought forth water from the rock to feed Israel, He showed His mercy and power before His people. The Lord said, “I have fed you with manna.” Yet even after witnessing these great wonders, Israel doubted the Lord and spoke against Him. God would not have given them a table in a monastery or a cave, but rather in the wilderness, to reveal His greatness and to expose their unbelief.

The Lord commanded Moses to go down into the desert where there was no water. There, He caused manna to descend from heaven and water to flow from the rock for His people. But afterward, a serpent named Nefertari began to bite them, and many among Israel died.

Then the people came to Moses and confessed, saying,

“The mercy and kindness of the Lord do not depart, even when man errs. We have sinned against the Lord and against you. Pray to the Lord that He may take the serpents away from us.”

Moses prayed for the people, and the Lord commanded him, saying,

“Make for yourself a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole in the midst of the assembly. Whoever is bitten and looks upon it shall live.”

So Moses made a bronze serpent and lifted it up on a pole, and everyone who was bitten by the serpent was healed when he looked upon the bronze serpent (Numbers 21:4–9).

Continues 👇🏾

text:
This event was given to us by our holy fathers as an image and prophecy of the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.

👉🏾The land of Arwe (the serpent) represents the dominion of the devil

👉🏾The fiery serpent represents the Lord Jesus Christ.

👉🏾Just as there was poison in the serpent of the wilderness, there is sin in the devil.

👉🏾But in the fiery serpent that Moses lifted up, there was no poison—just as in our Lord there was no sin.

👉🏾The Lord Jesus Christ was crucified in the likeness of sinful flesh (Romans 8:3), though He Himself was without sin. In this way, the fiery serpent on the pole became a symbol of Christ lifted up on the Cross for the salvation of the world.

He fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah 53:12:

“He was numbered with the transgressors.”

Our Lord knew the parable and its meaning, and He revealed it to us, saying,

“As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have eternal life” (John 3:14–15).

✍🏾

text.text: The Crucifixion of Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ

text:
When Pilate said to the Jews, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” they replied, “Release Barabbas for us, but crucify Jesus who is called Christ.” Then Pilate declared before them, “I am innocent of the blood of this righteous man.” But the people answered, “His blood be upon us and upon our children.” So Pilate released Barabbas and delivered our Lord to be crucified (Matthew 27:23–26).

✍🏾

text.text: The Crown of Thorns and the Curse of Adam

text:
As recorded by the holy Father Yohannes Afework, when Christ was brought before the people, the archangels stood before Him with fear and trembling, saying,

“He who forgives sins is now judged among the princes.”

At the same time, the people of Israel condemned Christ, declaring,

“He must be crucified.” (John 19:2).

By wearing the crown of thorns, our Lord removed the curse that came upon Adam, when God said,

“The earth will bring forth thorns and thistles for you” (Genesis 3:18).

Through His suffering, He took upon Himself the curse of sin and restored humanity to blessing.

✍🏾

On Megabit 27, when our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ was crucified, the Creator of heaven and earth was lifted up upon the Cross. At that moment:

The sun was darkened,

The moon became as blood,

The stars fell from heaven,

The veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom,

The earth shook and the rocks were split,

The graves were opened, and many of the righteous rose from the dead (Matthew 27:45–52).


All creation trembled, for the Lord of glory, the One who formed Adam with His own hands, was crucified for the salvation of mankind.

As Father Yohannes Afework beautifully writes,

“The hands that created Adam were nailed to the Cross;
woe to the feet that walked in Paradise,
and woe to the feet that walked upon the earth.”

Through His holy Passion, He destroyed death by death and brought light to those who sat in darkness.

text:
According to the order of Demetrius, the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church commemorates the Crucifixion of our Lord Jesus Christ on Tikimt 27 every year, giving thanks for the redemption accomplished on the Cross.

On this same day, the Church also remembers Abune Meba Zion, the holy father who lived in the 15th century. When he prayed to the Lord, saying,

“Show me the sufferings You endured on the Friday of Your Passion,”
our Lord Jesus Christ revealed to him the full vision of His sufferings.

From that day forward, Abune Meba Zion lived in deep remembrance of the Passion of Christ. Out of holy compassion, he would strike his back with a whip and beat his head with a rod, meditating upon the thirteen sufferings of the Cross. He wept continually until he lost his sight.

But the Holy Virgin Mary, our compassionate Mother, appeared to him carrying a cup of light and anointed his eyes, restoring his sight. Because of this miraculous mercy, he is called “The Rod of Mary.”


Therefore, the 27th of Tikimt is a day of covenant and remembrance a day on which the faithful recall the suffering, death, and mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ and the covenant made with Abune Meba Zion.

On this holy day, the Church celebrates with reverence and gratitude, saying:

“By His Cross, He has exalted our fathers,
and by His Word, He has enlightened the righteous.”

Through the Cross, the world has received salvation, and through His suffering, we have received life.

May the blessings and intercession of Abune Meba Zion,
and the mercy of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ,
be upon us forever. Amen.

Dear followers of the Orthodox faith, we greet you with the peace and grace of God. Today, we share with you an important lesson on the virtue of meekness, based on the Holy Scriptures May you read it with understanding and apply it with humility in your lives.

✍🏾

text.text: The Great Prophet Moses – The Meekest Man on Earth

text:
One of the greatest examples of meekness in the Old Testament is the High Prophet Moses. The Holy Scripture testifies of him, saying,

“Now Moses was very meek, above all the men who were on the face of the earth.”(Numbers 12:3)

Although Moses was born among the Israelites and raised in Pharaoh’s palace, he did not boast of his royal upbringing. When God called him to deliver His people from bondage, Moses humbly replied,

“Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the children of Israel out of Egypt?”
(Exodus 3:11)

When the people of Israel sinned and provoked God’s wrath by making a golden calf, Moses interceded for them with compassion, saying,

text.text: Elihu Son of Barachel Meek in Wisdom and Patience

text:
Elihu, the son of Barachel the Buzite, is another great example of meekness revealed through patience, respect, and discernment. During the trial of the righteous Job, Elihu quietly listened as Job and his three older friends spoke at length. Yet when their words strayed from truth, Elihu did not remain silent.

The Scripture says:

“So these three men ceased answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes. Then the wrath of Elihu, the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was aroused; his wrath was aroused against Job because he justified himself rather than God. Also against his three friends his wrath was aroused, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job. Now because they were older than he, Elihu had waited to speak to Job.”(Job 32:1–4)

Elihu’s restraint is a mark of meekness. Though he was young, he honored the elders by waiting for them to finish before speaking. When he finally spoke, his words were humble yet filled with divine understanding:

“I am young in years, and you are very old; therefore I was afraid, and dared not declare my opinion to you.

I said, ‘Age should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.’
But there is a spirit in man, and the breath of the Almighty gives him understanding.”
(Job 32:6–8)

Elihu acknowledged that true wisdom comes not merely from age, but from the Spirit of God dwelling within a person. His humility allowed him to discern rightly between human reasoning and divine truth.

He continued,

“I waited for your words, I listened to your reasonings, while you searched out what to say.
Indeed, there was no one who refuted Job, no one among you who answered his words.”
(Job 32:11–12)

✍🏾

text.text: The Holy Virgin Mary – The Meek and Faithful Mother

text:
Our Lady, the Blessed Virgin Mary, is the perfect image of meekness, humility, and faith. She is often called “the Meek Dove” because of her gentle spirit and total obedience to the will of God. When the angel Gabriel brought her the divine message, she did not question or doubt but submitted herself entirely to the Lord’s plan, saying:

“Behold, I am the servant of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word.”
(Luke 1:38)

In her humility, she accepted the mystery of the Incarnation with quiet faith. Though she became the Mother of God, she never sought honor or recognition. Instead, she treasured the works of God in silence, pondering them deeply in her heart:

“But Mary kept all these things and pondered them in her heart.”
(Luke 2:19)

At the wedding in Cana of Galilee, her meekness and trust in her Son were again revealed. Seeing the need of others, she gently said to the servants,

“Do whatever He tells you.”(John 2:5)

Her words show not only her faith but her humility in serving God’s purpose quietly and effectively.

When many abandoned Christ during His suffering, the Holy Virgin remained faithful to the end. She stood weeping at the foot of the Cross, sharing in the pain of her Son with a heart full of love and compassion. There, her meek devotion was honored, for Christ entrusted her to all humanity, saying:

“ Behold your mother, .”(John 19:26–27)
