Dear beloved followers of the Orthodox faith, peace and grace be with you. Today, through the blessings of God, we share with you this important teaching so that you may read, understand, and grow in the knowledge of truth.

✍🏾

Emmanuel means “God is with us.”

As the Prophet Isaiah prophesied,

“Behold, a virgin shall conceive in her womb and bear a son, and shall call his name Emmanuel.”Isaiah 7:14; Matthew 1:23

This prophecy was fulfilled in the mystery of the Incarnation, when the angel announced to the pure and holy Virgin Mary that she would conceive in her womb the Son of God not by the will of man, but by the power of the Holy Spirit. The angel said to her:

“Behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call His name Emmanuel, which means God with us.” Isaiah 7:14; Matthew 1:23

Emmanuel is a name formed from two words:

‘Amane’  - meaning “with us,”

‘El’ (ʾĒl) - meaning “God.”

Together, they declare the eternal truth that God is with His people the source of divine peace, reconciliation, and perfect unity between the Creator and His creation.

To say “God with us” means that He took our flesh, our soul, and our spirit, and became one with us yet without sin.

Therefore, Emmanuel expresses the holy mystery of union between God and man. In other words:

“God became man, and man was united with God.”

This is the mystery of Tewahedo the perfect and inseparable union of divinity and humanity in the one person of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ.

✍🏾

When praising Him, the holy scholars revealed the mystery of divine unity, saying:

“This name is great; it must not be divided into two.”
(Hay. Abe. Zesawiros)

This teaches us that the name Emmanuel proclaims the perfect and indivisible union of God and man.

✍🏾 Therefore, to save us, the Son, one of the Holy Trinity, took flesh from the holy Virgin Mary. He united this flesh with His own divine Word not as two separate beings, but as one perfect and inseparable Person and through this divine union, He accomplished our salvation.

✍🏾 From the very moment He was conceived in the womb of the Virgin, He fulfilled the mystery of perfect unity (Tewahedo). He did not make Himself two God alone and man alone but remained one Lord, one Christ, both perfect God and perfect man, without confusion, separation, or division.

✍🏾 Therefore, today and forever, the Word of God remains united with the human body He assumed. This body, sanctified and glorified, is continually honored by the holy Cherubim. Truly, our Lord has loved us to this immeasurable extent by becoming one with us so that we may be one with Him.

God With Us - Emmanuel

✍🏾

✍🏾 Therefore, today and forever, the Word of God remains united with the human body He assumed. This body, sanctified and glorified, is continually honored by the holy Cherubim. Truly, our Lord has loved us to this immeasurable extent by becoming one with us so that we may be one with Him.

God With Us - Emmanuel

✍🏾 The Creator exists in three divine persons:
The Holy Trinity - the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

✍🏾In His oneness, He is called:
God, El Shaddai, Alpha and Omega, the First and the Last - One eternal Lord.

✍🏾Through His Incarnation, He is known as:

Emmanuel - God with us, the Savior of the world, Jesus Christ.

✍🏾The Fulfillment of the Promise

When Adam ate from the forbidden tree and was condemned to death, he lived in sorrow upon the earth. In his grief, he pleaded with God for mercy  to restore him to his former place of glory.

Out of His infinite compassion, God fulfilled His promise by being born from the offspring of Adam to redeem humanity and grant salvation.

On that holy and appointed day, the prophecy was fulfilled:
Our God became one with us.
Through this divine union, the sin of mankind was forgiven, and humanity was sanctified.

Continues 👇🏾

text.text: Living in the Presence of God

text:
If God is with us, we are called to live holy lives separated from sin, walking in righteousness, and glorifying His name. When a person strives to live according to God’s will, the Lord will never abandon them.

However, when people encounter suffering, hardship, or increasing trials, they often feel as though God has forsaken them. Yet, our Creator never forgets His children. He allows trials for a divine purpose to purify, strengthen, and guide us toward holiness.

✍🏾Especially in these days of hardship and turmoil, when troubles surround us and spiritual battles rage, we Christians must remain steadfast in faith.
If we fall into murmuring and complaint against God, we will find no peace.

Instead, let us remember that God never forgets His creation. He is with all who trust in Him. What He desires from us is simple and true:

To do what is pleasing in His sight,

To worship Him faithfully,

To live a genuine Christian life,

To obey His commandments and walk in His ways.

May our merciful God never depart from us.
May His divine presence dwell continually within us.
May He make us steadfast in His holy house forever.Amen.

Dear beloved followers of the Orthodox faith, peace and grace be with you. Today, through the blessings of God, we share with you this important teaching so that you may read, understand, and grow in the knowledge of truth.

Although the righteous saint Abba Yim’ata was martyred in Ethiopia, his birthplace was in Asia Minor, within the boundaries of the ancient Roman Empire. Abba Yim’ata is one of the Nine Saints who came to Ethiopia.
Though they were all born and raised under the same empire, each of them came from a different region. What united them was not their homeland but the grace and power of the Holy Spirit.
The secret of their unity can be explained in three divine truths:

👉🏾 Their faith in Monotheism (Tewahedo)

👉🏾 Their shared goal – the Kingdom of God

👉🏾 Their common monastic life

✍🏾

All of the Nine Saints, including Abba Yim’ata, were of noble and royal descent. Yet, they chose to despise worldly honor and pursue heavenly glory. Having studied the Holy Scriptures deeply, they renounced the comforts of their homeland and traveled to the deserts of Egypt and beyond.

During the 5th century A.D., when believers in the true faith of Tewahedo were persecuted by heretics, these saints chose exile rather than abandoning their faith. Among them, it is believed that Abba pentelewon and Abune Aregawi were the first to depart.

At that time, no land was more fitting as a refuge for the faithful than Ethiopia. Thus, around 470 A.D., during the reign of King Al'ameda of Ethiopia, the saints arrived under the leadership of Abune Aregawi.

The king, recognizing that they were men of God, received them with great honor. He granted them a place in Aksum known as Bet Qetin to dwell and serve the Lord.

✍🏾
Upon entering Ethiopia, their first task was to learn the Gë

language. Having mastered it through diligence and tradition, they began their ministry in the Aksum region.

At that time, Christianity, which had been kindled earlier by Abune Selama, Be-Abraha We-Atsbeha, and Abune Muse I, had grown weak among the people. Abba Yim’ata and his companions rekindled that flame of faith.

They preached the Gospel in the local tongue, strengthened those who were wavering, and turned back those who had fallen away. They also translated many holy books brought from their homeland into

ëz, preserving and spreading divine wisdom.

Their life together was filled with love, humility, and prayer. They ate and prayed as one family, and the grace of God never departed from among them.

👉🏾👉🏾 👉🏾Abba #Yim’ata #Tsadiq (Tikimt 28)

Dear beloved followers of the Orthodox faith, peace and grace be with you. Today, through the blessings of God, we share with you this important teaching so that you may read, understand, and grow in the knowledge of truth.

Although the righteous saint Abba Yim’ata was martyred in Ethiopia, his birthplace was in Asia Minor, within the boundaries of the ancient Roman Empire. Abba Yim’ata is one of the Nine Saints who came to Ethiopia.
Though they were all born and raised under the same empire, each of them came from a different region. What united them was not their homeland but the grace and power of the Holy Spirit.
The secret of their unity can be explained in three divine truths:

👉🏾 Their faith in Monotheism (Tewahedo)

👉🏾 Their shared goal – the Kingdom of God

👉🏾 Their common monastic life

✍🏾Their Journey and Purpose

All of the Nine Saints, including Abba Yim’ata, were of noble and royal descent. Yet, they chose to despise worldly honor and pursue heavenly glory. Having studied the Holy Scriptures deeply, they renounced the comforts of their homeland and traveled to the deserts of Egypt and beyond.

During the 5th century A.D., when believers in the true faith of Tewahedo were persecuted by heretics, these saints chose exile rather than abandoning their faith. Among them, it is believed that Abba pentelewon and Abune Aregawi were the first to depart.

At that time, no land was more fitting as a refuge for the faithful than Ethiopia. Thus, around 470 A.D., during the reign of King Al'ameda of Ethiopia, the saints arrived under the leadership of Abune Aregawi.

The king, recognizing that they were men of God, received them with great honor. He granted them a place in Aksum known as Bet Qetin to dwell and serve the Lord.

✍🏾Their Work in Ethiopia

Upon entering Ethiopia, their first task was to learn the Gëëz language. Having mastered it through diligence and tradition, they began their ministry in the Aksum region.

At that time, Christianity, which had been kindled earlier by Abune Selama, Be-Abraha We-Atsbeha, and Abune Muse I, had grown weak among the people. Abba Yim’ata and his companions rekindled that flame of faith.

They preached the Gospel in the local tongue, strengthened those who were wavering, and turned back those who had fallen away. They also translated many holy books brought from their homeland intoGëëz, preserving and spreading divine wisdom.

Their life together was filled with love, humility, and prayer. They ate and prayed as one family, and the grace of God never departed from among them.

Continues 👇🏾

text:
After some time, Abba Yim’ata’s next divine calling was to spread the monastic life throughout Ethiopia. For this, the Nine Saints were led by the Holy Spirit to different regions:

👉🏾 Petelewon: in Tsoma’et

👉🏾 Gerima: in Medera

👉🏾 Likanos: in Konatsil

👉🏾 Aregawi: in Damo

👉🏾 Tsihma: in Tsediya

👉🏾 Others founded monasteries in various regions as the Holy Spirit directed them.

👉🏾Abba Yim’ata, under the divine guidance of the Holy Spirit, chose Geralta (in present-day Tigray) as his dwelling and place of ministry.

When Abba Yim’ata reached the place prepared by God, it is said that even a river parted before him. He built a holy monastery there and performed many miracles. Through his prayer and teaching, he made many disciples who continued his spiritual work.

The Monastery of Abune Yim’ata in Geralta remains one of the most remarkable and awe-inspiring places in Ethiopia. It stands high upon the mountains, reached only by great effort and courage. Yet, its beauty and sanctity reflect the unwavering faith and perseverance of our forefathers.

Abba Yim’ata lived a life of struggle and holiness in that monastery, and he peacefully rested in the Lord on Tikimt 28, the day of his commemoration.

✍🏾

The life of Abba Yim’ata Tsadeq is a shining example of faith, humility, and steadfastness in the truth of the Tewahedo faith.
Through his prayers and the intercession of all the Nine Saints, may God strengthen our faith, guide our hearts toward holiness, and grant peace to our souls.

text.text: ? If He is God, to Whom Does He

text:
Dear brothers and sisters who follow the Orthodox teachings ,we greet you with the peace of God. Today’s teaching is presented based on the above topic. May you read it attentively and learn from it with understanding.

✍🏾

text.text: Christ Alone Bears the Sins of Humanity

text:
When the arm of God was revealed for the salvation of mankind  to become a sin offering and to give His life unto death  the prophet declared:
“He bore the sin of many and made intercession for the transgressors.” (Isaiah 53:12)

This means that it is Christ Himself alone, not angels, not righteous men, nor martyrs, who can bear the sins of humanity. As the Psalmist also prays:

“Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of Your name; deliver us and forgive our sins, for Your name’s sake.” (Psalm 79:9)

Even before Christ came in the flesh, Isaiah had already foretold that He would intercede for mankind.

The Fulfillment of Prophecy in Christ

After these prophecies were fulfilled and God appeared in the flesh, the Apostle Paul clearly wrote:

“For it pleased the Father that in Him all fullness should dwell, and through Him to reconcile to Himself all things, whether on earth or in heaven, having made peace through the blood of His cross.” (Colossians 1:19–20)

This sacred word reveals two important truths:

1. When God appeared in the flesh and lived among us, He reconciled humanity to Himself.

2. Even now and forever, Christ continues to live and intercede for us. (Hebrews 7:25)

This teaches us that the precious blood shed on the Cross is, today and until the coming of the Lord, the only way for a sinner to repent, to be baptized in the saving Name of the Lord Jesus, to receive forgiveness, and to be reconciled with God.

Forgiveness of sins and reconciliation are accomplished only through His blood, which was shed once for all, for the salvation of mankind.

✍🏾

text.text: The Arm of God Revealed for Salvation

text:
As we have seen, Scripture declares:

“According to the law, almost all things are purified with blood, and without shedding of blood there is no remission.” (Hebrews 9:22)

Because there was no mediator on earth who could forgive sins or reconcile mankind to God, the Lord Himself revealed His own arm as the Savior.

As the prophet Isaiah testifies:
“Truth has fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter… So His own arm brought salvation for Him; and His righteousness, it sustained Him.” (Isaiah 59:15–17)

✍🏾

Again, in another prophecy, God Himself speaks, saying:
“I looked, but there was no one to help; I was astonished that there was no one to uphold; therefore My own arm brought salvation for Me, and My wrath sustained Me.” (Isaiah 63:5)

This divine word was fulfilled when God sent forth His own arm His Son, our Lord Jesus Christ to save humanity from eternal death.
As it is written:

“Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” (John 1:29)

And again:

“There is now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus.” (Romans 8:1–4)
For through His own blood, He purchased the Church of God. (Acts 20:28)

👉🏾“Sing to the Lord a new song, for He has done marvelous things; His right hand and His holy arm have gained Him the victory.” (Psalm 98:1)

Through the mystery of the Incarnation, the Lord’s own right hand His divine power manifested in Christ accomplished salvation for all who believe. Therefore, let every soul give thanks to the Lord, for His mercy endures forever.

text:
The Apostle writes concerning our Lord Jesus Christ:
“He did not enter the Most Holy Place every year with the blood of another. Otherwise, He would have had to suffer often since the foundation of the world. But now, once for all, at the end of the ages, He has appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of Himself. text:

“Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.” (Matthew 11:28)

“Abba, Father.” (Romans 8:15; cf. James 4:7–8)

text:
If this truth sounds bold, it is indeed a holy boldness, firmly rooted in the Word of God. The Apostle John writes:

“These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life. And this is the confidence that we have in Him, that if we ask anything according to His will, He hears us. And if we know that He hears us whatever we ask we know that we have the petitions that we have asked of Him.” (1 John 5:13–15)

In the Holy Scriptures, intercession means praying to God on behalf of others. Those who intercede stand before God with love and faith, seeking His mercy and blessing for others. This holy service is a work of compassion and unity in the body of Christ.

✍🏾

The prophet Zephaniah reveals God’s acceptance of intercession:

“My daughters who are scattered, who intercede for me beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, shall bring me My offering.” (Zephaniah 3:10)

This shows that there are those who intercede for the work and people of God, and that the Lord receives their prayers with favor.

✍🏾

The Apostle Paul urged all believers to live a life of prayer and intercession:

“The Lord is near. In everything, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.” (Philippians 4:6)

He further commanded in his letter to Timothy:

“I urge, therefore, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people for kings and all who are in authority.” (1 Timothy 2:1–2)

This shows that intercession is not limited to priests or elders alone but is a calling given to all the faithful, so that peace and righteousness may dwell among people.

✍🏾

The Apostle James teaches about intercession as part of the life and healing of the Church:

“If anyone among you is sick, let him call for the elders of the Church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord. The prayer of faith will save the sick, and the Lord will raise him up. And if he has committed sins, they will be forgiven. Confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The effective prayer of a righteous man avails much.” (James 5:14–16)

This passage forms the biblical foundation for the Orthodox practice of communal prayer, confession, and the anointing of the sick. It reveals the power of intercession as a means of grace, healing, and forgiveness.

✍🏾

text.text: The Intercession of the Saints on Earth

text:
The Apostle Paul again bears witness to the prayers of the saints:

“While they themselves pray for you, they long for you because of the exceeding grace of God in you.” (2 Corinthians 9:14)

This shows that those who are still in the flesh living in this world pray for one another out of love and the grace that God has given them. Such intercession strengthens the unity of believers and expresses the communion of the faithful.

Examples of Intercession in the Bible

Intercession is a sacred practice in which believers pray to God on behalf of others. The Scriptures provide numerous examples of this holy calling, demonstrating both human and divine intercession.

Abraham Intercedes for Sodom

Abraham prayed to God on behalf of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, pleading for mercy for the righteous, particularly for Lot and his family:

“Then Abraham drew near and said… ‘Far be it from You to slay the righteous with the wicked.’” (Genesis 18:23–32)

This shows that intercession is an act of love and advocacy for others, even in the face of divine judgment.

text.text: Jewish Elders Intercede for the Centurion

text:
The elders of the Jews interceded with Jesus on behalf of a centurion whose son was sick:

“When he heard about Jesus, he sent to Him the elders of the Jews, begging Him to come and heal his servant. And when they came to Jesus, they urged Him earnestly, saying, ‘He is worthy for this to be done for him, for he loves our nation, and he himself built us a synagogue.’” (Luke 7:2–5)

✍🏾

text.text: The Virgin Mary Intercedes at Cana

text:
At the wedding in Cana, Mary interceded with Jesus for the hosts when the wine ran out:

“The wine has run out.” (John 2:3)

Through her request, Jesus performed His first miracle, turning water into wine. This shows the power of humble and faithful intercession.

✍🏾

text.text: The Holy Spirit Intercedes for Believers

text:
The Apostle Paul teaches that the Spirit of God intercedes on behalf of the saints:

“The Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groanings that cannot be uttered. And He who searches the hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit, because He intercedes for the saints according to the will of God.” (Romans 8:26–27)

The Holy Spirit guides our prayers, teaching us to pray according to God’s will and helping us to pray persistently and rightly.

✍🏾

Jude exhorts believers to pray continually in the Spirit, maintaining the love of God and awaiting His mercy:

“But you, beloved, building yourselves up on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit, keep yourselves in the love of God, waiting for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ that leads to eternal life.” (Jude 20–21)

✍🏾

While living on earth, a Christian should pray for:

Oneself

The Church

All the saints

Authorities and rulers

The nation and all people

As the Scriptures command:

“I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people, for kings and all who are in authority.” (1 Timothy 2:1–2)

text:
Beloved in Christ,Let us reflect today on the teaching of our Lord Jesus Christ, who said: “Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.” (Matthew 5:5)

In these words, our Savior calls us to a life of humility, gentleness, and trust in God. He is Himself the perfect example of meekness, and through His life, suffering, and victory, He shows us how to walk in meekness and inherit both the blessings of this world and the eternal Kingdom of Heaven.

✍🏾

text.text: Our Lord Jesus Christ: The Perfect Example of Meekness

text:
The perfect example of meekness in the New Testament is our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, the crown of all the saints. He said in His Gospel:

“Learn from Me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.”
(Matthew 11:29)

Long before His coming, the Prophet Zechariah had already foretold this, saying:

“Say to the daughter of Zion, ‘Behold, your King is coming to you, meek and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.’”
(Zechariah 9:9; Matthew 21:4)

Christ, therefore, is the perfect and complete example of meekness and gentleness.

✍🏾

Saint Peter bore witness to the meekness of Christ, saying:

“For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, that you should follow in His steps.
He committed no sin, nor was deceit found in His mouth.

2. This Land Where We Live

text:
The meek are loved by all around them, and God’s blessings are abundant in their lives. This brings them both spiritual and physical prosperity. Nothing can truly trouble them because they have already tasted the joy of God’s kingdom, and His grace is multiplied in their lives.

Examples from the Fathers:

Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, and many other patriarchs were meek, and God blessed them abundantly in the land where they lived.

God chose the prophet Moses to lead Israel because of his meekness.

Boaz received God’s favor for his gentle spirit.

David, who appeared small in the eyes of men, was raised to be king of Israel

The human body, formed from the earth, is also symbolically “earth.” The meek make their bodies temples of God by bringing their souls into obedience and sanctity. In this way, they “inherit” their bodies, using them for righteous deeds and as vessels of holiness.

Saint Peter teaches:

“Sanctify Christ as Lord in your hearts, and always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you for the reason of the hope that is in you, but do it with gentleness and reverence.”(1 Peter 3:15)

The meek follow this teaching by submitting their bodies to the spirit and cultivating holiness.

Saint Ephraim the Syrian said:

“The Spirit of wisdom dwells in the humble and meek heart.”

Thus, their meek hearts become the dwelling place of the Holy Spirit.

4. Those Who Live in Sin

The “earth” can also symbolize the realm of sin, where the proud and worldly-minded live. The meek, however, through wisdom and Christ-like humility, guide sinners away from evil and towards righteousness. By their words and deeds, they transform sinners into children of God.

Saint Paul instructs:

“Brothers, if anyone is overtaken in any fault, you who are spiritual should restore him in a spirit of gentleness, considering yourself, lest you also be tempted.”
(Galatians 6:1)

The meek correct others with patience and gentleness, leading them to salvation and eternal life.

Dear brothers and sisters who follow the Orthodox teachings ,we greet you with the peace of God. Today’s teaching is presented based on the above topic. May you read it attentively and learn from it with understanding.

✍🏾

text.text: Saint John the Baptist’s Teaching on Meekness

text:
“All virtues are good. But meekness is the most important of all. Meekness is the virtue that distinguishes man from beasts and makes him like the holy angels. That is why our Lord Jesus Christ taught and praised meekness in words. He did not only teach us in words but also showed us in action.”(Homily 61 on the Gospel of John)

Saint John teaches that meekness lifts humanity above the impulses of anger and pride, shaping us into the image of the angels. It is the virtue by which we become truly human gentle, patient, and filled with divine grace.

✍🏾

text.text: Meekness - The Weapon of Christ Against the Devil

text:
“If you are like Christ, the devil cannot see you face to face. He knows the form of Christ, and he knows the weapons of Christ, and he has been severely wounded by this. These are humility and meekness. Because Christ did not conquer the devil in Corinth by declaring that He was Christ, but with these words, He trapped him and chased him away with humility and meekness.”(Homily 78 on the Gospel of John)

Saint John reveals that meekness and humility are the true weapons of Christ. The devil cannot withstand them, for these virtues destroyed his power at the Cross. A meek soul, therefore, is stronger than any sword it defeats evil without hatred and conquers through peace.

✍🏾

text.text: The Beauty of a Meek Tongue

text:
“Though your mouth be made of gold or precious stones, it cannot shine like a tongue adorned with the jewel of meekness.”(Homily 78 on the Gospel of John)

A gentle word spoken from a meek heart is more beautiful than any earthly treasure. Speech seasoned with meekness carries the grace of the Holy Spirit and builds peace among all who hear it.

✍🏾

“There is no greater power than meekness. As fire is quenched by water, so a mind filled with anger is quenched by meekness. By meekness we practice other works of virtue, we quench our brother’s anger, and we save our brother’s mind from anxiety.”

(Homily 2 and 15 on the Gospel of John)

Meekness extinguishes anger just as cool water calms fire. It brings peace to the heart and unity among believers. Through meekness we learn forgiveness, patience, and true spiritual strength.

✍🏾

“What could be more difficult than these commandments? It is not enough to suffer alone. But like a dove, we should not be angry at the suffering we suffer, for anger is quenched not by anger, but by meekness.”(Homily 33 on the Gospel of Matthew)

✍🏾

We must distinguish between true meekness and false or imitation meekness. True meekness comes from spiritual maturity and inner strength, while false meekness arises from fear, lack of self-confidence, or a sense of inferiority. Such false meekness easily changes into pride, selfishness, and arrogance when circumstances shift.

✍🏾Fake meekness is an insincere meekness practiced for selfish motives such as gaining recognition, false praise, power, wealth, knowledge, or other worldly benefits or with the hidden intention of harming others. We must guard ourselves against this kind of deceitful meekness, which hides behind outward gentleness, and we must not be deceived by its appearance.

text: Beloved in Christ, just as our bodies long for food and water, our souls long for God, His Word, and His salvation. We invite you to read, reflect, and learn how to hunger and thirst for righteousness,

Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, in the fourth Beatitude, teaches us that “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.”

✍🏾 Righteousness is truth and holiness the life we live with God, who Himself is Truth, and with all His creation. It is to live on earth according to the will of God, and then to live eternally with Him and His saints in the Kingdom of Heaven.

✍🏾 In the spiritual life, to hunger and thirst for righteousness means to long for and to obtain righteousness to “feed” upon it continually through:

👉🏾Fasting

👉🏾 Prayer

👉🏾 Worship

👉🏾 Almsgiving

👉🏾 Service

This does not only mean obeying God’s commandments outwardly, but also striving with all our heart for the inner life of holiness. True righteousness is not the mere fulfillment of the law, but the longing to be united with the God of righteousness Himself.

✍🏾 When we speak of struggling for righteousness, we mean:

👉🏾To earnestly desire righteousness within our hearts,

👉🏾To pray fervently with our lips to obtain it, and

👉🏾To labor throughout our lives in performing deeds that are good and pleasing to God.

✍🏾 As Saint John Afework taught, our Lord described “those who hunger and thirst for righteousness” as those whose desire arises from within. Therefore, true hunger for righteousness is not something we display to impress others or imitate human appearance it is a deep, spiritual yearning that flows from the heart and the conscience.

When our Lord used both words hunger and thirst He showed that righteousness is not a casual wish, but an urgent and essential need for the soul.

Just as the body cannot live without food and water, the soul cannot live without righteousness. Hunger and thirst drive us to seek what sustains life; likewise, hunger and thirst for righteousness drive the faithful to seek holiness with all their strength, until they are filled with the grace and peace of God.

Hunger and Thirst for Righteousness

✍🏾 Just as physical hunger and thirst compel us to seek food and water with all our strength, so spiritual hunger and thirst compel us to seek righteousness with all our heart and mind. The Lord teaches us that just as our physical life cannot continue without food and water, our spiritual life cannot be sustained without righteous deeds.

✍🏾When we feel spiritual hunger, we must long for righteousness as we long for bread; when we feel spiritual thirst, we must seek righteousness as we seek water. Only then can our souls be nourished, refreshed, and strengthened in the grace of God.

To “hunger and thirst for righteousness” means to desire and strive for:

👉🏾 God Himself,( the source of all righteousness )

👉🏾 His Holy Word, (which enlightens and strengthens the soul)

👉🏾 His Holy Flesh and Precious Blood, (which give life and salvation)

👉🏾 Dwelling continually in His holy house and rejoicing in the goodness found in Him;

👉🏾 Loving and following His divine law and way;

👉🏾 And ultimately, inheriting the kingdom of heaven prepared for those who live in righteousness.

In this way, the faithful grow in spiritual life, being filled not with earthly food, but with the true nourishment that comes from God alone.

text.text: Diligence: Hungering and Thirsting for God

text:
King David, the man after God’s own heart, teaches us to draw near to God through faith and love, believing that He alone is the source of true satisfaction for the soul.

✍🏾 Through the prophet Jeremiah, God revealed His grief, saying:

“My people have committed two evils: they have forsaken Me, the fountain of living waters, and hewed out for themselves broken cisterns that can hold no water.”
(Jeremiah 2:13)

This shows that God Himself is the fountain of living water. To thirst for righteousness, therefore, means to long for this divine water with all our heart through thought, word, and deed.

✍🏾David expressed this spiritual thirst beautifully when he said:

“O God, You are my God; early will I seek You. My soul thirsts for You; my flesh longs for You in a dry and weary land where there is no water.”(Psalm 63:1)

And again he said:

“As the deer pants for the water brooks, so my soul pants for You, O Lord. My soul thirsts for the living God; when shall I come and appear before God?”(Psalm 42:1–2)

These words reveal the depth of his yearning not for earthly pleasure, but for communion with the living God.

✍🏾

text.text: In seeking righteousness, David also said:

text:
“Thus will I bless You while I live; I will lift up my hands in Your name. My soul shall be satisfied as with marrow and fatness, and my mouth shall praise You with joyful lips.”
(Psalm 63:4–5)

To hunger and thirst for God, then, is to desire His presence, His word, and His righteousness more than anything else. It is to live diligently, seeking Him in prayer, in obedience, and in purity of heart until our souls are filled and satisfied by His divine grace.

text.text: 2. Hungering and Thirsting for the Holy Word

text:
✍🏾 To hunger and thirst for righteousness also means to long for the Holy Word of God. Our father David declares:

“Your word is sweeter to my taste than honey and the honeycomb.”
(Psalm 119:103)

This teaches us that the Word of God is spiritual food for the soul something we eagerly desire, hear, and live by.

✍🏾Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ said:

 “Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of the Lord.”
(Matthew 4:4)

This reminds us that true life comes not from physical sustenance alone, but from continual communion with God through His Word. We are called to be diligent in hearing, meditating upon, and obeying it.

✍🏾 The prophet Amos also foretold a time of spiritual famine, saying:

“Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will send a famine on the earth not a famine of bread or thirst for water, but of hearing the Word of the Lord.”
(Amos 8:11–12)

✍🏾 St. Peter teaches us that the Word of God is like pure milk for the newborn, essential for spiritual growth:

“Therefore, as newborn babes, long for the pure milk of the Word, that you may grow thereby in salvation, if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is gracious.”
(1 Peter 2:1–3)

✍🏾 By the Word of God, we mean:

👉🏾The commandments and laws given by God through the prophets,

👉🏾The Word of the Father made flesh in Jesus Christ,

👉🏾The Holy Gospel that He taught and preached during His incarnation.

To hunger and thirst for the Word is to continually seek it, meditate upon it, and allow it to guide every thought, word, and deed, so that we may grow in righteousness and salvation.

👉🏾Question :-What are the requirements to be a priest

👉🏾Answer :-

text:
My beloved child in Christ, you have asked a good and holy question: What are the requirements to be a priest?

The priesthood is not an earthly honor to be sought after, but a heavenly responsibility to be carried with fear and trembling before God. Among the faithful men, women, and clergy, the priest bears a spiritual duty higher than all others, for his service is not of this world but of heaven.

When His Holiness Abune Shenouda was asked about the priesthood, he said:

“The priesthood I am giving you is not an appointment, but a responsibility.”

Appointment is light and fills the stomach, but responsibility brings sleepless nights, deep concern for souls, and unceasing prayer for forgiveness and mercy.

A true priest never ceases to examine his own life and the lives of his spiritual children. Through fasting, prayer, and supplication, he intercedes before God, following the Lord’s command:

👉🏾“Feed my lambs, feed my sheep.” (John 21:16)

Before a priest ordained, the Holy Scriptures teach that he must be able to instruct the faithful, lead his household in godliness, be the husband of one wife, and faithfully guide his family with discipline and love. He must maintain a good reputation among people and live in peace with all.

✍🏾The Apostle also warns against unworthy habits: a priest must not be given to much wine, not double-tongued, not greedy for money, and not quick-tempered. Instead, he should be humble, gentle, forgiving, patient, and peaceful  a true example for the flock of Christ.

✍🏾A priest sits on the throne of the Apostles and receives from God the authority to bind and loose sins. As Saint John Afework wrote:

“The Lord confirms in heaven what priests have done on earth, and accepts the thoughts of His servants.”

✍🏾Thus, the mysteries performed by priests on earth are sanctified by heaven itself. Because of this great responsibility, bishops must exercise great caution before ordaining anyone to the priesthood. The faithful may also express their testimony about the candidate’s character and life before the bishop confers ordination.

text.text: The Essential Qualities of a Priest

text: The priest must develop a life that leads to holiness. He must strive daily to live in purity of heart and thought, keeping himself away from every form of sin. His words and actions must reflect the holiness of God whom he serves.

A priest must be well instructed in the faith and grounded in the teachings of the Holy Church. He should dedicate himself to reading and learning the Word of God and the writings of the Fathers, so that if the faithful ask him tomorrow, he will   answer the questions , can instruct, guide, and defend the truth with wisdom.

The priest must rule over his desires and emotions with discipline. He should be slow to anger, measured in speech, and temperate in all things. Without self-control, the priest cannot shepherd the souls of others, for he who is overcome by his passions cannot lead others to freedom in Christ.

1. He must be well-versed in the mysteries of the faith (Council of Nicaea, 325, Canon 19).

2. He must not be a new convert (Canons 2–9).

3. He must be in good spritual health (Acts 78).

4. He must be at least thirty years old (Sixth Synod, Canon 13).

So, my child, understand that the priesthood is not a title of honor but a life of sacrifice. It is a path of humility, purity, and tireless service for the glory of God and the salvation of souls.

May the Lord, the High Priest of our faith, grant that those called to this sacred ministry may be found worthy through purity, wisdom, and meekness.

text.text:
May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.

Dear brothers and sisters in Christ,
Peace and grace to you all.Through the blessings of our Lord Jesus Christ and the intercession of His holy Mother, we share this teaching entitled “Mother of God: The Thornless Flower.”
Let us read, learn, and meditate upon it with humble hearts.

✍🏾

text.text: The Holy Virgin Mary is a true flower.

text:
According to science, a plant must meet three main conditions to be considered a true plant. These are:

👉🏾True roots

👉🏾 True stems

👉🏾 True branches

Such plants are able to prepare their own food by absorbing water and minerals from the soil through their roots and using sunlight through their leaves and stems, in a process known as photosynthesis.

However, green organisms that lack true roots, stems, and branches  such as algae and fungi  cannot prepare their own food and are therefore not regarded as true plants.

The Virgin Mary as the True Plant of Life

Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, fulfills this likeness in the spiritual sense:

Her root is the holy mountains (Ps. 86:1).

Her stem is the holy branch (Isa. 11:1).

Her branches are the vine that grows in heaven (John 15:5).

Thus, she is called the True Flower of Life, who brought forth the fruit of life, our Lord Jesus Christ the spiritual food and drink for the world.

When the Virgin Mary read the prophecies concerning her, she did not exalt herself.
Instead, she said with humility:

“I would have drawn water, chopped wood, and served her as a maidservant.”

Even when the Archangel Gabriel announced, “You are found worthy to bear the Son of God,” she humbly replied:

“Behold, I am the handmaid of the Lord.”

Such humility is beyond measure she, the Mother of God, still called herself a servant.

✍🏾

Some proud women, led by delusion, dare to say, “If I had lived in her time, I too would have given birth to Christ.”
Such words reveal a lack of modesty and understanding.

Likewise, some women in Israel still wait in vain, saying that Christ has not yet been born and that He will be born from among us in the future.

But in truth, even these women  who imagine themselves worthy to bear Christ, the food and drink of life are not even certain that they are properly nourishing their own children.they are like the foolish who cannot prepare their own food, yet speak proudly as if they could feed others. Their words are empty and lack truth.

✍🏾

The true flower, our Lady the Holy Virgin Mary, was remembered by the Creator even before the foundation of the world.After creation, she was revealed in the prophecies of the prophets, proclaimed in the preaching of the apostles, and glorified in the heart of every faithful soul the smallest Adam.She is the flower that never withers, the ever-living blossom of divine grace.

A flower gives rest to the eyes, hope to the heart, and fragrance to the nose.Likewise, our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, is the rest of the eyes, the hope of hearts, and the fragrance of the soul first to her blessed parents, and then to all mankind.

“You are a beautiful flower, your fragrance coming forth from the root of Jesse,”
as the wise man said (Wudasie Maryam Ze ehud,  Isaiah 11:1).

✍🏾

A flower brings healing, yet its medicine is only temporary.
But the True Flower, our Lady, brought forth the Savior of the world, Jesus Christ, who grants eternal healing and salvation.
For this reason, she is rightly called “Mother of Salvation.”

“For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.”(Luke 2:10–11)

text:
A flower attracts bees and produces honey.
In the same way, our Lady, the True Flower, drew to herself the Son, Christ, and brought forth the sweet law of the Gospel, which is as honey to the soul.

Honey is good, nourishing, and healing.So too are Christ and the Gospel both sweet to those who receive them and a remedy for the soul’s wounds.

“The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.” (Psalm 86:2)
“Hear, O daughter, and see; incline your ear; forget your people and your father’s house, for the King will desire your beauty, for He is your Lord.” (Psalm 45:10–11)

✍🏾

text.text: The Flower that Nourishes Flesh and Soul

text:
Flowers provide food for the body for example, plants like cabbage and other edible greens.
In the same way, our True mother and Lady provided food not only for the body but also for the soul :Christ Himself.

“Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life.” (John 6:56; Matthew 26:26)

✍🏾

Scholars have said:

“In the likeness of man, how shall we liken you, O Virgin?”

Let us remain silent in awe, recognizing that we cannot fully describe her glory. Yet our Lady reveals herself through her own humility and holiness.

✍🏾

text.text: How can she be compared to earthly flowers?

text:
A flower may be found on earth and remain on earth, but the Virgin Mary is a lush flower that neither withers nor fades both earthly and heavenly.

A flower may be a rose surrounded by thorns, but our Lady is a pure rose without thorns.

Gold is found in the earth and the mud, yet it is not defiled by the earth. Similarly, though Mary was born among humans, she is a thornless golden flower, unstained by sin, set apart and sanctified.

“The Most High has sanctified His dwelling place.” (Psalm 45:4)

✍🏾

If a flower provides medicine, it is only a temporary remedy that cures temporary illnesses.
But our Lady, the Living Flower, provides an eternal medicine - Christ Himself - which, once received, never needs to be repeated.

A flower reproduces its seeds through its male and female parts. The male part, when mature, fertilizes the female part of the same flower, producing new flowers - a natural process called self-pollination.
Alternatively, male pollen can be transferred to the female part of another flower through bees, birds, humans, or the wind, a process known as cross-pollination.

But our Blessed Lady conceived and bore the Son of God without any male seed, through the work of the Holy Spirit.
Thus, she surpasses all other flowers, as the Scriptures praise:

“Aaron’s rod budded without being planted or watered; you are like her.”
(Wudase Mariam Ze ehud)

(Commemorated on Hidar 3)

text:
Beloved faithful who follow the Orthodox teachings , we greet you in the peace of Our Lord Jesus Christ.Today, we bring you a blessed teaching based on the life and holiness of Saint Neakuto Leab, that you may read, learn, and be strengthened in faith.

✍🏾

The father of Saint Neakuto Leab was Saint Gebre Mariam (Harbe), the elder brother of Saint Lalibela, and his mother was called Merkez. Before his birth, Saint Gabriel the Archangel appeared to Saint Lalibela and told him,

 “The one who will be born from your brother is holy and good. He shall be your heir.”

In time, Saint Merkez gave birth to the holy child Neakuto, who was raised in the palace by Saint Lalibela and saint Meskel kibra, growing in wisdom and grace. When he became old enough to study, a teacher named Isaac instructed him, and through the power of the Holy Spirit, Neakuto quickly learned the teachings of the Holy Church.

✍🏾

After becoming a deacon, Neakuto served his Creator faithfully for twenty years. At the request of Saint Lalibela and by the will of God, he entered into marriage with a devout woman, and their union was blessed in the sacrament of matrimony. Yet Saint Neakuto said to his wife,

“My sister, let us preserve our virginity for the glory of God.”
She agreed, and they lived together in purity for twenty-five years.

✍🏾

text.text: His Service and Ascension to the Throne

text:
Saint Neakuto lived in fasting, prayer, and humility. He often spoke with the holy angels and practiced great asceticism carrying iron and stones, bowing down a thousand times a day. Saint Lalibela ordained him and made him governor of a district, and when Lalibela’s time of departure came, he anointed Neakuto as king over all Ethiopia.

Even as a ruler, Saint Neakuto continued in fasting, prayer, and service. The Archangel Raphael appeared to him and revealed that he would bear a son. Wishing to preserve his virginity, Neakuto prayed, and the Holy Virgin Mary comforted him in a vision, telling him that the child to be born would be by divine will. His son was named Haile Meskel.

✍🏾 The child was so beautiful that no one could compare to his grace or appearance. Fearing that his son might fall into pride because of his beauty, Saint Neakuto prayed earnestly to the Father, saying,

“Lord, this child, boasting of his appearance, may fall into sin and perish. Please, take him this very day and number him among the blessed children who rest in peace.”

The Creator heard his humble prayer, and the child was taken from this world in peace on the 16th of Tikmt.

✍🏾 Saint Neakuto did not know his wife more than once, preserving his vow of purity. As for food, he ate only a small portion of Zengada bread on Saturdays and Sundays in the Church of Saint Mary, refusing the food of the palace. Out of deep love and reverence for his Creator, he tied around his neck a stone that no man could lift, praying without ceasing until his sweat fell upon the ground, remembering the sufferings of Christ for the salvation of the world.

Even as a ruler, Saint Neakuto continued in fasting, prayer, and service. The Archangel Raphael appeared to him and revealed that he would bear a son. Wishing to preserve his virginity, Neakuto prayed, and the Holy Virgin Mary comforted him in a vision, telling him that the child to be born would be by divine will. His son was named Haile Meskel.

✍🏾 The child was so beautiful that no one could compare to his grace or appearance. Fearing that his son might fall into pride because of his beauty, Saint Neakuto prayed earnestly to the Father, saying,

“Lord, this child, boasting of his appearance, may fall into sin and perish. Please, take him this very day and number him among the blessed children who rest in peace.”

The Creator heard his humble prayer, and the child was taken from this world in peace on the 16th of Tikmt.

✍🏾 Saint Neakuto did not know his wife more than once, preserving his vow of purity. As for food, he ate only a small portion of Zengada bread on Saturdays and Sundays in the Church of Saint Mary, refusing the food of the palace. Out of deep love and reverence for his Creator, he tied around his neck a stone that no man could lift, praying without ceasing until his sweat fell upon the ground, remembering the sufferings of Christ for the salvation of the world.

Continues 👇🏾

Continued 👇🏾

✍🏾 His Holy Departure (Hidden by the Father)

text:
✍🏾 On the 3rd of Hidar, after the consecration of the temple called Debre Zion, the body of the great Prophet Moses was enveloped in the light of the Holy Spirit. Then, an angel of God named Gabriel appeared and lifted Saint Neakuto upon his back, leading him through the heavenly gate with the Archangel Gabriel and with Christ Himself.

A fiery chariot appeared, shining like flame, with wings like an eagle and great in height. Then our Lord Jesus Christ, the King of Glory, came to him surrounded by all His angels, by the twenty-four heavenly priests, by the prophets and apostles, by the righteous and martyrs, by the virgins and nuns, and by His most holy Mother, the Virgin Mary.

✍🏾The Lord said to him,

“From the day you were conceived until now, your sins are forgiven. You have shared in My suffering being pierced and bound for My sake and have forsaken worldly comfort for a bed of ashes. Therefore, I give you a house, a throne, garments, and a crown equal to My servant Yohannes Welde Negodguwad, for you have remembered My Passion.”

After these words, our Lord received him, and Saint Neakuto was hidden without seeing death.

✍🏾 The Blessing of His Monastery
From that day, water began to flow from the natural cave where the church is built like tears streaming from the mountain. To this day, this holy water heals those who come in faith.

The Monastery of Saint Neakuto Leab is located about 6 kilometers from the city of Lalibela, at the entrance to the town. It can be reached easily by any means of transport, or by a 30-minute walk

text: Beloved in Christ, just as our bodies long for food and water, our souls long for God, His Word, and His salvation. We invite you to read, reflect, and learn how to hunger and thirst for righteousness,

text.text: 3. Hungering and Thirsting for His Holy Flesh and Precious Blood

text:
Hungering and thirsting for righteousness means hungering and thirsting for the holy flesh and precious blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, where true righteousness is found. When we say “hungering and thirsting for righteousness,” our Lord teaches in His Gospel,

“Whoever drinks of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall become in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.”
(John 4:14)

He also says,

“I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me shall never hunger, and whoever believes in me shall never thirst.”(John 6:35)

Here, the Lord refers to the spiritual hunger the deep longing of the soul for the bread of life, which is His own body.

This truth was foreshadowed in the Old Testament when the Israelites hungered and the Lord fed them with heavenly manna, and when they thirsted and drank water that flowed from the rock. The manna and the water symbolized the Body and Blood of Christ, the true food and drink that give eternal life.

Our Lord Himself declared this clearly, saying:

“I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me will never hunger, and whoever believes in me will never thirst.

I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever; and the bread that I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.
Truly, truly, I say to you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you have no life in you.

Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.
For My flesh is true food, and My blood is true drink.
Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood abides in Me, and I in him.”(John 6:33–56)

Saint John the Apostle also reveals this mystery in the Book of Revelation:

“And he said to me, ‘Write, Blessed are those who are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb.’ And he said to me, ‘These are the true words of God.’”
(Revelation 19:9)

Therefore, to hunger and thirst for righteousness is to desire the Holy Communion the life-giving flesh and precious blood of Christ through which the faithful are united with Him and receive eternal life.

text.text: 4. Hungering and Thirsting for the House of God

text:
Hungering and thirsting for righteousness also means longing for heavenly life the spiritual life lived in the house of God, through prayer and worship. The righteous soul finds joy and peace in the dwelling of the Lord.

King David expressed this divine longing, saying,

“I rejoiced when they said to me, ‘Let us go into the house of the Lord.’”(Psalm 122:1)

He also said,

“Blessed are those who dwell in Your house; they will be ever praising You.”(Psalm 84:4)

To live in the house of the Lord according to His will is the greatest blessing. David further declared,

“Better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere; I would rather be a guest in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.” (Psalm 84:10)

He prayed with deep desire, saying,

“One thing have I desired of the Lord, that will I seek after: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the Lord, and to inquire in His temple.”(Psalm 27:4)

Saint Paul also taught his spiritual son Timothy about the holiness of God’s house, saying,

“I am writing to you so that you may know how one ought to behave in the house of God, which is the Church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.”
(1 Timothy 3:15)

Thus, to hunger and thirst for righteousness means to desire to live continually in the presence of God, to pray without ceasing, and to dwell spiritually in His holy Church.

5. Hungering and Thirsting for the Will of God

text:
Hungering and thirsting for righteousness also means striving to do the will of God in all things.

When our Lord passed through Samaria, His disciples brought Him food, saying, “Rabbi, eat.” But He replied,

“I have food to eat that you do not know about.”
The disciples said to one another, “Has anyone brought Him something to eat?”
Then Jesus said to them,
“My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me, and to finish His work.”(John 4:32–34)

In this, our Lord teaches that the true food of a Christian is to fulfill the will of God and to serve Him faithfully. This is what we must hunger and thirst for daily to please God through obedience and holy deeds.

Hungering for righteousness also means to labor in service that leads to holiness and justice. The Lord said,

“Blessed is that servant whom his master, when he comes, finds so doing.”(Matthew 24:46; Luke 12:43)

He also said,

“Blessed are those servants whom the master finds watching when he comes; truly I tell you, he will gird himself, have them recline at table, and will come and serve them.
And if he comes in the second or third watch and finds them so, blessed are those servants.”
(Luke 12:37–38)

Therefore, blessed are those who hunger and thirst to do the will of God, who serve Him diligently and remain steadfast in their calling until the Lord comes.

Those who hunger in this way shall be filled, for our Lord has promised,

“Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.”(Matthew 5:6)

text: Dear beloved in Christ, followers of the Orthodox faith , we greet you in the name of our Lord and Savior. Today, we continue our lesson on the divine words: “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.” Let us read with attention, reflect deeply, and learn from this holy teaching.

text.text: 6. Hungering and Thirsting for Truth and Justice

text:
Righteousness is truth and justice.
When we say hungering and thirsting for righteousness, it means to sincerely seek truth and justice, to pray earnestly for them, and to live according to them in all our deeds. The true Christian life is a life dedicated to truth and justice.

Christ Himself is the Truth, as He declared:

 “I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life.” (John 14:6)

And in Deuteronomy it is written:

 “He is the Rock, His work is perfect; for all His ways are justice. A God of truth and without iniquity, just and upright is He.” (Deut. 32:4)

✍🏾God is a God of truth and justice. Therefore, those who worship Him must also live in truth and righteousness.

✍🏾

text.text: The Righteousness of God in Scripture

text:
The heart of God was revealed through the words of His servant David:

“The word of the Lord is right, and all His works are done in faithfulness. He loves righteousness and justice; the earth is full of the goodness of the Lord. By the word of the Lord the heavens were made, and all their host by the breath of His mouth.” (Psalm 33:4–6)

And again,

 “Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne; mercy and truth go before Your face.” (Psalm 89:14)

✍🏾Because God is a God of truth and justice, all who believe in Him must strive to walk in the same way doing what is right and fair before Him.

The prophets also bear witness:

“Do justice and righteousness.” (Jeremiah 22:3)
“Let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like a mighty stream.” (Amos 5:24)

Thus, we are called to hunger and thirst for truth, justice, and righteousness in our lives, in our hearts, and in our dealings with others.

text.text: 7.Hungering and Thirsting for the Kingdom of Heaven

text:
To hunger and thirst for righteousness is also to long for the Kingdom of Heaven, which is the ultimate goal of every believer.
Our Lord taught:

“Seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness.” (Matthew 6:33)

And again:

 “For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world, yet loses his own soul?” (Mark 8:36)

Therefore, our greatest desire must be the salvation of our soul to live in unity with Christ and to inherit His kingdom.

✍🏾

text.text: Abiding in Christ, the Source of Righteousness

text:
Our Lord said:

 “Abide in Me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself unless it abides in the vine, neither can you, unless you abide in Me. I am the vine; you are the branches. Without Me you can do nothing.” (John 15:4–5)

✍🏾Only when we remain in Christ can we bear the fruits of righteousness. Apart from Him, we are lifeless branches that wither and perish.

Those who abide in Him and keep His words alive in their hearts will receive what they ask, for their will is joined with His divine will.

text:
“Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.” (Matthew 5:6)

Those who hunger and thirst for righteousness are truly blessed, for they have sought the right and the greatest thing the will of God and have labored earnestly to find it.

Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, while on the Cross, said,

“I thirst.” (John 19:28)

This thirst was not merely for water, but a divine expression of His holy desire for righteousness among humankind. Yet, the children of men had no righteous work to offer Him; instead, they gave Him vinegar a symbol of sin and corruption as the Psalmist prophesied:

“For my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.” (Psalm 69:21)

✍🏾 This reveals that God thirsts for the righteous deeds of His children. He longs for their faithfulness, purity, and good works, and He rejoices when He finds righteousness dwelling within them.

✍🏾

The Scripture declares:

“For the eyes of the Lord run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to show Himself strong on behalf of those whose heart is perfect toward Him.” (2 Chronicles 16:9)

✍🏾 God’s eyes are fixed upon the righteous. His servant David said:

“The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears are open to their cry.” (Psalm 34:15)

Thus, He not only sees their works but listens to their prayers with compassion.

The wise Solomon also wrote:

“The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.” (Proverbs 15:3)

✍🏾 This means that God observes all people, but His favor rests especially upon those who sincerely seek truth and righteousness.

✍🏾

Our holy father Abba Hiriakos, in the Eucharistic thanksgiving of the Blessed Virgin Mary, beautifully expressed this mystery, saying:

“God searched all the ends of the earth, and found none like you.
He loved your fragrance, He loved your blood, and sent His beloved Son to you.” (Holy Mary, verse 24)

This prayer reminds us that God continually seeks the fragrance of righteousness among His creation a life filled with faith, purity, and good works.

Continuing our meditation on the holy Beatitude, “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled,” we learn that the true satisfaction of the soul comes only from God, who rewards those who seek Him with faith and sincerity.

✍🏾

text.text: Those Who Seek God Wholeheartedly Will Find Him

text:
The Holy Scripture testifies:

“From there you will seek the Lord your God, and you will find Him if you seek Him with all your heart and with all your soul.” (Deuteronomy 4:29)

Again, the prophet Jeremiah declares:

“You will seek Me and find Me when you seek Me with all your heart.” (Jeremiah 29:13)

And the book of Proverbs proclaims:

“I love those who love Me, and those who seek Me diligently will find Me.” (Proverbs 8:17)

✍🏾 These holy words confirm that God reveals Himself to those who earnestly search for Him, not with divided hearts but with full devotion, love, and perseverance.

✍🏾

text.text: How God Satisfies the Hungry and Thirsty Soul

text:
The Lord, in His mercy, satisfies the spiritual hunger and thirst of His children through divine means:

👉🏾 He satisfies the hunger and thirst for His Holy Word through the true teachers of the Gospel who proclaim His truth faithfully.

👉🏾 He satisfies the hunger and thirst for His Holy Body and Precious Blood through the holy priests who serve the Divine Liturgy.

👉🏾 He establishes those who hunger and thirst in His house through prayer and fellowship.

👉🏾 He builds up the faithful by strengthening their faith and guiding their conduct according to His will.

✍🏾The covenant He gave us “They shall be filled” is not temporary but perfect and eternal. It assures us that all who seek Him in truth will never remain empty.

The promise “they shall be filled” reveals the immeasurable kindness and generosity of God. He not only satisfies the needs of His people but fills them with overflowing grace and joy.

As our Lord said:

“I have come that they may have life, and have it more abundantly.” (John 10:10)

He knows what our souls need and provides far more than we could ever ask or imagine.

Saint Paul, the apostle, also teaches:

“My God shall supply all your needs according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:19)

And again:

“Now to Him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us.” (Ephesians 3:20)

✍🏾 God’s generosity has no limit. When He gives, He gives in fullness both in this life and in the life to come. Therefore, those who hunger and thirst for righteousness shall be filled with divine wisdom, holiness, and eternal joy.

text.text: Examples of the Righteous Who Hungered and Thirsted for God

text:
We have many saints who labored for righteousness: prophets, apostles, fathers, martyrs, and righteous men of every generation. Yet above all, our Lord Himself became the model of perfect righteousness during His life in the flesh.

✍🏾 Our Father Abraham  the first to seek God with unwavering faith.
Scripture says, “He believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness” (Gen. 15:6).

👉🏾 Saint Paul teaches, “If Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about but not before God. For what does the Scripture say? Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness” (Rom. 4:1–3).

👉🏾 And again: “Know therefore that those who are of faith are the children of Abraham. The Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith and proclaimed the good news to Abraham, saying, ‘In you all nations shall be blessed.’ So then, those who are of faith are blessed with Abraham the faithful” (Gal. 3:6–9).

✍🏾 The Epistle to the Hebrews explains it beautifully:
“By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place he would later receive as an inheritance, not knowing where he was going. By faith he lived in tents with Isaac and Jacob, heirs of the same promise. For he looked for the city which has foundations, whose builder and maker is God. By faith Sarah herself received strength to conceive, even though she was past age, because she considered Him faithful who had promised. And from one man, as good as dead, came descendants as numerous as the stars of heaven and as the sand on the seashore” (Heb. 11:8–12).

✍🏾

The holy David, the man after God’s own heart, spoke often of his thirst for righteousness. Saint Ephraim, in the Hymn of the Blessed Virgin Mary, recalls an event that revealed the depth of David’s virtue.

When David was besieged by his enemies, he longed to drink water from the well of Bethlehem. Three of his mighty men broke through the enemy lines, risked their lives, and brought him that water. But when David saw the danger they had faced for his sake, he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out before the Lord, saying, “Is it not the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?” (2 Sam. 23:15–17; 1 Chr. 11:17–19).

✍🏾 By choosing righteousness over his own thirst, David showed humility, love, and reverence for the lives of his soldiers. He refused to satisfy his earthly desire at the cost of their blood. This act was counted to him as righteousness forever.

👉🏾The wise interpret this moment as a foreshadowing of our Lord Jesus Christ, who, out of divine righteousness and love, poured out His own blood for the salvation of humankind.

text:
Dear beloved in Christ, followers of the Orthodox faith, we greet you in the name of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. Continuing our lesson on the holy Beatitude, “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled,” we learn that the true satisfaction of the soul comes only from God, who rewards those who seek Him with faith and sincerity.

✍🏾

The Holy Evangelist Luke tells of a righteous and devout man in Jerusalem named Simeon, who was waiting for the consolation of Israel. The Holy Spirit had revealed to him that he would not die before seeing the Lord’s Anointed.

Moved by the Spirit, he entered the temple. When the holy parents brought the Child Jesus to fulfill the requirements of the Law, Simeon took Him into his arms and blessed God, saying:

“Lord, now You are letting Your servant depart in peace, according to Your word;for my eyes have seen Your salvation,which You have prepared before all peoples a light for revelation to the Gentiles,and the glory of Your people Israel.” (Luke 2:29–32)

Joseph and the Virgin Mary were amazed at what was spoken about Him. Simeon also blessed them and said to Mary:

 "This Child is appointed for the fall and rising of many in Israel,
and for a sign to be opposed,
so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.
And a sword shall pierce your own soul also.” (Luke 2:34–35)

text.text: ✍🏾Our Lord Jesus Christ, the Sun of Righteousness

text:
Our Lord Jesus Christ, who took on human flesh for our redemption and for our example, is the Sun of Righteousness and the perfection of holiness. He taught us to hunger and thirst for righteousness not only by His words but by the entirety of His life.

He proclaimed:

“Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness.”

👉🏾And He fulfilled this teaching through His works:

👉🏾His humble birth in a stable taught us meekness and lowliness of heart.

👉🏾His exile to Egypt blessed our own trials and sufferings.

👉🏾His fasting sanctified the practice of fasting for all believers.

👉🏾His baptism in the Jordan established the mystery of baptism for the Church.

👉🏾His life among the poor and tax collectors revealed mercy and compassion.

👉🏾His miracles healed the bodies of the sick, and His teachings healed the souls of the wounded.

👉🏾His cleansing of the temple showed holy zeal for the purity of God’s house.

👉🏾His crucifixion gave us His holy flesh and precious blood for our salvation.

👉🏾His resurrection on the third day made Him the firstfruits of the resurrection for all humanity.

✍🏾Christ alone satisfies those who hunger and thirst for righteousness. In every step of His earthly life, He became the perfect example for us, calling us to strive for righteous deeds and a pure heart before God.

Dear followers of the Orthodox faith , we greet you with the peace of God. On this blessed day, we present to you the following teaching for your reflection and spiritual benefit.

✍🏾

text.text: The Exile of the Holy Family

text:
The Lady of all creation, the Queen of Heaven, the Blessed Virgin Mary, gave birth to her Son, our Lord and God Jesus Christ, and later descended into the land of Egypt with Him.

As written in the Holy Gospel, when our Lord was two years old, wise men came from the East to Bethlehem and worshipped Him, offering gold, frankincense, and myrrh (Matthew 2:1–18).

When Herod heard that a King had been born, he ordered the slaughter of one hundred forty-four thousand innocent children. At the command of Saint Gabriel, the Holy Virgin Mary took her only Son, together with Joseph the Righteous and Saint Salome, and fled into exile with only a donkey and a few provisions.

She left Galilee and entered the land of Egypt, traveling under great hardship. She suffered hunger, thirst, sorrow, cold, heat, and fatigue. Her tears fell, her feet bled, and her strength was exhausted. Though she carried the Bread of Life, she herself became hungry. Though she carried the Water of Life, she herself became thirsty. All of this she endured for our salvation.

It is said that only Satan fails to honor the Virgin Mary. Even animals, plants, and stones honor the Mother of God. Saint Joseph the Righteous and Saint Salome also deserve honor, for they accepted the suffering of exile with the Virgin and her holy Son.

✍🏾

text.text: Why the Savior Was Exiled to Egypt and Ethiopia

text:
The exile of our Lord Jesus Christ to Egypt and Ethiopia was not without purpose:

1. To fulfill prophecy:
“Behold, the Lord rides on a swift cloud and will come to Egypt” (Isaiah 19:1; Hebrews 3:7).

2. To follow the pattern of His forefathers:
Abraham, Jacob, and the prophet Jeremiah all dwelt in Egypt

3. To destroy idolatry in Egypt:
As prophesied in Isaiah 19:1.

4. To sanctify the monasteries of Egypt and Ethiopia.

5. To reveal the truth of His humanity:If He were not truly man, He would not have experienced exile. Even if Herod had found Him, He could not have harmed Him without His divine permission, especially concerning His saving Passion on Friday.

6. To bless future exiles and martyrs.

7. To atone for Adam’s persecution through His own suffering.

✍🏾The Journey Through Egypt and Ethiopia

text:
Tradition teaches that the Virgin Mary remained in exile for three years and six months (forty-two months). When she fled from Herod, she first traveled from Galilee to the border of Syria (Debre Libanos).

When Saint Gigar, who had hidden them, was put to death by Herod, the Holy Virgin went down into Egypt. remaining there for a long time and moving from place to place. She passed through barren wildernesses and remote deserts.

Later, she entered the northern part of Ethiopia, arriving at Debre Bizen (present-day Eritrea). From there she blessed Debre Damo, Aksum, Debre Abay, Waldba, and reached Lake Tana. She stayed especially at Tana Kirkos for one hundred days. She then traveled to Gojam, blessing Debre Libanos, Debre wegeg, and Debre Hazelo. Regions she did not reach on foot she blessed by cloud and vision. She received Ethiopia as a tithe together with her beloved Son.

Tradition states that it was here in Ethiopia that the angel Gabriel announced to her the death of Herod.

The Mother of Light entered Debre qusquam carrying food and gifts brought by the people of our land (the land of Ophir) on five camels, and there she rested joyfully with Joseph and Salome. Four hundred years after the persecution of Christ, on this same day, the mountain of Debre qusquam in Egypt was built and sanctified as a dwelling-place of saints.

It is also said that around the year 390, our Lord Jesus Christ descended upon Debre Kusquam with His Virgin Mother, the holy apostles, thousands of angels, the righteous, and the martyrs. At that time, the Patriarch of Alexandria, Saint Theophilos, together with the great Saint Cyril, built the church, gathered the faithful, and protected it. The Lord then sanctified the place and filled it with joy.

✍🏾This day is a day of great joy for all Christians, so let us rejoice. The Lord of heaven and earth, who endured persecution for our sake, returned from exile on this day. If we remember her suffering and feel sorrow, we must also remember her return and rejoice.

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings , we greet you with the peace of God. Today, in honor of the Feast of Debre Qusquam, we offer you this important teaching and encourage you to read and learn from it.

✍🏾

Mount Qusquam is a mountain in southern Egypt. Mount Qusquam is the place where Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, along with Saint Joseph and Saint Salome, rested when they returned from exile.

✍🏾Mount Qusquam is also the place where our Lord Jesus fled from those who wanted to kill Him and found refuge, and where Saint Gabriel announced to Saint Joseph in a dream that King Herod had died.

✍🏾This is according to the Holy Gospel: when Herod wanted to kill Christ, the angel of God, Saint Gabriel, appeared to the aged Joseph in a dream and said, "Take the child and his mother and flee to Egypt" (Matthew 2:13–15).

✍🏾

✍🏾Mount Qusquam is blessed and sanctified because our Lord performed many miracles there. Regarding the sacredness of this mountain, Saint Theophilos, Archbishop of Alexandria, said in his sermon on the Assumption of Mary: "This is a mountain that is higher than all the mountains of the world. In it dwells the Holy God. The Son of God loved and honored this mountain, and He dwelled with His Holy Mother above all the nations of the world. text: Dear followers of the Orthodox faith  peace be unto you. Today we present a refined teaching on the life of the Great Martyr Saint George. May it strengthen your faith.

text.text: ✍🏾The Birth and Early Life of Saint George

text:
saint George, the Great Martyr, whose name means “bright star” or “sun,” was born in Palestine in the city of Lydda. He was born on Tir 20, 277 AD.

His father, Zorothos (Anastasius), was a nobleman of Lydda. His mother, Theobsta (Ecclesia), was a devout Christian woman. Besides Saint George, she had two daughters named Martha and Asia.

When Saint George was ten years old, his father passed away. A righteous Christian king took him in and raised him with love. Under this prince, George learned military discipline and grew in both strength and wisdom.

When Saint George reached twenty years of age, the king had a beautiful fifteen-year-old daughter. During a great feast, the prince declared, “Let George marry her and inherit all my possessions.” Soon after making this promise, our Lord, whose will was different, took the soul of the king.”This saddened George deeply, and after completing the days of mourning, he traveled to Beirut.

At that time, the people of Beirut worshipped a dragon and even sacrificed their own daughters to it. Seeing this terrible practice, Saint George confronted the dragon. Armed with faith and the power of the Holy Cross, he defeated the dragon and turned the hearts of the people toward the worship of the true God.

✍🏾

text.text: Confession of Faith Before Seventy Kings

text:
When Saint George later returned to Persia, Emperor Dudianus assembled seventy kings and set up seventy idols for worship. Seeing this, and being committed to the Christian faith, Saint George boldly entered the palace and confessed before them all that he was a follower of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

Dudianus, recognizing him, said, “You are one of us. I will appoint you ruler over ten regions if you worship my god Apollo.”
Saint George answered, “Your titles and rewards belong to you. I will not deny my Lord Jesus Christ.”

In rage, Dudianus ordered severe tortures. But Saint George prayed, “Do not take my life until I have put this apostate to shame.” God heard him and strengthened him. Even after dying three times from torture, the Lord raised him again, granting him great endurance.

Among the many torments he endured:

• He was tied to a tree and beaten while his flesh was torn with iron.

• Iron shoes with long nails were forced onto his feet, and he was ordered to walk.
God sent Saint Michael to heal him

• He was pierced with seventy nails, burned on the head, struck with a hammer, and rolled with a wooden beam tied to his stomach.

• His flesh was cut with a saw, and salt was sprinkled onto the wounds.

• His body was chopped into pieces, yet our Lord Jesus Christ healed him at midnight and strengthened him again.

The Lord said to him, “You will struggle for My name for six more years. You will die three times and rise in the fourth time. I will not leave you in your sufferings.”

text:
“Hidar 7 is the day on which the Holy House of Saint George is celebrated, the faithful witness of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, the sun of Persia and Lydda, the star of Tarsus and Beirut, the light of the sea and the radiance of the day.”

Saint George completed his martyrdom on Miyaziya 23. The faithful prepared precious garments and perfumes, wrapped his holy body, and brought it to Lydda. But upon arrival, they found that his entire family his father Zorothos, his mother Theobsta, his sisters Martha and Asia, and his betrothed had passed away.

An uncle named Andrew received the body. The people gathered, and the Archbishop of Jerusalem, Abba Tewodros, was called. He consecrated a church in Saint George’s honor and placed the holy body there with reverence. From that day, many miracles were manifested.

✍🏾

Our wise King Menelik brought soil from the tomb of Saint George in Lydda, transporting it by ship and mule. He used this holy soil as the foundation when building the church of Saint George, surrounding it with strong, blessed walls

The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church honors Saint George on:

• Miyaziya 23 – His day of rest (martyrdom)

• Hidar 7 – The celebration of his liturgy and the feast of his Holy House.

• Tir 18 – The commemoration of his burial (Zerwote Atsmu).
