text:
Dear beloved in Christ, followers of the Orthodox faith, we greet you in the name of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. Continuing our lesson on the holy Beatitude, “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled,” we learn that the true satisfaction of the soul comes only from God, who rewards those who seek Him with faith and sincerity.

✍🏾

✍🏾The fourth Beatitude is translated in some Amharic Bibles as “those who hunger and thirst for righteousness.” Some understand this to refer to those who physically hunger and thirst during fasting, seeking righteousness through spiritual discipline. Because the expression “they shall be satisfied” can appear ambiguous, this translation is used to give clarity.

✍🏾Although we recognize the deep meaning behind hungering and thirsting for righteousness, we continue to use the phrase “those who hunger and thirst for righteousness,” as it is also taught in the other Oriental Orthodox Churches and is well understood. True hungering and thirsting for righteousness includes the spiritual longing for righteousness and the willingness to struggle for it. A person who hungers for righteousness puts forth effort to obtain it, and this includes the discipline of fasting.

✍🏾For this reason, the teachers of the Church explain that hungering and thirsting for righteousness is closely linked with fasting.

👉🏾Saint Paul teaches in Romans 14:17:

“The kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.”

👉🏾Again in 1 Corinthians 8:8 he says:“Food does not bring us closer to God; we are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.”This reveals the spiritual value of fasting.

👉🏾He further teaches in 1 Corinthians 6:13:

👉🏾“Food is for the stomach, and the stomach for food; but God will destroy them both.”
Through this he shows that fasting is a work of righteousness. Therefore, fasting and thirsting for righteousness are inseparably connected.

✍🏾Since the purpose of the Church is to guide mankind toward righteousness, the ultimate goal of the Christian life is to attain righteousness. This is achieved through continuous striving. Our Lord taught in Matthew 7:7–11:

Continuing our lesson on the holy Beatitude, “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled,” we learn that the true satisfaction of the soul comes only from God, who rewards those who seek Him with faith and sincerity.

✍🏾Hungering and Thirsting for Righteousness

✍🏾The fourth Beatitude is translated in some Amharic Bibles as “those who hunger and thirst for righteousness.” Some understand this to refer to those who physically hunger and thirst during fasting, seeking righteousness through spiritual discipline. Because the expression “they shall be satisfied” can appear ambiguous, this translation is used to give clarity.

✍🏾Although we recognize the deep meaning behind hungering and thirsting for righteousness, we continue to use the phrase “those who hunger and thirst for righteousness,” as it is also taught in the other Oriental Orthodox Churches and is well understood. True hungering and thirsting for righteousness includes the spiritual longing for righteousness and the willingness to struggle for it. A person who hungers for righteousness puts forth effort to obtain it, and this includes the discipline of fasting.

✍🏾For this reason, the teachers of the Church explain that hungering and thirsting for righteousness is closely linked with fasting.

👉🏾Saint Paul teaches in Romans 14:17:

“The kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.”

👉🏾Again in 1 Corinthians 8:8 he says:“Food does not bring us closer to God; we are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.”This reveals the spiritual value of fasting.

👉🏾He further teaches in 1 Corinthians 6:13:

👉🏾“Food is for the stomach, and the stomach for food; but God will destroy them both.”
Through this he shows that fasting is a work of righteousness. Therefore, fasting and thirsting for righteousness are inseparably connected.

✍🏾Since the purpose of the Church is to guide mankind toward righteousness, the ultimate goal of the Christian life is to attain righteousness. This is achieved through continuous striving. Our Lord taught in Matthew 7:7–11:

Continues 👇🏾

text:
✍🏾“Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you. Everyone who asks receives; and he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened. Or which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a serpent? If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him?” (Matthew 7:7-11)

✍🏾 In this teaching, our Lord assures us that God grants righteousness to those who earnestly seek it:

👉🏾He gives righteousness to those who ask.

👉🏾He grants righteousness to those who seek.

👉🏾He opens the door of righteousness to those who knock.

✍🏾 Just as a loving earthly father provides good gifts to his children, so our heavenly Father abundantly gives what is good to those who desire righteousness and draw near to Him with faith and sincerity.

The first step in striving for righteousness is cleansing from sin. Just as a physically ill person loses appetite and does not feel hunger or thirst, a person living in sin has little desire for righteousness. A sick person may not enjoy food even when he eats it; likewise, a sinner does not enjoy spiritual things.

But when the sick recover, their appetite returns. In the same way, when a sinner repents and washes away his sins, he begins to hunger and thirst for righteousness again. Therefore, one must separate himself from sin in order to develop spiritual hunger.

✍🏾Just as the immediate need of a hungry and thirsty person is food and water (James 2:15–16), the immediate duty of the one who hungers for righteousness is to strive for righteousness alone. And the goal of this striving must be the attainment of righteousness.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings ,we greet you with the peace of God. Today, based on the the above mentioned title, we present to you the following teaching and entrust all of you to read and learn from it.

✍🏾“Blessed are the merciful, for they will find mercy”

Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ taught in the fifth Beatitude:
“Blessed are the merciful, for they will obtain mercy.” (Matthew 5:7)

Mercy is a union of three virtues:

👉🏾 Compassion

👉🏾 Kindness

👉🏾 Forgiveness

👉🏾

is the feeling of the heart that understands others, feels for them, makes their pain our own, and moves us to help them.

👉🏾

is sharing what we have wealth, knowledge, strength, and other blessings with those who lack them, expecting nothing in return.

👉🏾

means pardoning those who have harmed us, even when they do not deserve forgiveness, and letting go of anger or punishment.

Kindness and forgiveness flow from a compassionate heart.

Church scholars teach that mercy is of two kinds:

👉🏾 Physical mercy

👉🏾 Spiritual mercy

Physical mercy is providing what a person in need lacks.

Spiritual mercy is helping a person repent from sin and return to God.

✍🏾

The place where our Lord Jesus Christ healed the sick in body through miracles and healed the sick in soul through His teachings is known as “Awde Mihret,” meaning “the Square of Mercy.”
Even today, the platform from which the Gospel is proclaimed in the church bears this name to show that the Church is the place of mercy.

The Church, redeemed by the precious blood of Christ, is where people show mercy to one another and where God shows mercy to His people. From the days of our forefathers until now, the Church has preserved this identity as the Square of Mercy.

✍🏾

May the God of Mercy be the One who grants us mercy throughout our lives. In this fifth beatitude(Anketse Bitsuan), we reflect on:

👉🏾 the mercy of God

👉🏾 the power of mercy

👉🏾 and the righteous leaders who became examples of mercy.

✍🏾God is a God of mercy. He is kind and compassionate, slow to anger and full of steadfast love. Showing mercy is His nature. For this reason, the Church praises Him saying:

“Glory to the King,Glory to the God of mercy.”To show mercy is to imitate God.

King David, the one after God’s own heart, said:

👉🏾“The Lord is merciful and forgiving, slow to anger and abundant in kindness.He will not always rebuke, nor will He keep His anger forever.He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us according to our iniquities.As the heavens are high above the earth, so great is His mercy toward those who fear Him.As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us.”

✍🏾The prophet Jeremiah also declared:

✍🏾“It is because of the Lord’s steadfast love that we are not consumed,for His mercies never fail.” (Lamentations 3:22)

👉🏾This teaches us that we live only because of His unfailing compassion.

text:
Answer :- My Child, You ask a question as deep as the sea. To hold the Holy Bible in your hands is to hold a universe of meaning. Many in this world see it as a mere book of history, a collection of ancient laws, or a source of moral stories. But for us, the children of the Holy Church, it is something infinitely more.

Let us sit together in the stillness of our hearts and understand what this sacred treasure truly is.

text.text: It is a Love Letter from God

text:
.

Imagine you are in a distant land, far from your father's house. You are lonely, confused, and have forgotten the way home. Then, a messenger arrives, bearing a letter. It is from your Father. In it, He tells you of His boundless love for you. He reminds you who you are, where you came from, and how to find your way back to His embrace. He warns you of the dangers on the road and promises to be with you always.

This, my child, is the Holy Bible. It is God the Father's letter to His exiled children, written not with ink, but with the very breath of the Holy Spirit through the hands of His chosen prophets and apostles. As the Apostle Paul teaches, "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness" (2 Timothy 3:16).

text.text: It is the Testimony of the Living Word.

text:
The Holy Bible is the divinely inspired collection of writings that reveals God’s work in creation, His covenant with His people, His laws, His prophets, and ultimately His salvation given through our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

The Bible is not a book about many things; it is a book about One Person: our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ. He is the Living Word of God, and the Bible is the written Word that points to Him on every page.

In the Old Testament, He is promised, prophesied, and foreshadowed. Adam is a type of Christ who was to come. The sacrifice of Isaac points to His sacrifice. The Ark of Noah is a symbol of the salvation in His Church. The prophets spoke of His coming, His suffering, and His glory. Our Lord Himself said to those who studied the scriptures without seeing Him: "You search the scriptures, for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and these are they which testify of me" (John 5:39).

In the New Testament, He is revealed. The Gospels are the icon of His life on earth. The Epistles are the explanation of His life within us. The Revelation of St. John is the vision of His ultimate victory.

text.text: It is a Pharmacy for the Soul.

text:
The Holy Fathers, like St. John Chrysostom, do not call the Bible a library, but a spiritual pharmacy. Are you sick with the fever of anger? There is a psalm to cool you. Are you wounded by the arrow of despair? There is a Gospel passage to be a healing balm. Are you weak from the temptations of the flesh? There is an apostolic word to give you strength.

It is food for the hungry, water for the thirsty, and a lamp for those walking in darkness. As the Prophet-King David sings, "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path" (Psalm 118:105, LXX).

The Holy Fathers, like St. John Chrysostom, do not call the Bible a library, but a spiritual pharmacy. Are you sick with the fever of anger? There is a psalm to cool you. Are you wounded by the arrow of despair? There is a Gospel passage to be a healing balm. Are you weak from the temptations of the flesh? There is an apostolic word to give you strength.

It is food for the hungry, water for the thirsty, and a lamp for those walking in darkness. As the Prophet-King David sings, "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path" (Psalm 118:105, LXX).

Continues 👇🏾

It is the Book of the Church.

text:
This is a truth of great importance, my child. The Bible did not fall from heaven into the hands of individuals. It was born from the womb of the Holy Church. It was the Church that wrote it, the Church that compiled it, the Church that preserved it, and it is only within the Church, guided by her Holy Tradition, that it can be truly and safely understood. To try and interpret the Bible on your own, apart from the mind of the Holy Fathers who have guided us for two thousand years, is to set sail on a vast ocean without a compass or a rudder.

Our Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, in its ancient wisdom, has preserved the fullness of this divine letter, including sacred books like Enoch and Jubilees, which testify to the richness of the faith handed down to us.

So, when you next pick up the Holy Bible, do not treat it as any other book. First, make the sign of the cross. Say a prayer, asking the Holy Spirit who inspired its words to illuminate your mind. Read it not to win arguments, but to meet Christ. Read it slowly, and let its words wash over you, cleanse you, and heal you.

It is God Himself speaking to you. Listen with all your heart.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings ,we greet you with the peace of God. Today, based on the the above mentioned title, we present to you the following teaching and entrust all of you to read and learn from it.

✍🏾God’s Mercy Revealed on the Cross

✍🏾First, the prophet Isaiah testified to the boundless mercy of God shown through the suffering of Christ:

“Surely He has borne our griefs and carried our sorrows; yet we considered Him stricken, smitten by God, and afflicted. But He was wounded for our transgressions, He was bruised for our iniquities; the chastisement for our peace was upon Him, and by His stripes we are healed.” (Isaiah 53:4-5)
Through His suffering, He carried our sins and revealed the depth of His mercy.

✍🏾Again, through the prophet Ezekiel, the Lord declared His desire not for destruction, but for repentance and life:

“Do I have any pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord God? Is it not that he should turn from his way and live?” (Ezekiel 18:23)
Christ accepted the cross so that humanity might turn back from its wicked ways.

✍🏾God, who seeks not the ruin of humanity but its restoration, showed mercy to the people of Nineveh. When they returned through fasting and prayer,
“God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God relented from the disaster He had said He would bring upon them.” (Jonah 3:10)

This same mercy reached its fullness at the Cross, when our Lord prayed,

“Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.” (Luke 23:34)
And as He taught,“Greater love has no one than this, than to lay down one’s life for his friends.” (John 15:13)

He revealed His perfect love by giving His life for all.

✍🏾

👉🏾The Lord forgives all who come to Him with repentance, for His heart is rich in compassion. Scripture says of Him:

“When He saw the multitudes, He had compassion on them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.” (Matthew 9:36)

✍🏾When the prophet Nathan rebuked King David, David replied:
“I am in great distress; let me fall into the hand of the Lord, for His mercies are great; but let me not fall into the hand of man.”
(2 Samuel 24:14)

For truly, “The Lord desires mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.” (Hosea 6:6)
Therefore, we also must hold mercy in the highest honor.

✍🏾

text.text: God Gives Mercy to Every Heart That Truly Asks

text:
God gives mercy to anyone who asks with a sincere heart. Our Lord says in the Gospel, “Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives, and he who seeks finds, and to him who knocks it will be opened.” Matthew 7:7 to 8 shows that He grants mercy to all who ask with their whole heart. This is why we pray, “Lord, Christ, the Merciful.”

👉🏾David understood this well. He prayed, “Have mercy on me, O Lord, according to your lovingkindness; according to the multitude of your tender mercies blot out my transgressions. Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. For I acknowledge my transgressions, and my sin is ever before me. Against you, you only, have I sinned, and done evil in your sight.” Psalm 51:1 to 4 gives us a model of honest repentance. With the same spirit he said, “But as for me, in the multitude of your lovingkindness I will come into your house; in your fear I will worship toward your holy temple,” Psalm 5:7. We also rise early, drawn by His mercy, and come before Him.

👉🏾Luke tells us of the tax collector who “stood far off, would not even lift his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast and said, God, be merciful to me a sinner.” Luke 18:13 shows a humility we are meant to learn from. When we seek mercy with this kind of heart, we should also show mercy to those who have wronged us.

text.text: God Shows Mercy to the Weak, the Despised, and the Helpless

text:
Saint Luke shows us that God’s mercy reaches those whom society rejects. The tax collector, considered one of the despised of his time, “stood far off and would not even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, i am sinner.’” Because of his humility, he received greater mercy than the proud Pharisee and returned to his house justified (Luke 18:13–14). God lifts up those who lower themselves before Him.

✍🏾

When our Lord saw Zacchaeus climbing a tree to see Him, He said, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.” Zacchaeus came down quickly and welcomed Him joyfully. The crowd murmured because Jesus chose to stay with a sinner, but Zacchaeus stood before the Lord and said, “Lord, half of my possessions I will give to the poor, and if I have taken anything from anyone unjustly, I will restore it fourfold.”Jesus declared, “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham” (Luke 19:5–9). Mercy transformed his life and brought salvation to his home.

✍🏾

At the Pool of Bethesda, a helpless man cried out, “Lord, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred; and while I am coming, another steps down before me” (John 5:7). The Lord saw his suffering and had mercy on him, commanding him to rise, take up his bed, and walk. His weakness became a moment of divine compassion and healing.

Saint Yohannes Afewerk teaches that mercy is profound wisdom and a strong shield for those who practice it. He explains that mercy is the companion of God, standing beside Him and blessing those whom He loves. It should never be despised, for through its purity it grants great spiritual freedom to all who live by it.

He continues by saying that mercy has great power, especially when shown to the rejected and to those who have fallen into sin. Mercy breaks chains, extinguishes burning trials, removes corruption, and takes away the gnashing of teeth. Through mercy, the gates of heaven are opened with ease. In summary, “mercy is the queen who makes a person resemble God.”
(Chrysostom, Commentary on James 2:13)

✍🏾

text.text: The Main Characteristics of Mercy in the Bible

text: Using the above teaching as a foundation, we now consider the primary qualities of mercy as revealed in Holy Scripture.

text.text: 1. Mercy Is a Virtue Through Which We Imitate God

text:
True Christians are called to imitate Christ. Showing mercy is one of the essential virtues by which we resemble our Lord. God is merciful, kind, and forgiving.

Our Lord teaches us directly:
“Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful” (Luke 6:36).

Saint Paul also instructs us to follow Christ’s example, saying,
“Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, just as God in Christ forgave you” (Ephesians 4:32).

✍🏾Mercy Is Given Freely by God

The mercy God has shown us is not something we earned. The apostle teaches,

“He saved us, not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to His mercy, by the washing of regeneration and renewing of the Holy Spirit” (Titus 3:5).Therefore, when we show mercy, it must be genuine, wholehearted, and without discrimination.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings ,we greet you with the peace of God. Today, based on the verse above, we present to you the following important lesson. We entrust you all to read it with diligence and learn from it.

✍🏾God Shows Mercy to the Weak, the Despised, and the Helpless

Saint Luke shows us that God’s mercy reaches those whom society rejects. The tax collector, considered one of the despised of his time, “stood far off and would not even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, i am sinner.’” Because of his humility, he received greater mercy than the proud Pharisee and returned to his house justified (Luke 18:13–14). God lifts up those who lower themselves before Him.

✍🏾Zacchaeus the Tax Collector

When our Lord saw Zacchaeus climbing a tree to see Him, He said, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.” Zacchaeus came down quickly and welcomed Him joyfully. The crowd murmured because Jesus chose to stay with a sinner, but Zacchaeus stood before the Lord and said, “Lord, half of my possessions I will give to the poor, and if I have taken anything from anyone unjustly, I will restore it fourfold.”Jesus declared, “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham” (Luke 19:5–9). Mercy transformed his life and brought salvation to his home.

✍🏾The Helpless Man at Bethesda

At the Pool of Bethesda, a helpless man cried out, “Lord, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred; and while I am coming, another steps down before me” (John 5:7). The Lord saw his suffering and had mercy on him, commanding him to rise, take up his bed, and walk. His weakness became a moment of divine compassion and healing.

✍🏾The Power of Mercy

Saint Yohannes Afewerk teaches that mercy is profound wisdom and a strong shield for those who practice it. He explains that mercy is the companion of God, standing beside Him and blessing those whom He loves. It should never be despised, for through its purity it grants great spiritual freedom to all who live by it.

He continues by saying that mercy has great power, especially when shown to the rejected and to those who have fallen into sin. Mercy breaks chains, extinguishes burning trials, removes corruption, and takes away the gnashing of teeth. Through mercy, the gates of heaven are opened with ease. In summary, “mercy is the queen who makes a person resemble God.”
(Chrysostom, Commentary on James 2:13)

✍🏾The Main Characteristics of Mercy in the Bible

Using the above teaching as a foundation, we now consider the primary qualities of mercy as revealed in Holy Scripture.

1. Mercy Is a Virtue Through Which We Imitate God

True Christians are called to imitate Christ. Showing mercy is one of the essential virtues by which we resemble our Lord. God is merciful, kind, and forgiving.

Our Lord teaches us directly:
“Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful” (Luke 6:36).

Saint Paul also instructs us to follow Christ’s example, saying,
“Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, just as God in Christ forgave you” (Ephesians 4:32).

✍🏾Mercy Is Given Freely by God

The mercy God has shown us is not something we earned. The apostle teaches,

“He saved us, not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to His mercy, by the washing of regeneration and renewing of the Holy Spirit” (Titus 3:5).Therefore, when we show mercy, it must be genuine, wholehearted, and without discrimination.

Continues 👇🏾

text.text: 2. Showing Mercy as an Expression of Love

text:
Showing mercy is one of the clearest signs that love truly lives in the heart. God the Son became man so that humanity could receive divine mercy, and He calls us to reflect this same mercy toward one another. Love is not proven by repeating the words “I love you,” but by showing compassion, kindness, and forgiveness from the heart.

Our Lord teaches that this love must extend even beyond those who care for us. It includes those who oppose us, misunderstand us, or treat us with hostility.

Matt. 5:45-47 teaches that God “makes His sun rise on the evil and the good.” Just as Christ showed mercy even to those who crucified Him, we are called to imitate Him by showing mercy to all human beings without discrimination. As it is written, “Love works kindness” (1 Cor. 13:4).

Our Lord also taught us the meaning of true love:

👉🏾“Do to others as you would have them do to you. For if you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them. And if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same. And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to receive back. But love your enemies, and do good, hoping for nothing in return, and your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High. For He is kind to the ungrateful and the evil.”
(Luke 6:31-35)

This teaching shows that mercy is not just an action; it is the outward expression of genuine love. True Christian love reaches beyond those who love us and embraces even our enemies, just as God shows kindness to all, including the ungrateful and the wicked.

3. Mercy as a Requirement on the Day of Judgment

text:
Doing works of mercy is not optional for a Christian; it is something we will be asked about on the Day of Judgment. Our Lord taught:

👉🏾“When you give a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind. You will be blessed, because they cannot repay you. You will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
(Luke 14:13-15)

The righteous will inherit the kingdom because they practiced mercy throughout their lives. Our Lord said:

“Then the King will say to those on His right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry and you gave Me food; I was thirsty and you gave Me drink; I was a stranger and you welcomed Me; I was naked and you clothed Me; I was sick and you visited Me; I was in prison and you came to Me.’

Then the righteous will answer Him, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You drink? When did we see You a stranger and welcome You, or naked and clothe You? When did we see You sick or in prison and visit You?’

And the King will answer, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these My brothers, you did it to Me."(Matthew 25:34-40)

But those who refused to show mercy will face judgment:

“Then He will say to those on the left, ‘Depart from Me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels. For I was hungry and you did not feed Me; I was thirsty and you did not give Me drink; I was a stranger and you did not welcome Me; I was naked and you did not clothe Me; I was sick and in prison and you did not visit Me.’

They will answer, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison and did not minister to You?’

Then He will reply, ‘Truly I tell you, inasmuch as you did not do it for one of the least of these, you did not do it to Me.’

And they will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”
(Matthew 25:41-46)

This teaching shows that mercy is one of the defining marks of those who belong to the Kingdom of God.

text: Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings we greet you with the peace of God. Today, based on the topic mentioned earlier, we present to you the following important teaching, and we entrust you all to read and learn from it:

text.text: ✍🏾 The Meaning of the Name Michael

text:
The name Michael in Hebrew is composed of three parts:

“Mi” meaning “Who”( ማን)

“Ka” meaning “like”( እንደ)

“El” meaning “God"( እግዚአብሔር )

When read together, it means “Who is like God?”

This name expresses the humility and reverence of the archangel who proclaims that no being can be compared with God.

✍🏾

Saint John the Evangelist testified in his vision, saying, “I saw the seven angels who stand before God.” Among these, God chose and appointed Saint Michael as the chief of the seven archangels.

On Hidar 12, our Church celebrates the feast of this great angel with honor and splendor. When God cast Satan down because of his pride, Saint Michael was appointed in his place over the heavenly hosts, the ten cities and the hundred orders of angels.

✍🏾

text.text: His Guardianship Over the People of God

text:
The authority of Saint Michael is not limited only to the angels, but also extends to the people of God. This truth is shown clearly in the Old Testament, where he is revealed as the protector of Israel, the chosen people of God.

👉🏾For example, Scripture tells us that Saint Michael appeared to Joshua near Jericho:

“He lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a man stood before him with a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua went to him and said, ‘Are you for us or for our adversaries?’ And he said, ‘As the captain of the army of the Lord, I have now come.’”(Joshua 5:13)

His Leadership in the Exodus

When God delivered Israel from slavery in Egypt, Saint Michael was the angel appointed to lead them. Since his charge was over the people of God, he fought against the devil on their behalf and strengthened them through intercession. Yet when they sinned, God allowed punishment to fall on them, for the angel’s authority carried both protection and judgment.

God warned them clearly: “Beware of him. Obey his voice; do not provoke him, for My name is in him.” (Exodus 23:21)

✍🏾

This reveals why Saint Michael was placed over God’s people. And if the passages above are not enough to show that it was Saint Michael guiding Israel, the book of Daniel makes it unmistakable. Saint Gabriel told Daniel that Michael had been sent and held special authority over God’s people. Gabriel declared: “I will tell you what is written in the book of truth. There is none who stands with me in these matters except Michael your prince.” (Daniel 10:21)

From this testimony, we understand that the angel who appeared to Joshua and who led the people of Israel was indeed Saint Michael.

✍🏾

text.text: His Role Continues in the New Testament

text:
The role of Saint Michael continues in the New Testament, as the prophet said in his vision: “At that time Michael, the great prince who stands for the children of your people, will arise” (Dan. 12:1). Therefore, Saint Michael is also our leader, protecting us from the snares and traps of Satan and standing before God in prayer on our behalf. For we are the people of God and heirs of His inheritance.

God appointed the prophet Moses as the leader of His people because he was exceedingly humble and loved them to the point of offering his own life for their sake (Num. 12:3; Ex. 32:32). His leadership was not for domination or control, but for redeeming the people through teaching, intercession, and guidance. This is why Saint Stephen testified, saying, “God sent him as ruler and redeemer” (Acts 7:35). In the same way, Saint Michael serves as a guardian and intercessor for God’s people.

✍🏾Saint Michael: Protector and Intercessor of God’s People

✍🏾Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ taught that the holy angels protect and help us, standing before Him on our behalf, saying, “See that you do not despise one of these little ones; for their angels always see the face of my Father in heaven.” (Matthew 18:10)

✍🏾 If even the angels assigned to protect us care so deeply and are so zealous for our salvation, how much more does Saint Michael, exalted in holiness as the chief of the angels, intercede for us before God? (Luke 13:6-9)

✍🏾Psalm 33:2 reminds us of his role: He “stands up for the children of Your people.” This shows clearly that Saint Michael helps us live righteous lives through his prayers and intercession, using the authority and power given to him by God.

May the prayers and blessings of the Archangel Saint Michael be upon us forever!

text.text: 4. He Who Shows Mercy Will Receive Mercy

text:
Showing mercy is not only a virtue but a living proclamation of God’s own mercy. Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ taught, “For with the judgment you judge, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you” (Matthew 7:2). Those who practice mercy will themselves receive mercy.

He also taught, “Whatever you want men to do to you, do also to them, for this is the Law and the Prophets” (Matthew 7:12). Anyone who desires to be shown mercy must extend mercy to others.

👉🏾King David, the one after God’s own heart, said: “Blessed is he who considers the poor; the Lord will deliver him in the day of trouble. The Lord will preserve him and keep him alive; he will be blessed on the earth; and You will not deliver him to the will of his enemies” (Psalm 41:1). Mercy opens the door for mercy.

✍🏾In teaching us how to pray, Our Lord said, “Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors” (Matthew 6:12). He added, “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you; but if you do not forgive men, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses” (Matthew 6:14–15). Forgiveness is the path to receiving forgiveness.

Furthermore, He taught: “If you bring your gift to the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift” (Matthew 5:23–24). Mercy and reconciliation come before sacrifice.

✍🏾Also, “Whenever you stand praying, if you have anything against anyone, forgive him, that your Father in heaven may also forgive you your trespasses” (Mark 11:25–26).

Saint Peter once asked our Lord, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Up to seven times?” Jesus responded, “Not seven times, but seventy times seven” (Matthew 18:21–22). Forgiveness must not be limited, but continual.

And He said to the Pharisees: “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick. Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance” (Matthew 9:12–13). This teaches that mercy comes before sacrifice.

Saint James also teaches, “For judgment is without mercy to the one who has shown no mercy; mercy triumphs over judgment” (James 2:13).

Saint Augustine taught: “Even if you think you possess wealth, you still need eternal life. You hear the voice of the poor who ask from you, but you also ask before God. As you treat the one who asks you, so God will treat you.”

“My fellow,” he explains, means “a poor person like me.” Even those who have a little wealth on earth remain poor before God.

Saint Yohannes Afewerk teaches: “Blessed are the merciful, for they shall learn.” The mercy a person shows cannot be compared to the mercy God shows. Human mercy is small; God’s mercy is beyond measure. When a person offers a little mercy, God grants abundant mercy in return.

5. He Who Does Not Show Mercy Will Not Receive Mercy

text:
The wise Solomon said, “Whoever shuts his ears to the cry of the poor will also cry himself and not be heard” (Proverbs 21:13). One who refuses mercy will not find mercy.

The rich man was condemned for not showing mercy to Lazarus (Luke 16:19–31). A person who denies mercy not only loses the mercy due to them but also risks having the mercy previously given taken away. God shows mercy so that we may imitate Him toward our neighbor.


Our Lord taught this clearly through a parable:
“The kingdom of heaven is like a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants. As he began the reckoning, one was brought to him who owed ten thousand talents. Since he could not pay, the master commanded that he, his wife, his children, and all he had be sold so that payment might be made.

The servant fell before him and pleaded, ‘Lord, have patience with me, and I will repay you everything.’ The master was moved with compassion, released him, and forgave the entire debt.

But that same servant went out and found a fellow servant who owed him one hundred denarii. He seized him and began to choke him, saying, ‘Pay me what you owe.’ His fellow servant fell at his feet and begged him, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you.’ Yet he refused and threw him into prison until the debt was paid.

When the other servants saw what had happened, they were deeply grieved, and they reported everything to their master. The master summoned him and said, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you pleaded with me. Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had mercy on you?’ In anger, the master delivered him to the tormentors until he should repay all that was owed.

Our Lord concludes: ‘So will My heavenly Father do to each of you, if you do not forgive your brother from your heart.’”
(Matthew 18:23–35)

Question :-Will animals go to heaven? My friemd was making reference to Romans 8:21-22 Any information on animal afterlife?

Answer :-My dear child, your question about animals in the afterlife, and your friend's reference to the powerful words of St. Paul in Romans 8:21-22, touches a chord in many hearts, for indeed, we witness the suffering of all creation and naturally yearn for its redemption. It is a compassionate and insightful question.

Let us turn our hearts and minds to the wisdom of the Holy Spirit, as revealed in Scripture and understood by the Holy Fathers.

You mentioned:
👉🏾Romans 8:21: "Because the creation itself also will be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God."

👉🏾Romans 8:22: "For we know that the whole creation groans and labors with birth pangs together until now."

These verses are profoundly significant. St. Paul is speaking here of the cosmic redemption that awaits all creation, not just humanity. When Adam and Eve fell into sin, their sin had repercussions not only for humanity but for the entire created order, subjecting it to decay, suffering, and death what St. Paul calls "the bondage of corruption." The "groaning" of creation is its suffering under the curse of sin, awaiting its liberation.

Now, concerning animals specifically and their place in this redemption:

1.  The Restoration of Creation, Not Individual Animal Souls in the Human Sense:

The Orthodox understanding, drawing from the Fathers, emphasizes that while God loves and cares for all His creation, the "heaven" or eternal life promised to humanity is fundamentally different from what might be understood for animals.

✍🏾Human beings are created in the image and likeness of God, possessing an immortal, rational, spiritual soul capable of communion with God, of moral choice, repentance, and personal salvation unto deification (theosis). Our eternal destiny is a personal, conscious relationship with the Creator in His Kingdom.

✍🏾Animals possess a "soul" (psyche or nephesh* in Hebrew, meaning "life principle"), which gives them life, sensation, and instinct. However, this is generally understood not to be an immortal, rational, spiritual soul in the same way as human souls. Animals do not have moral responsibility, nor do they seek personal communion with God in the way humans do. Therefore, their "salvation" or "afterlife" is not understood in terms of individual, conscious, eternal existence in the same manner as for humans.

2.  The New Heavens and New Earth:

When St. Paul speaks of creation being "delivered from the bondage of corruption," he points to the New Creation—the "new heavens and a new earth" spoken of in Isaiah (65:17) and Revelation (21:1). This will be a transfigured, glorified creation, where the effects of the Fall are utterly removed. There will be no more suffering, decay, or death.

In this renewed creation, it is a pious and beautiful hope that animals, in some transfigured form, will indeed be present. The Prophet Isaiah gives us wonderful imagery of this harmonious new creation: "The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them" (Isaiah 11:6, Septuagint). This suggests a world where the natural order, currently scarred by predation and suffering, is restored to its original peaceful state of harmony as God intended.

Continues 👇🏾

text:
Our Lord Himself taught that not a single sparrow falls to the ground without our Father's knowledge (Matthew 10:29). This speaks to God's immense providence and love for all His creatures. While we may not fully comprehend the ultimate destiny of individual animals, we trust in God's perfect wisdom and goodness, knowing that His plan for the restoration of creation is comprehensive and glorious.

So, to summarize, my dear child: the Holy Scriptures and the wisdom of the Fathers point to a future where all creation, including the animal kingdom, will be freed from the corruption and suffering caused by sin, participating in the glorious liberty of the children of God in the new heavens and new earth. While this is not understood as individual animals having an immortal soul and conscious eternal life like humans, it is a profound affirmation of God's love and ultimate redemption for everything He has made.

Our Lord Himself taught that not a single sparrow falls to the ground without our Father's knowledge (Matthew 10:29). This speaks to God's immense providence and love for all His creatures. While we may not fully comprehend the ultimate destiny of individual animals, we trust in God's perfect wisdom and goodness, knowing that His plan for the restoration of creation is comprehensive and glorious.

So, to summarize, my dear child: the Holy Scriptures and the wisdom of the Fathers point to a future where all creation, including the animal kingdom, will be freed from the corruption and suffering caused by sin, participating in the glorious liberty of the children of God in the new heavens and new earth. While this is not understood as individual animals having an immortal soul and conscious eternal life like humans, it is a profound affirmation of God's love and ultimate redemption for everything He has made.

✍🏾 There are 14 feasts of Saint Michael in a year. They are:

✍🏾 There are 14 feasts of Saint Michael celebrated throughout the year. Each commemorates a specific act of protection, mercy, or deliverance that God performed through His archangel.
The day Saint Michael was appointed to lead the people of Israel, where he defeated the devil.
The day when thousands of angels gathered and celebrated the feast together. It is known as The Day of the Thousands of Angels.
The day he helped Duratwas and his wife Theobstan.
The day he helped the poor boy Telafinos and protected Jacob from his brother Esau.
The day he appeared in human form to a man who had nothing to eat, drink, or wear, became a guarantor for him when he borrowed money, helped Samson, and destroyed the nations.
The day he spoke to Balaam’s donkey and saved a man named Matthew and his wife and children.
The day he brought Adam into Paradise and released the prophet Jeremiah from prison.
The day he lifted the prophet Habakkuk by a strand of his hair, carried him from Jerusalem to Babylon where Daniel was imprisoned, and fed Daniel in the lions’ den.”
The day he rescued Bahran from the sea and saved Afomiya from Satan.
The day he rescued the poor boy Telhasa from the sea, defeated King Sennacherib and the army of the Assyrians, and saved the righteous King Hezekiah.
The day he saved Sosna from the rebenat and helped Emperor Constantine defeat Maximian.
The day Saint Raphael offered the annual incense of prayer before God.
The day he helped the martyr Fasilides, and when the prophet Isaiah visited and advised King Hezekiah.

The day the prophet Samuel anointed David as king, and Saint Michael stood with him. On this feast he presents 14 petitions before the Creator.

✍🏾Saint yared teaches that the petitions of Saint Michael are fourteen. These are the supplications he offers to the Creator on each of his fourteen feasts, asking for mercy and forgiveness for humankind.

✍🏾Therefore, we should always remember the feasts of Saint Michael, which are celebrated every month of the year.

"The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear Him, and delivers them." (Psalm 34:7)

May the intercession of the Archangel Saint Michael never leave us!

✍🏾 There are 14 feasts of Saint Michael in a year. They are:

✍🏾 There are 14 feasts of Saint Michael celebrated throughout the year. Each commemorates a specific act of protection, mercy, or deliverance that God performed through His archangel.

1. Hidar 12
The day Saint Michael was appointed to lead the people of Israel, where he defeated the devil.

2. Hidar 13
The day when thousands of angels gathered and celebrated the feast together. It is known as The Day of the Thousands of Angels.

3. Tahisas 12
The day he helped Duratwas and his wife Theobstan.

4. Tir 12
The day he helped the poor boy Telafinos and protected Jacob from his brother Esau.

5. Yekatit 12
The day he appeared in human form to a man who had nothing to eat, drink, or wear, became a guarantor for him when he borrowed money, helped Samson, and destroyed the nations.

6. Megabit 12
The day he spoke to Balaam’s donkey and saved a man named Matthew and his wife and children.

7. Miyaziya 12
The day he brought Adam into Paradise and released the prophet Jeremiah from prison.

8. Ginbot 12
The day he lifted the prophet Habakkuk by a strand of his hair, carried him from Jerusalem to Babylon where Daniel was imprisoned, and fed Daniel in the lions’ den.”

9. Sene 12
The day he rescued Bahran from the sea and saved Afomiya from Satan.

10. Hamle 12
The day he rescued the poor boy Telhasa from the sea, defeated King Sennacherib and the army of the Assyrians, and saved the righteous King Hezekiah.

11. Nehase 12
The day he saved Sosna from the rebenat and helped Emperor Constantine defeat Maximian.

12. Pagume 3
The day Saint Raphael offered the annual incense of prayer before God.

13. Meskerem 12
The day he helped the martyr Fasilides, and when the prophet Isaiah visited and advised King Hezekiah.

14. Tikimt 12
The day the prophet Samuel anointed David as king, and Saint Michael stood with him. On this feast he presents 14 petitions before the Creator.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teaching we greet you with the peace of God. Today, according to the topic mentioned above, we present to you this important teaching, and we entrust you to read and learn from it:

✍🏾 “Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to serve those who will inherit salvation?” Heb. 1:14

✍🏾 On this day, our Church Fathers instruct us to commemorate the Feast of the Holy Angels, celebrated on Hidar 13.

✍🏾 The Church celebrates this feast according to the order established by our Fathers, who were guided by the Holy Spirit.

The first and highest ministry of the holy angels is to praise the God who created them. In their unceasing worship they glorify, honor, and exalt Him, saying: “Holy, holy, holy, Lord of Spirits, your creation fills the earth.” Enoch 9:39; Isaiah 6:2-4.

As it is written: “You are worthy, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power, for You created all things, and by Your will they existed and were created.” Revelation 4:11.

The angels praise the God of gods, the Lord of lords, and the King of kings.

👉🏾Saint John the Evangelist also describes their worship:
“I looked and heard the voice of many angels around the throne… and their number was myriads of myriads. They said with a loud voice, ‘Worthy is the Lamb who was slain, to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing.’ And every creature in heaven, on earth, under the earth, and in the sea said, ‘Blessing and honor and glory and might be to the One seated on the throne and to the Lamb forever and ever.’” Revelation 5:11-14.

In addition to this divine ministry of praise and thanksgiving, the holy angels also serve as manifestations of the power, goodness, and mercy of their Creator toward His creation. Their ministry is especially revealed in their care for Adam and all his children throughout history.

✍🏾

The names used for angels in Scripture and in the tradition of the Church all point to their identity as messengers and servants of God. Each term highlights a different aspect of their ministry.

• (
Means “to send.” The root shows their role as those who are sent by God.

Means “the one who is sent” or “the sender.”
Example: “When the Jews sent to ask him…” John 1:19.

•

Means “sent” or “one who serves.”
Example: “She arose and served them.” Matthew 8:15.
It shows the angelic role of carrying out God’s works.

•

A general meaning, expressing their obedience and service to the will of the Creator.

•

Means “sent, messenger, servant.”
Example: “The messenger of our Lord…” 1 Peter 1:1.
This emphasizes both being sent and being a servant.

•
Used in the Acts of the Apostles to describe one who is dispatched for a divine purpose.

Means “messenger” or “servant.”
Example: “They are messengers…” Romans 13:4.

•

This refers to a written message or letter, such as “The Epistle of the Apostle John.” 1 John 1:1.
The word connects angels with the concept of delivering God’s message.

•
According to Amharic grammar, “angel” means a messenger of God, a heavenly and divine being created to serve His will.

✍🏾The Ministry of the Holy Angels

The first and highest ministry of the holy angels is to praise the God who created them. In their unceasing worship they glorify, honor, and exalt Him, saying: “Holy, holy, holy, Lord of Spirits, your creation fills the earth.” Enoch 9:39; Isaiah 6:2-4.

“I looked and heard the voice of many angels around the throne… and their number was myriads of myriads. They said with a loud voice, ‘Worthy is the Lamb who was slain, to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing.’ And every creature in heaven, on earth, under the earth, and in the sea said, ‘Blessing and honor and glory and might be to the One seated on the throne and to the Lamb forever and ever.’” Revelation 5:11-14.

In addition to this divine ministry of praise and thanksgiving, the holy angels also serve as manifestations of the power, goodness, and mercy of their Creator toward His creation. Their ministry is especially revealed in their care for Adam and all his children throughout history.

✍🏾The Meaning of Their Names

The names used for angels in Scripture and in the tradition of the Church all point to their identity as messengers and servants of God. Each term highlights a different aspect of their ministry.

• (መላክ)Melak
Means “to send.” The root shows their role as those who are sent by God.

• (ላኪ )Laki
Means “the one who is sent” or “the sender.”
Example: “When the Jews sent to ask him…” John 1:19.

• (ተልእከ) (Tel-e-k)
Means “sent” or “one who serves.”
Example: “She arose and served them.” Matthew 8:15.
It shows the angelic role of carrying out God’s works.

• Servant
A general meaning, expressing their obedience and service to the will of the Creator.

• (ልኡክ) Li-uk
Means “sent, messenger, servant.”
Example: “The messenger of our Lord…” 1 Peter 1:1.
This emphasizes both being sent and being a servant.

• “Emissary”
Used in the Acts of the Apostles to describe one who is dispatched for a divine purpose.

• (ላእከ) La-e-ke
Means “messenger” or “servant.”
Example: “They are messengers…” Romans 13:4.

• Message
This refers to a written message or letter, such as “The Epistle of the Apostle John.” 1 John 1:1.
The word connects angels with the concept of delivering God’s message.

• Angel
According to Amharic grammar, “angel” means a messenger of God, a heavenly and divine being created to serve His will.

Continues 👇🏾

text:
The nature of the holy angels is subtle and spiritual. They are spirits, not physical beings.
They cannot be touched or seen with bodily eyes, they have no flesh and bones, they do not marry, and they are not given in marriage, meaning they have no natural power to reproduce.(Luke 24:39, Matthew 22:30)

Teachings of the Church Scholars About the Nature of Angels

The scholars of the Church have handed down two explanations regarding the nature of the angels:

This view teaches that angels were created from a spiritual and fiery nature.
Its basis is Psalm 103:4:
“He makes His angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire.”

According to this understanding, angels are described as spiritual beings with a fiery, luminous nature, fitting their role as God’s servants and messengers.

text.text: 2. “Unsearchable nature” (A nature known only to God)

text:
Another teaching of the Church Fathers states that the nature of angels is mysterious and cannot be fully described, for it is known only to God.

Saint Epiphanius of Cyprus, in his book Aximaros, argues that if angels were simply made of wind and fire, then death would have power over them, since these elements belong to the created world.He notes that even Adam, while in the flesh, triumphed over death by God’s grace.

Therefore, Epiphanius teaches that the angels’ nature is not of earthly or elemental substance, but from a hidden nature known only to God.
As he writes:“No one knows what the nature of angels is, except God alone.”

He also teaches that God created the angels on Sunday and established them in three heavenly ranks:Ior, Rama, and Erer (as recorded in Aximaros).

text: Dear followers of the Orthodox teaching, we greet you with the peace of God. Today, according to the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following teaching, and we entrust you to read and learn from it:

Fasting of the Prophets: This is one of the seven great fasts of the Church. It is observed every year from Hidar 15 until the eve of the Nativity.

✍🏾 The Fast of the Prophets lasts for 44 days before the Nativity. During this fast, the faithful remember the fulfillment of the prophecies spoken by the prophets and the completion of the 5500 years of human suffering.

✍🏾When God the Father willed to save the world, the prophets guided by the Holy Spirit prophesied in every generation about:

👉🏾 His taking on human flesh

👉🏾 His flight into Egypt

👉🏾 His baptism in the Jordan River

👉🏾 His enlightening the darkened world through His teaching

👉🏾 His suffering for the salvation of mankind

👉🏾 His crucifixion and death

👉🏾 His resurrection, ascension, and second coming

✍🏾 The prophets longed to see these prophecies fulfilled. They prayed and fasted, saying, “Stretch out Your strength and stretch out Your hand.” They counted days, weeks, months, and years, waiting for the moment when God would become man for the salvation of the world.

✍🏾

Dear followers of the Orthodox teaching, we greet you with the peace of God. Today, according to the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following teaching, and we entrust you to read and learn from it:

✍🏾The Fast of the Prophets

Fasting of the Prophets: This is one of the seven great fasts of the Church. It is observed every year from Hidar 15 until the eve of the Nativity.

✍🏾 The Fast of the Prophets lasts for 44 days before the Nativity. During this fast, the faithful remember the fulfillment of the prophecies spoken by the prophets and the completion of the 5500 years of human suffering.

✍🏾When God the Father willed to save the world, the prophets guided by the Holy Spirit prophesied in every generation about:

👉🏾 His taking on human flesh

👉🏾 His flight into Egypt

👉🏾 His baptism in the Jordan River

👉🏾 His enlightening the darkened world through His teaching

👉🏾 His suffering for the salvation of mankind

👉🏾 His crucifixion and death

👉🏾 His resurrection, ascension, and second coming

✍🏾 The prophets longed to see these prophecies fulfilled. They prayed and fasted, saying, “Stretch out Your strength and stretch out Your hand.” They counted days, weeks, months, and years, waiting for the moment when God would become man for the salvation of the world.

✍🏾Names and Significance of the Fast

✍🏾The Fast of the Prophets is called the “Fast of the Prophets (tsome Nebiyat)” because it commemorates the fulfillment of the prophecies and prayers of the holy prophets who awaited the birth of our Lord.

👉🏾 It is also called the “Fast of Adam(tsome adam)” because it marks the fulfillment of the promise of salvation given to Adam.

👉🏾It is called the “Fast of the Sermon” (tsome sibket )because it is a time when the gospel about the birth of Christ is widely preached.

👉🏾The fast ends on the day of the Nativity, which is why it is also known as the “Fast of the Nativity.”(tsome lidet)

👉🏾 It is called the “Fast of the Apostles”(tsome hawaryat) because the holy apostles said, “We fast on the day of the Resurrection, and what do we do on the day of the Nativity?” They observed the fast that the prophets observed before the birth of Christ.

👉🏾 It is also called “Philip’s Fast”(tsome filipos). The Apostle Saint Philip traveled throughout Africa, teaching the Gospel in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, performing miracles, and converting many to the faith. He died as a martyr among those who rejected his teachings. When his disciples were about to bury his body, they observed a week of fasting and prayer, asking God to return the body of the apostle to them. God granted their request, and his body was returned on the third day and buried in glory.

👉🏾 After finding the body of the apostle, his disciples continued the fast until the birth of our Lord. That is why the prophets also call it “Philip’s Fast.”

✍🏾Additionally, after the angel Gabriel announced to the Holy Virgin Mary that she would conceive the Son of God through the Holy Spirit, our Lady observed a fast before giving birth, saying, “What shall I do, since I have conceived a God whom heaven and earth cannot contain?” This fast is therefore also known as the “Fast of Mary.”(tsome Mariam)

Continues 👇🏾

text: Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on the, we greet you in the name of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important teaching. May each of you read, learn, and benefit from it.

“Qebela” means preparing oneself to fast. Preparation includes readiness of both spirit and body.

Fasting is practiced by
👉🏾 Strengthening the spirit through prayer

👉🏾 Training the stomach through abstinence

According to the interpretation of Saint Yared, fasting is not only refraining from food, but also avoiding all forms of evil:

👉🏾 Seeing evil

👉🏾 Speaking evil

👉🏾 Hearing evil

👉🏾 Touching evil

👉🏾 Walking toward evil

True fasting is guarding all these spiritual senses.

The eve of the fast is a time to welcome the fast with thanksgiving and joy, preparing the soul to enter the season of blessing. It is not a time to indulge in uncommon or excessive foods and drinks “because the fast is coming.” Such practices have no spiritual or religious basis.

✍🏾

Meaning of the Word “Qebela”

The word Qebela comes from the Gë`ëz term “Tekebele”, which means:

to receive

to welcome

to accept

✍🏾

Semune Qebela refers to the week of preparing ourselves to receive the fast. It is the period when the faithful ready their bodies and souls before the official beginning of the fast.

It is a time of:

staying spiritually awake

preparing the body through discipline

preparing the soul through repentance and prayer

getting ready to enter the fast with reverence

Just as someone cleans and arranges their house to welcome an honored guest, a Christian prepares his or her heart to welcome the great “guest,” which is the fast itself.

✍🏾

Although Qebela is meant to be a week of spiritual readiness, unfortunately, many activities seen today such as noise, unnecessary celebrations, eating and drinking in excess, and general distraction do not reflect the true meaning of Qebela.These behaviors do not prepare the soul to meet the fast.

Originally, Qebela existed because Christians desired to meet the fast properly, just as one receives a noble visitor with honor and cleanliness of heart.

According to the teachings of the Apostles, fasting is:

The foundation of Christian life

A sign of imitating God

A life of self-control and moderation

Fasting is therefore not just avoiding food, but ordering one’s entire life toward God.

Accepting the fast improperly is itself a mistake. God desires everything to be done decently and in order (1 Corinthians 14:40). The fast should be welcomed with guidance from a priest, with proper internal and external preparation.
This includes:

seeking guidance from one’s priest

preparing both outwardly and inwardly

entering the fast with repentance, prayer, and humility

Fasting is not something to be avoided or taken lightly. It is a gift that requires readiness, respect, and spiritual awareness.

✍🏾How to Accept the Fast

a. Preparation of Conscience

text:
In the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, Sabbaths, feasts, and holy days are given a special welcome on the eve through prayer, hymns, teachings, and spiritual gatherings.

A similar pattern is found in Jewish practice:
At sunset on Friday, the approach of the Sabbath is announced. The people gather, bow toward the rising sun, pray, recite the Ten Commandments, and light candles, saying, “Welcome, Sabbath.” They then share a simple meal and spend the night in praise.

In the same way, Qebela marks the period from the end of the Fast of Nineveh until the eve of the Great Fast, during which priests, monks, nuns, and believers make preparations to welcome the fast.

The great scholar Abba Dioscorus teaches about the greatness of the Fast of our Lord:

“He lived in the wilderness of Corinth for 40 days and 40 nights in order to fast as a man. He was tempted by the devil in three ways so that He might overcome for our sake. By His lordship He defeated the army of the evil one who had been contending for 5,500 years and ruling in darkness.”

This reminds us that the fast is not ordinary. It is a divine gift that Christ Himself sanctified through His example.

When we fast in this world following the example of our Lord Jesus Christ, we prepare so that:

👉🏾to Defeat the enemy

👉🏾to Receive grace, blessings, and spiritual strength

text.text: b. Spiritual Preparation Before the Fast

text:
During this season, our fathers in the monasteries and convents:

👉🏾Prepare offerings and spiritual materials

👉🏾Choose places where they will spend the eight weeks

👉🏾 Prepare prayer books

👉🏾 Plan their time for fasting, prayer, and almsgiving

👉🏾 Meet the faithful to gather candles, incense, raisins, and clothing

👉🏾 Speak with their spiritual children, giving advice and consolation

👉🏾 Encourage confession: “Do not be ashamed to confess your sins” (Sirach 4:26)

👉🏾 Reconcile with those from whom they are estranged

👉🏾 Plan to spend nights in prayer and days in the Divine Liturgy

This is the true spirit of preparing for the fast.

✍🏾Misunderstanding of Fasting Today

Sadly, in many places, fasting has become associated with feasting, eating rich foods, drinking wine, and indulging in excess actions that contradict the very purpose of fasting.

As Saint Peter warns:
“Be sober and vigilant, for your enemy the devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.” (1 Peter 5:8)

Excessive celebrations weaken the soul and open doors to temptation.

May the Fast Purify Our Bodies and Souls

May the fast be for us a source of blessing, spiritual renewal, and victory over the enemy.

May the Lord accept our fasting, our prayers, and our repentance.

Dear friends who follow the Orthodox teachings we greet you with the peace of God. Today, according to the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important teaching and ask each of you to read and learn from it with understanding.

✍🏾

text.text: The Seven Canonical Fasts of the EOTC

text:
The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church observes seven officially decreed fasts. These are:

1. The Great Fast (Abiy tsom )

2. The Fast of the Apostles ( Tsome Hawaryat )

3. The Fast of the Assumption (St. Mary’s Fast) Tsome Felseta

4. The Fast of the Prophets (Tsome Nebiyat)

5. The Fast of Gehad or gad )

6. The Fast of Nineveh( Tsome Nenewe)

7. Tsome Dihnet :-The Weekly Fast (Wednesdays and Fridays)

These fasts have been practiced from ancient times, and each carries a spiritual purpose for the growth and salvation of the believer.

✍🏾Teachings on Fasting from the Holy Books

The Holy Scriptures, along with ancient Church books such as Haymanote Abew and Fetha Negest, give instructions on how the faithful should fast.

a. Haymanote Abew (Three Centuries), Chapter 20:18–29

Do not break the fast commanded by the Lord, especially Wednesday and Friday, unless due to sickness.

Even on major feast days such as Pentecost, Epiphany, or baptisms, Wednesday and Friday fasting is kept, except for the ill.

Those who observe Abiy Tsom must keep the fast with great care, especially during the seven days before Easter (Semune Hammamat).

If a brother visits you to eat during your voluntary fast (such as Monday, Tuesday, or Thursday), eat with him in love and good conscience, but do not neglect the mandatory fasts of Wednesday, Friday, and the Forty Days.

Fasting on Saturday until sunset is not encouraged. There are times when fasting on Saturday is appropriate, but never until the sixth or seventh hour (sunset).

On Sunday morning, go to church early, avoiding distraction, and stand with reverence throughout the Divine Liturgy, reflecting on the suffering, death, and resurrection of Christ.

✍🏾Guidance for Proper Fasting

a. Learning from the Fathers

text: The book “Ask Your Father and He Will Tell You” teaches that we must learn how to fast from the holy fathers and follow their footsteps.

Saint Epiphanius says:
“A person whose mother is not the Church cannot have God as Father.”
Without the Church, it is impossible to know God, and without God, it is impossible to know the Church.

Therefore, it is the duty of every Christian to:

attend church regularly

learn the Word of God

pray faithfully

receive the Holy Body and Blood of Christ . as the Fathers say, "the Church is for Christians".

This devotion should increase even more during fasts.

✍🏾

During fasting:

The soul becomes master over the body.

The soul governs, instructs, and disciplines the flesh.

A person who does good becomes holy in both soul and body and inherits the Kingdom of Heaven.

One who does evil loses both body and soul to destruction.

When Scripture calls someone a sinner, it means the will of the flesh has conquered him.
When it calls someone righteous, it means he has conquered the desires of the flesh and brought his soul into obedience to God.

The life of a Christian is therefore a constant struggle between the will of the soul and the will of the flesh.


The Holy Scriptures teach that fasting is a time of:

humility

prayer

repentance

(Ezekiel 8:21; Nehemiah 1:4; Daniel 9:3)

Therefore, we must enter fasting with a humble heart, seeking the mercy of God and purifying our lives through sincere repentance.

text.text: 6. Showing Mercy Made the Samaritan Stand Out From the Priest and the Levite

text:
Our Lord teaches that mercy toward those in need reveals the true servant of God. In the Parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:30–37), He said:

✍🏾A man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among robbers who stripped him, beat him, and left him half dead. A priest happened to come down that way, saw him, and passed by on the other side. Likewise, a Levite came, saw him, and passed by. But a Samaritan, as he traveled, came to where the man was; and when he saw him, he had compassion. He approached him, bound his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He placed him on his own donkey, brought him to an inn, and cared for him. The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper, saying, “Take care of him; and whatever more you spend, when I return, I will repay you.”

After telling the parable, the Lord said:

“Which of these three was a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?”The reply was, “He who showed mercy.”Then the Lord said, “Go and do likewise.”

In this, Christ teaches that what made the Samaritan more favored than the priest and the Levite was his kindness and compassion. Mercy, not position or title, makes one pleasing to God.

Saint Paul gives the same instruction when he says:
“Remember the prisoners as if you were bound with them, and those who suffer, as if you yourselves were in the body.” (Hebrews 13:3)
We are called to stand with the suffering as though their pain were our own.

text.text: 7. A Heart Filled With Mercy Shows Compassion Even to Sinners

text:
A merciful heart does not measure a person by their failures. Instead, it sees the image of God in every soul and desires their restoration.

When the scribes and Pharisees brought to Christ the woman caught in adultery, they demanded judgment. Christ instead revealed the truth of all humanity: “Let the one who is without sin be the first to cast a stone.” When they left one by one, acknowledging their own sin, Christ told the woman, “Neither do I condemn you; go, and sin no more.” (John 8:11)

He teaches us not to stand as judges like the Pharisees, but to offer mercy as He did.

text:
✍🏾As the Evangelist Luke writes, a Pharisee named Simon invited our Lord to eat with him. The Lord entered Simon’s house and reclined at the table. A woman from the city, known to be a sinner, heard that He was in the house. She brought an alabaster jar of perfume and stood behind Him at His feet. Overcome with sorrow, she wept, and her tears fell upon His feet. She washed His feet with her tears, wiped them with the hair of her head, kissed His feet continually, and anointed them with the perfume.

When Simon saw this, he said within himself, “If this man were truly a prophet, He would know who and what kind of woman is touching Him, for she is a sinner.” Perceiving his thoughts, our Lord spoke and said, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” Simon replied, “Speak, Master.”

Our Lord said, “A certain creditor had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty. When they had nothing to repay, he forgave them both. Which of them, then, will love him more?” Simon answered, “I suppose the one who was forgiven more.” The Lord said to him, “You have judged rightly.”

Turning toward the woman, He said to Simon:
“Do you see this woman? I entered your house; you gave Me no water for My feet, but she washed My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair. You gave Me no greeting, but she has not ceased to kiss My feet from the moment I entered. You did not anoint My head with oil, but she has anointed My feet with perfume. Therefore I tell you: her many sins are forgiven, for she has loved much. But the one who is forgiven little loves little.”

Then He said to the woman, “Your sins are forgiven. Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

In this holy event, the Lord teaches us to show mercy rather than judgment, to welcome the repentant, and to imitate His compassion toward every sinner who returns with a humble heart.

Faithful Examples

✍🏾

Joseph held great authority in the land of Egypt, yet he showed extraordinary mercy to his brothers who betrayed him, threw him into a pit, and sold him into slavery. He forgave them without recalling the years of suffering he endured because of their actions. Instead of seeking repayment or revenge, he provided them with grain during the famine so they would not die of hunger. He welcomed them and their families to live safely in Egypt and pardoned all the wrong they had done to him.
(Genesis 50:21)

✍🏾

Moses also stands as a model of mercy. He pleaded earnestly before God on behalf of the children of Israel, who repeatedly rebelled against Him. He bowed before the Lord and said:

“Lord, if I have found favor in Your sight, let my Lord go among us, for we are a stiff-necked people. Forgive our wickedness and our sin, and accept us as Your inheritance.”(Exodus 34:9)

Again, when the people committed the great sin of making the golden calf, Moses interceded for them with remarkable selflessness, saying:
“O Lord, this people has committed a great sin and made for themselves gods of gold. Now forgive their sin; but if not, blot me out of the book You have written.”
(Exodus 32:32)

In both examples, Moses shows a shepherd’s heart, choosing mercy even when the people had deeply wounded both God and himself.

He forgave them without recalling the years of suffering he endured because of their actions. Instead of seeking repayment or revenge, he provided them with grain during the famine so they would not die of hunger. He welcomed them and their families to live safely in Egypt and pardoned all the wrong they had done to him.
(Genesis 50:21)

✍🏾The Great Prophet Moses

Moses also stands as a model of mercy. He pleaded earnestly before God on behalf of the children of Israel, who repeatedly rebelled against Him. He bowed before the Lord and said:

“Lord, if I have found favor in Your sight, let my Lord go among us, for we are a stiff-necked people. Forgive our wickedness and our sin, and accept us as Your inheritance.”(Exodus 34:9)

Again, when the people committed the great sin of making the golden calf, Moses interceded for them with remarkable selflessness, saying:
“O Lord, this people has committed a great sin and made for themselves gods of gold. Now forgive their sin; but if not, blot me out of the book You have written.”
(Exodus 32:32)

In both examples, Moses shows a shepherd’s heart, choosing mercy even when the people had deeply wounded both God and himself.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.

text.text: The Meaning and Purpose of Fasting

text:
The prophet Isaiah said, “Is this the fast that I have chosen? Should a man humble his soul on such a day? Should he humble himself like a reed, and spread sackcloth and ashes under his feet?” (Isaiah 58:5)

✍🏾 The reed (Engcha) is a type of grass that grows near water. In the Old Testament, priests sometimes referred to it in their rituals, saying, “The Lord is tried, the devil is bound.” When a reed grows, it bends and lowers itself naturally.

✍🏾 Isaiah teaches us to humble ourselves like the reed. True fasting is not about outward display but inner humility: “Humble yourselves like a reed,” meaning, fast sincerely and quietly, without seeking praise or showing off.

✍🏾 Fasting is a time to treasure humility and allow it to grow. A true Christian is one who endures trials patiently, listens carefully, and submits willingly to God’s will.

✍🏾 The prophet Ezra also emphasizes humility in fasting, saying, “I proclaimed a fast there by the Ahava River, that we might humble ourselves before our God, and seek from him a right way for us and our children and all our possessions” (Ezra 8:21). Through fasting, we submit ourselves fully to God and seek His guidance in all aspects of our lives.

✍🏾

Fasting is not a human tradition. It is God Himself who established it. When God commanded Adam and Eve, “You shall not eat of the tree,” He gave humanity the first commandment, which is the foundation of fasting.

Adam lost his glory because he broke God’s law through food. Likewise, if we fast, we gain blessing; but if we neglect fasting, we lose spiritual grace.

✍🏾

King David said, “My flesh grows weak for lack of fatness.” (Psalm 109:24)

Daniel also said, “I ate no pleasant bread; neither came meat nor wine into my mouth.” (Daniel 10:3)

These verses teach us to abstain from the foods forbidden during the fasting seasons.

Saint Paul explains that fasting directs us toward God:
“Food does not bring us closer to God; we are no worse if we do not eat and no better if we do.” (Romans 14:7; 1 Corinthians 8:8)

This shows that fasting is a spiritual act that draws the heart nearer to God.

The Holy Fathers also teach that no one fasts and remains without reward, for the blessings received through fasting far exceed any pleasure gained from eating.

✍🏾

Saint Isaac the Syrian teaches that fasting is:

“Fasting is a healing of the soul and a quencher of passions. It is the beginning of all virtues and a giver of grace to God. Fasting brings glory to the pure, acts as a jewel of purity for the virgins, and is the mother of prayer. It becomes a source of tears, a teacher of harmony, and a stimulant to all good works. By humbling the body before God, fasting also strengthens humility.

✍🏾 As Mar Isaac writes (Article 4, Chapter 6), fasting not only nourishes the soul spiritually but also prolongs life, as it aligns the believer with God’s will and strengthens the body through discipline.

The Example of the Saints and the Obligation of Fasting

text:
The lives of our ancestors who lived long and holy lives through fasting and prayer are living evidence of its blessings. For example:

👉🏾 St. Cyril of Alexandria lived 108 years.

👉🏾 St. Anthony lived 105 years.

👉🏾 St. Macarius of Alexandria lived 100 years on earth.

When believers fast, our God extends their lives to allow for repentance and growth in holiness.

✍🏾Prayer, intercession, and worship during fasting increase the spiritual benefits we gain. As St. Jared teaches: “Be like a person who fasts and prays for his sins.”

✍🏾 A Christian does not have the authority to decide whether to fast or not, because fasting is a commandment from God, given to all Christians as a law.

👉🏾The prophet Joel reminds us that fasting and praying are Christian obligations: “Sanctify a fast and proclaim a congregation” (Joel 2:15).

✍🏾 St. Paul also teaches that we should not give any cause for stumbling in spiritual life or ministry by creating excuses or neglecting God’s commandments.

✍🏾 Let us approach the upcoming Fast of the Prophets with joy, love, and devotion.
