Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings ,we greet you with the peace of God. Today, continuing our teaching on the purpose of fasting, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage you to read attentively and benefit from it.

✍🏾

text.text: Fasting as a Path to God’s Mercy

text:
Fasting is a spiritual discipline given to us so that we may fear God, draw near to Him, and ask for His mercy. Scripture teaches that fasting strengthens our prayers and helps us present our struggles before the Lord.

“Therefore we prayed to God for this, and He answered our prayers” (Ezra 8:23).

Fasting is a way to seek God’s help, and it is a spiritual tool that makes our prayers earnest and sincere.

The prophet Joel instructed the people of Israel during times of trouble, saying:

“Sanctify a fast, proclaim a solemn assembly; gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land to the house of the Lord your God, and cry out to the Lord” (Joel 1:14).

Through this, we learn that fasting calls us back to God with humility and repentance.

Job also shows us the same spiritual call:

“Return to Me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning; blow the trumpet in Zion; sanctify a fast, proclaim a solemn assembly” (Job 2:12).

We cannot find God’s will, peace, or unity while giving ourselves over to eating, drinking, and the desires of the flesh. True spiritual growth comes from discipline, prayer, and humbling the body for the sake of the soul.

Our Lord Jesus Christ taught us to do the works of righteousness, and God has shown through the prophets that fasting is necessary for those who seek deliverance from sorrow and tribulation.

Fasting is also a tool for building and renewing a righteous generation.
“Your ancient ruins will be rebuilt; your foundations will stand for generations. You will be called the repairer of the broken walls, the restorer of paths to dwell in” (Isaiah 58:12).

Again the Scripture teaches:
“I have not chosen a fast where a person merely afflicts himself for a day. But if one humbles himself in this fast, then he will trust in the Lord. He will dwell in the blessings of the earth, and the Lord will feed him with the heritage of Jacob, for the Lord has spoken” (Isaiah 58:5).

Through fasting, God reforms the broken, rebuilds the fallen, and strengthens the generations to come.

✍🏾

text.text: Fasting as a Way of Worship

text:
Fasting is not only a spiritual discipline but also a form of worship offered to God. Through fasting, believers humble themselves, prepare their hearts, and strengthen their communion with the Holy Trinity.

In the Book of Acts we read that the Church worshipped through fasting:

As recorded in Acts 13:1–2, the Holy Spirit chose Barnabas and Saul during a time of fasting and prayer. After the believers fasted, prayed, and laid their hands upon them, they sent them out for the work of the ministry.

This shows that fasting accompanied prayer, worship, and the commissioning of apostolic work.

When a person begins the path of true worship, fasting and prayer become essential practices. Our Lord Jesus Christ Himself taught us their importance through His own life and commandments.

The holy apostles also fasted before their missionary journeys, preparing themselves spiritually as they went out to bring back a lost and wandering generation. Fasting strengthened them and opened the way for the Holy Spirit to work through them.

Fasting is also our weapon against the powers of darkness. Through it, believers receive strength to cast out demons and resist evil spirits.

Fasting, united with prayer, is a true act of worship, a source of spiritual power, and a shield of protection for all who follow Christ

text:
Dear brethren in Christ, peace be to you.Today we remember the blessed mother Saint Welete Petros, a pillar of the Orthodox faith and a defender of the Tewahedo Church during the trials of Emperor Susenyos.

✍🏾

Saint Welete Petros was born in Daro in eastern Ethiopia.
Her father was Bahir Aseged, and her mother was Christos A-E-beya.She had two brothers, Yohannes and Zedengel, who served as high officials during the reign of King Susenyos.

After the death of her father, her mother remarried a military commander and had three more children. The place where Welete Petros later lived with her husband, Bitwoded Si-Ele Kristos, still contains her historical memorial stone.

✍🏾

text.text: The Crisis of Faith Under Emperor Susenyos

text:
While she lived peacefully with her husband, Emperor Susenyos abandoned the Tewahedo faith and accepted the teachings of Roman Catholics. He commanded all Ethiopians to follow the new religion, creating deep conflict between faithful Orthodox Christians and the king’s supporters.

When her husband brought the robe of Abune Simeon as an offering to the king, showing loyalty to the Catholic influence, Welete Petros was deeply grieved. Seeing the faith of her fathers dishonored, she refused to remain in the same house with someone who had accepted heresy. She sought a way to flee and secretly contacted monks from Tana for help.

✍🏾

text.text: Her Escape and Early Monastic Life

text:
Abba Fetele Selassie, the abbot of Tana Kirkos Monastery, sent two nuns to bring her safely to the monastery. By this time, all her children had passed away. When her husband discovered her flight, he sent soldiers to retrieve her. Yet by God’s protection, she and the two nuns hid deep within a forest until the soldiers left. The place where they concealed themselves is still known as “Saga Welete Petros,” and a church was later built there in her memory.

text.text: The Trials and Perseverance of Saint Welete Petros

text:

Seeing her unshaken, the emperor placed her under house arrest, ordering her to live among her relatives so she would remain under close watch.

She escaped from the place where she was confined and traveled to Zege Monastery. There, with her two faithful companions, Welete Paulos and Ehte kristos , she encouraged the monks and the local faithful to stand firm in the Tewahedo faith.

After staying there for some time, criticism and accusations from those opposed to her mission increased. So she left Zege and journeyed to Waldiba Monastery, continuing her mission of strengthening believers wherever she went.

✍🏾The Ministry of Saint Welete Petros in Waldeba and Tselemt

text:
After Saint Welete Petros entered the holy monastery of Waldeba and completed her week of spiritual preparation, she began teaching the fathers and mothers of the monastery, urging them to remain steadfast in the Tewahedo faith. Her words strengthened hearts, restored courage, and rekindled devotion among the monastics.

✍🏾When Emperor Susenyos learned how boldly she continued to resist the foreign teachings and how she strengthened the monks and the faithful to stand firm in Orthodoxy, he grew deeply troubled. Her influence was turning many back from their apostasy, and this angered him. He repeatedly sent soldiers to seize her, but while she remained in Waldeba they could not capture her. Seeing their persistence, she departed from Waldeba and journeyed to Tselemt.

✍🏾In Tselemt her teachings spread quickly, like fire racing through dry grass. The believers welcomed her with love and accepted her guidance. Many prepared themselves for martyrdom rather than abandon the faith of their fathers. Hearing this, Emperor Susenyos declared, “If I leave her alone, she will never leave me,” and commanded Balambaras Filatawos, the governor of Tselemt, to arrest her and bring her before him.

✍🏾The governor seized Saint Welete Petros and brought her to the emperor. They attempted to persuade her to accept the new religion, but she stood firm, unwavering in her confession of the true Tewahedo faith.

✍🏾Three Catholic priests came forward and challenged her with theological arguments. Wolete Petros responded with wisdom and clarity, exposing their errors and embarrassing them. Day after day they returned to pressure her, but she stood anchored on the rock of unity. Nothing could shake her.

✍🏾At last, one of the priests admitted to the king, “Trying to convert her is like pouring water on a rock.” Suseniyos, furious, decided to kill her. But his advisors warned him: “If you kill her now, the entire nation will take her death as a sacrifice for the faith. And if the people perish, whom will you rule? Let her be imprisoned instead.” The king listened and chose exile over execution.

✍🏾Melkea Christos, a prominent Catholic official, approached Suseniyos and said, “O king, if it pleases you, give her into my custody until winter ends. I will counsel her, and Alphonsus, the teacher of the Friars, will read to her. If she still refuses, then send her into exile.” The king agreed.

✍🏾Wolete Petros was taken to Gondar, where the Catholic bishop resided. She remained there with her two companions, Wolete Christos and Ehte kristos.Welete Paulos has been staying in Zege. Alphonsus Mendes visited her constantly, attempting to teach her the doctrine of Leon. The king also questioned her repeatedly about converting to Catholicism, but her answer remained unchanged: “Absolutely not.”

👉🏾Keremt passed, and Hidar arrived. Neither pressure, nor counsel, nor intimidation shook her devotion to the oneness of God as preserved in the Orthodox faith. Seeing her unbreakable resolve, Suseniyos finally ordered that she be sent into exile at Gerbel Bereha under military escort.

text.text: The Steadfast Faith of Welete Petros

text:
✍🏾When her aged mother heard what had happened, she sent a servant to her, and her devoted follower, Ehte kirstos, came to her immediately.

✍🏾Welete Petros lived in exile at Gerbel Barha for three years, often suffering from illness. She endured all her pain for the sake of her faith. After being released from exile, she settled in a place called Chanqa in Dembiya. When the persecution subsided, many nuns who had abandoned their monastic robes out of fear gathered around her, and she advised them to return to their monasteries and remain firm. Later, she traveled to Tana Kirkos.
She then went to the island of Mitsli, where she gathered a number of monks around her and strengthened them to fight for their religion. Yet she herself continued to suffer. When she heard that a man named Meziraete kirstos had come to the area with a royal letter forcing Orthodox believers to accept Catholic baptism, she instructed the monks, sent them into the desert for safety, and once again went into exile. When peace returned to the country, she came back to Misli at the age of forty-nine.

✍🏾After returning from exile, she made her home in a place called Menzo. There she lived in prayer and supplication. Abba Tsega Christos, the abbot of Debre Mariam who had been with her at Mitsli Monastery, translated Metshafe hawin for her.

✍🏾When Emperor Suseniyos was struck by God’s judgment . and when the Orthodox faith returned , Abune Markos, the Egyptian bishop, came to Ethiopia and met her on his journey. The bishop said that news of her separation from her husband and her suffering for the faith had reached all the way to Egypt.

She then established a monastery in Menzo and lived there as a monastic mother. The monastery she founded housed both men and women. After the restoration of the Orthodox faith and the reign of Emperor Fasil, she traveled to Gondar to greet the king and to see her relatives.

The king received her with great honor and visited her daily. Whenever he entered, he greeted her respectfully because of the strength of her faith and the holiness of her life.

✍🏾Welete Petros lived the monastic life faithfully and departed this world at the age of fifty. She is commemorated in her monastery on Hidar 17. The feast of her companion Welete Kristos is celebrated on Hidar 7.

✍🏾Standing firm in the faith is not determined by gender. Our Church has many saints like Welete Petros. Today’s sisters and mothers should learn from her example, standing strong in the faith and fighting for the truth.

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings , we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

Ruth showed deep mercy toward Naomi, who had lost her husband and her two sons. Though Ruth herself had nothing, she chose to care for Naomi with unwavering devotion. She left her homeland, Moab, and journeyed with her to Bethlehem.

When Naomi urged her to return to her own people, Orpah turned back, but Ruth remained faithful to the end. Her kindness and sacrifice made her worthy of the blessing spoken to her:
“May the Lord reward you according to your work, and may your reward be full from the Lord, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to seek refuge.” (Ruth 2:12)

✍🏾

During the great famine in the days of Elijah, the widow of Zarephath had only a handful of flour and a little oil left. She told the prophet,“I am gathering sticks to prepare a meal for myself and my son, that we may eat it and die.” (1 Kings 17:12)

Even in such desperate poverty, she shared what little she had with Elijah. Because of her mercy and obedience, God blessed her household throughout the famine.

Our Lord Himself confirmed her blessedness, saying that Elijah was sent not to any widow in Israel, but to the widow of Zarephath (Luke 4:26).

✍🏾

While our Lord was teaching, a poor widow came and placed two small copper coins into the treasury. Christ called His disciples and said:

“Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all the others. For they gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in all she had to live on.”(Mark 12:42–44; Luke 21:1–4)

Her offering became a symbol of pure, heartfelt sacrifice. It is remembered in the intercessory prayer found over 260 times in the Book of Acts:

“Lord, accept the thanksgiving I offer in my time of need, remembering the thousands of angels who serve You at all times, just as You accepted the small offering of the poor woman more than those who gave from their abundance.”

✍🏾

Tabitha, also called Dorcas, lived in Joppa and was known for her abundant good works and almsgiving. Scripture says:

“Now in Joppa there was a certain Tabitha, full of good works and almsgiving. In those days she fell sick and died. And they laid her in an upper chamber. And when the disciples heard that Peter was near Joppa, they sent two men to him, begging him not to delay in coming to them. And Peter arose and went with them. And when he was come, they brought him up into the upper chamber: and all the widows stood before him weeping, and showing the coats and garments which Dorcas had made while she was with them. And Peter put them all forth, and kneeled down, and prayed; and turning to the body, he said, ‘Tabitha, arise.’ And she opened her eyes: and when she saw Peter, she sat up. And he gave her his hand, and lifted her up; and when he had called the saints and widows, he presented her alive.” (Acts 9:36–43)

Anba Abram is one of the saints of the twentieth century, remembered especially for his deep compassion and his countless works of mercy. Among the many stories of his kindness, the following two examples are often told:

• After his ordination as a bishop, Anba Abram turned his episcopal residence into a refuge for the homeless, the poor, orphans, and strangers. Anyone who came in need found shelter and comfort under his care.

• One day, a poor woman came to him seeking help. Anba Abram had no money at that moment, but someone had recently given him a new cloak. He told the woman honestly that he had no money, then told her to sold the cloak and get the money she needed.
The woman went to the market to sell the cloak, and the original owner recognized it. He bought it back and returned it to Anba Abram.

Before handing it to him, the man asked, “Father, why did you not wear this cloak during the winter?”
Anba Abram answered simply, “My cloak is above,” meaning his treasure is in heaven.

The man gave the cloak back, and Anba Abram asked him, “Did you pay the woman the full price she deserved?”and the man replied that he had gave .

text.text: Hypocritical Mercy Will Not Lead Us to Righteousness

text:
True mercy must come from the heart. As stated earlier, works of compassion should be done without seeking benefit or praise. Yet in our time, some people use charity to promote themselves or their organizations. They turn the suffering of the poor into public display and media content, forgetting the dignity and privacy of those in need. This behavior is shameful and empty.

✍🏾

text.text: Charity Without Love Has No Reward

text:
Saint Paul teaches,
“If I give all I have to feed the poor and give my body to be burned, but do not have love, it profits me nothing.”(1 Corinthians 13:3)
Kindness done without love carries no spiritual value.

✍🏾

👉🏾“Our Lord teaches us to avoid false, showy acts of mercy. He said:“Be careful not to do your alms before men to be seen by them; otherwise you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven. When you give alms, do not blow a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets so that they may be praised by men. Truly, I say to you, they have received their reward. But when you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing, so that your alms may be in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.”
Matthew 6:1-4

Giving must be secret, humble, and pure. God sees what is done in secret and rewards openly.

👉🏾He also rebuked the hypocrites who focus on outward acts while neglecting the heart of God’s law:
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, yet you have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. These you ought to have done, without leaving the others undone.”
Matthew 23:23

✍🏾

👉🏾The Holy Apostle teaches us that true heavenly wisdom is pure and free from hypocrisy.“But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality and without hypocrisy.”(James 3:17)

👉🏾When Saint Yohannes Afework was teaching, a man came to him and said, “I give alms, and I seek praise for it. If I am not praised, I will not give.” Saint Yohannes explained this with the parable: “It is better to sow, even if weeds grow, than not to sow at all and inherit nothing.”

When seed is sown, weeds may appear. The farmer may remove them, or even if he does not, some good grain will still be found among the weeds. In the same way, those who give for the sake of vain praise may later repent. Their hearts can eventually turn away from pride and toward true compassion.

👉🏾However, the one who refuses to give and only stands outside criticizing others finds it hard for his heart to return to mercy. This does not mean that we should encourage vain praise, but that we should at least practice giving. Even imperfect giving can become a path toward purity when the heart opens to repentance.

text.text: The Call to Practice True Mercy

text:
Mercy should not remain a theory we admire from a distance. It is something we must practice according to our ability. We are not called to advise others while doing nothing ourselves, but to become examples through our own works of compassion.

✍🏾 Mercy is practiced with faith, hope, and love, not for the shallow popularity that rises and fades in this world. The model of our mercy should not be famous individuals, but Christ, the true God of mercy, and the saints who walked in His footsteps with pure hearts.

✍🏾 We do acts of kindness from inner compassion, not through excessive publicity or the pressure of other people. The Church, as the refuge of the poor, teaches mercy not only through words but also by living it in concrete action.

✍🏾Our fathers taught us that almsgiving is never lost. “He who has pity on the poor lends to the Lord, and He will repay him,” as it is written in Proverbs 19:17. The one who gives in sincerity receives blessings many times over.

👉🏾Saint John the Baptist taught the incomparable value of mercy. He said, “Giving alms is better than performing miracles, and feeding the hungry in the name of Christ is better than raising the dead in the name of Christ. When you perform a miracle, you become a debtor to the Creator, but when you give alms, you are lending to the Creator.”

✍🏾 Our Lord also taught us to value eternal treasures over earthly ones:

“Do not lay up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy and where thieves break in and steal; but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys and where thieves do not break in and steal. For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.”(Matthew 6:19-21)

Therefore, let us store our treasures with God in heaven, so that our hearts may remain with Him.

✍🏾 What God observes is not the size of what we give, but the compassion behind it. Even if we have nothing and simply say with a sincere heart, “May God give us so we may give,” He sees the intention and grants according to His mercy. Since we cannot help every person in need, we offer help where the need is most urgent and where our compassion can bring real relief.

✍🏾 Mercy begins at home, in the Church, and among our neighbors. As it is written in the Book of Feteha Negest (Article 11, Number 452), “Do not spend your money where there is no security.” True mercy is given where it benefits others, for God always does what brings benefit and goodness to His children.

✍🏾 Scripture commands us: “Let not mercy and truth forsake you; bind them around your neck; write them on the tablet of your heart.”
Proverbs 3:3
If we desire to receive mercy, we must cast aside cruelty and practice compassion toward the wrongdoer, and kindness toward the one in need.

✍🏾The promise of the Lord is eternal: “Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit.” King David also proclaimed, “Your goodness and Your mercy shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the Lord forever.”
Psalm 23:6
Let us be steadfast in showing mercy so that the mercy of God may follow us all our days.

✍🏾And continually, let us pray for God’s mercy:
“Let us all hope for the blessings of Your glorious Father, who is full of mercy; let us abstain from all evil deeds, and let us unite in every good deed; blessed is He who gave us His holy Body and precious Blood.”(Liturgy)

✍🏾 The foundation of fasting is obedience to God. While certain times forbid specific foods for religious reasons, fasting is not limited to food alone. The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church teaches two kinds of fasting:

👉🏾 Fasting from certain foods (such as abstaining from meat)

👉🏾 Fasting from all sin, which we must practice at all times

✍🏾 The reason we avoid certain foods is not because they are evil, but because of obedience to the spiritual order. When we willingly restrain the body, we turn our thoughts toward the heavenly life where there is no eating and drinking, and we give thanks to God.

👉🏾 Blessings in our work and ministry

If we fast according to the proper order, we also receive blessings in our daily work, in the rain, and in divine mercy.

👉🏾 In the days of the prophet Joel, when the rain ceased and the trees withered, the people received blessing during fasting and prayer (Joel 1:12-14).

✍🏾 Blessings in harvest

(Psalm 108:24; Galatians 5:24).

✍🏾 It reveals hidden things (Daniel 10:1-3).

Ezra 8:21

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾 The order of the Holy Church is guided by moderation and spiritual wisdom.

✍🏾 Many people fast until 3, 6, 7, 9, or 11 o’clock according to their custom, but the canons of the Church actually prescribe specific fasting hours.

✍🏾 In the Fetha Negest it is written:

“They shall fast until the twelfth hour, and they shall fast until the ninth hour, except on feast days such as the Nativity and Baptism which fall on Wednesdays and Fridays.”(Ft. Ngs. Art. 15:565–566)

✍🏾 After listing the fasts, the same article, in number 572, adds:

👉🏾 “They shall fast until the ninth hour in the afternoon… but whoever fasts beyond this will receive a greater reward. However, they shall not fast on Sundays and Saturdays, except by abstaining from forbidden foods.”

✍🏾 The Great Fast (Hudade) has a different order from the regular Wednesday and Friday fasts.

👉🏾 “They shall fast until sunset on the first weeks of the Great Fast. During the remaining weeks, they shall fast until the eleventh hour, but in the month of Semone Hmamat they shall fast until the rising of the star.”
(Ft. Ngs. Art. 15:595)

✍🏾 The first week of the Great Fast, known as Zewerede, is observed until the Twelfth hour.

✍🏾 In Fetha Negest number 578, it is also taught about Semone hmamat:

“They shall fast both Friday and Saturday of Semone Hmamat together, and whoever is able should not eat anything until the rooster crows at night. But whoever is unable to fast both days should at least fast on Saturday.”

✍🏾

text.text: Summary of Fasting Hours in the Church

text:
👉🏾 The Six Regular Fasts: Until the ninth hour.
(Wednesday, Friday, Gena Fast, Nineveh Fast, Apostles’ Fast, Filseta Fast)

👉🏾 Weeks of the Great Fast (except Zewerede and Hmamat): Until the eleventh hour

👉🏾 First Week of the Great Fast (Zewerede): Until the twelfth hour

👉🏾 Semone Hmamat: Until the rising of the star.

text: Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

text.text: Blessed Are the Pure in Heart

text:
👉🏾Our Lord taught in the sixth Beatitude, “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God” (Matthew 5:8). In the spiritual life, the heart holds a central place. Scripture uses the word heart to describe the whole inner life. It includes the mind, desire, emotion, and will.

✍🏾When the wise Solomon said, “My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes observe my ways” (Proverbs 23:26), he was calling us to walk in the will of God. He also taught, “Keep your heart with all diligence, for from it flow the issues of life” (Proverbs 4:23). This means we must guard our inner spiritual life with care.

✍🏾Our Lord explained, “Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks. A good person out of the good treasure of the heart brings forth good, and an evil person out of the evil treasure brings forth evil” (Luke 6:45). A person speaks and acts from what fills the heart. Words reveal the life within.

✍🏾He also warned, “This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me” (Matthew 15:8). In other words, there are those who speak religious words, yet their actual life and actions do not reflect closeness to God.


👉🏾Saint James teaches:

“Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners; and purify your hearts, you double-minded.” (James 4:8)

✍🏾This instructs us to cleanse our inner life, the heart, so that God may draw near to us. Purity begins within. When the heart is purified, the whole life becomes aligned with God.

✍🏾

is a life free from the stains of sin, surrendered to God in love, lived with sincerity and faithfulness. It is a heart that reflects the presence of God.

The perfect example of such purity among all humanity is the Holy Virgin Mary, our Redeemer’s Mother. She is pure in spirit, pure in speech, and pure in deed.

For this reason the Church rightfully calls her:

“

.”

Her body was pure, her soul was pure, and her heart was pure. Because of this purity, she became the dwelling place of the Most High. The divine nature, which no creature can behold, took flesh from her and became man for our salvation.

Our holy fathers praised her, saying:

“She was pure and holy like the Ark on Sinai. She dwelt in the Temple as the Ark once dwelt in the sanctuary. Her food was heavenly, and her drink was the drink of peace.”

👉🏾Saint Dioscorus also proclaimed her purity in the Divine Liturgy, saying:

“By the will of the Father, He came down and was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, the pure one. He was born of her, He dwelt among us, He was held in the arms of His Mother, and He was nourished as a child.”

✍🏾

text.text: The Main Manifestations of Purity of Heart

text:
Saint Paul teaches:

“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)

This means no one begins with a pure heart. Purity is restored through repentance. This is why Saint David prayed:

“Create in me a clean heart, O Lord, and renew a right spirit within me.” (Psalm 51:10)

Through true repentance, God grants a renewed, purified heart.

text.text: The prophet Ezekiel also calls the people to repentance:

text:
“Cast away from you all your transgressions by which you have sinned, and make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why should you die, O house of Israel? For I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord God. Therefore turn and live.” (Ezekiel 18:31–32)

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings , we greet you all with the peace of God. Today, according to the topic mentioned above, we present to you this important spiritual lesson. May it be read with understanding and kept with faith.

✍🏾

The Ark of Zion is symbolically represented by our Mother, the Holy Virgin Mary. Every year on hidar 21, the Church celebrates the feast of our mother.

✍🏾 “Zion” means tower and refuge. Concerning this, the psalmist David said, “Man calls Zion our mother, and man was born in her.” (Ps. 86:5). This reveals the mystery prepared for the salvation of Adam and his children, who had been held under the condemnation of sin for five thousand five hundred years. In order to free humanity from the prison of Sheol, God the Son chose to take flesh from the Holy Virgin Mary, who was descended from the lineage of David.

✍🏾 He dwelt in her holy womb, and after nine months and five days, He was born for the salvation of the world. Therefore, we, the faithful of the Orthodox Church, honor, glorify, and give thanks to the Holy Virgin Mary. She is the dwelling place of God, the tower of refuge, and the foundation of our salvation.

✍🏾

text.text: The Ark of Zion as a Type of the Virgin Mary

text:
👉🏾The Ark of Zion is symbolized by the Virgin Mary. We celebrate her annual feast on Hidar 21st. Among the many reasons for this celebration, the most important is that the Ark of Zion shattered the idol Dagon and performed miracles during its captivity among the Philistines.

👉🏾The great prophet Moses carved two tablets of stone, built a wooden ark, and ascended the mountain as God commanded him.

👉🏾“And I made an ark of acacia wood, and hewed two tables of stone like the first, and went up into the mount, and the two tables were in my hand: and he wrote upon the tables the ten commandments, which the LORD spake unto you in the mount out of the midst of the fire, as they were written at the first: and the LORD gave them unto me.” (Deuteronomy 10:1-4)
They carried the ark of the covenant with them and entered the land of their possession.

👉🏾While Zion is a symbol of our Lady, the Virgin Mary, the tablets of the law contained within her symbolize our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

👉🏾The ark was made of acacia wood, a sign of the purity of the Mother of God.

✍🏾It was covered with pure gold, both inside and out, showing her holiness and purity in conscience and body. When the Israelites carried the Ark of Zion before them, they overcame all who opposed them.

✍🏾

The Philistines rose up against Israel for war and gathered together to fight. The Israelites were defeated, and the ark of the covenant was taken. The elders of Israel said, “Why has the LORD struck us today before the Philistines? Let us bring back the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh, that it may go before us and save us from the hand of our enemies.” But the children of Israel had sinned, and God delivered the ark into the hands of the Philistines. (1 Samuel 4:1-11)

The elders of Israel said, “Why has the LORD struck us today before the Philistines? Let us bring back the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh, that it may go before us and save us from the hand of our enemies.” But the children of Israel had sinned, and God delivered the ark into the hands of the Philistines. Continues 👇🏾

text:
✍🏾 The Philistines brought the ark of the LORD into the house of Dagon and set it beside the idol. The next morning, Dagon had fallen on his face before the LORD.

✍🏾 They were astonished, yet they set Dagon back in his place, shut the door, and departed. The following morning, Dagon had fallen on his face again, and both his head and hands were broken. The hand of the LORD was heavy upon the people of Ashdod, and plagues struck them boils, rats, and a great calamity in the city.

✍🏾 The Philistines sent the ark to Ashkelon, saying, “We have taken it away.” The people of Ashkelon were greatly alarmed: “Why have you brought the ark of the God of Israel to kill us and our people?” they asked.

✍🏾 The ark remained with the Philistines for seven months. Their land suffered, plagues spread, and many people perished. Finally, they returned the ark to the house of Aminadab on the hill, where it remained for twenty years.

✍🏾 After twenty years, God delivered the Philistines into the hand of David, and he defeated them. The prophet of the LORD declared, “Arise, O Lord, into your resting place, you and the ark of your sanctuary.” David returned to Israel with the ark of the LORD, rejoicing and singing with great glory. He placed it in a tent that he had prepared for it.

✍🏾

text.text: The Feast of Hidar Zion is celebrated for several reasons:

text:
1. The prophet Zechariah saw Zion in the form of the seal of the covenant.

2. It is the day Menelik I entered Axum carrying the Ark of Zion.

3. During the reign of Queen Gudit (Yodit), after the Ark was hidden on Lake Zway, it returned to Axum.

4. Between 333–339 A.D., Kings Abraha and Atsbeha built the great church in Axum and consecrated it on this day.

For these sacred events, the Holy Orthodox Tewahedo Church honors the Virgin Mary, the living Ark of Zion, and celebrates the feast with great pomp and devotion. (Medble Tarikh, p. 152)

text: Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

Just as we wash our bodies daily to preserve physical cleanliness, we must also guard the purity of our hearts every day. Repentance is not a one-time act but a continual labor. Loving God with a pure heart leaves no room for loving the passing things of this world.

This is why the Apostle James warns us:
“You adulterers! Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God? Whoever wishes to be a friend of the world becomes an enemy of God.” (James 4:4)

Worldly love separates us from God. Purity of heart means turning away from the world and following God wholly.

Our Lord also teaches:
“He who loves father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me; and he who loves son or daughter more than Me is not worthy of Me. And he who does not take up his cross and follow Me is not worthy of Me.” (Matthew 10:37-38)

These words are addressed to those who choose to follow Him with an undivided, pure heart.

Saint Peter, whose heart was sincere, once said to the Lord:
“Behold, we have left everything and followed You. What shall we have?”
And the Lord replied:
“Truly I say to you, in the regeneration, when the Son of Man sits on the throne of His glory, you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” (Matthew 19:27-28)

Those who follow Christ with a pure heart will behold His glory and share in His kingdom.

3.

text.text: Living a Life Filled With Love

text:
When we speak of a pure heart, we mean an inner life free from sin, free from wrongdoing, free from doubt, and filled with holy love. A clean house is not defined by emptiness but by what is kept within it. In the same way, purity of heart is not only freedom from sin but the presence of genuine love.

Saint Paul teaches that love is the foundation and fulfillment of every virtue:

👉🏾“If I give all my possessions to feed the poor, and if I surrender my body to be burned, but do not have love, I gain nothing.” (1 Corinthians 13:3)A pure heart, therefore, is a heart saturated with holy love.

Our Lord, when revealing the two greatest commandments, said:
“You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind. This is the first and greatest commandment. And the second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments hang all the Law and the Prophets.” (Matthew 22:37-40)

✍🏾He taught this so that these two commandments of love might take root in our hearts and shape our entire lives.

It is indeed a blessing to dwell in the love of God and to live in love toward others. The Lord said:
“Blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it.” (Luke 11:28)

This blessing belongs to those who hear His word with a pure heart and obey it with a pure heart.

In the Gospel of John, Christ teaches:

“If you love Me, keep My commandments.” (John 14:15)
And again:

👉🏾“This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.” (John 15:12)
These words show clearly that a pure heart is never empty; it is filled with divine love.

Saint John also declares in his revelation:

👉🏾“Blessed is he who reads, hears, and keeps the words of this prophecy.” (Revelation 1:3)
And later:“Behold, I am coming quickly. Blessed is he who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.” (Revelation 22:7)
The pure in heart are those who hear the word of God and keep it faithfully.

Blessed indeed are those whose hearts are filled with pure love, the love of God and the grace of the Holy Spirit, for they shall see God.

This blessing belongs to those who hear His word with a pure heart and obey it with a pure heart.

In the Gospel of John, Christ teaches:

“If you love Me, keep My commandments.” (John 14:15)
And again:

👉🏾“This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.” (John 15:12)
These words show clearly that a pure heart is never empty; it is filled with divine love.

Saint John also declares in his revelation:

👉🏾“Blessed is he who reads, hears, and keeps the words of this prophecy.” (Revelation 1:3)
And later:“Behold, I am coming quickly. Blessed is he who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.” (Revelation 22:7)
The pure in heart are those who hear the word of God and keep it faithfully.

Blessed indeed are those whose hearts are filled with pure love, the love of God and the grace of the Holy Spirit, for they shall see God.

Continues 👇🏾

text:
Our father David asks in his psalm:

“Who shall ascend into the hill of the Lord? Who shall stand in His holy place? He who has clean hands and a pure heart, who has not lifted up his soul to vanity nor sworn deceitfully. He shall receive blessing from the Lord and righteousness from the God of his salvation.” (Psalm 24:3-5)

To stand before God requires purity of heart and a life striving for righteousness.

Saint Paul teaches his spiritual son Timothy:

“Flee youthful desires and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.” (2 Timothy 2:22)

And again:

“The goal of the commandment is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith.” (1 Timothy 1:5)

Righteousness grows out of a pure heart.

👉🏾Saint John also teaches:
“Whoever abides in Him does not sin. Whoever sins has neither seen Him nor known Him. Let no one deceive you: He who practices righteousness is righteous.” (1 John 3:6-7)

Purity of heart means abiding in Christ and living in righteousness.

✍🏾

”

In the prophecy of Isaiah, God declares that He will gather those who are far and reveal what was hidden. The term “Zion” appears throughout Scripture and is interpreted according to its context. The Holy Scriptures are explained in an ordered, faithful, and traditional manner. One word may carry different meanings depending on where and how it appears, so careful examination is required.

The word Zion can mean:

👉🏾The Virgin Mary

👉🏾Jerusalem

👉🏾The Church

👉🏾The Kingdom of Heaven

👉🏾The Temple

Likewise, Jerusalem can mean:

👉🏾The House of Israel (House of Jacob)

👉🏾The Temple

👉🏾The Virgin Mary

👉🏾The Cross

👉🏾Christ Himself

If we fail to understand the context, and attempt to interpret these terms carelessly, we will lose the mystery instead of uncovering it. To avoid confusion, we must examine Scripture carefully, learn from the Fathers, and pray with humility for God’s enlightenment.

text.text: 1. Zion Refers to the Virgin Mary

text:
“The Virgin Mary is called Zion
“For the Lord has chosen Zion; He has desired her for His dwelling place. ‘This is My resting place forever; here I will dwell, for I have desired her. I will abundantly bless her provision; I will satisfy her poor with bread. I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her saints shall shout for joy.’” (Ps. 132:13-16)

In this mystery, the Virgin Mary, who is Zion, reveals the blessings promised to those who believe in her covenant, her motherhood, and her intercession:

👉🏾 She grants honor to her faithful.

👉🏾 She fills her poor with gladness and grace.

👉🏾 She provides nourishment for body and soul.

👉🏾 She grants new birth through baptism, making believers children of God, sharers of one Body and Blood.

👉🏾 She strengthens her priests and servants with life and spiritual vitality.

👉🏾 The saints who trust in her purity receive the joy of the Holy Spirit.

Mary, the dwelling place of the Prince of Peace
She bore the Son of God in her womb after nine months and five days, fulfilling the prophecy:
“For unto us a Child is born, unto us a Son is given…” (Isaiah 9:6)
Christ, who is our peace (Eph. 2:14), dwelt in her, the true land of peace. As the psalm says: “Glorious things are spoken of you, O city of God.” (Ps. 86:3)

✍🏾The Scripture that says, “I am appointed as King on the mountain of praise” (Ps. 2:6) is understood by the Church as a prophecy pointing to the mystery of the Incarnation. The Virgin Mary is called Mount Zion because, just as Mount Zion was a strong and trusted refuge for Israel, so the Virgin Mary is a refuge for all who believe. The name “Zion” itself means refuge, and our Lady truly becomes the place of safety for sinners seeking mercy, for the righteous seeking protection, and for all Christians who trust in the covenant of compassion given to her through her motherhood and intercession.

✍🏾Because she became the living dwelling place of God, she is called the Mountain of the Temple, the Cradle of the Flesh, the Cradle of Righteousness, and the Cradle of Salvation. For nine months and five days she bore Christ, the Savior of the world, in her holy womb. she carried Christ with humility and endured suffering for the salvation of humanity. She inclined her head toward her womb, for within it the angels were glorifying their Creator, and she listened to their praise as one hears a sacred liturgy. (John 1:42 ).

text:
✍🏾Through her mercy, she receives the praise and prayers of those who call upon her with faith.

The Son of God, the Messiah, the King of our souls and bodies, the Lord of lords and King of kings (Rev. 19:11-16), was born of the Virgin Mary, who became the true temple of Zion. To her the angel said, “Fear not, Mary, for you have found favor with God” (Luke 1:30). Since Christ reigned gloriously in her womb, she is honored above all creation. Those who seek refuge in her find grace, protection, and intercession through the motherhood God entrusted to her.

✍🏾It is God who chose the Virgin Mary to be His Mother, His throne, and His dwelling place. As it is written, “The Most High has sanctified His dwelling place” (Ps. 45:4). God chose Mount Zion because He loved it, and likewise He chose the Virgin Mary, setting her apart and sanctifying her as His holy habitation.

✍🏾 “He chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion which He loved” (Ps. 77:68).
Just as He chose Zion, He chose the Virgin Mary who comes from the tribe of Judah. She is pure and undefiled, for in her was fulfilled the word, “God will sit on the throne of His holiness” (Ps. 46:8). Her womb became the world, for in it the Creator entered His creation, and it became His throne (Ps. 131:13).

✍🏾 “Who then can resist the one whom God has chosen?” (Rom. 8:34)
Those whom God honors are truly honored, not merely those appointed by men, but those appointed by God Himself. The Virgin Mary stands above all creation because God chose her.

✍🏾

text.text: The Virgin Mary: Joy of All the Living

text:
The Virgin Mary is the joy of all who live. “The joy of all the earth is Mount Zion” (Ps. 47:2). For a time, this referred to the earth where humanity was created from dust. But in its fullness, it reveals that the joy of all the living is our Lady, the Virgin Mary.

Why? Because:

👉🏾 “The joy we lost in the garden of Eden, the joy we lost in Eve, has been restored to us by our Lady, the Virgin Mary, the source of our joy, our Mother of Mount Zion.”
(Thursday Praise of Saint Ephraim)

Through her, humanity’s lost joy returned, as the Lord Himself confirmed when He said to the disciple, “Behold your mother” (John 19:26).

She is the prophesied Sabbath, the promised blessing, the ladder Jacob saw, the bridge of reconciliation, our crown, our grace, and our inheritance. She is the one given to us by God as a gift of mercy and a refuge for all generations.

👉🏾 “You have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God” (Hebrews 12:22)

✍🏾 Mount Zion here refers to the heavenly Jerusalem, the kingdom of heaven.

✍🏾 The kingdom of heaven is not an earthly city depending on the sun or moon for light. Its radiance comes from the glory of God, and its lamp is the Lamb. Therefore, the Jerusalem of David on earth is not the Mount Zion being described.

✍🏾 Since the heavenly Jerusalem represents the kingdom of heaven, translating the Jerusalem of Zion as an earthly Mount Zion or Jerusalem leads to a misunderstanding of the interpretation.

text:
✍🏾 Because the Ark of the Covenant dwells in the temple, the Ark of Zion is also called the Temple of Zion.

👉🏾 “Every place where the ark of the Lord enters is holy” (1 Kings 8:11)

👉🏾 “Praise be to You, O Lord, in Zion” (Psalm 64:11)

✍🏾 In Zion, on Mount Zion, in the temple:

👉🏾 Thanksgiving is offered

👉🏾 spiritual Songs are sung

👉🏾 The Divine Liturgy is sanctified

👉🏾 Seatat and Mahlet are offered 

👉🏾 The word of God is proclaimed

👉🏾 Praise rises to God

👉🏾 The mourning are comforted

👉🏾 Tears are wiped away

👉🏾 The distressed find peace

✍🏾 In the temple, we give thanks to God for all He has done:

👉🏾 “Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift” (2 Corinthians 9:15)

👉🏾 “I thank You for what You have done for us” (Psalm 51:9)

✍🏾 The temple of Mount Zion is the place where we speak with God, where questions are answered, sins forgiven, histories transformed, snares broken, and mysteries opened. For this reason, the Lord declares that He will not be silent concerning Zion, nor will He rest concerning Jerusalem, the land of peace.

text: Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

God Himself is pure in His nature, and all His works are pure. As King David declared:
“The way of God is perfect; the word of the Lord is tested; He is a shield to all who trust in Him.”
(Psalm 18:30)

A pure heart resembles God by speaking pure words and rejecting evil thoughts. David teaches us:
“My heart overflows with a good theme; I speak the things concerning the King; my tongue is the pen of a ready writer.”
(Psalm 45:1)

A heart purified by grace produces good works: thanksgiving, humility, mercy, and spiritual wisdom.

God is patient, and a pure heart becomes the storehouse of patience. Saint Paul teaches:
“Our mouth is open to you, our heart is enlarged. You are not restricted by us… I speak to you as to my children: be enlarged also.”
(2 Corinthians 6:11-13)

A pure heart is wide and compassionate, able to bear others gently.

David also wrote:
“He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us according to our iniquities. For as the heavens are high above the earth, so great is His mercy toward those who fear Him. As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us.”
(Psalm 103:10-12)

Those who imitate God must therefore treasure patience.

Our Lord Himself revealed the height of godliness:
“Love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who persecute you… that you may be children of your Father in heaven. For He makes His sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.”
(Matthew 5:44-45)

Purity of heart is to imitate God’s mercy.

6. Being the Temple of God

The Apostle Saint Paul teaches:
“Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you? If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him; for the temple of God is holy, and that temple is you.”
(1 Corinthians 3:16-17)

The heart of a Christian is the dwelling place of God.

Saint Peter also exhorts us:
“Sanctify Christ the Lord in your hearts.”
(1 Peter 3:15)

Paul further warns the faithful regarding purity of life:
“Every sin a person commits is outside the body, but the one who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body. Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God? You are not your own; you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body.”
(1 Corinthians 6:18–20)

To honor the heart is to honor the temple of God.

He also writes:
“What agreement has the temple of God with idols? For we are the temple of the living God. As God has said: ‘I will dwell in them and walk among them; I will be their God, and they shall be my people.’”
(2 Corinthians 6:16-17)

God dwells in the purified heart.

To the Ephesians, Paul further teaches the unity and growth of this spiritual temple:
“You are built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus Himself being the chief cornerstone. In Him the whole building is joined together and grows into a holy temple in the Lord. In Him you also are being built together for a dwelling place of God in the Spirit.”
(Ephesians 2:20–22)

A heart rooted in Christ becomes a holy dwelling prepared for God.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.

Dear faithful followers of the Orthodox teachings on the John's Repentance page, we greet you with the peace of God. Based on the topic above, we present to you this lesson so that you may read, learn, and be strengthened in spiritual understanding.

✍🏾The Fast of the Prophets is one of the seven great fasts of the Church. It is observed every year from Hidar 15 until the eve of the Feast of the Nativity.

The fast lasts 44 days before the Nativity. During this period, the faithful remember the fulfillment of the prophecies of the holy prophets and the completion of the 5500 years of human suffering before the coming of the Savior.

What the Prophets Foretold

When God the Father decreed the salvation of the world, the prophets spoke through the Holy Spirit concerning:

His taking on human flesh

His exile into Egypt

His baptism in the Jordan

His enlightening of the darkened world through His divine teaching

His sufferings for the salvation of mankind

His crucifixion and death

His resurrection

His ascension

His glorious second coming

Prophets from every generation proclaimed these mysteries under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit.

The Prophets’ Longing and Fasting

Desiring to see the fulfillment of God’s promise, the prophets prayed earnestly and fasted with strong determination. They counted the days, weeks, months, and years, waiting for the moment when God would become man for the salvation of the world. In their prayers they cried, “Stretch out Your strength; stretch out Your hand!” longing for the salvation to come.

Because the prophecies and prayers of the prophets were fulfilled through the birth of our Lord Jesus Christ, this fast is called “Tsome Nebiyat – the Fast of the Prophets.”

✍🏾

text.text: Other Names of the Fast of the Prophets

text: Because this holy season carries many spiritual meanings, the Fast of the Prophets is known by several traditional names in the Church:
Since the promise of salvation that God gave to Adam was fulfilled through the birth of Christ, this fast is also called Adam’s Fast.
During this season the Church proclaims extensively the mystery of God becoming man. Because the gospel of the Incarnation is widely preached, it is called the Preaching Fast.
The fast concludes on the Feast of the Nativity, when we celebrate the birth of the Savior. For this reason, it is also known as the Nativity Fast.

The holy apostles said, “If we fast during the feast of the Resurrection, what shall we do during the feast of the Nativity?”
In remembrance of the prophets who fasted before the coming of Christ, the apostles also kept this fast. Therefore, it is called the Apostles’ Fast.

The Apostle Saint Philip preached the Gospel throughout Afrakya, performing miracles and bringing many to the faith. He was martyred by those who rejected his teaching.
When his disciples prepared to bury him, they fasted and prayed for a week, asking God to return the apostle’s body to them. On the third day, God granted their request, and the disciples buried him with honor.
After receiving his body, they continued fasting until the Nativity. Because of this memory, the fast is called Philip’s Fast.

After the Archangel Gabriel announced to the Holy Virgin Mary that she would conceive the Son of God through the Holy Spirit, she humbled herself and fasted, saying, “What shall I do, for I have conceived God whom heaven and earth cannot contain?”
For this reason, the fast is also known as Mary’s Fast.

text.text: ✍🏾The Fast of the Prophets and the Period of Teaching

text:
During this fast:

The prophets fasted and prayed.

The apostles fasted and received blessings.

The Church Fathers established the tradition that we, the faithful, should also observe this fast so that we may receive blessings like them.

Since the promise of salvation that God gave to Adam was fulfilled through the birth of Christ, this fast is also called Adam’s Fast.

2. The Preaching Fast

During this season the Church proclaims extensively the mystery of God becoming man. Because the gospel of the Incarnation is widely preached, it is called the Preaching Fast.

3. The Nativity Fast

The fast concludes on the Feast of the Nativity, when we celebrate the birth of the Savior. For this reason, it is also known as the Nativity Fast.

4. The Apostles’ Fast

The holy apostles said, “If we fast during the feast of the Resurrection, what shall we do during the feast of the Nativity?”
In remembrance of the prophets who fasted before the coming of Christ, the apostles also kept this fast. Therefore, it is called the Apostles’ Fast.

5. Philip’s Fast

The Apostle Saint Philip preached the Gospel throughout Afrakya, performing miracles and bringing many to the faith. He was martyred by those who rejected his teaching.
When his disciples prepared to bury him, they fasted and prayed for a week, asking God to return the apostle’s body to them. On the third day, God granted their request, and the disciples buried him with honor.
After receiving his body, they continued fasting until the Nativity. Because of this memory, the fast is called Philip’s Fast.

6. Mary’s Fast

After the Archangel Gabriel announced to the Holy Virgin Mary that she would conceive the Son of God through the Holy Spirit, she humbled herself and fasted, saying, “What shall I do, for I have conceived God whom heaven and earth cannot contain?”
For this reason, the fast is also known as Mary’s Fast.

✍🏾The Fast of the Prophets and the Period of Teaching

During this fast:

The prophets fasted and prayed.

The apostles fasted and received blessings.

The Church Fathers established the tradition that we, the faithful, should also observe this fast so that we may receive blessings like them.

Continues 👇🏾

text: Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

Participating in the Holy Mysteries with purity of heart is essential, for it is through them that we receive complete forgiveness of sins and the sealing of holiness. Before approaching this divine mystery, every believer must purify the heart through sincere repentance.

The Apostle Paul teaches:
“This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, whenever you drink it, in remembrance of me. For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes. Whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. Let each person examine himself, and then eat of the bread and drink of the cup. For whoever eats and drinks in an unworthy manner eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the body of the Lord.”
(1 Corinthians 11:25–29)

Through this teaching, the Church calls us to approach the Holy Mysteries with a purified heart and a reverent spirit.

Paul also warns:
“I do not want you to be participants with demons. You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot be partakers of the Lord’s table and the table of demons.”
(1 Corinthians 10:19–21)
This reminds us that purity and spiritual discipline are required when drawing near to the Holy Sacrament.

During the Divine Liturgy, the priest proclaims:
“Let the clean receive the sacrifice; the unclean shall not approach.”

By partaking worthily in this Holy Sacrament, we receive perfect cleansing and the blessing of a heart made pure forever.

✍🏾

text.text: For They See God: How Do We See God?

text:
The apostle Saint Paul teaches, “He alone is immortal, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no man has seen or can see” (1 Timothy 6:16). No one sees God in His divine essence with physical eyes. Our eyes cannot even look at the full glory of the sun, let alone the infinite majesty of God. We also cannot see spiritual beings with the senses of the body.

✍🏾Our Lord explained in the Sermon on the Mount, “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God,” revealing that God is not seen with the eyes of the body but with the purified heart. In the Gospel of John He said, “I came into this world for judgment, that those who do not see might see, and those who see might become blind” (John 9:39). This shows that spiritual sight comes from faith, not from physical vision.

✍🏾Although many saw Christ with their physical eyes and heard His voice, the Pharisees, who claimed to understand the law, remained blind because they refused to believe. The apostles, however, opened their hearts in faith, received the light of truth, and became the light of the world.

✍🏾As Saint John Afework taught, just as our bodily eyes are needed to see earthly things, the eyes of the heart (the mind and inner life) are needed to see God. Just as the eye must be healthy to see clearly, the heart must be purified from sin to perceive the presence of God.

A blemish on the eye obscures vision. In the same way, sin darkens the heart and blocks the light of God. Those who cleanse their hearts by righteous living make their inner life a dwelling place for God. They sanctify their hearts, converse with Him in prayer, and see His works within them.

We Christians see God in our hearts in the following ways:

text:
👉🏾 As Saint John the Evangelist teaches, “No one has ever seen God; the only begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, He has declared Him” (John 1:18). Humanity has not seen the Father in His divine nature. Yet God revealed Himself fully through His Son, Jesus Christ.

✍🏾When Philip said, “Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us,” Christ answered, “Have I been with you so long, Philip, and you still do not know me? He who has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father?’ Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me?” (John 14:8-11). His words reveal His perfect unity with the Father. This is why the Church teaches that in seeing Jesus Christ, we have seen God. He is the natural Son, equal in divinity with the Father.

✍🏾The Apostle Saint Paul further confirms this truth: “He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation. For by Him all things were created, visible and invisible… all things were created through Him and for Him” (Colossians 1:15-16). Through Christ, the invisible God becomes visible, not in essence, but in revelation.

✍🏾Saint Peter also testified: “Not to all the people, but to us who were chosen by God as witnesses, who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead” (Acts 10:41). The apostles saw Him with their eyes, walked with Him, touched Him, listened to His voice, and held His teachings in their hearts. They shared meals with Him even after His resurrection.

We also share in this reality. Though we have not seen His earthly body as they did, we receive His holy flesh and precious blood in the Divine Liturgy. Through this mystery, we unite ourselves to Him and to the faith of those first witnesses.

✍🏾

text.text: In What He Has Done for Us

text:
We see God in our hearts when we recognize His works in our lives. When we understand with humility that every blessing, every mercy, and every guidance we receive is not from our own strength but from God, His presence becomes clear in our inner sight.

👉🏾David, filled with awe at God’s goodness, proclaimed, “Taste and see that the Lord is good; blessed is the man who trusts in Him” (Psalm 34:8). The goodness of God is something the heart experiences, not just the mind.

👉🏾Solomon likewise taught, “Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will direct your paths” (Proverbs 3:5-6). When the heart recognizes God as the one who guides every step, it begins to see Him.

Isaiah comforted God’s people with the words: “Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you and help you; I will uphold you with the right hand of My righteousness” (Isaiah 41:10). Every moment of help in our lives is another way God reveals Himself.

Jeremiah declared God’s loving intention toward us: “I know the thoughts that I think toward you, thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you a future and a hope” (Jeremiah 29:11). His plans for us are another sign of His presence.

✍🏾Saint Paul taught that we come to know this goodness through inner renewal: “Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, that you may prove what is that good, acceptable, and perfect will of God” (Romans 12:2). As our minds and hearts are renewed, we begin to understand His will and recognize His works in our lives.

✍🏾In knowing what He has done for us, in trusting His guidance, and in perceiving His mercy, we see God within our hearts.

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

We also see God through spiritual revelation, when the Holy Spirit opens the eyes of the heart to understand divine truths that cannot be known by human reasoning alone.

When our Lord asked His apostles in Caesarea Philippi, “But who do you say that I am?” Simon Peter answered with conviction, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Our Lord responded, “Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah, for flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven. And I say to you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven” (Matthew 16:15-19).

This confession did not arise from human understanding. It was a revelation given by God in Peter’s heart, showing that true knowledge of God is granted by divine illumination.

Our Lord taught the same mystery when He said, “When the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide you into all the truth. For He will not speak on His own authority, but whatever He hears He will speak, and He will declare to you what is to come” (John 16:13). The Holy Spirit is the one who reveals God to believers and enlightens their inner understanding.

Saint Paul explained this spiritual sight when he wrote, “For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I shall know fully, just as I am fully known” (1 Corinthians 13:12). Full knowledge of God is revealed gradually as our hearts are purified and enlightened.

He prayed for the faithful, saying:
“I ask that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you the Spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of Him, the eyes of your understanding being enlightened, so that you may know the hope of His calling, the riches of the glory of His inheritance in the saints, and the exceeding greatness of His power toward us who believe. He raised Christ from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly places, far above all rule and authority, power and dominion, and every name that is named, in this age and in the age to come. He put all things under His feet and gave Him as head over all things to the Church” (Ephesians 1:17-22).

Finally, he taught, “We have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may know the things freely given to us by God” (1 Corinthians 2:12).

text:
👇🏾

✍🏾Saint Paul taught the same truth when he wrote, “For since the creation of the world, His invisible attributes, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood through the things that have been made” (Romans 1:20).

By reflecting on creation, our hearts perceive the invisible God through His visible works.

Creation is therefore not merely the background of human life; it is a revelation that allows the pure heart to see God’s power, His providence, and His glory.

✍🏾

Many holy people in Scripture saw God in visions and heard His voice, demonstrating that God reveals Himself to those who are pure in heart.

👉🏾

When the sons of Eli sinned against God, He called Samuel, who was pure in heart. The Scripture says:

“And the Lord came and stood, and Samuel called as at other times, Samuel: and Samuel said, ‘Speak; for thy servant heareth.’” (1 Samuel 3:1-14)

Saul also heard the voice of God on the road to Damascus:

 “As I journeyed and came near Damascus about noon, suddenly a great light from heaven flashed around me. I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’ And I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ He said, ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting.’” (Acts 22:6-9)

Those who were with Saul saw the light but did not hear the voice, showing that hearing God’s call requires spiritual attentiveness.

✍🏾

David, the noble king and servant of God, testified to God’s help in trials:

 “All my bones say to you, O Lord, who is like you? You deliver the poor from the hand of him who oppresses, the needy and the poor from the hand that snatches them away.” (Psalm 35:10)

He also declared:

 “I saw the Lord always before me, for he is at my right hand, that I should not be shaken.” (Acts 2:25)

This teaches us that God is always present before the pure in heart. In trials and temptations, those with pure hearts will see His protection and assistance.

✍🏾

text.text: Seeing God in the Lives of Others

text:
We also see God through the lives of righteous people, whose faith and holiness reveal His presence and power.

A clear example is the life of Job, the upright and blameless man. God Himself testified to Job’s righteousness:

“And the Lord said to Satan, ‘Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, one who fears God and turns away from evil.’” (Job 1:8)

Even when Satan challenged Job’s faithfulness, God preserved him, saying:

“Behold, all that he has is in your power; but do not lay your hand on him.” (Job 1:12)

Through Job’s life, we witness God’s justice, protection, and blessing. His patience, obedience, and fear of God reveal how God works in and through the lives of those who are pure in heart.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.
Amen.

text.text: The Division of Time during the Fast of the Prophets

text:
According to the tradition of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church:

👉🏾Hidar 6 – Tahsas 7 or 13:
Zemene Astemhhro (Season of Instruction)

👉🏾Hidar 13 – Hidar 19:
Kidist (Holy Week)

👉🏾Hidar 20 – Hidar 26:
Mikurab (Synagogue Week)

👉🏾Hidar 27 – Tahsas 3:
Metsagu

👉🏾Tahsas 4 – Tahsas 6:
Debre Zeyt (three days only)

👉🏾Tahsas 7 – Tahsas 13:
Zemene Sibket

👉🏾Tahsas 14 – Tahsas 20:
Zemene Birhan (Season of Light)

👉🏾Tahsas 21 – Tahsas 27:
Zemene Nolawi (Season of the Shepherds)

👉🏾Tahsas 28 – Tahsas 29:
Lidet (Nativity Days)

✍🏾

It is a season set apart to instruct the faithful about the goodness and mercy of God, who forgives all our sins. During this time, believers are reminded that, just as God shows compassion toward us, we are called to forgive one another.

✍🏾

text.text: Purpose of the Season of Astemhro

text:
During this period:

The Church continually asks God for forgiveness on behalf of her children.

Believers repent and seek forgiveness for their sins.

Teaching is given abundantly, guiding the faithful toward spiritual renewal.

✍🏾

text.text: The Sabbaths of the Season of Instruction

text:
According to the writings of St. Yared, the Sundays of this season are:

1. Astemhro (E-tezekiro)

2. Astemhrot (Lotu Sbhat)

3. Mkurab (Synagogue – “God is perfect in His existence”)

4. Metsagu (Yibelu Israel)

5. Debre Zeyt (The Sabbath given for the rest of humankind)

These divisions were established by St. Yared in Dǝgwa Ze-Astemhro.The names of the four Sundays, except the first Astemhro , are the same as the Sundays of the Great Lent.

✍🏾

text.text: Are the Sundays the Same as the Sundays of Lent(abiy tsom)?

text:
The names of the Sundays match those of the Lenten season.
However, the content is different.

During the nights and services of these weeks:

the Psalms chanted,

the readings appointed for the Divine Liturgy, and

the teachings delivered

all differ in focus and mystery.

✍🏾

When we say that the teachings “differ in mystery,” we mean that their spiritual emphasis matches the appointed time.
However, the Church always teaches one unchanging foundation:

The eternal Word of God is proclaimed in every season.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.

text.text: by attaining the Stages of Holiness to see the Holy Trinity

text: The Holy Church teaches that the path to holiness and the vision of the Holy Trinity is cultivated through ten virtues. These virtues are grouped into three major stages of purification and spiritual growth.

text.text: 1. The Purity of the Flesh ( ንፅሐ ሥጋ)

text: This first stage focuses on disciplining the body and the senses so that they become instruments of righteousness. It includes three forms of purity:

text.text: a. Purity of the Flesh – Mearge Tsmawe (መዓርገ ጽማዌ)

text: This means guarding the senses, refusing to imitate the desires of the world, and listening only to the word of God with a humble and obedient heart.

text.text: b. Purity of the Heart – Mearge Libawe (መዓርገ ልባዌ)

text: This is the willingness to receive the word of God deeply, storing understanding and spiritual knowledge like precious treasure.

text.text: c. Purity of the Sweet Song – Mearge Tea‘me Zimare (መዓርገ ጣዕመ ዝማሬ)

text: This is the devotion of praising God day and night, imitating the ceaseless hymns of the holy angels.

text.text: 2. The Purity of the Soul (ንፅሐ ነፍስ)

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾by attaining the Stages of Holiness to see the Holy Trinity

The Holy Church teaches that the path to holiness and the vision of the Holy Trinity is cultivated through ten virtues. These virtues are grouped into three major stages of purification and spiritual growth.

1. The Purity of the Flesh ( ንፅሐ ሥጋ)

This first stage focuses on disciplining the body and the senses so that they become instruments of righteousness. It includes three forms of purity:

a. Purity of the Flesh – Mearge Tsmawe (መዓርገ ጽማዌ)

This means guarding the senses, refusing to imitate the desires of the world, and listening only to the word of God with a humble and obedient heart.

b. Purity of the Heart – Mearge Libawe (መዓርገ ልባዌ)

This is the willingness to receive the word of God deeply, storing understanding and spiritual knowledge like precious treasure.

c. Purity of the Sweet Song – Mearge Tea‘me Zimare (መዓርገ ጣዕመ ዝማሬ)

This is the devotion of praising God day and night, imitating the ceaseless hymns of the holy angels.

2. The Purity of the Soul (ንፅሐ ነፍስ)

This second stage concerns the inner transformation of the soul, cultivating four spiritual dispositions:

a. Mearge Anb'e (መዓርገ አንብዕ)

Deep reflection Crying on the sacrifice of Christ and the sins of humanity, allowing the heart to be humbled and grateful.

b. Mearge Kunene (መዓርገ ኲነኔ)

The subduing of fleshly desires so that the will of the soul may govern and lead according to righteousness.

c. Mearge Fiqir (መዓርገ ፍቅር)

The cultivation of perfect love: loving God first and loving all people sincerely and without hypocrisy.

d. Mearge Huset (መዓርገ ሁሰት)

It includes the spiritual ability to be present in  wherever one is, shining like sunlight, and to perceive what is happening in another place while remaining in one place.

3. The Purification of the Heart (ንፅሐ ልቡና)

This final and highest stage includes the mysteries granted to those who have reached spiritual maturity:

a. Mearge Nitsare Mela’ekt (መዓርገ ንፃሬ መላእክት)

The grace of seeing angels, similar to the prophets and the saints who beheld heavenly visions.

b. Immersion in the Ocean of Divine Grace, mearge Tesetmo , መዓርገ ተሰጥሞ

At this level, the soul becomes deeply united with the mercy, peace, and illumination of God.

c. Mearge Kewine esat (መዓርገ ከዊነ እሳት )

The state in which the body is surrounded by divine light, shining from head to toe like fire, as witnessed in the lives of holy men and women.

Netsrote Silus Kidus (ነጽሮተ ሥሉስ ቅዱስ)

The attainment of the seeing of the Holy Trinity. Those who reach this stage behold the divine mystery and join the angels in ceaseless praise.

These ten virtues describe the spiritual ladder that leads believers from bodily discipline, to the purification of the soul, and finally to the illumination of the heart. At the highest stage, the saints see God and praise Him together with the heavenly hosts.

text.text: In The Second Coming of the Lord

text:
The Holy Church teaches that on the Last Day, when our Lord comes in His majesty to judge the living and the dead, every human being will behold Him. Saint John the Evangelist describes this awe-inspiring moment in the Revelation:

“Behold, He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him, even those who pierced Him; and all the tribes of the earth will wail because of Him.”
Revelation 1:7

Even those who crucified Him, long buried, will rise and see Him.  the Prophet Hosea described the terror of the unrepentant on that day:

“They will say to the mountains, ‘Cover us,’ and to the hills, ‘Fall on us.’”Hosea 10:8

This is the fear of those who rejected God’s mercy. Scripture does not soften the reality. It tells us plainly:

“It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.”
Hebrews 10:31

When humanity stands before the throne of judgment, nothing will be hidden. All will see God, though not all will rejoice.

For the faithfuls , the Final Day is not terror but fulfillment. Saint Paul teaches the mystery of spiritual sight:

“The Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom. And we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory.”
2 Corinthians 3:17-18

What the righteous taste now through the Holy Spirit, they will behold clearly after the Resurrection. Their vision is not fear but light. Their transformation begins now and completes then.

Our Lord Himself explained that in the age to come, the righteous will rise in purity and glory:

“They will be like the angels of God in heaven.”
Matthew 22:30

Those who lived in faith, repentance, and love will be filled with clarity, holiness, and the joy of the Kingdom forever. Their sight of God will be eternal praise, not judgment.

✍🏾

text.text: Who Are the People to Whom God Has Revealed Himself?

text:
The Church teaches that no human being has ever seen God in His divine essence, for the Godhead is invisible, incomprehensible, and beyond all created perception. Yet, in His love, God has revealed Himself to humanity in different ways.

Saint John declares:
“No one has ever seen God; the only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, He has made Him known.”
(John 1:18)

The revelation of God is therefore known fully in the Incarnation, when the Son of God became man for our salvation.

Through the Incarnation, our Lord Jesus Christ revealed the Father to us. The apostles, who walked with Him in purity of heart, received this grace.

Christ said to them:

“Blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear.”
Matthew 13:16

And again:

“Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.”Luke 10:23

The apostles saw God in the flesh and heard His teachings directly. Through them, the revelation of God spread to the whole world.

✍🏾

text.text: God Revealed Himself to the Holy Prophets and Fathers

text:
