text:
Before the fall, Adam and Eve lived in purity and communion with God. Their hearts were without corruption, and they experienced God’s presence directly in the Garden.

a. Their Creation and Life with God

“The Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul.”
Genesis 2:7

God planted Eden and placed Adam there:

“The Lord God planted a garden in Eden… and there He put the man whom He had formed.”
Genesis 2:8

God entrusted Adam with work and commandment:

“The Lord God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to dress it and keep it.”
Genesis 2:15

He commanded him concerning the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge:

“Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat… but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, you shall not eat.”
Genesis 2:16–17

b. The Creation of Eve

God revealed His care further:

“The Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam… and He took one of his ribs… and made it into a woman and brought her to Adam.”Genesis 2:21–22

c. After the Fall

Even after they sinned, Adam and Eve encountered God when He came to judge them:
Genesis 3:1–8

This encounter shows the holiness and justice of God, and the consequences of disobedience.

During the Fast of the Prophets, the Church designates each Sunday with a special name and appointed readings. These Sundays resemble the pattern of the Great Fast, yet each has its own theme, hymn, and teaching that prepares the faithful for the mystery of the Incarnation.

1

Dates: Hidar 6–12 

This week is called “(Astemhro)” because it reflects the revelation of God’s mercy and the beginning of spiritual instruction that leads believers out of darkness.

“Etezekiro...
“Do not remember our sins; do not leave us to destruction…”

“Fetsm lene senaytye
“Perform for us the goodness that is with You…” can also be offered as an alternative hymn.

Psalm: “Remember not our former sins, O Lord; let Your mercy come quickly to us, for we are brought very low.” (Ps. 78:8)

👉🏾Gospel: Matthew 6:5–16

👉🏾Liturgy: Kidase Egzi-e

👉🏾Teaching Focus

The Church proclaims that God, through His compassion, delivered the world from the 5,500 years of curse and darkness. Through His goodness and patience, He brings the faithful from the death of body and soul into the light of salvation.

Dates: Hedar 13–19 

This week is called “Holy or kidst ” because it emphasizes the sanctification of the Sabbath and thanksgiving to God who made it holy.

Hymns of Saint Yared

“Let the Sabbath be hallowed to Him who sanctified it…”

“In heaven and on earth, in the sea and in all the deep places, He has done whatever He pleased.” (Ps. 134:6)

👉🏾Gospel: John 5:16–28

👉🏾Liturgy: The Liturgy of Saint Athanasius

Kidst in the Great Fast 

Psalm

“Geneyu Le Egziabher”
A call to give glory and strength to the Lord, acknowledging His majesty and His holiness.

Misbak

“Egziabher-se semayate gebre amin…”
“But God created the heavens; faith and virtue are before Him; holiness and the splendor of glory are in His sanctuary.”
(Psalm 95:5–6)

This response teaches that God is the Creator of all, the source of truth, virtue, and holiness. 

Gospel Reading

Matthew 6:16–25.and the liturgy is :The Liturgy of Epiphanius

This week’s sermon focuses on God’s forgiveness, the call to submit ourselves to His will, the holiness that He requires from His people, and the honoring of the Holy Sabbath.

Hymns of Saint Yared

“Etezekiro...
“Do not remember our sins; do not leave us to destruction…”

“Fetsm lene senaytye
“Perform for us the goodness that is with You…” can also be offered as an alternative hymn.

Psalm: “Remember not our former sins, O Lord; let Your mercy come quickly to us, for we are brought very low.” (Ps. 78:8)

👉🏾Gospel: Matthew 6:5–16

👉🏾Liturgy: Kidase Egzi-e

👉🏾Teaching Focus

The Church proclaims that God, through His compassion, delivered the world from the 5,500 years of curse and darkness. Through His goodness and patience, He brings the faithful from the death of body and soul into the light of salvation.

Dates: Hedar 13–19 

This week is called “Holy or kidst ” because it emphasizes the sanctification of the Sabbath and thanksgiving to God who made it holy.

Hymns of Saint Yared

“Lotu sbhat welotu akotet lekedesat lesenbet…”
“Let the Sabbath be hallowed to Him who sanctified it…”

✍🏾Readings

Psalm during the Liturgy:
“In heaven and on earth, in the sea and in all the deep places, He has done whatever He pleased.” (Ps. 134:6)

👉🏾Gospel: John 5:16–28

👉🏾Liturgy: The Liturgy of Saint Athanasius

Kidst in the Great Fast 

Psalm

“Geneyu Le Egziabher”
A call to give glory and strength to the Lord, acknowledging His majesty and His holiness.

Misbak

“Egziabher-se semayate gebre amin…”
“But God created the heavens; faith and virtue are before Him; holiness and the splendor of glory are in His sanctuary.”
(Psalm 95:5–6)

This response teaches that God is the Creator of all, the source of truth, virtue, and holiness. 

Gospel Reading

Matthew 6:16–25.and the liturgy is :The Liturgy of Epiphanius

This week’s sermon focuses on God’s forgiveness, the call to submit ourselves to His will, the holiness that He requires from His people, and the honoring of the Holy Sabbath.

text: Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

The fourth week of the Fast, covering the days from Hidar 27 to Tahsas 7, is called Metsagu, meaning “a sick or bedridden person.”

✍🏾

text.text: Why the Day Is Called Metsagu

text:
It commemorates the day when Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ opened the eyes of the man who was born blind, revealing His divine power and mercy.

👉🏾Hymn of the Day (Sunday)

The hymn composed by Saint Yared begins with:
“Yebelu Israel…”(“The people of Israel said, ‘We have neither seen nor heard of the man who was born blind and whose eyes were opened on the Sabbath)
It recounts the disbelief of the Israelites who said they had never seen or heard of a miracle such as the healing of the man born blind.

👉🏾Psalm of the Day

Psalm 4:2–3
"O sons of men, how long will you remain in darkness? Why do you love vanity, and why do you seek falsehood? Know that God is revealed in His righteousness.”
This psalm teaches us to recognize and believe in the wondrous works God performs for His faithful ones.

👉🏾Gospel Reading

John 9:1to the end.
The Gospel narrates the healing of the young man who was born blind. Through this miracle, Christ reveals His divine authority to heal both physical afflictions and the sicknesses of the soul. The Liturgy of the day is the Mass of God.

✍🏾Spiritual Meaning of the Week

During this week, we reflect on both the healing of the body through Christ’s miracles and the healing of the soul through His teachings.

Many people today suffer not only from physical illnesses but from spiritual blindness that keeps them from seeing the light of righteousness. These diseases include:

👉🏾Gossip

👉🏾Heresy

👉🏾Hatred

👉🏾Violence

👉🏾Theft

👉🏾Lying

👉🏾Adultery

👉🏾Immorality of all forms

👉🏾Corruption, even among those entrusted with sacred duties

These sins are deeper wounds than any bodily disease.

✍🏾The True Cure

Physical illnesses may be healed by holy water or medicine. But the sickness of sin has only one remedy: repentance.
Every person afflicted by these spiritual diseases is called to return to our Lord Jesus Christ, the eternal Healer of both body and soul.

The fifth and final week of the Fast is known as Debre Zeyt, covering Tahsas 4 to 6.

Hymn of the Day (Sunday)

The hymn for this week is:
“Ser'a Senbete le-seb’e…”(“God created the Sabbath as a day of rest for all creatures in heaven and on earth.”)It praises God who established the Sabbath for all creatures in heaven and on earth.

👉🏾Psalm of the Day

Psalm 131:15–16
"I will bless her widows, I will satisfy her poor with bread, I will clothe her priests with peace, and her righteous ones will rejoice greatly."
This psalm proclaims God’s care for His Church and His people.

👉🏾Gospel Reading

Luke 12:32–41
Christ teaches that since no one knows the hour of their death or the passing of the world, every Christian must live in constant spiritual readiness and Instead of gathering perishable wealth, we must increase righteous deeds that prepare the soul for the Kingdom of God.
The Liturgy of the week is the Liturgy of Saint Athanasius.

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

The period from Tahsas 7 to Tahsas 26 during the Fast of the Prophets is known as the Season of Sermon.

Why It Is Called the Season of Sermon(Zemene sibket)

It receives this name because during this time the Prophets foretold, taught, and proclaimed the coming of the Lord in the flesh.As the Church remembers their testimony and continues to proclaim the mystery of the Incarnation, this period is called the Season of Sermon, meaning a time of proclamation and divine teaching.

The first Sunday of the Season of Sermon is itself called “Sermon.”(Sibket)

Meaning of the Day

On this Sabbath, the Church teaches that the Incarnation of Christ was revealed beforehand in the Torah of Moses, in the writings of the Prophets, and in the Psalms.

Because the prophets proclaimed His coming long in advance, this day is named “Sermon,” which signifies a message that unites humanity with God.

During this week the Church reflects on the genealogy of Christ, from the calling of Abraham to the kingdom of David, recognizing the prophetic preparation for the birth of the Savior.

On the Sabbath of Sermons, the Gospel reading declares that our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ is the One about whom Moses and the Prophets wrote.

Gospel Reading

(John 1:45)This part affirms that Christ is the fulfillment of the Law and the Prophets.

Teachings of the Prophets

David the Prophet and King, through the Holy Spirit, foresaw and sang about the salvation brought by Christ.(“Send forth Your hand from above and save me.”)

Isaiah the Prophet, one of the greatest among them, proclaimed the mystery of the Incarnation, saying:
“Oh, that You would rend the heavens and come down, so that the mountains might shake at Your presence!” (Isaiah 64:1)
The Church teaches this prophecy as pointing to Christ descending from heaven and being born of the Virgin Mary.
Following the apostolic teaching, the Church preaches Christ at all times.

Saint Paul teaches:
“We preach Christ crucified.” (2 Corinthians 4:5)
The Church proclaims the hope of salvation that our Lord Jesus Christ granted and accomplished for humanity.

As Saint Yared sings,
“We preach the Son who existed before the world, who is the Savior.”
The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church continually proclaims Christ the Son of God, who died for our sins and rose to give life to all, whether in times of abundance or in times of hardship, in every season and circumstance.

Part 6 Continues ...

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.
Amen.

✍🏾

Genesis 18:1–15

At the heat of the day, while Abraham sat at the door of his tent in the plains of Mamre, the Lord appeared to him. When he lifted his eyes, he saw three men standing nearby. Recognizing the divine presence, he ran from the tent door to meet them and bowed himself to the ground in deep reverence.

Abraham said, “Lord, if I have found grace in Your sight, do not pass by Your servant. Let a little water be brought, so that Your feet may be washed, and rest yourselves under the tree. I will bring a morsel of bread for your refreshment; after that, you may continue on your way, since you have come to your servant.”
And they replied, “Do as you have said.”

✍🏾

Job 19:23–27; Job 42:1–6

Job cried out in the midst of deep suffering:
“Oh, that my words were written! Oh, that they were inscribed in a book, engraved with an iron tool and lead, carved forever in the rock! But I know that my Redeemer lives, and that He will stand upon the earth at the end of time. After my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I shall see God; I myself will behold Him, and not another. My heart longs with desire.”
(Job 19:23–27)

Later, when God answered him from the whirlwind, Job humbled himself and said:
“I know that You can do all things, and that no purpose of Yours can be withheld. Who is the one who speaks without knowledge? I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know. Hear me, and I will speak; I will ask You, and You make me to understand. I had heard of You with my ears, but now my eyes have seen You. Therefore I humble myself in dust and ashes and repent.”
(Job 42:1–6)

✍🏾

Genesis 28:10–17; Genesis 32:30

Jacob left Beersheba and journeyed toward Haran. When the sun had set, he found a place to rest for the night. He took a stone, set it under his head, and lay down to sleep.

In his dream he saw a ladder set upon the earth, reaching up to heaven. The angels of God were ascending and descending upon it, and the Lord stood above it and said:

text:
Exodus 33:11–16; Exodus 24:9–11

The Lord spoke with Moses face to face, as a man speaks with his friend. After receiving God’s word, Moses returned to the camp, while Joshua the son of Nun remained in the tent, devoted to the service of God.

Moses said to the Lord, “You command me to lead this people, yet You have not shown me whom You will send with me. You know me by name, and You have said that I have found favor in Your sight. Now, therefore, show me Your way, so that I may truly know You, and know that I have found favor before You. Consider also that this nation is Your people.”

The Lord answered, “My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” But Moses replied, “If Your presence does not go with us, do not bring us up from here. For how will it be known that I and Your people have found favor in Your sight unless You go with us? It is Your presence that sets us apart from all the peoples on the face of the earth.”
(Exodus 33:11–16)

Earlier, Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders of Israel had gone up the mountain, where they saw the God of Israel. Under His feet there appeared a pavement shining like the heavens themselves, clear and radiant like a sapphire stone.
(Exodus 24:9–11)

✍🏾

2 Chronicles 18:18–22

The prophet Micaiah spoke boldly before the kings and said,
“Hear the word of the Lord: I saw the Lord seated on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing on His right hand and on His left. And the Lord said, ‘Who will persuade Ahab king of Israel to go up and fall at Ramoth-Gilead?’ One spoke in one manner and another in another manner.”

Then a spirit came forward and stood before the Lord and said, “I will persuade him.”
The Lord said to him, “By what means?”
The spirit answered, “I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.”
The Lord said, “You shall persuade him, and you shall prevail; go out and do so.”

Micaiah concluded, “Now therefore, behold, the Lord has allowed a lying spirit to enter the mouths of your prophets, for the Lord has declared calamity against you.”(2 Chronicles 18:18–22)

✍🏾

2 Samuel 7:18; Psalm 16:8–11

David went in and sat before the Lord and said,
“Who am I, Lord God, that You have brought me this far?”

And again he proclaimed,
“I have set the Lord always before me; because He is at my right hand, I shall not be shaken.
Therefore my heart is glad, and my tongue rejoices; my flesh also rests in hope.
For You will not abandon my soul to Sheol, nor allow Your Holy One to see corruption.
You have made known to me the path of life; in Your presence is fullness of joy, and at Your right hand are pleasures forever.”
(Psalm 16:8–11)

text:
1 Kings 3; 1 Kings 9:1–5

Solomon went to Gibeon, the chief high place, and offered a thousand burnt offerings on the altar.
In the night the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream and said,
“What shall I give you?”

Solomon answered,
“You have shown great mercy to Your servant David my father, because he walked before You in truth, righteousness, and uprightness of heart. You have continued this mercy by giving him a son to sit on his throne this day. And now, O Lord my God, You have made Your servant king in place of David my father, and I am but a little child; I do not know how to go out or come in.

Your servant is among Your chosen people, a great people too numerous to count.
Therefore give Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people, to discern between good and evil. For who is able to judge this great people of Yours?”

Solomon’s request pleased the Lord.

After Solomon had completed the house of the Lord, the king’s house, and all that he desired, the Lord appeared to him again as He had appeared at Gibeon and said,
“I have heard your prayer and your supplication. I have consecrated this house which you have built, to put My name there forever; My eyes and My heart will be there always.

If you walk before Me with integrity of heart and uprightness, as David your father walked, and keep My commandments and My statutes, then I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, as I promised David, saying, ‘You shall not lack a man on the throne of Israel.’”

God blessed him and confirmed the covenant with him.

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

The second Sunday of the preaching season is called “Light.”

On this day, the Church remembers how the holy prophets preached that the Light of our souls would be born, and that the true Light would come into the world. This Light is our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, who is the Light of faith and the Light of life.

Before the coming of Christ, humanity lived in spiritual suffering. Both body and soul were separated from God, who is the true Light. Therefore, this week is a time to remember how the prophets proclaimed in advance that the Light of our souls would be born and that the true Light would shine upon the world.

During this week, the Church also remembers the fourteen generations from the birth of King David to the Babylonian exile, teaching how God prepared the way for the coming of Christ through history.

✍🏾 The Prayer of the Prophets

One of the ways the holy prophets awaited, guarded, and revealed God’s salvation was through their longing for Light.

King David prayed:

“Send out Your light and Your righteousness; let them lead me.”(Psalm 43:3)

Through this prayer, he was not only asking for guidance, but also crying out for the coming of the Son of God. The meaning of this prayer is: “Send us Your Son, who is Light, righteousness, and truth, so that He may lead us into the Kingdom of Heaven.”

The Prophet Isaiah also proclaimed this hope of salvation (Isaiah 49).

✍🏾

As Saint John the Evangelist testified:

 “The true Light, which gives light to everyone, was coming into the world.”(John 1:9)

This Sabbath is dedicated to preaching the Light of Jesus Christ, who alone is the True Light that enlightens every human soul.

Our Lord Himself proclaimed:

 “I am the Light of the world. Whoever follows Me will not walk in darkness, but will have the Light of life.”
(John 8:12)

On this holy Sabbath, the Church preaches about His divine Light and teaches believers to make Christ the Light of their lives, that they may walk in truth and inherit the Kingdom of Heaven.

✍🏾

On this day, the Church proclaims Jesus Christ as “Light from Light” and “the ineffable Light,” the true and eternal Light.

In the hymn of Saint Yared, we sing:

“The Light has come into the world.”

Following the teaching of our holy fathers and the instruction of Saint Ephrem in the Monday Praise of the Virgin Mary, the Church proclaims:

 “The true Light that shines upon all who live in this world, all creation rejoices in Your coming for the love of humanity. You saved Adam from his error, You freed Eve from the curse of death, You gave us the Spirit by whom we are born anew, and with the angels we praise You.”

Therefore, we give thanks to our God and Savior Jesus Christ, who is the Light of our lives and the salvation of our souls.

(Part 6)

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾The Second Sunday – “Light” 

The second Sunday of the preaching season is called “Light.”

On this day, the Church remembers how the holy prophets preached that the Light of our souls would be born, and that the true Light would come into the world. This Light is our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, who is the Light of faith and the Light of life.

Before the coming of Christ, humanity lived in spiritual suffering. Both body and soul were separated from God, who is the true Light. Therefore, this week is a time to remember how the prophets proclaimed in advance that the Light of our souls would be born and that the true Light would shine upon the world.

During this week, the Church also remembers the fourteen generations from the birth of King David to the Babylonian exile, teaching how God prepared the way for the coming of Christ through history.

✍🏾 The Prayer of the Prophets

One of the ways the holy prophets awaited, guarded, and revealed God’s salvation was through their longing for Light.

King David prayed:

“Send out Your light and Your righteousness; let them lead me.”(Psalm 43:3)

Through this prayer, he was not only asking for guidance, but also crying out for the coming of the Son of God. The meaning of this prayer is: “Send us Your Son, who is Light, righteousness, and truth, so that He may lead us into the Kingdom of Heaven.”

The Prophet Isaiah also proclaimed this hope of salvation (Isaiah 49).

✍🏾The True Light

As Saint John the Evangelist testified:

 “The true Light, which gives light to everyone, was coming into the world.”(John 1:9)

This Sabbath is dedicated to preaching the Light of Jesus Christ, who alone is the True Light that enlightens every human soul.

Our Lord Himself proclaimed:

 “I am the Light of the world. Whoever follows Me will not walk in darkness, but will have the Light of life.”
(John 8:12)

On this holy Sabbath, the Church preaches about His divine Light and teaches believers to make Christ the Light of their lives, that they may walk in truth and inherit the Kingdom of Heaven.

✍🏾The Light of Our Lives 

On this day, the Church proclaims Jesus Christ as “Light from Light” and “the ineffable Light,” the true and eternal Light.

In the hymn of Saint Yared, we sing:

“The Light has come into the world.”

Following the teaching of our holy fathers and the instruction of Saint Ephrem in the Monday Praise of the Virgin Mary, the Church proclaims:

 “The true Light that shines upon all who live in this world, all creation rejoices in Your coming for the love of humanity. You saved Adam from his error, You freed Eve from the curse of death, You gave us the Spirit by whom we are born anew, and with the angels we praise You.”

Therefore, we give thanks to our God and Savior Jesus Christ, who is the Light of our lives and the salvation of our souls.

Part 7 Continues ...

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.
Amen.

text:
The third Sunday of the Zemene sibket  is called “Nolawi.”
The word Nolawi means “Shepherd” or “Guardian.”

On this day, the Church remembers how the holy prophets foretold that the Son of God would appear as the true Shepherd and Guardian of humanity. Jesus Christ is proclaimed as the true Shepherd, and on this day the Church sings, sanctifies, and gives thanks.

✍🏾

The prophets saw the people of Israel, and indeed all humanity, as sheep without a shepherd. They prophesied about the coming of the true Shepherd who would gather, protect, and guide His flock.

On this holy Sabbath, the Church reflects on the fourteen generations from the Babylonian exile to the birth of Christ, showing how God prepared the world for the coming of the Good Shepherd.

On this holy Sabbath, the Church teaches that the prophets prayed, saying:

“Hear, O Shepherd of Israel,You who lead Joseph like a flock,
You who dwell between the cherubim, shine forth.”(Psalm 80:1)

Through this prayer, they were crying out for the coming of the true Shepherd, so that:

👉🏾the scattered sheep would be gathered,

👉🏾the wolf would not destroy the flock, and

👉🏾the human race, separated from the faithful Shepherd because of sin, would be restored and fed.

By this, the Church proclaims that Jesus Christ is the true Shepherd, who gathers, protects, and feeds His people.

✍🏾

When the prophecies were fulfilled, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ revealed Himself as the true Shepherd, saying:

 “I am the Good Shepherd. The Good Shepherd gives His life for the sheep.”(John 10:11)

He also declared:

“I am the Good Shepherd. I know My sheep, and am known by My own, just as the Father knows Me and I know the Father; and I lay down My life for the sheep.”
(John 10:15)

By the Spirit of God, the righteous King David proclaimed:

“The Lord is my Shepherd; I shall not want.
He makes me lie down in green pastures.”(Psalm 23:1–2)


During this holy fasting season, the Church lifts its prayer before God:

👉🏾Lord, send out Your Light and Your righteousness.

👉🏾O Good Shepherd, remember us, for we have wandered.

👉🏾Restore the love in our hearts that has grown cold.

👉🏾Grant us Your true peace, that we may return to our true Shepherd,
our Savior Jesus Christ, who never abandons His flock.

✍🏾

text.text: 1. The True Protector of the Flock

text:
The faithful protector of all Christians is our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. He is the true Shepherd and the true Guardian of the Church.

The priests of the Church are also protectors of the flock, because they received the command given through Saint Peter:

“Feed My sheep.”

Yet, in an age of deception and false teaching, believers must learn to distinguish between true shepherds and wolves.

Our Lord warned:

 “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.”
(Matthew 7:15)

We recognize them by their fruits, for as a good tree bears good fruit, so a true shepherd brings good to his flock.

A wolf does not come to protect the sheep, but to destroy and devour them. In the same way, false shepherds do not seek the salvation of souls but their own gain. Their end is destruction, because they lead many away from the truth.

Therefore, the faithful must be watchful, faithful in doctrine, and firm in their spiritual life.

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾The Fast of the Prophets is a holy season of fasting that is prescribed by God’s law. It is not only a time of abstaining from food, but a time of repentance, humility, prayer, and return to God. Through this fast, the faithful weaken the power of sin and strengthen their spiritual life.

The Holy Scriptures teach us that fasting must be proclaimed and entered with a sincere heart. Although this message was spoken through the prophet Joel, it reveals the same truth taught by the prophets: that fasting brings divine blessing.

The Word of God says:

👉🏾 “Now, says the Lord, return to Me with all your heart, with fasting and weeping and mourning. Do not rend your garments, but your hearts. Return to the Lord your God, for He is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and He relents from sending calamity. Who knows if He will turn and leave a blessing behind Him, a grain offering and a drink offering for the Lord your God? Blow the trumpet in Zion; sanctify a fast; call a solemn assembly. Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children and nursing infants. Let the bridegroom go out from his chamber, and the bride from her wedding.”(Joel 2:12–16)

✍🏾Through this teaching, the Church understands that fasting is not only a physical discipline, but a spiritual calling to return to God with a broken and humble heart.

✍🏾The Orthodox Tewahedo Church, based on the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Prophets, and the Apostles, has established a holy fast called the Fast of the Prophets, also known as the Fast of the Nativity.

This fast is founded on the spiritual preparation made by the prophets before the birth of the Savior. Through prayer, fasting, and prophetic revelation, they prepared themselves and the people to receive the coming of the Messiah.

✍🏾

The basis of this holy fast is:

The prophets spiritually counted and awaited the appointed weeks before the birth of the Lord.

Fasting is a sacred remembrance of the spiritual struggles and hope of the prophets who waited for salvation.

✍🏾

The holy Prophet Daniel revealed the mystery of the coming of the Messiah through his prophetic vision:

“Seventy weeks are determined upon your people and upon your holy city,
to finish the transgression, to make an end of sins,
to make reconciliation for iniquity,
to bring in everlasting righteousness,
to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the Most Holy.

Know therefore and understand, that from the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem unto the Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks, and sixty-two weeks: the street shall be built again, and the wall, even in troublous times.

And after the sixty-two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for Himself: and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.

And He shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week He shall cause the sacrifice and the offering to cease; and for the overspreading of abominations He shall make it desolate, even until the consummation, and that determined shall be poured upon the desolate.”(Daniel 9:24–27)


The holy prophets Isaiah, Jeremiah, Malachi, and many others proclaimed the coming birth of our Lord Jesus Christ in advance through fasting, prayer, and earnest supplication. Their hearts were fixed on the promise of salvation, and they longed to see the fulfillment of God’s word.

text:
According to the canon of feasts and spiritual order of the Church, the prophets lived in hope:

They desired to see the Savior,
To hear His word,To witness His works.

In the same spirit, we fast so that we may partake of their hope, behold His salvation, hear His word, and share in the blessing of His holy Nativity.

We rejoice in our God who has made us worthy to share in this joy, just as the angels praised Him saying:

“Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.”

✍🏾

✍🏾According to the tradition handed down by our holy fathers, the Fast of the Prophets was established as follows:

👉🏾The prophets fasted for forty (40) days in expectation of the Messiah.

👉🏾Abraham the Syrian fasted for three (3) days.

👉🏾Together with one day (Gehad tsom )additional sacred day, the total becomes forty-Fout (44) days of fasting before the Nativity.

✍🏾This fast is distinct from the Great Fast (Abiy Tsom / Hudade). Each fast has its own spiritual purpose and appointed time. The order of the Church is wisely established for the spiritual growth of all.

✍🏾May our Almighty God, who has granted us time for repentance and preserved us until this day, grant us forgiveness, compassion, and mercy, and make us worthy to inherit His eternal Kingdom, according to His great goodness.

text:
In the year of King Uzziah's death, I saw the sovereign master seated on a high, elevated throne. The hem of his robe filled the temple. Seraphs stood over him; each one had six wings. With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and they used the remaining two to fly.

They called out to one another, "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord who commands armies! His majestic splendor fills the entire earth!"

The sound of their voices shook the door frames, and the temple was filled with smoke.

I said, "Too bad for me! I am destroyed, for my lips are contaminated by sin, and I live among people whose lips are contaminated by sin. My eyes have seen the king, the Lord who commands armies."

But then one of the seraphs flew toward me. In his hand was a hot coal he had taken from the altar with tongs.He touched my mouth with it and said, "Look, this coal has touched your lips. Your evil is removed; your sin is forgiven." (Isaiah 6:1–7)

✍🏾

“In the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, while I was among the exiles by the River Chebar, the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.”(Ezekiel 1:1)

He saw the glory of God revealed in a heavenly vision:

“Above the expanse over their heads was the likeness of a throne, like the appearance of a sapphire stone; and upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness of a Man. From the appearance of His waist upward I saw the likeness of brightness, like glowing metal, and from His waist downward I saw the likeness of fire. Brightness surrounded Him, like the appearance of a rainbow in the cloud on a rainy day. This was the appearance of the glory of the Lord. When I saw it, I fell upon my face, and I heard the voice of One speaking.”(Ezekiel 1:26–28)

Later, he saw the divine throne again above the cherubim:

“Above the expanse that was over the heads of the cherubim appeared the likeness of a throne, like a sapphire stone. And He said to the man clothed in linen, ‘Go in among the wheels, even under the cherubim, and fill your hands with coals of fire from between the cherubim, and scatter them over the city.’ And he went in as I watched.”(Ezekiel 10:1–2)

✍🏾

“I watched until thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took His seat. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of His head was like pure wool. His throne was a fiery flame, and its wheels were burning fire. A stream of fire flowed and came forth from before Him. Thousands upon thousands ministered to Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him. The court was seated, and the books were opened.”(Daniel 7:9–10)

“I watched because of the sound of the great words which the horn was speaking. I watched until the beast was slain, and its body destroyed and given to the burning fire. As for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was taken away, yet their lives were prolonged for a season and a time.”(Daniel 7:11–12)

 “I saw in the night visions, and behold, One like the Son of Man came with the clouds of heaven. He came to the Ancient of Days, and they brought Him near before Him. Then to Him was given dominion and glory and a kingdom, that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve Him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and His kingdom is one that shall not be destroyed.”
(Daniel 7:13–14)

“ He showed me this: I saw the Lord standing by a tin wall holding tin in his hand.

The Lord said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "Tin." The Lord then said, "Look, I am about to place tin among my people Israel. I will no longer overlook their sin.Isaac's centers of worship will become desolate; Israel's holy places will be in ruins. I will attack Jeroboam's dynasty with the sword."
."(Amos 7:7–9)

“I saw the sovereign One standing by the altar and he said, "Strike the tops of the support pillars, so the thresholds shake! Knock them down on the heads of all the people, and I will kill the survivors with the sword. No one will be able to run away; no one will be able to escape.Even if they could dig down into the netherworld, my hand would pull them up from there. Even if they could climb up to heaven, I would drag them down from there.
Even if they were to hide on the top of Mount Carmel, I would hunt them down and take them from there. Even if they tried to hide from me at the bottom of the sea, from there I would command the Sea Serpent to bite them.
Even when their enemies drive them into captivity, from there I will command the sword to kill them. I will not let them out of my sight; they will experience disaster, not prosperity." (Amos 9:1–5)

✍🏾

After six days, Jesus took Peter, James, and John and led them up a high mountain by themselves. There He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and His clothing became as white as light. Suddenly, Moses and Elijah appeared and spoke with Him.

Peter said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If You wish, let us make three tabernacles: one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

While Peter was still speaking, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and a voice came out of the cloud saying:

“This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Hear Him.”

When the disciples heard this, they fell on their faces and were filled with great fear. Jesus came to them, touched them, and said, “Rise, and do not be afraid.” When they lifted up their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus alone.

✍🏾

The pure in heart will see God because of their unwavering faith. The first martyr, Saint Stephen, exemplified this truth. When he stood before the Jews with steadfast faith, and they stoned him, he was filled with the Holy Spirit. Looking up to heaven, he saw the glory of God  Son of Man standing at the right hand of God. He declared:

“Behold, I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.”
(Acts 7:54-60)

Similarly, Saint John, in his vision, received a message from the Spirit concerning those who die in the Lord:

“Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from henceforth. The Spirit said to me, ‘Write this down, so that they may rest from their labors, and their works will follow them.’”
(Revelation 14:13)

Thus, those who accept martyrdom for the sake of their faith, like Saint Stephen, will behold the glory of God and be received into His presence with honor and everlasting joy.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

Saint Paul teaches us the humility and reverence required in receiving divine revelations. He says:

“It is necessary to boast, though it is not profitable; yet I will speak of visions and revelations of the Lord. I know a man in Christ whether in the body or out of the body, God knows who was caught up to the third heaven fourteen years ago. I know such a man, whether in the body or out of the body, God knows. He was caught up into paradise and heard ineffable words, which it is not lawful for a man to speak. On behalf of such an individual I will boast, but on my own behalf I will not boast, except about my weaknesses.(2 Corinthians 12:1-6)

✍🏾

Saint John describes the glory and majesty of God as revealed to him in a vision:

👉🏾“After this I looked, and behold, a door was opened in heaven; and the first voice I heard was like a trumpet, saying, ‘Come up hither, and I will show thee things which must take place hereafter.’ Immediately I was in the Spirit, and behold, a throne was set in heaven, and One sat upon the throne, appearing like jasper and sardius stone.

Around the throne were twenty-four other thrones, and upon them sat twenty-four elders, clothed in white raiment, with golden crowns upon their heads.”
(Revelation 4:1-4)

✍🏾

text.text: Blessed Are Those Who Believe Without Seeing

text:
When the apostles told Saint Thomas about the resurrection of our Lord, he said,

“Unless I put my hand into His side and see, I will not believe.”

Jesus appeared to him and said,

“Reach here your finger and see My hands; and reach here your hand and put it into My side. Do not be unbelieving, but believing.”

Thomas responded,“My Lord and my God.”

Jesus then said“Because you have seen Me, you have believed; blessed are those who have believed without seeing.”
(John 20:27-29)

This shows that true faith does not require physical sight but comes from a heart that trusts in God. Those whose faith is steadfast, like the apostles and the venerable Abba Hiriakos, experience the presence of God in their lives:

“He is wonderful who does not dare, yet is humble among us; he is supreme who is unattainable, yet serves as an example to us; he is an untouchable fire, yet we have seen Him, touched Him, and eaten and drunk with Him,” speaking with complete faith as if among the holy apostles.

✍🏾Today, the hearts of the faithful, when purified, see God continually. Through prayer, worship, and obedience, they perceive His guidance, help, and protection from temptation. In the end, they will see Him giving them the kingdom prepared before the foundation of the world, and they will live with Him forever, praising His glory.

👉🏾Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God. (Matthew 5:8)

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾Our Lord taught in the seventh Beatitude:
“Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the children of God.” (Matthew 5:9)

Peace means tranquility, calmness, rest, and contentment.
It refers to a right and holy relationship with God, oneself, and other people, founded on:

• Love
• Unity
• Harmony

Gideon declared, “The Lord is Peace” (Judges 6:24), teaching that God Himself is the source of peace. God is truly a God of peace.

Peace is one of the Fruits of the Holy Spirit, and its foundation is love (Galatians 5:22).

The Holy Gospel is called the “Gospel of Peace” because it is the message of reconciliation that God sent to humanity, and which our Lord Jesus Christ preached to the whole world (Acts 10:36; Ephesians 6:15).

Peacemakers are the living fruits of the Gospel, beloved by God.
They actively work to establish peace:

• Between human beings and God
• Between God who dwells in the heart and the inner life of a person
• Between the soul and the body

✍🏾

(2 Corinthians 5:18–20 )
Active peacemakers establish peace between people and God by first reconciling themselves with God. Through repentance, confession, prayer, and obedience, they become vessels of peace.

After making peace with God, they help others to become steadfast in faith, to repent, and to return to God.

👉🏾The Apostle Paul teaches:

“All things are of God, who has reconciled us to Himself through Jesus Christ, and has given us the ministry of reconciliation; that is, in Christ God was reconciling the world to Himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and has committed to us the word of reconciliation. Therefore, we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were pleading through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.”(2 Corinthians 5:18–20)

This holy work of reconciliation is also carried out through the intercessions of the saints, by which many souls are drawn back to God.

✍🏾

text.text: How Peacemakers Establish Peace Among People

text:
Peacemakers first live in peace with others themselves. A person who is not at peace with people cannot bring peace between people.

After establishing peace in their own relationships, peacemakers work to create peace among others in three ways:

👉🏾

, they do not create conflict, spread rumors, or increase misunderstandings and hatred.

👉🏾

, they actively help to resolve the problems that cause division, anger, and hostility.

👉🏾

, they allow love, forgiveness, and compassion to govern relationships between people.

Peace among people can exist at different levels:

• Between individuals
• Between families
• Between communities
• Between nations

A true peacemaker does not divide people but unites them through wisdom, patience, and love.

text.text: Peace Between the Soul and the Body

text:
Active peacemakers establish peace between the soul and the body by listening to their conscience and refusing to let fleshly desires rule their spiritual life. When the desires of the body rise against the spirit, inner conflict appears. Peace is restored when the will of the flesh is subjected to the soul.

This spiritual discipline is strengthened through:

• Fasting
• Prayer
• Almsgiving
• Perseverance in prayer

These holy practices purify the heart and bring order between the spirit and the body.

Saint Yared (ቅዱስ ያሬድ) teaches about fasting:

“Fasting heals the wounds of the soul, destroys the desires of the flesh, and teaches humility to the young.”

Inner peace is established by trusting in God and casting all our worries upon Him (Psalm 4:8; 1 Peter 5:7). This is the foundation for becoming a true peacemaker and being called a child of God.

Through these practices, the believer lives in harmony, and the peace of God dwells within the heart.

text.text: 1. Making Peace Between Man and God

text:
The way the world pursues peace and the way Christianity teaches peace are different.

The world focuses on peace between people, achieved through:
• Building good relationships
• Resolving conflicts by scientific, cultural, or legal means
• Maintaining order and security

Christian teaching, however, emphasizes that true peace begins with a good relationship between man and God.

Peace between man and God means harmony in all aspects of this relationship:

• Creator and creature
• Father and son
• Worshipper and God
• Prayer-maker and prayer recipient
• Lawgiver and judge

This relationship was first disrupted when the Devil desired to be God, turning what should have been harmony between Creator and creature into enmity.

✍🏾Through repentance, faith, and reconciliation, peacemakers restore this divine harmony, becoming instruments of God’s peace in the world.

✍🏾The peace between man and God is founded on God’s love, but this peace was broken when man sinned. Enmity arose when man disobeyed God’s command and was expelled from Paradise (by eating the fruit of the forbidden tree), creating a barrier between humanity and God (Hebrews 9:3).

✍🏾

text.text: Peace in the Old Testament (Torah System)

text:
In the Old Testament, peace with God was symbolized and temporarily restored through sacrificial practices:

The burnt offering represented reconciliation between man and God (Leviticus 6:8–13).

The blood sacrifice was offered for God alone, symbolizing atonement for sin (Hebrews 9:22; Romans 6:23).

Although these sacrifices atoned for temporary sins, they could not fully remove the enmity between man and God (Hebrews 10:4).

The wall of enmity was ultimately broken down by our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ, through His sacrificial death on the cross.

✍🏾As the Mediator of the New Covenant, God incarnate reconciled humanity to Himself, restoring the lost peace and bringing man back into true fellowship with God.

✍🏾The Apostle Paul speaks of the salvation that restores peace between man and God:

👉🏾“For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, having been reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.” (Romans 5:10)

He further explains:

👉🏾“But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace, who has made the two one, having abolished the law of commandments contained in ordinances, and having broken down in his flesh the middle wall of hostility, that he might create in himself one new man from the two, making peace, having killed the hostility, and by him reconcile both to God in one body, through the cross.” (Ephesians 2:13–16)

👉🏾This teaches that our Lord Jesus Christ is our peace, who removes the barrier of hostility between humanity and God.

Paul also affirms:

👉🏾“God was pleased for all his fullness to dwell in him, and through him to reconcile to himself all things, whether on earth or in heaven, by making peace through the blood of his cross.” (Colossians 1:20)

✍🏾Through the sacrifice of His blood, Christ restores harmony and establishes true peace, reconciling man with God and created the foundation for peace among people and within the soul.

✍🏾The Apostle Paul speaks of the salvation that restores peace between man and God:

👉🏾“For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, having been reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.” (Romans 5:10)

He further explains:

👉🏾“But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace, who has made the two one, having abolished the law of commandments contained in ordinances, and having broken down in his flesh the middle wall of hostility, that he might create in himself one new man from the two, making peace, having killed the hostility, and by him reconcile both to God in one body, through the cross.” (Ephesians 2:13–16)

👉🏾This teaches that our Lord Jesus Christ is our peace, who removes the barrier of hostility between humanity and God.

Paul also affirms:

👉🏾“God was pleased for all his fullness to dwell in him, and through him to reconcile to himself all things, whether on earth or in heaven, by making peace through the blood of his cross.” (Colossians 1:20)

✍🏾Through the sacrifice of His blood, Christ restores harmony and establishes true peace, reconciling man with God and created the foundation for peace among people and within the soul.

Continues 👇🏾

text.text: The Peace That Comes From God

text:
The Apostle James teaches:
“Let him who turns a sinner from the error of his way know that he will save his soul from death and cover a multitude of sins.” (James 5:20)

To turn a sinner from sin through repentance is to create peace between man and God. For this reason, God is rightly called the God of Peace
(Romans 15:33; Philippians 4:9; Hebrews 13:20).

The peace given by our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ is not like the peace of the world.
He said:

“Peace I leave with you, My peace I give unto you; not as the world gives, do I give unto you.” (John 14:27)

The peace of Christ is an inner peace that no one can steal.
It is peace with God and peace with others that remains firm even in trials.

Saint Paul teaches:

“The peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:7)

This divine peace is deeper than human thought and stronger than human fear.
It guards the heart, strengthens the soul, and keeps the believer firm in faith.

✍🏾Our Lord said:
“These things I have spoken to you, that in Me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation; but be of good cheer, I have overcome the world.” (John 16:33)

✍🏾True peace is found when we live in communion with Him.
Even in times of temptation and suffering, the believer overcomes the world through the peace of Christ.

The Apostle Paul teaches:

“Therefore, being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.” (Romans 5:1),“Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body; and be thankful.” (Colossians 3:15)


Our Lord told His disciples:
“Do not think that I came to bring peace on earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.” (Matthew 10:34)

This does not mean that Christ came to create violence or war. Rather, He came to establish eternal peace between man and God, not political peace or earthly kingdoms. He did not come to take political power or to free Israel from Roman rule, as many expected.

The “sword” He spoke of is the Word of God, which separates truth from falsehood and light from darkness.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

Our Lord God and Savior Jesus Christ established peace among people. In His time, He especially reconciled the Jews with the Gentiles, and also the Jews with the Samaritans.

✍🏾Rather than those who claimed to be children of the kingdom, Christ praised the faith of the Gentiles. When the centurion said, “Only say the word, and my servant will be healed,” the Lord responded, “Truly I tell you, I have not found such great faith, not even in Israel” (Matthew 8:10; Luke 7:9). In this way He revealed the depth of the Gentile’s faith and opened the preaching of the Gospel to all peoples.

✍🏾He preached the Gospel in Samaria and commanded His apostles to preach there and to the ends of the world
(Acts 1:8; Mark 16:15; Matthew 28:19).Even Herod and Pilate, who had been enemies, temporarily reconciled with one another during the judgment of Christ
(Luke 23:11–12).

✍🏾The Apostle Paul teaches, “At that time you were alienated from the commonwealth of Israel and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and being without God in the world. But now in Christ Jesus, you who were once far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ… So then you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God” (Ephesians 2:12–13, 19). Through this, he declares that the Gentiles who believe in the Gospel are made one with the faithful of Israel in Christ.

✍🏾Our Lord taught us to live in peace with all people. He said, “You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.’ But I say to you, do not resist an evil person. Whoever slaps you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also. Whoever wants to sue you and take your cloak, give him your garment as well. If anyone compels you to go one mile, go with him two. Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.”He continued, “You have heard, ‘Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I say to you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven. For He makes His sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.”(Matthew 5:38–45)
Through this, He teaches us that true peace requires sacrifice and a heart shaped by mercy.

✍🏾The Apostle Paul likewise says, “Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but associate with the humble. Do not be wise in your own opinion. Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Consider what is good in the sight of all people. If it is possible, as much as depends on you, live at peace with everyone. Beloved, do not avenge yourselves, but leave room for the wrath of God; for it is written, ‘Vengeance is mine; I will repay,’ says the Lord. If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him something to drink; for in doing this you will heap coals of fire on his head. Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.”
(Romans 12:16–21)

👉🏾He taught that peace must be pursued with all people, and he worked to reconcile believers such as Onesimus and Philemon, making them co-workers in Christ (Philippians 1:16–17).

✍🏾Saint Paul, the Lamp of the World, taught extensively about peace throughout his epistles. To the Corinthians he wrote, “God has called us to peace” (1 Corinthians 7:15), 

He exhorted the Romans, “Let us follow the things which make for peace and for the edification of one another” (Romans 14:19), urging believers to actively seek what builds up the community and strengthens unity.

text:
To the Hebrews he taught, “Follow peace with all men, and seek holiness, without which no one will see the Lord” (Hebrews 12:14). he teaches them to follow the way of Peace, 

Saint Paul also warned the Corinthians against division:
“I appeal to you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that you be united in the same mind and in the same judgment. For it has been reported to me by those of Chloe’s household that there are quarrels among you.”(1 Corinthians 1:10–11)

✍🏾

In the Old Testament, Abigail stands as a shining example of a true peacemaker. When anger flared between David and Nabal, she acted with wisdom and diligence to bring reconciliation (1 Samuel 25). Abigail was a woman of great intelligence and beautiful character, while her husband Nabal was harsh and foolish in his behavior.

When David sent messengers to greet Nabal, Nabal responded arrogantly, saying, “Who is David? Who is the son of Jesse? Many servants are running away from their masters today. Should I take my bread, my water, and the meat I have prepared for my shearers and give it to men whose origins I do not know?” His pride and disrespect provoked David’s anger.

When Abigail learned of this, she hastened to meet David. She dismounted from her donkey, fell on her face before him, bowed to the ground, and spoke with humility and wisdom. She said, “My lord, the Lord has restrained you from coming to bloodshed and from avenging yourself. The Lord will certainly establish a lasting house for you, for you fight the battles of the Lord. Please forgive the offense of your servant. When the Lord has fulfilled all His good promises toward you and made you ruler over Israel, let this not be a stumbling block or a burden on your conscience, that you shed innocent blood or avenged yourself with your own hand. And when the Lord has dealt well with you, remember your servant.”

David prised the Lord who sent her, blessed her good judgment, and blessed her for keeping him from acting in anger. Her wisdom restored peace and prevented bloodshed.

✍🏾

text.text: Making Peace Between Soul and Body

text:
✍🏾Making peace between the soul and the body is the heart of true inner peace. A person who is reconciled with God and lives in peace with others gains a calm conscience and a steady heart. This stillness within is not accidental; it grows where trust in God is alive.

✍🏾Saint Paul teaches that inner peace is rooted in prayer and surrender. “In everything, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.”(Philippians 4:6).Peace comes when we entrust our worries to Him, believing that He is faithful to help us.

✍🏾Saint Peter gives a similar counsel,urging us not to allow anxiety to disturb our inner peace. He writes, “Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.”(1Peter 5:7). When the heart releases its burdens into the hands of God, it becomes light and quiet.

✍🏾The prophet Isaiah affirms this same truth: “You will keep in perfect peace the one whose mind is stayed on You, because he trusts in You.”(Isaiah 26:3). The soul that depends on God, leans on God, and rests in God is preserved in peace.

text.text: Making Peace Between the Holy Scriptures and Their Interpretation

text:
👉🏾Saint Cyril of Alexandria teaches that the words of our Lord, “Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God,” also apply to those who bring peace within the understanding of the Holy Scriptures. A peacemaker is not only someone who reconciles people, but also someone who brings harmony to the interpretation of God’s word.

✍🏾Those who labor to unite the teachings of the Law and the Prophets, the Old Testament and the New Testament, the four Holy Gospels, and the Epistles are blessed. These scholars act as mediators, revealing the mystery that binds all the Scriptures together. By showing how each part completes the other, they build peace within the Church’s understanding and guard the unity of faith.

✍🏾The holy fathers who gathered at the Councils of Nicaea, Constantinople, and Ephesus are also true peacemakers. They reconciled differing interpretations, defended the Orthodox faith, and guided the Church to a unified confession. Through their spiritual labor, they protected the faithful from division and preserved the right understanding of the Scriptures.

✍🏾Blessed also are those who bring together believers who differ in reading or emphasis, helping them discover the deeper unity found in the mystery of the Scriptures. By guiding them toward agreement on what is shared and charity in what differs, they allow the Church to live in harmony.

They are called children of God because, in their work, they imitate the life of the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who reconciled all things to Himself and brought peace through truth.

✍🏾

text.text: For They Are Called Children of God

text:
To be called a child of God is a great privilege. Just as a son is an heir, so too are the children of God heirs of His promises (Romans 8:17).

👉🏾The Evangelist Saint John says:
"But as many as received Him, to them He gave power to become children of God, even to those who believe in His name; who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God" (John 1:12-13).

Thus, the children of God are those who believe in His name and are born of God. These children of God love one another, for Saint John continues:
"Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God; and everyone who loves the Father loves Him who is born of Him. By this we know that we love the children of God: when we love God and keep His commandments" (1 John 5:1-2).

✍🏾The promise that God has given to His children is that they will be set free from the bondage of corruption and will attain the glorious freedom of the children of God (Romans 8:21).

✍🏾The children of God are those who are led by the Holy Spirit. They are not afraid of suffering for Christ’s sake, and they are heirs of glory. Saint Paul explains in his letter to the Romans:

👉🏾"For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are the children of God. For you have received the Spirit of adoption as sons, whereby we cry, ‘Abba, Father.’ The Spirit Himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God. If children, then heirs; heirs of God; if indeed we suffer with Him, then we are joint heirs with Christ, so that we may also be glorified together" (Romans 8:14-17).

text:
✍🏾The children of God also live as examples of holiness in the world. Saint Paul writes to the Philippians:

👉🏾"Do all things without murmuring or disputing, so that you may be blameless and innocent, children of God without blemish in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom you shine as lights in the world, holding fast the word of life" (Philippians 2:14-16).

✍🏾Thus, the children of God are both heirs of eternal glory and lights to the world. They shine by their faith, obedience, and love, showing others the way of life in Christ.

✍🏾The children of God are recognized by their love, for they imitate the love of their Heavenly Father. The Evangelist Saint John teaches:

👉🏾"See what kind of love the Father has bestowed on us, that we should be called children of God; and so we are. The world does not know Him, and therefore it does not know us. Beloved, now we are children of God; it does not yet appear what we will be. But when He appears, we shall be like Him, for we shall see Him as He is" (1 John 3:1-2).

✍🏾Through this teaching, Saint John shows that the children of God imitate their Father in love. The distinction between the children of God and the children of the devil becomes clear in how they live. Saint John confirms:

"Whoever does not practice righteousness, nor loves his brother, is not of God" (1 John 3:10).

✍🏾Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ has broken down the wall of enmity between man and God and has proclaimed peace. He has also established peace among men. Through His birth, He brought peace to the soul and the body.

✍🏾Blessed are those who, following His example, preach love and establish peace between man and God. Blessed are those who strive to keep others from sin, uphold the law of God, and turn hearts back to God so that they may live in harmony.

✍🏾

text.text: They are called children of God

text:
because they have taken Jesus Christ as their model and have sought to establish peace between man and God. Blessed are those who work to establish love among all people, who seek to resolve disagreements and enmity, and who transform hatred into unity and love. They themselves strive to live in peace with all men.

✍🏾In doing so, they reconcile man with man and man with God. By imitating the Son of God, Jesus Christ, they are truly called children of God.

✍🏾Blessed are those who have established inner peace by subduing the conflict between the will of the soul and the will of the flesh. They bring the will of the flesh into submission to the will of God, casting all their worries upon Him with complete faith, trusting fully in His providence, and removing fear of worldly concerns from their hearts.

✍🏾 They are called children of God because they treasure righteousness and justice. God is the source of truth and justice, and those who follow Him bear the fruits of righteousness. As Saint James teaches:
"The fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace" (James 3:18).

👉🏾We need to strive for peace in every aspect of our lives. By doing so, we imitate God, cultivate righteousness, and are rightly called children of God.

text: Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

The Feast of Be’ata Le-Maryam, celebrated on the third day of Tahsas ,is one of the thirty-three feasts of the Holy Virgin. In Gë`ëz, the name refers to the commemoration of the day when Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, was brought into the temple.

✍🏾

text.text: The Prayer and Vow of Saint Joachim and Saint Hannah

text:
The parents of Our Lady, Saint Joachim and Saint Hannah, lived many years without a child. Infertility in those days was regarded as a great shame, and those considered barren were often excluded from joining the faithful in the temple. Even so:

Their love for one another never diminished.

They never forgot God for even a single day.

They waited with hope for His work to be revealed.

They continually vowed to give back the child God would grant them.

God heard their sincere prayers, and in His mercy He gave them a daughter: the Holy Virgin Mary. Though she was their child for a time, she was ultimately given for the salvation of Adam and all creation.

✍🏾

text.text: The Childhood of the Holy Virgin

text:
The psalmist David says, “I will go into Your house with burnt offerings; I will pay You the vows my lips have spoken in my distress” (Psalm 65:12). In the same spirit, Saint Joachim and Saint Hannah went to the temple to fulfill the vows they had made. God heard their prayer and granted them a child, and they, in turn, offered that child back to Him. This reflects the pattern found in the Torah, where Hannah, the mother of the prophet Samuel, having suffered greatly because of her barrenness, vowed that if God granted her a son, she would dedicate him to the house of the Lord. God answered her prayer, and she faithfully brought Samuel to serve before Him (1 Samuel 1:22–28).

These noble and righteous parents, chosen to become the ancestors of the Sun of Righteousness, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, likewise dedicated their three-year-old daughter, the Holy Virgin Mary, to God. They went to the priest Zechariah, explained the vow they had made, and entrusted their blessed child into his care.

✍🏾

text.text: The Heavenly Provision for the Virgin

text:
“When the priest Zechariah became concerned about the food of the Virgin, he entrusted the matter to God. In response, God sent the holy archangel Saint Phanuel, one of the most glorious angels, to provide for her. As recorded in the Book of Enoch, Phanuel is described as:

“The fourth of the glorious archangels, appointed over those who repent, to be the hope of those who will inherit eternal life.”
(Enoch 10:8–15)

This same angel, by God’s wisdom and will, was appointed as the heavenly steward of the Mother of the Lord. He served her with complete faithfulness.

The Psalmist testifies, “He gave the bread of angels to eat” (Psalm 77:25). In this way, the Holy Virgin lived in the temple nourished by heavenly bread and a heavenly cup, provided through the hand of an angel. It is called heavenly bread and a heavenly cup because it was received from above and given by divine grace.

Likewise, in the Torah, the people of Israel lived on manna that came down from heaven (Exodus 16:10–13). The Scriptures also record that the prophet Elijah was strengthened for forty days by food given to him by an angel (1 Kings 19:9).

In the same manner, Our Lady lived in the temple under the protection of angels, guarded, nourished, and preserved by their ministry.

✍🏾The Holy Virgin as the True Ark of the Covenant

text:
For the Lord has chosen Zion; He has desired her for His dwelling place:‘This is My resting place forever; here I will dwell, for I have desired it.’”(Psalm 131:14)

The entrance of the Virgin Mary into the temple signifies the entrance of the true Ark of the Covenant into the earthly sanctuary. The ancient ark was a symbol of the true and living Ark, Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary.

In the first temple, beyond the second veil, was the Holy of Holies. This sacred place is a symbol of the heart of Our Lady, the true Holy of Holies, the image of her pure body and soul. The ark within it was covered with gold and held the golden pot of manna, Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tablets of the covenant (Hebrews 9:3–4).

Our Lady is pure in spirit, soul, and body, shining with the holiness of pure gold in every aspect of her being.

Within her womb was found the true manna, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, announced by the angel. Just as Aaron’s rod blossomed without being planted or watered, the Holy Virgin conceived without seed. Her womb remained virgin, and the seal of her purity was unbroken, revealing the mystery of how she became the Mother of God without corruption.

The first temple was a model of Our Lady, and the ancient ark foreshadowed her. She, the Ark of Faith, entered the earthly temple on Tahsas 3; and now she dwells eternally in the temple of heaven, the kingdom of God, which is her everlasting resting place (Psalm 131:13–14).

May the intercession, love, tenderness, and motherly care of the Holy Virgin Mary be with us forever. May her prayers strengthen us as we strive to walk in purity and faith, just as she was preserved in holiness from her youth.

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

👉🏾Making peace is the primary task of the Church. The Church is the house of God, where humanity is reconciled with God through repentance, and where people live with God in love. It is a spiritual institution that teaches love to reign among people and preaches forgiveness. In this way, it contributes to peace among people. It also promotes inner peace by teaching a person to submit the body to the soul.

✍🏾 In the liturgy, the Covenant, and all other prayers, the Church always prays for peace. It also has a prayer called “Mestebekue Be-ente Meskel .” This is what it has learned from the Creator, the holy prophets, the holy apostles, and the holy scholars. For example, the following prayer sections for peace are briefly presented.

The Church testifies that peace is found in the Resurrection of Christ, proclaiming:

“Christ rose from the dead with great power and authority; He bound Satan; He set Adam free; peace is found.”Through His Resurrection, Christ defeated the devil, freed humanity from bondage, and restored peace and joy.

✍🏾 During the Holy Liturgy , the priest prays for peace for all, saying:“On this Holy day , let us ask God, our God, who keeps all things in perfect peace, to protect us throughout our lives.”

✍🏾 After His Resurrection, our Lord greeted His disciples with the words, “Peace be with you” (John 20:21). Following this tradition, the Church prays for the faithful by proclaiming, “Peace be with you all,” twelve times during the liturgy .

✍🏾 The faithful respond, “With your spirit,” asking that God’s true peace may dwell within them. This shows the importance of peace in the Christian life. Likewise, when our Lord healed the sick and forgave sins, He said, “My child, go in peace” (Mark 5:34; Luke 7:50).

✍🏾The Holy Church, following this example, instructs the faithful to “go in peace” (enter your homes in peace) at the end of the Liturgy.

✍🏾 The Church continually prays for peace during the Liturgy, according to the words of the Prophet Jeremiah: “Seek peace and pray to God for it” (Jer. 29:7).

✍🏾 In the Liturgy, the priest prays for the peace of the Church, saying:“Remember, O Lord, the peace of the Holy Church, which is one, which the Apostles gathered together.”

✍🏾 The deacon also proclaims:
“Pray for the peace of the Church, which is one, which the Apostles gathered together.”
When the deacon says, “Pray in the holy Church and in the assembly,” the people respond, “Bless our assembly and keep it in peace.”

✍🏾 In addition, during the Liturgy, the Church glorifies God with the angels, saying:“Glory to God in heaven, and on earth peace to people of good will.”

✍🏾When the deacon proclaims, “Pray for peace and love, for they are perfect, and greet one another with a holy greeting,” priests greet priests, deacons greet deacons, men greet men, and women greet women.

✍🏾 In the Liturgy prayer for peace( Be ente kidsat), the Church says:

“We pray for peace, that God, whose Body and Blood make us one, may unite us through His forgiveness.”When praying for peace in the country, it also says:
“We pray for our country, Ethiopia, that God may grant it perfect peace throughout its history.”

✍🏾 At the conclusion of this prayer, the Church humbly asks God, saying:“May He protect all of us who pray and intercede in peace and unity of spirit; grant us love, enlighten our eyes and hearts, and let us approach to God and ask Him to accept our prayers according to His will.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾Peace and the Church:

👉🏾Making peace is the primary task of the Church. The Church is the house of God, where humanity is reconciled with God through repentance, and where people live with God in love. It is a spiritual institution that teaches love to reign among people and preaches forgiveness. In this way, it contributes to peace among people. It also promotes inner peace by teaching a person to submit the body to the soul.

✍🏾 In the liturgy, the Covenant, and all other prayers, the Church always prays for peace. It also has a prayer called “Mestebekue Be-ente Meskel .” This is what it has learned from the Creator, the holy prophets, the holy apostles, and the holy scholars. For example, the following prayer sections for peace are briefly presented.

The Church testifies that peace is found in the Resurrection of Christ, proclaiming:

“Christ rose from the dead with great power and authority; He bound Satan; He set Adam free; peace is found.”Through His Resurrection, Christ defeated the devil, freed humanity from bondage, and restored peace and joy.

✍🏾 During the Holy Liturgy , the priest prays for peace for all, saying:“On this Holy day , let us ask God, our God, who keeps all things in perfect peace, to protect us throughout our lives.”

✍🏾 After His Resurrection, our Lord greeted His disciples with the words, “Peace be with you” (John 20:21). Following this tradition, the Church prays for the faithful by proclaiming, “Peace be with you all,” twelve times during the liturgy .

✍🏾 The faithful respond, “With your spirit,” asking that God’s true peace may dwell within them. This shows the importance of peace in the Christian life. Likewise, when our Lord healed the sick and forgave sins, He said, “My child, go in peace” (Mark 5:34; Luke 7:50).

✍🏾The Holy Church, following this example, instructs the faithful to “go in peace” (enter your homes in peace) at the end of the Liturgy.

✍🏾 The Church continually prays for peace during the Liturgy, according to the words of the Prophet Jeremiah: “Seek peace and pray to God for it” (Jer. 29:7).

✍🏾 In the Liturgy, the priest prays for the peace of the Church, saying:“Remember, O Lord, the peace of the Holy Church, which is one, which the Apostles gathered together.”

✍🏾 The deacon also proclaims:
“Pray for the peace of the Church, which is one, which the Apostles gathered together.”
When the deacon says, “Pray in the holy Church and in the assembly,” the people respond, “Bless our assembly and keep it in peace.”

✍🏾 In addition, during the Liturgy, the Church glorifies God with the angels, saying:“Glory to God in heaven, and on earth peace to people of good will.”

✍🏾When the deacon proclaims, “Pray for peace and love, for they are perfect, and greet one another with a holy greeting,” priests greet priests, deacons greet deacons, men greet men, and women greet women.

✍🏾 In the Liturgy prayer for peace( Be ente kidsat), the Church says:

“We pray for peace, that God, whose Body and Blood make us one, may unite us through His forgiveness.”When praying for peace in the country, it also says:
“We pray for our country, Ethiopia, that God may grant it perfect peace throughout its history.”

✍🏾 At the conclusion of this prayer, the Church humbly asks God, saying:“May He protect all of us who pray and intercede in peace and unity of spirit; grant us love, enlighten our eyes and hearts, and let us approach to God and ask Him to accept our prayers according to His will.

Continues 👇🏾
