👇🏾

✍🏾In another part of the Liturgy, the Church prays for the peace of the country, saying:
“O Lord, grant Your peace to the country, and Your truth to the Church.”

✍🏾 The venerable Abba Dioscorus also prays, saying:
“O Lord, give Your peace to the country and Your truth to the Church. O King of Peace, Jesus Christ, grant us Your peace, forgive us our sins, and make us worthy to go and enter our homes in peace.”(Liturgy of Dioscorus)

✍🏾 Before the distribution of the Holy Body and Precious Blood, the Church calls everyone to give thanks, saying:
“In peace and love, praise and sing to Jesus Christ.”

✍🏾 At the conclusion of the Liturgy, the faithful pray for the blessing of peace, saying:
“Amen. May God bless us, His servants, with peace.”

✍🏾The Church calls God the God of peace. That is why she declares in her prayers, “God is peace.” She also glorifies Jesus Christ, the foundation and crown of all, saying: “Jesus Christ, King of Peace, and Prince of Peace.”

✍🏾 Saint Ephrem, in the Hail Mary, says: “He has made peace among us,” and explains how and by what power this peace was given: “By His cross and His holy resurrection.” Through Him, our Lord Jesus Christ, we have received true peace. This echoes the teaching of the Apostle Saint Paul, who said: “He made peace through the blood He shed on the cross; by Him, He reconciled to Himself all things, whether on earth or in heaven.”

✍🏾 The Covenant Prayer (tselote kidam)begins with these words:
“Peace be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, and to the Virgin Mary, the Mother of God, through the grace of His cross and the grace of His help, for the sake of all the Christian people in the world.”
Through this prayer, the faithful ask that God’s presence and peace may be with all of us.

✍🏾The Church praises the Lord Jesus Christ as the Banner of Peace. As Saint Yared said in the Metshafe diguwa:

“The sign of peace has been born to us, the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who is the banner of our peace.”Abba Giorgis Zegascha, in the Prayer of the Hours, also says:
“The sign of peace, the sign of salvation, has been given to us through Him.”

✍🏾The Holy Church, which calls our Lord Jesus Christ the God of Peace, also calls His Mother, the Holy Virgin Mary, the Abode of Peace.

✍🏾The Church, in her prayer, says:
“Come, let us prise the Blessed Virgin Mary, the Mother of our peace, the Mother of the martyrs, the Sister of the angels, let us prostrate for the grace of our Mother Mary.”

This reminds us that the Blessed Virgin Mary is the abode of peace. She is the dwelling of our peace, Jesus Christ. Through her birth, we have received the peace that was lost.

✍🏾 The Church also praises her during the Hours, saying:
“Peace be upon you, O spiritual dove; we bow down to you.”

✍🏾 The holy apostles are remembered as the Apostles of Peace. For example, in the hymn celebrating the martyrdom of Saints Peter and Paul.

✍🏾The Church also calls the door on the west side “Deje Selam” (Peace Door). This is the door through which a person can forgive someone who has wronged them before entering the Church. The Church also uses names such as “Debre Selam” and “Mekane Selam” for its buildings, signifying places where true peace can be found.

✍🏾 The Church uses the title “Melake Selam” (Messenger of Peace) for the holy angels, as they bring the message of peace to mankind. The priests are also named Melake Selam or Laeke Selam, reflecting their role as chief messengers of peace.

✍🏾 Priests are given this title as well, because they reconcile people with God through repentance, reconcile people with one another, and guide the soul to live in harmony with the body through spiritual education. The Church performs all of this as a spiritual institution that nurtures and maintains peace.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

Abune Gebre Menfes Qidus was born in the land of Nehisa (Egypt). His father’s name was Simeon, and his mother’s name was Aklesia. They lived without children for thirty years and grieved greatly.

One day, Aklesia entered the temple of God, fell before the Holy Trinity, and prayed with tears, asking God to grant her a son whose glory would surpass earthly honor and belong to heaven. God accepted her prayer. She conceived on Megabit 29 and gave birth on Tahsas 29.

At the moment of his birth, the child stood up and glorified God, saying:

“Glory to the Father, glory to the Son, and glory to the Holy Spirit, who has come into the world as the Light of the world.”

From his infancy, Abune Gebre Menfes Qidus lived an angelic life. He did not depend on or eat earthly food or drink but lived in constant thanksgiving to God.

✍🏾

When he was three years old, Saint Gabriel the Archangel, by the command of God and with the blessing of the Holy Virgin Mary and the saints, took him to a monastery and placed him at its gate.

The abbot of the monastery, Abba Zemdebirhan, found the child, raised him with care, taught him the Scriptures, and clothed him in the monastic habit. God granted him the gift of healing, and through his prayers, thousands of blind people were healed in a single day.

When bishops and priests heard of his holiness and came to honor him, Saint Gabriel carried them by his wings and presented them before the Lord, revealing the greatness of Abune Gebre Menfes Qidus in heaven.

Later, when the bishops and priests heard of his holiness and came to collect tax from him, Saint Gabriel the Archangel carried them by his wings and presented them before the Lord. The Lord revealed to them that many souls would be saved from death and from hell through the  spiritual labor of Abune Gebre Menfes Qidus.

Then the Lord commanded him, saying:
“Go into the wilderness and separate yourself from people. Let your dwelling be among sixty lions and sixty wild tigers.”

Abune Gebre Menfes Qidus replied with humility, saying,
“My Lord, what will these creatures eat?”

The Lord answered him,
“Let them eat the dust upon which you tread, and it shall be their food.”

According to the command of God, Abune Gebre Menfes Qidus went into the wilderness and lived peacefully among the wild animals, and they obeyed him in gentleness. Just as the lions submitted to the Prophet Daniel by the power of God, so too the wild animals humbled themselves before the servant of God. They licked the dust sanctified by his footsteps, as though it were nourishment given by heaven.

✍🏾

After thirty years of this , the Lord appeared to Abune Gebre Menfes Qidus in a divine vision, revealing Himself in three forms, and said to him,
“What do you ask of Me?”

Abune Gebre Menfes Qidus replied,
“First, let me pray for the people of the land of Gebota, that You may have mercy upon them.”

The Lord accepted his prayer and, by his intercession, three thousand sinners were delivered from hell and brought into Paradise.

text:
After this, the Lord said to him,“Go to Ethiopia, O chosen land, for the sake of the souls who have been saved through you.”

Then Saint Gabriel the Archangel carried Abune Gebre Menfes Qidus to the (Mdire kebd) in a chariot borne by the wind. From there, he was taken to Ziquwala (Debre Kidus). Seeing with a pure heart the sins of the Ethiopian people, he stood by the seashore and began to pray with great sorrow.

After forty days of prayer, an angel appeared to him and said,
“I will bless all those who remember you and who call upon your name.”

He continued in prayer for one hundred years, saying,
“If You do not forgive Ethiopia, I will not depart from this sea.”

After the completion of the hundred years, the Lord said to him,

“Arise. My mercy is upon all of Ethiopia. Through your prayers, I have granted forgiveness. Come forth

After this, Abune Gebre Menfes Qidus was raised from the earth and stood between heaven and earth for seven years, like a pillar of fire, without resting his eyes, persevering in unceasing prayer for the world.

Satan, who never ceases from envy, came against him in the form of a crow and struck him with blindness. After two weeks, Saint Michael and Saint Gabriel descended from heaven and healed him by the power of God.

From there, they returned to Zquwala, where they saw the Holy Trinity resting under the shade of the elders of the temple. The Trinity said to them:

"We have asked you pby the throne of God. Please sending out us , one by one."

As they departed, they saw the Trinity as three in one, and they fell down in awe. But God lifted them up and said:

"Go to Zquwala and defeat your enemies."

They obeyed, arriving like a flash of lightning, and empowered by the seven archangels they destroyed thousands of demons

Abba Samuel Zewaldba, Abba Anbese Zehazelo, and Abba Binyam Gibts heard the news of Abune Gebre Menfes Qidus and came to seek him. On the seventh day, he revealed himself to them.When Abune Gebre Menfes Qidus met his companions, he saw that his lions had eaten the lions of other saints. Filled with anger, he rebuked them, saying,
“Is it flesh and blood that the Lord has commanded you to eat, or only the dust beneath my feet?”

By God’s power, the lions regurgitated the other lions they had eaten, restoring them unharmed. After this, his lions spat on the ground in humility, then rose and received his blessing, saying,
“O my Father!”

Immediately, the angels of darkness came to take their soul, and Abune Gebre Menfes Qidus repent and said,
“Is not all this because of me?”

In repentance, he bound his own feet with ropes and hung himself upon a great cliff.then Satan cut the rope, but Saint Michael the Archangel ,Saint Gabriel the Archangel received him and saved him.

“Leave me alone.”

text: Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾 The martyr Saint Arsema is commemorated annually for the migration of her holy body, as well as the dedication of her church and shrine, in the regions of Armenia, Cilicia, Syria, Antioch, and Egypt.

Saint Arsema was born to Saint Theodoros and Saint Athnosiya her righteous parents. They were saints adorned with godly conduct and praised for their good works. They devoted themselves to fasting, prayer, almsgiving, and tithes, and were diligent in every spiritual labor.

Despite their righteous life, they were deeply sorrowful because they had no children until old age. Saint Athnosiya, like Hannah, the mother of the prophet Samuel, went to church morning and evening, weeping before God. Their unceasing prayer was that God would grant them a child.

God, who fulfills the desires of the faithful, heard her prayer and appointed the Archbishop of Caesarea to intercede for her. The God instructed Lydianos to pray for her. Through God’s mercy, Saint Arsema was born to her father Saint Theodoros and her mother Saint Athanasius.

According to the account of her martyrdom, her family belonged to a noble priestly lineage who served God with sincerity and faithfulness.

✍🏾The martyr Saint Arsema was among the holy women who diligently learned the Holy Scriptures from her family. She did not keep knowledge in words alone, but translated what she learned into righteous practice and devoted herself continually to prayer and spiritual discipline.

✍🏾During the time of this great martyr, the pagan king who ruled Armenia was called Dertads. In direct opposition to the command of God given to Moses:

👉🏾 “You shall not make for yourself molten gods”(Exodus 34:17)this king worshiped the sun as an idol.

✍🏾He persecuted the Christians of his time and issued a decree, saying:

👉🏾“You must worship the god that I worship. If you refuse, you will be punished for disobeying my command.”

✍🏾The cruel King Dirtads inflicted severe suffering and torture upon twenty-seven Christians because they refused to obey his command. These faithful believers fulfilled the word of our Lord, who said:

✍🏾“If anyone desires to come after Me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Me.”

👉🏾For this reason, they were beaten and subjected to great cruelty, because they would not bow down to the idol that the king worshiped.

✍🏾Saint Arsema, who witnessed their suffering and steadfast faith, was deeply strengthened by their example. According to the account of her life, she began to live a life of spiritual struggle and holy courage, imitating their endurance.

✍🏾At the age of twenty, Saint Arsema openly rebuked the king’s injustice and boldly confessed the divinity of God, standing together with the martyrs who were suffering for the sake of Christ.

✍🏾The king’s servant, amazed by her courage, beauty , and the wisdom of her words, did not dare harm the young woman who willingly accepted martyrdom. Instead, he brought her, together with the twenty-seven Christians, to the king’s palace.

✍🏾When the king saw Saint Arsema, of whom much had been spoken, he was captivated by her beauty and eloquence. Being ruled by earthly desire, he sought her for his own pleasure and begged her to become his wife. He attempted to deceive her by offering gold, silver, and the riches of this world.

✍🏾But Saint Arsema, knowing that bodily beauty is temporary and that worldly wealth is vain and passing, remained firm in her holy resolve and answered the king, saying:

👉🏾“I am the bride of Christ the King, and I do not desire the perishable wealth and pleasures of this world.”

text:
👇🏾

✍🏾When the king heard Saint Arsema’s confession, he was filled with rage. He called his servants and ordered that the lions kept in the palace be released upon her and the Christians. But by the power of God, the lions became gentle. Instead of harming the faithful, they turned against the king and his servants, chasing them until they fled and hid themselves.

✍🏾Enraged by the steadfastness of the Christians in their martyrdom, the king ordered that they be imprisoned and starved. On the fifth day, God filled the prison with heavenly light and sent down food and drink from heaven, which they received in bowls and cups.

✍🏾When the king saw this miracle, he brought them out and cast them into the fire. But God sent the Archangel Gabriel as he saved the three kids he also delivered to them unharmed from the flames.

✍🏾Seeing that the faith of the Christians could not be shaken, the king summoned his advisors and said, “What shall we do?” Following their counsel, he decided that all should be killed by the sword.

✍🏾As the martyrs were being slain, Saint Arsema beheld crowns of victory descending from heaven upon and awaited her own turn with holy longing. She prayed earnestly to God to strengthen her for martyrdom, and she encouraged the faithful, saying:

✍🏾 “Be courageous and steadfast.Do not let the suffering of this world overcome you.Do not be afraid.”

✍🏾When the king had finished killing the others, he turned to Saint Arsema and shouted in anger, saying, “I will not kill you as quickly as the rest.” He subjected her to severe and painful torture, cutting off both of her breasts. When this cruelty did not satisfy him, he ordered that both of her eyes be gouged out.

✍🏾While she endured this suffering, our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, appeared to her and granted her eyes of heavenly light, strengthening her and filling her with divine consolation.

✍🏾At last, when the king grew weary of torturing her, he commanded that she be beheaded by the sword on the twenty-ninth of Meskerem, together with the remaining holy virgins. Thus, they all received the crown of martyrdom.

As the holy prophet David said in the Psalms:

👉🏾“I have made a covenant with My chosen ones.”

✍🏾So also did our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ establish His covenant with Saint Arsema, His faithful martyr.

May the prayers, blessings, intercession, and covenant of the martyr Saint Arsema be with us all. Amen.

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

Peacemaking reflects the heart of God. The noble prophet David teaches us, saying:

“Seek peace and pursue it.”
(Psalm 34:14)

Even in our time, there are faithful fathers, mothers, sons, and daughters who pray for peace and strive to live in peace. For this, we give thanks to God. However, it is deeply painful to witness the rise of criticism, bullying, and insults, especially on social media. These behaviors, born of selfishness and lack of love for others, have widened the divisions among us.

Instead of working to live together in peace, many have come to believe that “it is better to separate than to remain united.” More troubling still is that some who claim to represent the Church, and who speak in the name of the Church, have themselves become sources of division, thereby harming the peace of the Church.

In the religious sphere especially, we now argue over minor and unnecessary matters to the point that people say, “Going to church removes peace, but staying away gives peace.” By our lack of peace, we have caused many to distance themselves from the Church of God.

text:
According to Christian teaching, peace is not achieved by destroying or silencing one side, but by living together in love. Our fathers taught that peace is built through love, and this love is revealed in Jesus Christ, the God of peace.

Even while enduring suffering, Christ did not speak evil, and the apostles did not answer insult with insult. They taught love through endurance. Yet today, as Saint Paul said:

“They do not know the way of peace.”(Romans 3:17)

We have wasted much time in arguments, turning even the Church into a place of conflict. While doing so, when do we find time to serve peacefully? When we criticize a servant of God while he lives and praise him only after his death, this does not create peace. If we love people while they are alive, peace will grow among us.

Even if we cannot become apostles of peace like the ancient Fathers, we must at least avoid destroying peace.

✍🏾

The Gë`ëz phrase “Gebaryane Selam” is often translated into Amharic as “reconcilers.” While this captures part of its meaning, it does not fully express the richness of the original term.

The role of Gebaryane Selam is not limited to reconciliation. It includes:

1. Strengthening peace by establishing love.

2. Restoring peace when it is lost, through reconciliation.

3. Preserving peace after it is restored, working diligently to prevent further conflict.

Thus, the term is best understood as “those who make peace.” Peace is not automatic; it requires understanding, heartfelt willingness, and spiritual commitment, and it can only be achieved through prayer and dedicated service.

✍🏾When teaching His disciples about their apostolic mission, our Lord said:

“When you enter a house, greet it. If it is worthy (and if a child of peace is there), let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.”(Matthew 10:13; Luke 10:6)

Whoever receives a messenger sent by God will receive peace from God. This peace is not only for the individual but also flows outward, creating unity of spirit with others.

✍🏾The Apostle Saint Paul writes to the Ephesians:

“Make every effort to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.”(Ephesians 4:3)

The unity of the Spirit is sustained through peaceful worship, peaceful service, and peaceful living.

Our Lord also taught:
“Have salt in yourselves, and have peace among yourselves.”(Mark 9:50)This highlights that peace is essential for Christian life and the unity of the Spirit.

✍🏾We conclude this lesson on peacemaking with the words of Saint Paul:

👉🏾“May the Lord of peace Himself give you peace always in every way.”(2 Thessalonians 3:16)

And again:

👉🏾“Finally, brothers, rejoice, be perfected, listen to my exhortation, be of one mind, live in peace, and the God of love and peace will be with you.”
(2 Corinthians 13:11)

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

(Matthew 5:11–12)

👉🏾Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ said:

“Blessed are you when they revile you and persecute you and say all kinds of evil against you falsely for My sake. Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven; for so they persecuted the prophets who were before you.”
(Matthew 5:11–12)

In these words, our Lord teaches that sharing in suffering for His sake being reviled, persecuted, and falsely accused is a true manifestation of the Christian life. Suffering endured for Christ is not a sign of abandonment, but a mark of faithfulness.

The Evangelist Luke also writes:

“Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you, and revile you, and cast out your name as evil, for the sake of the Son of Man. Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, for indeed your reward is great in heaven; for in like manner their fathers did to the prophets.”(Luke 6:22–23)

These words show clearly that hatred, exclusion, and separation are also part of the path prepared for those who follow Christ.

👉🏾In the previous verses, our Lord had been referring to “them” in the third person, speaking from a distance in time, extending to the end of the world, and in place, to the ends of the earth. But at this point, He changes His manner of speech and addresses them directly as “you,” speaking in the second person.

✍🏾By doing so, He speaks first to the Christians who were present at the Sermon on the Mount, and at the same time to all who would later be gathered into His Holy Church. He addresses them personally as “you.” In this verse, He speaks especially of His disciples those who are reviled, persecuted, hated, excluded, and falsely accused of all kinds of evil for His name’s sake, that is, for the sake of the Son of Man.

✍🏾 In this verse, our Lord teaches that the reason Christians suffer is because they believe in Him the God who became Man and because they follow Him. In short, they suffer because they are Christians. This verse is a unique and powerful teaching about the suffering that will come upon the Church, and about the glory that is revealed through enduring suffering for Christ’s sake.

✍🏾In this passage, our Lord makes special mention of the holy prophets who suffered before. By this, He teaches that just as people persecuted the prophets whom God sent in earlier times, they will also persecute His disciples. God sent the prophets, and He also sent the apostles. Both the prophets and the apostles were taught that they would endure suffering for His sake and, through that suffering, enter into eternal joy.

✍🏾 Just as persecuting the prophets who were the messengers of God is truly persecuting the God who sent them, so persecuting Christians is persecuting Christ Himself. Christians are the Body of Christ, and He identifies Himself with them.

This truth is clearly revealed in the words of our Lord to Saul:

👉🏾“And he fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?’ And he said, ‘Who are You, Lord?’ Then the Lord said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.’”(Acts 9:4–5)

👉🏾Our Lord did not say, “Why are you persecuting Christians?”
He said, “Why are you persecuting Me?”

Therefore, persecuting Christians is persecuting Christ Himself.

text.text: Blessed Are You When You Are Criticized

text:
Our Lord God and Savior Jesus Christ endured constant criticism, insults, and mockery during His earthly ministry, especially from the Pharisees. Those who crucified Him mocked Him, saying, “He saved others; let Him save Himself.” Even the thieves who were crucified with Him spoke against Him in the same way(Matthew 27:44).

Therefore, a world that received Christ through criticism, rejection, and suffering cannot be expected to receive Christians with praise and honor. The servant is not greater than his Master.

👉🏾This is not a failure of Christianity, but its very nature. Our Lord clearly warned us:

“When all people speak well of you, remember that their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.”(Luke 6:26)

✍🏾If we seek praise, admiration, and approval from the world, we must examine ourselves carefully, for such honor often belonged to false servants rather than to true witnesses of Christ. If we are celebrated by the world while claiming to preach the Gospel faithfully, we should reflect deeply on the truth of our message.

✍🏾If we receive constant thanks, praise, and admiration from the world, we must be cautious, for such approval often accompanied false ministers rather than true servants of Christ. If we are praised and celebrated in the media while claiming to preach the Gospel faithfully being called great teachers, champions of the faith, or servants of truth then we should examine ourselves carefully.

✍🏾For the Gospel of Christ was never spread through applause, and the truth was never welcomed by the world without resistance.

✍🏾Christianity is the way of humility and the endurance of suffering for the salvation of others. This is not a theory or a metaphor; it is the very path shown by Christ and followed by His saints.

✍🏾The holy Apostle Paul, the light of the world and the chosen vessel of God, declared with deep humility: “We have become the scum of the world” (cf. 1 Cor. 4:13). If such a great apostle spoke of himself in this way, what then should we, who are servants in a sinful world, say about ourselves?

✍🏾True Christianity is found where a servant believes in his heart and lives by these words:
“I am foolish, you are wise.
I am weak, you are strong.
I am vile, you are noble.”

✍🏾Whether we accept it easily or resist it inwardly, Christianity remains this way. It is not a path of honor before the world, but a path of the Cross. Humility, rejection, and suffering are not accidents in Christian life; they are signs that one is walking in the footsteps of Christ.

✍🏾Saint Peter, teaching about the glory that comes through suffering, writes:
“If you are reproached for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you” (1 Peter 4:14).

✍🏾It is an honor for Christians to be reproached for the name of Christ. To be mocked, rejected, or spoken against because of faith in Him is not a shame, but a great honor. Such reproach is accompanied by the Spirit of honor that rests upon those who truly believe in Christ and follow His way.

✍🏾When the Apostle Peter teaches about the Christian life, he instructs believers to live with a pure conscience. He says:

text_entities.text: Blessed Are You When You Are Criticized

Our Lord God and Savior Jesus Christ endured constant criticism, insults, and mockery during His earthly ministry, especially from the Pharisees. Those who crucified Him mocked Him, saying, “He saved others; let Him save Himself.” Even the thieves who were crucified with Him spoke against Him in the same way(Matthew 27:44).

Therefore, a world that received Christ through criticism, rejection, and suffering cannot be expected to receive Christians with praise and honor. The servant is not greater than his Master.

👉🏾This is not a failure of Christianity, but its very nature. Our Lord clearly warned us:

“When all people speak well of you, remember that their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.”(Luke 6:26)

✍🏾If we seek praise, admiration, and approval from the world, we must examine ourselves carefully, for such honor often belonged to false servants rather than to true witnesses of Christ. If we are celebrated by the world while claiming to preach the Gospel faithfully, we should reflect deeply on the truth of our message.

✍🏾If we receive constant thanks, praise, and admiration from the world, we must be cautious, for such approval often accompanied false ministers rather than true servants of Christ. If we are praised and celebrated in the media while claiming to preach the Gospel faithfully being called great teachers, champions of the faith, or servants of truth then we should examine ourselves carefully.

✍🏾For the Gospel of Christ was never spread through applause, and the truth was never welcomed by the world without resistance.

“I am foolish, you are wise.
I am weak, you are strong.
I am vile, you are noble.”

text.text: Blessed are you when they persecute you.

text:
Our Lord, in His teaching on spiritual ministry and mission, taught us:
“Beware of men, for they will deliver you up to councils and scourge you in their synagogues. You will be brought before governors and kings for My sake, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles… You will be hated by all for My name’s sake… And when they persecute you in one city, flee to another… If they have called the Master of the house Beelzebub, how much more will they call those of His household!”
(Matthew 10:16–25) teaches us that preaching Christ is a life of enduring hardship and trial. This is an example for us to persevere when we are persecuted.

Also:

👉🏾“Before all this, they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, delivering you up to synagogues and prisons, and you will be brought before kings and governors for My name’s sake, for a testimony against them.”
(Luke 21:12–13) teaches us that persecution, imprisonment, and being brought before worldly courts are part of following Christ.

👉🏾In the Gospel of John, Our Lord said:
“If the world hates you, know that it has hated Me before it hated you. If you were of the world, the world would love its own. But because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, the world hates you. Remember the word that I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his master.’ If they persecuted Me, they will persecute you also; if they have kept My word, they will keep yours also. But all these things they will do to you for My name’s sake, because they do not know Him who sent Me.”(John 15:18–21)teaches that the Christian life calls us to be set apart from the world and, as a result, to be hated by it.

✍🏾In the parable of the sower and the seed, our Lord said:
“These are the ones sown on rocky ground; when they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy. But they have no root in themselves, and endure it only for a while. When tribulation or persecution arises because of the word, they immediately fall away.”
(Mark 4:16–17)

✍🏾Here, Our lord likens those who hear the word but stumble under trials, tribulations, and persecutions to seeds sown on rocky ground. The word of God can bear fruit in our lives only when we endure these trials. This teaches us that tribulation and persecution are part of the Christian journey, and we must persevere in order to turn the seed of God’s word into lasting fruit.


✍🏾As our Lord said in His Gospel, “In the world you will have tribulation; but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world” (John 16:33). The early Christians likewise experienced suffering and persecution. The Evangelist Luke records, “But the Jews stirred up the worshipers, the prominent women, and the leading men of the city, and stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and threw them out of their country. But they shook off the dust from their feet against them and came to Iconium. And they were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit with the disciples” (Acts 13:50-52). Here, Luke shows that the holy apostles followed our Lord’s teaching by shaking off the dust from their feet and moving on in times of tribulation and persecution.

text:
✍🏾 The Apostle Paul also taught that those born according to the flesh persecute those born according to the Spirit: “But just as then he who was born according to the flesh persecuted him who was born according to the Spirit, so also now” (Gal. 4:29). He further instructed the Thessalonians, “In order that no one might be shaken by this suffering, we told you in advance, while we were with you, that we would suffer; and so it happened, and you know” (1 Thess. 3:3-4). Paul emphasized that suffering is part of the path chosen for those who serve God. Indeed, the reward of true service may bring suffering on earth, yet it leads to the crown of life in heaven. Yet how often do we, who serve so little, expect praise, honor, and reward, and become discouraged at the slightest criticism?

✍🏾This beloved apostle, speaking of the joy found in persecution for Christ, says, “Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ’s sake; for when I am weak, then am I strong” (2 Corinthians 12:10). A reader may wonder how one can rejoice while suffering, being persecuted, and experiencing distress. Physically, it seems impossible. Yet spiritually, suffering becomes a source of glory, and enduring hardships for Christ brings profound honor in the eyes of God.

✍🏾In another teaching, the apostle instructs, “Bless and curse not those who persecute you” (Romans 12:14). This teaching surprises when viewed from a human, physical perspective. Naturally, a person condemns those who persecute him and does not bless them. But in Christianity, since our true adversary is the devil, we are called to pray for those who persecute us rather than condemn them. They, too, are in need of salvation, just as we are.

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾The Jews falsely accused our Lord, saying, “Do we not say rightly that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?” (John 8:48). When He cast out demons by His divine power, they said, “He casts out demons by Beelzebub, the prince of demons” (Luke 11:15). When He came eating and drinking, they said, “Behold, a glutton and a winebibber, a friend of tax collectors and sinners” (Matthew 11:19).

When they seized our Lord and brought Him before the high priest, the high priest tore his clothes and said, “He has spoken blasphemy. What further need do we have of witnesses? Behold, you have heard His blasphemy. What do you think?” They answered, “He deserves to die” (Matthew 26:65–66).

✍🏾Later, when our Lord came to His own country and taught in their synagogue, they were astonished and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom and these mighty works? Is this not the carpenter’s son? Is not His mother called Mary? Are not His brothers James and Joses and Simon and Judas? And are not all His sisters with us? Where then did He get all these things?” They were offended by Him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his own country and in his own house” (Matthew 13:54–57).

👉🏾When the Apostle Paul was preaching, some said, “What does this babbler want to say?” Others said, “He seems to be proclaiming foreign gods,” because he preached Jesus and the resurrection (Acts 17:18–19).

When Paul was defending himself, Festus said with a loud voice, “Paul, you are out of your mind! Your great learning is driving you mad” (Acts 26:24).

Therefore, Saint Paul teaches us:

✍🏾 “By honor and dishonor, by evil report and good report; as deceivers, yet true; as unknown, yet well known; as dying, and behold we live; as chastened, yet not killed; as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things.”
(2 Corinthians 6:8–10)

✍🏾

text.text: Suffering for Sin Is Not Righteousness

text:
However, if we are accused truthfully because of our bad deeds, we will not receive a reward in heaven. If we are rebuked for poor judgment, uncontrolled speech, confusion, sin, laziness, or negligence, this is the result of our actions, not righteousness.

Our Lord teaches that blessing belongs to those who are falsely criticized, reviled, and accused for speaking the truth and preaching Christ. But if we are accused and punished because of our sinful conduct, this suffering is not righteousness, it is correction for the wrong we have done.

Therefore, we must not deceive ourselves or others by saying, “We are suffering for the truth,” when the suffering has come upon us because of our sins (cf. John 3:11).

✍🏾

text.text: Rejoice and Be Glad, for Your Reward Is Great in Heaven

text:
Our Lord has given great hope to those who are reviled, persecuted, and falsely accused for His name’s sake. He says, “Great is your reward in heaven.” Indeed, the reward of eternal life in heaven is exceedingly great, and nothing surpasses it.

By saying, “Rejoice and be glad,” our Lord teaches that the reward we receive through faith in Him, through reproach, persecution, and hatred endured for His sake, is a source of true joy. He then adds, “For so they persecuted the prophets who were before you,” showing that those who suffer for His name share in the same honor and glory as the holy prophets who came before them.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾The Jews falsely accused our Lord, saying, “Do we not say rightly that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?” (John 8:48). When He cast out demons by His divine power, they said, “He casts out demons by Beelzebub, the prince of demons” (Luke 11:15). When He came eating and drinking, they said, “Behold, a glutton and a winebibber, a friend of tax collectors and sinners” (Matthew 11:19).

When they seized our Lord and brought Him before the high priest, the high priest tore his clothes and said, “He has spoken blasphemy. What further need do we have of witnesses? Behold, you have heard His blasphemy. What do you think?” They answered, “He deserves to die” (Matthew 26:65–66).

✍🏾Later, when our Lord came to His own country and taught in their synagogue, they were astonished and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom and these mighty works? Is this not the carpenter’s son? Is not His mother called Mary? Are not His brothers James and Joses and Simon and Judas? And are not all His sisters with us? Where then did He get all these things?” They were offended by Him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his own country and in his own house” (Matthew 13:54–57).

👉🏾When the Apostle Paul was preaching, some said, “What does this babbler want to say?” Others said, “He seems to be proclaiming foreign gods,” because he preached Jesus and the resurrection (Acts 17:18–19).

When Paul was defending himself, Festus said with a loud voice, “Paul, you are out of your mind! Your great learning is driving you mad” (Acts 26:24).

Therefore, Saint Paul teaches us:

✍🏾 “By honor and dishonor, by evil report and good report; as deceivers, yet true; as unknown, yet well known; as dying, and behold we live; as chastened, yet not killed; as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things.”
(2 Corinthians 6:8–10)

✍🏾 Suffering for Sin Is Not Righteousness

However, if we are accused truthfully because of our bad deeds, we will not receive a reward in heaven. If we are rebuked for poor judgment, uncontrolled speech, confusion, sin, laziness, or negligence, this is the result of our actions, not righteousness.

Our Lord teaches that blessing belongs to those who are falsely criticized, reviled, and accused for speaking the truth and preaching Christ. But if we are accused and punished because of our sinful conduct, this suffering is not righteousness, it is correction for the wrong we have done.

Therefore, we must not deceive ourselves or others by saying, “We are suffering for the truth,” when the suffering has come upon us because of our sins (cf. John 3:11).

✍🏾Rejoice and Be Glad, for Your Reward Is Great in Heaven

Our Lord has given great hope to those who are reviled, persecuted, and falsely accused for His name’s sake. He says, “Great is your reward in heaven.” Indeed, the reward of eternal life in heaven is exceedingly great, and nothing surpasses it.

By saying, “Rejoice and be glad,” our Lord teaches that the reward we receive through faith in Him, through reproach, persecution, and hatred endured for His sake, is a source of true joy. He then adds, “For so they persecuted the prophets who were before you,” showing that those who suffer for His name share in the same honor and glory as the holy prophets who came before them.

The first martyr, Saint Stephen, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to those who were about to stone him:

“Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those who foretold the coming of the Righteous One. You have now betrayed and murdered Him.”(Acts 7:52)

✍🏾the Jews persecuted and killed the holy prophets who prophesied about Christ, and later, when the appointed time came, they crucified Christ Himself, who was born of the Holy Virgin Mary.

✍🏾Saint Stephen taught by both word and deed that Christians attain glory by passing through suffering and by imitating the prophets and Christ Himself in endurance. He confirmed this teaching by accepting martyrdom and receiving immortal glory.

The light of the world, Saint Peter, also spoke about the glory that comes through suffering, saying:

✍🏾“Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery trial which is happening to you to test you, as though some strange thing were happening to you. But rejoice, inasmuch as you share in Christ’s sufferings, that when His glory is revealed you may also rejoice with exceeding joy. If you are reproached for the name of Christ, you are blessed, for the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you. Let none of you suffer as a murderer, a thief, an evildoer, or a meddler. But if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God in this matter.”
(1 Peter 4:12–16)

✍🏾Through this teaching, Saint Peter shows that just as gold is tested by fire, so the Christian faith is tested through suffering. He teaches us not to fear suffering for Christ, but to rejoice in it, for it leads to glory.

✍🏾Likewise, the most honored Apostle, Saint Paul, teaches that suffering with Christ is the path to sharing in His glory. He says:

👉🏾“If indeed we suffer with Him, we shall also be glorified together.”
(Romans 8:17)

✍🏾Saint Paul further expresses his deep longing to share in Christ’s sufferings, saying:

👉🏾“That I may know Him and the power of His resurrection, and the fellowship of His sufferings, being conformed to His death, if by any means I may attain to the resurrection from the dead.”
(Philippians 3:10–11)

✍🏾The highest reward in heaven is found in fellowship with Christ through suffering, for through suffering we are made partakers of His death and His resurrection.

✍🏾The First and the Last, the living Christ, said in the Book of Revelation to the Evangelist John, who was in exile on the island of Patmos:

✍🏾“Do not fear any of the things which you are about to suffer. Indeed, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison, that you may be tested, and you will have tribulation ten days. Be faithful until death, and I will give you the crown of life.”(Revelation 2:10)

✍🏾This teaching shows us that suffering for Christ leads to the crown of life. Since the ultimate goal of the Christian life is to receive this crown, we must strive to remain faithful, patient, and steadfast until the end.

For So They Persecuted the Prophets Who Were Before You

The prophets who came before were teachers of God’s truth and many of them became martyrs through suffering. Our Lord Himself spoke of these prophets, saying:

“O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to her, how often I wanted to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were not willing. Behold, your house is left to you desolate. For I tell you, you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’”
(Matthew 23:37–39)

This passage shows that the prophets whom God sent before were persecuted and killed for speaking the truth.

On the day of His ascension, our Lord said to His apostles:

“You will be My witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.”(Acts 1:8)

Accordingly, the light of the world, Saint Peter, taught that true witness includes sharing in the sufferings of Christ. He says:

“I, therefore, a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a partaker of the glory that will be revealed, exhort the elders among you: shepherd the flock of God which is among you, serving as overseers, not by compulsion but willingly, not for dishonest gain but eagerly; nor as being lords over those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock. And when the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.”(1 Peter 5:1–4)

This teaching shows that witnessing for Christ is not only by word, but also by sharing in His sufferings and living as an example to the flock.

✍🏾

Saint Peter also teaches the Christian virtues that are worthy of honor, saying:

“By these He has given us exceedingly great and precious promises, that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through evil desires. For this very reason, make every effort to add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge, to knowledge self-control, to self-control perseverance, to perseverance godliness, to godliness brotherly kindness, and to brotherly kindness love.”
(2 Peter 1:4–8)

He further teaches:

“If you endure suffering for doing good, this is commendable before God. For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that you should follow in His steps.”(1 Peter 2:20–21)

✍🏾

The former Fathers, in the Judgment of the King, wrote:

“Do not neglect the Christians who are suffering punishment for the sake of the name of our Lord, the purity of the faith, and the love of God. If you find that your wealth is of no use to you, send it to those who are imprisoned and suffering, so that they may find relief.”

They further describe the holy martyrs as those who are the brethren of Christ, the children of the Most High, the dwelling place of the Holy Spirit, and the witnesses of the sufferings of Christ, co-workers in the manifestation of His Lordship (Judgment of the King, Article 20, No. 745). For this reason, the Church honors them greatly.

✍🏾In the same article, we are commanded to honor those who suffer for Christ as martyrs. It teaches that those who are persecuted for their faith and those who are forced to flee from country to country for the name of Christ are worthy of honor, for they have shared in the sufferings of Christ and borne witness to His truth.

👉🏾Saint John also saw in a vision:
“When He opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been slain for the word of God and for the testimony which they held. And they cried with a loud voice, saying, ‘How long, O Lord, holy and true, until You judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?’ And a white robe was given to each of them, and it was said to them that they should rest a little while longer, until both the number of their fellow servants and their brethren, who would be killed as they were, was completed.”
(Revelation 6:9–11)

✍🏾This passage teaches us that the souls who shared in the sufferings of Christ were given white robes, which signify eternal glory. Therefore, rejoice and be glad, for great is your reward in heaven. This reward is eternal life.

✍🏾Birhane Alam, Saint Paul, in his letter to the Philippians, teaches that sharing in Christ’s suffering is a sign of our salvation. He says:

✍🏾“Only let your conduct be worthy of the gospel of Christ, so that whether I come and see you or am absent, I may hear of your affairs, that you stand fast in one spirit, with one mind striving together for the faith of the gospel, and not in any way terrified by your adversaries, which is to them a proof of destruction, but to you of salvation, and that from God. For to you it has been granted on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for His sake, having the same conflict which you saw in me and now hear is in me.”
(Philippians 1:27–30)

Saint John Afework also teaches that sharing in Christ’s suffering is a sign of salvation, saying:

👉🏾“Do not desire a time when there is no suffering, for you will gain nothing.”

A Christian gains eternal life by sharing in the sufferings of Christ.

Saint Yared Mahletay says:

“He adorned the heavens with stars; He adorned the earth with flowers; He adorned the Church with the blood of His martyrs.”

✍🏾The martyrs, who shared in the sufferings of Christ and bore witness to Him, are the true ornaments of the Church. Therefore, we too are called to share in the sufferings of Christ, and not merely to recount or listen to the accounts of the martyrs’ deaths.

✍🏾Saint Yared teaches us that although the deaths of the martyrs adorn the Church, their lives and endurance are given to us as an example to follow.

✍🏾The martyrs, by sharing in the sufferings of Christ, conquered the world just as Christ Himself conquered the world. The venerable Abba Hiryakos says:

✍🏾"May God grant us to be partakers of the sufferings of Christ and to be added to the company of martyrs, as well as to the company of the holy prophets, the apostles, the blessed martyrs, the righteous, the ordained priests, the diligent angels, and the perfect virgins, as the Lord teaches "(Qəddase Maryam, No. 159).

👉🏾 Our Lord also says:

 “Truly, truly, I say to you, a servant is not greater than his master, nor a messenger greater than the one who sent him. If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.”(John 13:16–17)

👉🏾“Do not desire a time when there is no suffering, for you will gain nothing.”

“He adorned the heavens with stars; He adorned the earth with flowers; He adorned the Church with the blood of His martyrs.”

 “Truly, truly, I say to you, a servant is not greater than his master, nor a messenger greater than the one who sent him. If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.”(John 13:16–17)

text.text: If You Know These Things and Do Them, You Are Blessed”

text:
The early Church Fathers, after explaining the nine Beatitudes recorded in the Gospel of Matthew, taught that a tenth beatitude would be revealed through the Gospel of John. Later, while explaining the words of our Lord in John 13:17, they said, “This is the beatitude we spoke of, which John brings.”

The focus of this lesson is imitating our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ by following the example He gave us. Just as He served others, we are called to serve one another. Those who know this teaching and practice it are truly called blessed.

✍🏾

text.text: The Foundation of the Tenth Beatitude

text:
The foundation of this beatitude is found in the event of Holy Thursday, when our Lord Jesus Christ washed the feet of His apostles.

Saint John the Evangelist writes:
“So when He had washed their feet, taken His garments, and sat down again, He said to them, ‘Do you know what I have done to you? You call Me Teacher and Lord, and you say well, for so I am. If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet. For I have given you an example, that you should do as I have done to you. Truly, truly, I say to you, a servant is not greater than his lord, nor is he who is sent greater than he who sent him. If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.’”(John 13:12–17)


Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ became man in the flesh for our redemption and as an example for us to follow. By His incarnation and His sacrifice on the Cross, He broke down the wall of separation and hostility between God and humanity, offering Himself as a ransom for our salvation. At the same time, He presented Himself as a living example, saying in effect, “Do likewise.”

In this way, Christ became the perfect model for us to imitate. This is the mystery of Christ-likeness that the Apostle Saint Paul taught when he said:
“Imitate me, just as I also imitate Christ.”(1 Corinthians 11:1)

This beloved Apostle also wrote to his disciple Timothy, saying:
“Without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifested in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen by angels, preached among the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up in glory.”(1 Timothy 3:16)

As Saint Paul teaches, the mystery of godliness is indeed very great. This mystery reveals that God became man for our salvation.

👉🏾The Apostle further confirms this truth, saying:

“For if we have been united with Him in a death like His, we shall certainly also be united with Him in a resurrection like His.”
(Romans 6:5)

This union with Christ is the foundation of Christian life and godliness.

text.text: The Main Teachings: Principles of Christian Life and Spiritual Service
1. Serving First by Action, Then by Word

text:
✍🏾 If you know how to serve before teaching, you are blessed.
Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ taught the Gospel first by action and then by word. He did not begin by speaking alone; He began by doing, so that His disciples would clearly understand His teaching.
Throughout His life, He showed before He spoke. In the same way, true spiritual service begins with practice, not with speech.

✍🏾 Our Lord :

He taught baptism by being baptized

👉🏾He taught fasting by fasting

👉🏾He taught prayer by praying

👉🏾He taught victory over temptation by overcoming the devil

👉🏾He taught service by serving

👉🏾He taught humility by humbling Himself

👉🏾He taught love by loving to the end 

He washed the feet of His disciples and then commanded them to wash one another’s feet. First, He showed them through His works; then, He taught them through His words.

By this, He taught us that Christian ministry begins with living Christianity, and only afterward preaching the life we have lived.

✍🏾 In the same Gospel, our Lord said:

“By this all will know that you are My disciples, if you have love for one another.”(John 13:35) This teaches us that the true sign of Christianity is not words, titles, or knowledge, but love lived in action.

He also said:

“Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.”(Matthew 5:16)

Visible good works are essential to spiritual service, because they lead others to glorify God.

Saint John the Evangelist confirms this teaching, saying:

👉🏾“My children, let us not love in word or speech, but in deed and in truth.”(1 John 3:18)Christianity is therefore a practical life, not a spoken theory.

✍🏾 Those who understand that spiritual service is the preaching of a life lived in practice, and who preach both by life and by word, are honorable.However, those who preach a life they do not live must first correct themselves.
Saint Paul speaks strongly about this, saying:

“You who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who preach that a man should not steal, do you steal? You who say, ‘Do not commit adultery,’ do you commit adultery? … The name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”(Romans 2:21–24)This teaches us that self-discipline and obedience must come first .

✍🏾

text.text: Blessed are you if you know how to serve with humility and do so in obedience.

text:
✍🏾 If you know how to serve with humility and practice it, you are blessed.Humility is a great and essential principle of spiritual service. Service that lacks humility is not true spiritual service. Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ carried out all His saving work in humility.

He was not born of kings, but of a humble Virgin.He was not born in a palace, but in a stable.
He was raised in simplicity and obedience.He accepted baptism in humility.He taught and served with humility throughout His ministry.On Holy Thursday, although He was Lord and Teacher, He humbled Himself and washed the feet of His disciples. One of the Fathers, Felix, called this act “the mystery of perfect humility.” Through this, our Lord revealed to us the true meaning of humility. Humility Is the Secret of True Greatness.

text:
✍🏾 In another place in the Gospel, our Lord clearly taught that humility is the secret of greatness, saying:

“Whoever desires to become great among you shall be your servant. And whoever of you desires to be first shall be slave of all. For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.”(Mark 10:43–45)

He also said:

“The greatest among you must become like the youngest, and the one who leads like the one who serves. For who is greater, the one who sits at the table or the one who serves? Is it not the one who sits at the table? Yet I am among you as the One who serves.”(Luke 22:26–27)

These words show that greatness in the Kingdom of God is not measured by position or honor, but by humble service.Christ’s Poverty as the Model of Humility

✍🏾 The Apostle Saint Paul also teaches this truth, saying:

“Though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, that you through His poverty might become rich.”(2 Corinthians 8:9)
Therefore, when our Lord says, “If you know these things and do them, you are blessed,” He teaches that Christian life and ministry must be carried out in humility. Knowing the teaching is not enough. The blessing comes only when humility is practiced.
Just as Christ humbled Himself and washed the feet of His disciples, so must we humble ourselves, serve others, and teach through the example of our lives.
A Warning Against False Humility

✍🏾Preaching humility while placing oneself above others, seeking honor, fame, or superiority, is hypocrisy. Such false service was common among the Pharisees.For this reason, our Lord strongly taught that serving in humility, especially in lowly and hidden ways, is the true foundation of Christian life and spiritual ministry.True humility is not spoken.It is lived.

✍🏾

text.text: Christianity as a Life of Imitating Christ

text:
Our Lord Jesus Christ taught that Christian life is a life of imitating of christ. He said, “If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them” (John 13:17). Christianity is not only knowing Christ, but doing what He did.

The Apostle Saint Paul clearly explains this principle when he says:

“Imitate me, just as I also imitate Christ” (1 Corinthians 11:1).
This means that Christian life and spiritual service are fulfilled by imitating Christ in our daily living.
After our Lord washed the feet of His disciples, He gave them a clear rule for service, saying:
“I have given you an example, that you should do as I have done to you” (John 13:15).

Therefore, spiritual service, expressed briefly, is doing to others what Christ has done for us. When lived out in practice, Christian life is the imitation of Christ in humility, love, and obedience.

Loving as Christ Loved
When our Lord gave the new commandment, He said:

“A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another as I have loved you” (John 13:34).
By this commandment, Christ teaches us that Christianity means loving one another according to His example of love, not according to human standards.

Saint John the Evangelist explains this teaching in his epistle, saying:

👉🏾“He who says he abides in Him ought himself also to walk just as He walked” (1 John 2:6).
To abide in Christ is not merely to confess Him with words, but to walk in the same path He walked.

👉🏾Our Lord further confirms this when He says:

“If anyone serves Me, let him follow Me; and where I am, there My servant will be also” (John 12:26).

👉🏾True service to Christ requires following Him in life, conduct, and sacrifice.

Saint Peter, the light of the world, teaches us about the example of Christ in his epistle, saying:

“For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that you should follow His steps”(1 Peter 2:21).

Saint Paul also explains the humility of Christ, saying:

“He emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, and coming in the likeness of men. And being found in appearance as a man, He humbled Himself and became obedient to the point of death, even the death of the cross”
(Philippians 2:7–8).

✍🏾Through this teaching, Saint Paul shows that Christ is both our Redeemer and our Exemplar. He redeemed us by His sacrifice, and He gave us a model for how to live through His humility and obedience.

✍🏾Blessed Are You If You Serve Even Those Who Hate You

text:
Our Lord Jesus Christ taught that Christian service and love are not limited to those who love us. From the beginning of His teaching on the law of the Gospel, He made this clear, saying:
“But I say to you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who persecute you, that you may be sons of your Father in heaven. For He makes His sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the righteous and on the unrighteous. For if you love those who love you, what reward have you? Do not even the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what more do you do than others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same? Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect”
(Matthew 5:44–48).

✍🏾Through this teaching, our Lord shows that true Christian love goes beyond natural affection. Loving only those who love us is easy and requires no spiritual struggle. But loving those who hate us reflects the perfection and mercy of God the Father.

👉🏾The Evangelist Saint Luke also records this teaching of our Lord, saying:

“But I say to you who hear: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you”(Luke 6:27–28).

✍🏾On Holy Thursday, our Lord Jesus Christ washed the feet not only of the apostles whom He loved, but also of Judas, who would soon deny and betray Him. By this action, Christ taught that Christian service is not limited to those who love us, but also extends to those who oppose us.

Through this act, our Lord revealed that Christian love is meant for everyone, not only for those who return love. Judas, though he knew he would betray the Lord, still received this act of humility and love. Christ loved him to the end.

✍🏾Later, when our Lord offered Himself as the ransom for our salvation on the Cross.He again showed this same mercy by praying for those who crucified Him, saying:

“Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do”(Luke 23:34).This is the fullness of Christian love.

👉🏾When our Lord said, “If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them” (John 13:17), He 

As I have loved the one who betrayed Me and washed his feet, so must your love extend to all people, and your service must include even those who hate you.

Therefore, brothers and sisters who serve in the Church, let us examine ourselves:

Whom do we truly serve?
Do we serve only those who praise us and honor us?Do we accept correction from those who criticize our service?Do we love those who advise us for our spiritual growth and salvation?

Let us teach and correct ourselves first, because the life and actions of Christ stand as a witness and a measure for our service.

✍🏾

text.text: Blessed Are You If You Obey in Love

text:
Our Lord God and Savior Jesus Christ taught His disciples, saying:

“Truly, truly, I say to you, a servant is not greater than his master, nor is a messenger greater than the one who sent him”
(John 13:16).

By these words, our Lord was comparing His disciples to Himself and teaching them humility and obedience. 

Obedience Not by Fear, but by Love In the world, earthly leaders such as presidents or prime ministers command their officials, and obedience is enforced by authority, punishment, or law. If officials disobey, they may be removed from their position or held accountable.

✍🏾But Christian obedience is different. As disciples of Christ, we are called to obey Him not out of fear, but out of love and willingness. Christ Himself, not a man and not an angel, humbled Himself and taught us by His own actions.

If we refuse to serve humbly, or if our hearts resist humility, then our actions silently declare, “We are greater than You.” This pride is the same sin that led to the fall and humiliation of Satan.

My beloved child, Wolete Wold, it is with a heavy heart that I hear of your struggles. Know this: you are not alone in your journey, and your burdens are heard.

Most certainly, we will pray for you. we will lift your name, Wolete Wold, before the Most High God, asking for His divine mercy, strength, and guidance to envelop you. May the All-Merciful Lord, who knows the depths of every heart and understands every pain, send His Holy Spirit to comfort you, to enlighten your path, and to grant you peace amidst your trials.

"Cast your burden upon the Lord, and He shall sustain you; He shall never permit the righteous to be moved." (Psalm 54:23, Septuagint)

Remember these words, my child, for they are a wellspring of hope. God does not abandon those who call upon Him in their distress. He is our refuge and our strength, a very present help in trouble (Psalm 45:1).

May the Theotokos, our Ever-Virgin Mary, intercede for you, and may the prayers of all the saints surround you as a shield. Keep your heart turned towards Christ, for in Him alone do we find true rest.

May God strengthen you, Wolete Wold.

If you are willing, would you like to share more about what you are struggling with, so that we may understand you better and help you more?

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

text.text: Blessed Are Those Who Know and Do

text:
Blessed are you if you not only know God’s Word but also practice it. Christianity is the imitation of Christ. Our Lord God and Savior Jesus Christ humbled Himself and washed the feet of His disciples. He said,

“You also ought to wash one another’s feet.”

He further said,

👉🏾“Blessed are you if you know and do the new commandment, ‘You also ought to wash one another’s feet.’”

He taught His disciples,
“Strengthen your Christian life by serving one another with humility and love.”

Just as He demonstrated humility on Holy Thursday, we too are called to teach humility by washing the feet of the faithful and priests on this sacred day each year.

✍🏾

text.text: Holy Thursday – The Day of the Mystery

text:
✍🏾This day is called the Day of the Mystery, because it is the day on which the mystery of the Eucharist was established. Following the teachings of the New Testament, we perform the mystery of repentance and partake in the Eucharist for those purified through true repentance (Matt. 26:26–28).

✍🏾To those who might say, “Lord, we already know this, why do You remind us?” the Lord teaches that knowledge alone is not enough. True greatness comes from knowing and doing.
As the Gospel of Luke says:

✍🏾“And that servant who knew his master’s will and did not prepare himself or do what was pleasing to him will be beaten with many stripes; but he who did not know and did what was worthy of stripes will be beaten with few stripes. For from everyone to whom much is given, much will be required; and from whom much has been entrusted, even more will be required.” (Luke 12:47–48)
Even those who know the Word of God, like the Pharisees, are not great if they do not practice it. But you, who know it and act according to it, are truly blessed.

✍🏾

text.text: Godliness – The Hope of Our Lives

text:
✍🏾Godliness is the hope and foundation of our Christian life. The apostle Paul wrote to his disciple Timothy:

“Train yourself to be godly. Training the body for the flesh has limited value, but godliness is valuable in every way, as it holds promise for the present life and the life to come. This is a trustworthy saying that everyone should accept. We labor and endure reproach because we have set our hope on the living God, who saves all people, especially those who believe.” (1 Timothy 4:7–10)

✍🏾Paul also teaches that:
“For anyone who says, ‘This life is enough for me,’ godliness is great gain.” (1 Timothy 6:6)

“O man of God, flee from worldly desires; pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness.” (1 Timothy 6:11)

Godliness is not only spiritual profit; it is a guide for holy living and a path to eternal reward.

✍🏾Godliness According to Saint PeterThrough the Holy Spirit, Saint Peter also instructs us to live godly lives:

“Grace and peace be multiplied to you through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord. His divine power has given us everything we need for life and godliness through the knowledge of Him who called us by His own glory and virtue.” (2 Peter 1:2–3)

✍🏾Saint Peter further teaches the practical steps to grow in godliness:

“For this reason, making every effort, add to your faith virtue; knowledge; to knowledge, self-control; to self-control, patience; to patience, godliness; to godliness, brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness, love.” (2 Peter 1:5–7)

text:
✍🏾Saint Peter teaches us to wait for the second coming of Christ with godly devotion:

“The Lord is not slow in keeping His promise, as some count slowness, but is patient with you, not wanting anyone to perish, but for everyone to come to repentance. But the day of the Lord will come like a thief, in which the heavens will pass away with a loud noise, and the elements will melt with fervent heat, and the earth and the works in it will be burned up. Since all these things are to be dissolved, what kind of people ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness, waiting for and hastening the coming of the day of the Lord? But we, according to His promise, are looking for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.” (2 Peter 3:9–13)
We are called to live in holy conduct and godliness, not merely in words or thoughts, but in action, fully preparing our hearts for the day of the Lord.

✍🏾The Holy Apostle Paul, writing to the Thessalonians, reminds us that imitating God often involves endurance and joy in trials:
“You became imitators of us and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction with joy of the Holy Spirit, so that you became an example to all the believers in Macedonia and Achaia.” (1 Thess. 1:6–7)

✍🏾Paul emphasizes that the apostles, though humbled by affliction, were exalted because they imitated Christ and became examples for others. 

Because the Thessalonian Christians imitated Christ in suffering, the apostle Paul testified:

“For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God in Christ Jesus who are in Judea. For you also suffered the same things from your own countrymen as they did from the Jews.” (1 Thessalonians 2:14)

✍🏾 Paul further teaches us how to live in this present age:

“The grace of God that brings salvation has appeared, teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly desires, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, looking for that blessed hope and the glorious appearing of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ, who gave Himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for Himself a people zealous for good works.” (Titus 2:11–14)

To imitate God or Christ means to make Him the perfect example in our lives. Christ Himself is the perfect example of all the Beatitudes. The saints who trusted in Him followed His example faithfully. The conclusion of the Beatitudes reminds us that our primary model is Christ Himself.

✍🏾

Christ demonstrated humility so that we could learn by example. The holy apostles recognized this, made Him their guide in ministry and life, and remained faithful even unto martyrdom, receiving the crown of glory from Him.

May our Lord help us, like the holy apostles and saints, to follow His example, to stand firm in our Orthodox faith, and to persevere in true Christianity, so that we may inherit the heavenly Kingdom prepared for those who love Him.

text.text: The Church’s rules regarding what should and should not be done during the Holy Mass are as follows:

text:
👉🏾 If a person who laughs during the Holy Mass is a priest, he is still required to receive Holy Communion. After  receiving the Holy Body, he must leave the church and perform repentance through prayer and fasting for one week.

👉🏾 If the person who laughs is a layperson, he must leave the church immediately without receiving Holy Communion.

👉🏾

text.text: Why did the Church judge that the priest should receive and then leave to be disciplined?

text:
✍🏾 Why was the priest allowed to continue serving and distributing Holy Communion after laughing? Because from inside the sanctuary no one can see that the priest laughed, and if he were sent out without receiving Holy Communion, it could cause confusion and doubt among the faithful.

✍🏾When the faithful see a priest leaving the Mass in the middle of the Holy Liturgy, they may begin to question the Holy Sacrifice, saying,“What did the priest see in the sacrifice?”This can cause confusion and doubt among the faithful.

✍🏾 But a believer should not say or do anything that is not acceptable in the holy temple. Since everyone can see him when he laughs, it may become a source of distraction and irritation to others.. Therefore, to preserve reverence in the church, he must leave immediately so that nothing inappropriate is said or done in the holy temple.

✍🏾No one should spit in the church. If a person is suffering from illness or discomfort, he should quietly receive the saliva in his handkerchief, without making any sound, and discreetly wipe it away.

✍🏾

text.text: Let no one speak foolish or meaningless words in the church or during the Holy Liturgy.

text:
✍🏾 Since the church is a house of prayer, where the faithful stand before God in fear and reverence, it is not permissible to leave before the Holy Liturgy is completed.

✍🏾However, if there is a very serious reason or illness, one may leave after the reading of the Holy Gospel.

✍🏾 The vestments worn by priests during the Holy Liturgy should be white, because white garments are pleasing and symbolize purity and divine glory.

✍🏾 When our Lord Jesus Christ revealed His divine nature, His garments became white as snow.

text:

👉🏾Bishops 

👉🏾Monks monasteries living in

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

“Lift up your hearts.”

Meaning:

To lift up your hearts means to raise our inner thoughts and desires toward heavenly things. It calls us to reflect deeply in our hearts on works that lead us to our heavenly home, and to translate these holy thoughts into righteous actions.

When the people respond, saying:

“If we think about the heavenly mystery, we have value in the sight of our Creator, God,”
they are affirming and emphasizing that our hearts and thoughts must be directed toward the Kingdom of Heaven, not toward earthly concerns. 

✍🏾

“Those who are sitting, rise up”

Meaning:

✍🏾This does not mean that everyone was physically sitting. Except for:The sick,The elderly.
All others are expected to stand during the Divine Liturgy.

✍🏾Spiritually, this declaration means:

👉🏾Rise from the bed of forgetfulness with vigilance

👉🏾Rise from the bed of sin with repentance and sincerity

👉🏾Stand before God with reverence, alertness, and prayer.

👉🏾 It teaches that it is impossible to remain spiritually idle when the mystery of God’s glory is being proclaimed.

✍🏾

“Look to the East.” - Why?

Meaning:

✍🏾In the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, looking to the East during the Divine Liturgy is a sacred command filled with deep spiritual and biblical meaning.

✍🏾 Church Orientation
Orthodox churches are built facing the East

👉🏾The Meqdes , also Bethlehem, is located on the eastern side of the church.

We pray facing the East during prayer.

👉🏾 When a deceased person is buried at a funeral, the body is laid with the head facing the West and the feet facing the East.

👉🏾 During the Divine Liturgy, the deacon proclaims, “Look to the East.” Why?

text.text: 1. Our father Adam’s garden was in the East (Gen. 2:8).

text:
👉🏾 When the garden was closed by the sword of the cherubim because of Adam’s sin, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ conquered death, judged sin, and opened it for us by His death (Luke 23:43).

👉🏾 When we turn to the East, we are reminded of the hope given to us to enter Paradise.

👉🏾 Our Lady’s garden, which was opened, is revealed to us through faith.

👉🏾 We remember the grace we have received in Christ.

👉🏾 We also remember that we are not earthly.

text.text: 2. The Lord was born in the East.

text:
The wise men saw the star in the East, and the star is a symbol of the mercy of God. Just as it led them to God, may it also lead us to the field of harvest (Matthew 22:14).

👉🏾 Whenever we turn to the East, we are reminded of the birth of the Lord,

👉🏾 His favor upon us,

👉🏾 And that the star of mercy is guiding us.

text.text: 3. The East is a symbol of Our Lady.

text:
Just as the sun rises from the East to dispel darkness, so from Our Lady, the Virgin Mary, came the Sun of Righteousness, Jesus Christ, who dispels the darkness of sin in the world (Malachi 4:2).

👉🏾 The prophet Ezekiel also saw Our Lady in the East; therefore, whenever we turn to the East, we remember Our Lady (Ezekiel 44:1–4).

👉🏾Since the Sun of Righteousness, Jesus Christ, was not born in darkness, we are reminded of Our Lady and are kept away from sin.

text.text: 4. The salvation of the world is found in the East.

text:
👉🏾 The Lord was crucified and saved the world in the East.

👉🏾 Since Jerusalem is an eastern city, whenever we turn to the East, we remember the crucified Christ and the price paid for us.
