text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord. Today, based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson. We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

👉🏾
The Holy Liturgy brings forgiveness of sins because it is offered with repentance and a contrite heart.

Through the Liturgy, both our spiritual and physical lives receive grace and healing.

✍🏾

The prayers offered during the Liturgy are powerful and acceptable before God.

✍🏾

When we participate in and consecrate the Holy Liturgy worthily, we unite with the angels and receive eternal blessings, for through the Holy Liturgy the Body and Blood of our Lord sanctify the faithful and grant life to those who partake reverently.

✍🏾

text.text: Four Major Fruits of Celebrating the Holy Liturgy

text:
During the Holy Liturgy, the faithful learn and come to know the dogma and teachings of the Church.

👉🏾 For example, when the Liturgy of St. Mary is celebrated (written by aba hriaqos ), it teaches:

👉🏾The mystery of the Holy Trinity

👉🏾The mystery of the Incarnation

👉🏾The role and holiness of the Virgin Mary

Thus, the Holy Liturgy itself becomes a living and active school of theology.
A person who participates in all 14 Liturgies learns the history of the Church, the saints, and the progression of salvation as preserved in the liturgical tradition.

The Liturgy teaches us:

👉🏾Love and patience

👉🏾Unity and forgiveness

👉🏾Fasting and prayer

Therefore, anyone who participates attentively receives continual spiritual guidance.

We receive exhortation within the Holy Liturgy.

👉🏾 For example, if a person has a quarrel with his brother, the Holy Liturgy (kidase egzi'e) teaches him to forgive. In this part of the Liturgy, we are instructed to submit ourselves to the Creator, to renew our commitment before God, and to preserve our covenant of communion with one another. By sanctifying and participating in the Holy Liturgy, we learn these foundational principles that are beneficial for all humanity.

✍🏾

text.text: The Holy Liturgy as Communal Prayer and Offering

text:
The Holy Liturgy is a sacred prayer in which Scripture readings and hymns are offered. All participate together the priest, the deacon, and the faithful.

The Church teaches:
“Do not stand naked before the prophet of God.”

This means that no one should stand before God during the Holy Liturgy without an offering or alms in hand. Even if we have little, we should approach Him with what we are able to offer, without fear or shame. If possible, it is appropriate to bring incense, raisins, candles, or other offerings.

During the Holy Liturgy, the priest prays specifically for the offerings brought by the faithful. If no offering is brought, we must ask ourselves, “For whom is this prayer offered?”

👉🏾 Therefore, we must prepare in advance for the celebration of the Holy Liturgy. Even if we are unable to participate in other spiritual services, we should always set aside time to attend and sanctify the Holy Liturgy.

✍🏾

text.text: Our Responsibility When We Come to the holy Liturgy

text:
When we come to church, we must:

👉🏾Stand reverently and participate actively

👉🏾Listen attentively to the Scriptures and apply them to our livesReceive Holy Communion with faith for eternal life
The Liturgy proclaims in its opening hymn:

👉🏾“Whoever does not remain until the end of the Liturgy, who does not listen to the Scriptures, and who does not receive the Holy Communion, let him be separated from the communion of the Church.”Therefore, preparation is essential.

✍🏾When a person stands for the Holy Liturgy, he must gather his five senses, give full attention, and participate in the Liturgy actively and reverently. For this reason, the deacon proclaims in the middle of the service, “Rise for prayer,” and the faithful humble themselves before God and ask for forgiveness, saying, “Lord, forgive us.”

✍🏾

text.text: participation of the Five Senses in the Holy Liturgy

text:
During the Holy Liturgy, the five senses eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and touch are sanctified together.

👉🏾

When the priest consecrates the Holy Liturgy, he does not remain still near the altar. He moves in specific ways, and each movement has deep spiritual and mystical meaning. By seeing these sacred actions, eye participate in the Holy Liturgy .

👉🏾

The priest, deacon, and faithful hear the hymns, prayers, and readings sometimes together and sometimes individually. Through attentive listening, the ears are participate in the Holy Liturgy .

👉🏾

The sense of smell is sanctified through the fragrance of incense, which symbolizes the prayers of the saints rising to God.

👉🏾

The tongue is sanctified when the faithful receive Holy Communion with reverence and faith.

👉🏾

The sense of touch is sanctified when we bow before God, kiss the Holy Gospel after its reading, and receive blessings by kissing the priest’s hand at the conclusion of the Holy Liturgy.

✍🏾

The lessons we learn in the Holy Liturgy are different from the lessons taught in formal courses, such as those at Awde Mihret. These are teachings revealed by the Holy Spirit, who has instructed many scholars, yet presents the truth in a way that is clear and accessible to all the faithful.

👉🏾 In the Holy Liturgy, we hear:

👉🏾The Holy Gospel

👉🏾The Epistles

👉🏾The Acts of the Apostles

👉🏾The Universal Epistles

👉🏾The Psalms of David

✍🏾All of these are proclaimed in melody, which helps the Word of God to be received not only by the mind but also by the heart.

✍🏾When a person faithfully participates in the Holy Liturgy, he is learned the entire Bible from the Old Testament to the New Testament. 

Through continual participation, the faithful grow in spiritual wisdom and are shaped over time, for the Holy Liturgy is a way of living the angelic life on earth, as mentioned earlier.

✍🏾

text.text: The Holy Liturgy as the Greatest Mystery of the Church

text:
The celebration of the Holy Liturgy is the greatest sacrament of our Church. Therefore, we must not only participate in it ourselves, but also teach and encourage our people to take part in this sacred mystery.

It is especially fitting to:

👉🏾Bring our children to the Holy Liturgy

👉🏾Teach them to bring offerings

👉🏾Prepare them in advance for the celebration

👉🏾Guide them to receive Holy Communion with faith and reverence

✍🏾

If we fail to do this, we risk losing the sacred heritage entrusted to us. Therefore, we must faithfully pass on this tradition to the next generation, so that the ancient and holy order of worship handed down to us may not be weakened or lost.

✍🏾 participation of the Five Senses in the Holy Liturgy

During the Holy Liturgy, the five senses eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and touch are sanctified together.

👉🏾 The Eye:

When the priest consecrates the Holy Liturgy, he does not remain still near the altar. He moves in specific ways, and each movement has deep spiritual and mystical meaning. By seeing these sacred actions, eye participate in the Holy Liturgy .

👉🏾 The Ear:

The priest, deacon, and faithful hear the hymns, prayers, and readings sometimes together and sometimes individually. Through attentive listening, the ears are participate in the Holy Liturgy .

👉🏾 The Nose:

The sense of smell is sanctified through the fragrance of incense, which symbolizes the prayers of the saints rising to God.

👉🏾 The Tongue (Taste):

The tongue is sanctified when the faithful receive Holy Communion with reverence and faith.

👉🏾 Touch:

The sense of touch is sanctified when we bow before God, kiss the Holy Gospel after its reading, and receive blessings by kissing the priest’s hand at the conclusion of the Holy Liturgy.

text.text: The Holy Liturgy and the Use of Recorded Media

text:
One of the sacred rites of the Church is the Holy Liturgy. The purpose of the Holy Liturgy is one: to offer the Holy Body and Precious Blood of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ to the faithful. According to the teachings of the Holy Fathers, the Holy Liturgy is a public and communal act of worship, not a private practice.

👉🏾 When the Holy Eucharist is celebrated , the Kidan and Mahlet  are offered during the Holy Liturgy, the faithful who participate receive grace and blessing.

👉🏾Likewise, when the priests lead the Prayer of the Seatat, the faithful who participate receive a blessing for both body and soul

Since the Holy Liturgy is a public prayer service, the priests and the faithful are seen walking around the church to receive the Eucharist, facing one another, and the Holy Liturgy is celebrated with the participation of both the priests and the faithful.

✍🏾 With the wisdom of technology, it is possible to listen to mezmur and to the Holy Liturgy. We can not only listen to what is recorded, but also learn from it.

👉🏾 Many beneficial developments that reduce fatigue are taking place through technology. One of these is sound recording, which provides great service in preserving memories of the past, songs, Holy Liturgies, teachings, and the advice of the Fathers. These are prepared in audio and video formats on cassettes and CDs, and we can also use them for learning.

However, it is not possible to consecrate the Church's Holy Liturgy at home using a cassette tape.

✍🏾 We hear that people living in the Gentile world used to gather in a prayer house and attempt to follow the Holy Liturgy on tape. These believers would leave their gathering place, stand on the street, and listen to the priest on the recording as he said, “Go to your homes in peace.” After hearing this, they would then return to their homes.

God saw their good intentions and helped the priests to consecrate and sanctify them, and as a result, churches were built for them. .

✍🏾 The sacrifices offered by the Old Testament priests were a model for the New Testament (faithful) sacrifice, so the faithful were not blamed for attempting this out of sincere desire to participate in the Holy Liturgy despite their difficulties. However, the effort they made standing on the road rather than in their homes is encouraging. It is bold for some to claim that they were blessed merely by quietly listening to the Holy Liturgy.

👉🏾 The Church does not have a technological Holy Liturgy, and the Holy Liturgy cannot be replaced by recordings in any way. Today, it is rare to find a place where a Church is not built, but participation in the Holy Liturgy still requires presence in the Church.

👉🏾

text.text: Therefore, the Holy Liturgy  must be celebrated in the presence of the Church.

text:
✍🏾The Holy Liturgy is celebrated only in a sacred place. This means it must take place in a consecrated church where the Tabot (Ark) is present, where ordained priests serve, where incense is offered, and where liturgical blessings are performed according to the tradition of the Church.

✍🏾During the Holy Liturgy, incense is offered, candles are lit, and offerings are presented. These are not optional practices or decorations. They are essential elements of the liturgical service. It is not possible to celebrate the Holy Liturgy without them. If these sacred elements are absent, the service cannot be considered the Holy Liturgy of the Church.

✍🏾The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church celebrates the Holy Liturgy while faithfully preserving its creed, dogma, apostolic faith, and sacred tradition, handed down from the Apostles and safeguarded by the Holy Fathers.

text:
👇🏾

The Holy Liturgy is a heavenly mystery celebrated on earth. Through it, we offer true and living worship to God, proclaim our foundational faith, and participate in the mysteries of the Church, especially the Sacrament of the Holy Eucharist.

✍🏾This heavenly reality is clearly revealed in Isaiah 6:1–end, where the prophet witnesses the worship of heaven:

👉🏾 “Seraphim stood above Him, each having six wings: with two he covered his face, with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew. And one cried to another and said:Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts;the whole earth is full of His glory.And the house was filled with smoke.”

On Sundays and major feast days, the faithful gather to participate in the Holy Liturgy .

Those who have properly prepared themselves through fasting, confession, prayer, and reconciliation receive the Holy Body and Precious Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Those who have not prepared themselves for the Sacrament of Holy Communion do not receive the Holy Body and Precious Blood. Instead, they receive a blessing, make the sign of the cross, and return with reverence, awaiting a future time when they are spiritually prepared.

The Holy Liturgy is a communal act of worship, led by priests, assisted by deacons, and prayerfully participated in by the entire congregation.

✍🏾

text.text: The service follows an established and orderly tradition

text:
:

👉🏾The sera'i priest stands to the west of the altar, facing east.

👉🏾The priest (nifk kahn) also stand to the south of the altar, facing north, according to the rite being performed.

👉🏾The sear'i deacon stands to the east, facing west.

👉🏾The nifk deacon also stands to the north, facing south, surrounding the altar in service and reverence.

👉🏾A fifth minister (assistant) stands to the left of the priest and lights the lamp for him when required.

✍🏾

Because the sacred book is placed on a bench, only the priest or another ordained priest may open it. This follows the established discipline of the Church.

✍🏾Throughout the Holy Liturgy, the clergy move according to the order of the rite, offering blessings, prayers, incense, and prostrations, all done with reverence, harmony, and obedience to the tradition of the Church.

✍🏾

text.text: Order of Service in the Qine Mahlet

text:
👉🏾In the Qine Maḥlet (ቅኔ መሕሌት), there are groups of believers and clergy who stand and serve according to the established order of the Church, both in the kidist and in the Mekdes.

👉🏾In the northeastern service area of the Qine Maḥlet, men stand and serve the faithful according to their assigned ministry.

👉🏾In the western part of the sanctuary, priests and deacons stand and serve.

✍🏾In the southern area, nuns, priests and deacons wives, and praying believers stand and serve in reverence, each according to their role.

✍🏾The believers who stand and serve in these areas participate in the service, 
The Sacrament of the Holy Eucharist is performed only in the sanctuary, and only by ordained priests.

✍🏾The sanctuary is the holy place where only priests may enter, where the Holy Body is consecrated, and from which the priests come forth to bless the faithful.

✍🏾In these various sections of the church, many services are carried out, including prayers, chanting, incense, blessings, and orderly participation .

✍🏾When the Holy Liturgy is celebrated, both clergy and faithful receive their portion of the Word of God, bow in reverence, and participate through prayer and blessing according to Church tradition.

✍🏾For this reason, we say that the Holy Liturgy is a worship that is visible, tangible, audible, and living. It is not abstract or hidden, but fully expressed through action, sound, movement, and sacred order.

text:
✍🏾It is possible to listen to the Holy Liturgy by recording, but this does not grant participation in the Sacraments through which blessings are given. Hearing alone cannot replace presence, preparation, and participation.

✍🏾As stated in the liturgical tradition of the Church, one of the essential matters the priest must confirm before beginning the Holy Liturgy is that the faithful are gathered. The Holy Liturgy is not a private act but a communal and ecclesial worship.

✍🏾The eyes of God are upon His temple, and His ears are attentive to the prayers of the faithful. Since God Himself has promised to place His eyes and His heart in His holy house, the faithful are called to go to church, gather together, and participate in the Sacraments.

As the Apostle teaches:

“To him who knows to do good and does not do it, to him it is sin.”
(James 4:17)

✍🏾Therefore, repentance, sanctification, participation in the Holy Eucharist, and obedience to what we know is good are not optional acts. Knowing the good and refusing to do it leads to sin.

The Lord also declares:

👉🏾 “My eyes will be open and My ears attentive to the prayer that is made in this place. Now I have chosen and sanctified this house, that My name may be there forever; My eyes and My heart will be there continually.”
(2 Chronicles 7:15–16)

From this, we understand that the worship offered in the church, through prayer and reverence, is a source of blessing established by God Himself.

✍🏾The Apostles also prayed in the temple, showing us the importance of gathering in a holy place:

👉🏾“Now Peter and John went up together to the temple at the ninth hour, the hour of prayer.”
(Acts 3:1)

👉🏾Thus, gathering together in the church for prayer is apostolic teaching, It is the life of the Church.

May our God, in His mercy and goodness, help us to apply the teachings of our holy fathers, to gather in His house, to participate in the heavenly order on earth, to return to a life of repentance, to partake worthily of the Holy Eucharist, and to inherit the Kingdom of Heaven.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today,based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it

✍🏾We celebrate the Holy Liturgy because our Lord Jesus Christ said:

👉🏾“Where two or three are gathered together in My name, there I am in the midst of them.”
(Matthew 18:20)

✍🏾Our gathering together,founded on the eternal promise of our Lord, becomes the means through which we receive His grace and divine help.

✍🏾Just as the Holy Liturgy is the true image of the one Heavenly Church, the gathering of believers is the first and essential foundation of the Holy Liturgy.

✍🏾The liturgical order that is fulfilled in the Holy Liturgy first existed in the world of the holy angels.On earth, this same heavenly order is fulfilled when the faithful gather together in the temple of God.(Isaiah 6:1)

✍🏾We now reflect on the deep reverence and spiritual understanding with which the ancient Church,in the time of the apostles, regarded the gathering of believers.Through faithful obedience to the word of the Lord, the Church received its order of worship from the heavenly hosts, and this sacred order of thanksgiving was handed down through Holy Tradition, becoming the foundation of the life of the Church.

✍🏾

text.text: The Ancient Tradition of Gathering Believers in the Holy Liturgy

text:
✍🏾The practice of gathering together to glorify God and offer sacrifice is already found in the Old Testament. However, the true foundation of the Christian Holy Liturgy was established when our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ celebrated the Passover with His disciples on the night before His suffering.(Luke 22:7)

✍🏾Just as God chose the sons of Jacob as the foundation of the congregation of Israel, Christ gathered the apostles and made them the foundation of the Church. He seated them at the table of the Kingdom of Heaven, forming the new assembly of believers, the true Israel.
(Luke 22:29–30)

✍🏾Through this act, the unity of the Church was established in and through the apostles. Having received understanding of the divine mysteries through the grace of the Holy Spirit, the apostles gathered the faithful and celebrated the Holy Liturgy together as one body.(Acts 20:7)

✍🏾This practice was firmly rooted in the apostolic Church.The Apostle Paul clearly speaks of believers coming together as a necessary condition for worship, saying:

👉🏾“When you come together as a church…”(1Corinthians 11:18)
He further explains that this order was not human invention, but divine tradition:

👉🏾“For I received from the Lord that which I also delivered to you.”
(1Corinthians 11:23)

✍🏾This reveals the mystery of the gathering of believers in the Holy Liturgy, a sacred practice that has been preserved and handed down through Holy Tradition as an essential part of the life of the Church.

✍🏾The Fathers of the Church, who were disciples and successors of the apostles, faithfully received this apostolic tradition and handed it down directly to the generations that followed. They confirmed its truth by teaching that the faith of the Church and the Holy Liturgy are inseparable, for the teaching of the Church is expressed in the Liturgy, and the Liturgy, in turn, proclaims and confirms the teaching of the Church.

✍🏾During the time of these apostolic Fathers, all believers took part in the Holy Liturgy and approached the Holy Mysteries. Even those who were sick were not excluded, but were brought so that they might receive and share in the grace of the Liturgy.

✍🏾Anyone who deliberately missed the Holy Liturgy without illness or serious reason was regarded as having separated himself from the life of the Church.For this reason, church buildings were constructed to accommodate the full celebration of the Holy Mysteries and the participation of the entire community. This ancient understanding of church architecture continues to be clearly seen in our Church today.

text:
✍🏾The structure and practice of the Holy Liturgy clearly show that every prayer offered by the priest and every proclamation made by the deacon are completed through the response of the faithful, who affirm them with “Amen.” The instructions found in the Metshafe kidase, which say, “Say, priest; say, deacon; say, people,” bear witness to this shared participation.

✍🏾Through this, we understand that the Holy Liturgy is a mystery of unity. It does not belong to the clergy alone, but is celebrated together by both the clergy and the faithful as one body. For this reason, the ancient instruction reminds us that the Holy Liturgy should not begin until the faithful are gathered, so that this unity may be fully expressed.

✍🏾The idea that the Holy Liturgy belongs only to priests, while the faithful are merely observers, is foreign to the life and order of the Church. Such thinking is a serious misunderstanding. The Holy Liturgy is not a performance to be watched, but a prayer of communion shared by the whole Church.

✍🏾The lack of active participation that is sometimes seen today, and the spiritual weakness that follows, arise from this misunderstanding. Since the Holy Liturgy is the communion of Christians, every Orthodox believer has the responsibility to prepare himself, to sanctify himself, and to participate fully in the life of the Church through the Liturgy.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today,based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾 Abune Tekle Haymanot, of Bulga Debre Tslalsh, also known as Zorere St. Michael Church , was conceived on Megabit 24 by his father, the priest Tsega Zeab, and his mother, the holy woman Egzi Hareya. He was born on Tahsas 24, 1197 AD, and was given the name Fisha Zion, which means the joy of Zion.

✍🏾On the third day after his birth, he descended from his mother’s arms and praised the Holy Trinity, saying, “One Father, one Son, one Holy Spirit.”He died on Nehase 24.

✍🏾 “Tekil” means a fruitful tree, a spice, a leaf, an edible and fragrant herbaceous plant, as well as a law or a system.(Matthew 15:13)

✍🏾 “Religion(haymanot)” means believing and testifying in the power of God, that God is the Creator of all, believing in the unity and Trinity of God, and in the succession of saints.

✍🏾 The phrase “Tekile Haymanot” means a plant of religion: a tree that bears the fruit of righteousness, a tree that escapes the heat of sin, a spice that delights believers with the word of the Gospel, a leaf that gives life, a leaf that satisfies the hunger of the soul when eaten, and a plant that is a shelter for the righteous.

“Tekle Haymanot” means the plant of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. This name explains the spiritual identity of the righteous man.

✍🏾 By the grace and guidance of his father, the priest tsega Zeab, he studied the Church’s teachings and order. At the age of fifteen, he received the ordination of deacon from the Archbishop of Alexandria, Abune Kerlos (Gerlos). In this way, he served the Holy Church from his youth.

✍🏾 One day, while the righteous Abune Tekle Haymanot was hunting with his friends, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ appeared to him and chose him as a new apostle for Ethiopian Christians. He was given the name Tekle Haymanot, which means the fruit of faith.

✍🏾 When our father began his apostolic journey, he said:
“O Lord Jesus Christ! Behold, I have left my house open for You, that You may open the door of the Kingdom of Heaven to me.
For me who am weak, there is no one to comfort me without You.
For me who am confused, there is no one to lift me up without You.
For me who am sad, there is no one to comfort me without You.
For me who am poor, I have no refuge without You.”(Gedle Tekle Haymanot, Chapter 28, Verses 2–3)

✍🏾After saying this, with a humble and broken heart, he prayed to his Creator and preached in different regions of Ethiopia, turning people:

👉🏾 From sin to active righteousness

👉🏾 From apostasy to faith

Because of this, he was called the light of the sun for Ethiopians.

✍🏾In his Letter to the Hebrews, Saint Paul describes the spiritual struggle of the saints:

👉🏾“They conquered kingdoms through faith” (Hebrews 11:33).
Likewise, our father Saint Tekle Haymanot, through spiritual struggle, humility, and miracles, converted King Motolomi, who was an unbeliever, to Christianity.

👉🏾 “They did righteousness” (Hebrews 11:33).In the same way, our father labored and struggled for the Gospel.

👉🏾 “They stopped the mouths of lions” (Hebrews 11:33).Likewise, our father crushed the head of the dragon.

👉🏾“They escaped the edge of the sword” (Hebrews 11:34).Our father was miraculously saved from the spear thrown by Motolomi.

👉🏾“They were strengthened from weakness” (Hebrews 11:34).
Our father was strengthened in many struggles, through fasting and prayer without rest.

✍🏾While doing all these things, and when the time of his rest came, he said to his disciples:

👉🏾“My children, it does not mean that all monks will enter the Kingdom of Heaven, but only those who have truly despised the world will enter. First seek the righteousness of God, fast and pray regularly, love one another, and keep His commandments strictly.”Later, he said:

👉🏾“I am the salt of the world, I am the darkness of myself. What shall I answer when I stand before the true Judge, the Lord?”

✍🏾He prayed with complete humility and deep spiritual inspiration. Therefore, our Church teaches us to remember the righteous, to pray for the poor in their name, and to make their memorial, as it is written in Matthew 10:41–42.

The righteous saints are:

👉🏾 Those whose prayers we believe in, whether they are in the flesh or have departed from this world,

👉🏾 Those who pray to God and intercede before God,

👉🏾 Those who bring us salvation of both body and soul,

👉🏾 They are our intercessors and mediators in times of trouble.

Among these saints is the Ethiopian righteous Abune Tekle Haymanot.

✍🏾 Our father Abune Tekle Haymanot:

👉🏾 Gave his whole life to God,

👉🏾 Bound himself like an ox,

👉🏾 Armed himself like a farmer,

👉🏾 Despised this world,

👉🏾 Devoted himself to fasting and prayer,

👉🏾 Lived a life of peace.

✍🏾 In addition, like the holy apostles:

👉🏾 He preached the Gospel throughout Ethiopia,

👉🏾 In the name of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, he healed sick bodies through miracles,

👉🏾 He healed sick souls through his teachings.

✍🏾 Among the feasts on which Abune Tekle Haymanot is remembered, his birth is commemorated on Tahisas 24.

✍🏾 When the Book of the Sinksar speaks of his birth, it honors him with the title “the new apostle.”

text: Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today,based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

The secret of our gathering in the Holy Liturgy is unity. The unity of the faithful forms the Holy Church, which is the Body of Christ. As Saint Paul teaches:

“You are the body of Christ, and individually you are body part of him.”(1 Corinthians 12:27)

✍🏾When the faithful gather, the Church is revealed not as an earthly institution or administrative body, but as a heavenly reality. This gathering is the fulfillment of the Church’s unity and holiness.

✍🏾The Church is not simply a crowd of people assembled in one place. It is the manifestation of the heavenly Body of Christ, the communion of believers who become its members through faith in His Name.

text.text: 2. The Perfection and Holiness of the Church

text:
✍🏾We must be attentive in our time, because new theological doctrines have appeared that reject many of the ancient traditions of the Church. These earthly doctrines show little concern for the Holy Liturgy, and even when they speak about it, they divide it into parts, emphasizing one while diminishing another, as if the mystery of God can be measured and ranked.

✍🏾When questioned about the Holy Liturgy, they focus almost entirely on the moment when the bread and wine are changed, while neglecting the rest of the sacred service. They attempt to explain and analyze this mystery not in the Orthodox and heavenly manner handed down by the Fathers, but through scientific, rational, and earthly reasoning.

✍🏾Such teachings are not in harmony with the Holy Scriptures nor with the Apostolic Tradition of the Church. The Holy Liturgy is not a subject for experimentation or proof, but a divine and heavenly mystery revealed through faith.

✍🏾The ancient Church, our holy Fathers, understood this deeply. Knowing that the Holy Liturgy is a participation in heaven itself, they were greatly concerned when even one believer was absent from the gathering of the faithful.

text.text: 3. The Holiness of the Church Comes from Christ

text:
The holiness of the Church does not come from the personal righteousness of its members. Each of us may be weak and sinful, yet the Church remains holy because Christ Himself is present in her.

✍🏾The unity of the faithful is the purity of the Church. This holiness is not our achievement. It is the gift of Christ, who dwells among us.

✍🏾The Church is pure not because we are without sin, but because Christ is in her midst. He is the medicine for our sickness, the source of her holiness, and the life of her body.

Thus, the Church truly deserves to be called:

👉🏾a holy nation

👉🏾a royal priesthood

👉🏾a chosen generation

As Scripture says:

👉🏾“But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation… that you may proclaim the praises of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.”(1 Peter 2:9)

For this reason, believers in the Apostolic age were called “saints.” They lived in constant fellowship and prayer, and as Saint Paul writes:

“I have had great joy and encouragement because of your love, for the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, brother.”(Philemon 1:7)

text.text: 4. The Gathering as a Heavenly Joy

text:
The gathering of the faithful was a fragrance of holiness and a source of heavenly joy. This joy enabled the early Christians to endure suffering with gladness and to preach the Gospel with courage in a hostile world.

Their unity was born from the love of God, and through it, the Church shone as a living witness to Christ.

text.text: 5. The Priesthood in the Holy Liturgy

text:
✍🏾Just as the gathering of the faithful reveals the Body of Christ, the priest who presides over the Holy Liturgy reveals the Priesthood of Christ, who is the Head of the Church:

👉🏾“Christ is the Savior of the body, the Church.”(Ephesians 5:23)

✍🏾The priest serves by grace, bearing witness to the eternal priesthood of Christ. His vestments are not personal decorations; they manifest the Church as the dwelling place of Christ.

For this reason, according to the Church’s order, the priest must not wear his liturgical vestments before the faithful gather. The Liturgy is not an individual act; it belongs to the whole Body.

The crown worn by the priest testifies to the eternal priesthood of Christ:

👉🏾“You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”(Psalm 109:4; Hebrews 7:1–22)

✍🏾In this way, the eternal priesthood of our Lord is manifested among the faithful in His eternal and heavenly sanctuary, the Holy Church. When we gather together, Christ Himself is in our midst. Therefore, our gathering in the Holy Liturgy is truly great, not because of our number or worthiness, but because our Savior, Jesus Christ, is present among us.

If Abraham was commanded to leave his land and his father’s house in obedience to God, how much more should we leave behind worldly desires when we ascend to Mount Zion, the assembly of the firstborn?(Genesis 12:1; Hebrews 12:22–24)

✍🏾 If the people of Israel prepared for three days before the revelation of God on Mount Sinai, washing their clothes and sanctifying themselves, how much more should we prepare to meet Christ Himself, who was crucified for us?

Our preparation must go beyond clean clothes. We must cleanse our hearts, bodies, flesh, and blood through repentance.
(Exodus 19:14–15)

✍🏾

✍🏾When the child Samuel heard the voice of God in the temple, he responded with readiness and obedience. Likewise, we who are gathered in the true Temple, the Holy Church, must respond attentively to God’s voice spoken through Scripture, prayers, hymns, and mysteries during the Holy Liturgy.(1 Samuel 3:1–14)

Therefore, our gathering in the Holy Liturgy is truly great, not because of our number or worthiness, but because our Savior, Jesus Christ, is present among us.

text:

 “I have sinned by eating from the tree which my Creator commanded me not to eat,” wept bitterly in repentance for fourteen weeks and ninety-eight years because of his sin.

Yet in the midst of judgment, God proclaimed hope and salvation, saying:

“I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her Seed.”
(Genesis 3:15)

✍🏾This was the first promise of redemption. At that very moment, God confirmed His mercy and revealed the mystery of the Incarnation. According to the teaching handed down in the Church, He emphasized this promise, saying:

👉🏾“With My perfect forgiveness and My complete mercy, after five and a half days, I will forgive you. I will come down to your dwelling and remain in your nature. O Adam, for your sake I will be born as a child; for your sake I will walk among men; for your sake I will fast forty days and forty nights; for your sake I will patiently accept suffering and the Cross; and for your sake I will be crucified upon the wood.”(cf. Book of Clement; 3 Maccabees 4:23–24; Ezekiel 4:1; Sirach 24:6; Galatians 4:4)

✍🏾This divine promise reveals the boundless love of God, who chose to become man in order to restore fallen humanity and grant salvation to Adam and all his descendants.

👉🏾that the Word would truly take flesh

👉🏾be born of the Holy Virgin Mary,

👉🏾be crucified upon the Cross,and save the world.

text.text: Bethlehem and the Mystery of the Nativity

text:
✍🏾 Saint John Chrysostom  teaches that Bethlehem is like the Kingdom of Heaven.

In speaking about the birth of our Lord, the Second Adam, Christ revealed in Bethlehem the blessed life of the Kingdom that humanity lost through the first Adam. Through His Nativity, Christ restored our lost sonship and reconciled us with the Father.

For this reason, the prophet Micah foretold:

“But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for Me One who is to be ruler in Israel, whose goings forth are from of old, from everlasting.”(Micah 5:2)

✍🏾

text.text: Saint Ephrem the Syrian on the Nativity

text:
✍🏾 Saint Ephrem the Syrian, in his homilies on the Nativity, speaks of the great mystery of salvation revealed on this holy day:

“A great light has dawned on those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death. God, who dwells among the saints, became man from a pure Virgin in order to save us. Come, behold this wonder and give thanks for the mystery revealed to us. He became man without ceasing to be God. The Word was united to the flesh, and the ageless Divinity clothed Himself in humanity.”

👉🏾The Nativity reveals the incomprehensible humility of God and His immeasurable love for mankind.

✍🏾The perfect forgiveness and reconciliation accomplished by our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ began with His Nativity. The birth of our Lord holds a central place in the history of salvation and reveals the unique and incomprehensible wisdom of God, who became man in order to save the world.

✍🏾Through the Nativity, heaven and earth were united, and those who were once separated angels and human beings were joined together in praise. The tongues of the shepherds were made worthy to glorify God together with the angels. Even the animals, though without understanding, bore witness to the humility of the Creator.

✍🏾The heavenly hosts glorified Him as King of kings, whose authority has no end and whose kingdom is eternal. The kings of the earth approached Him with reverence, offering gold for His kingship, frankincense for His priesthood, and myrrh for His saving sacrifice.

✍🏾The Holy Virgin Mary, the Mother of God, together with the righteous Joseph, was granted this unique and divine honor. Thus, the Nativity of our Lord is truly wondrous, beyond human understanding, and full of glory, humility, and salvation for the whole world.

✍🏾

.

This is the land that Caleb gave to Israel when they inherited the land during the time of Joshua, by the power of God, kebron is the land belonged to Judah and later became the city of David.

✍🏾First, Caleb married a wife named Kebita, and the place was called Kebita, which means house of praise. This was because Caleb understood, by the Spirit of God, that the birth of Christ would be revealed in this land and that angels would praise God there.

👉🏾Later, Caleb married a wife named Ephrathah, and after her name the place was called Ephrathah.

✍🏾Ephrathah means a fruitful tree, a tree that bears fruit. This is a symbol of Our Lady, the bearer of the Fruit of Life, because she gave birth to Christ, the Fruit of Life, as Saint Jared says in the Book of Revelation.

👉🏾Later, Caleb married a wife named Ephrathah, and after her name the place was called Ephrathah.

✍🏾Ephrathah means a fruitful tree, a tree that bears fruit. This is a symbol of Our Lady, the bearer of the Fruit of Life, because she gave birth to Christ, the Fruit of Life, as Saint Jared says in the Book of Revelation. 

Continues 👇🏾

“I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live forever; and the bread which I will give for the life of the world is My flesh.” (John 6:51)

✍🏾 At the birth of Christ, angels joined with human beings in an extraordinary way and praised Christ the King, saying,

“Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.” (Luke 2:14)

✍🏾 The heavenly King, who is praised by angels, archangels, powers, and all the glorious heavenly hosts, today, out of love for us, embraced us with indescribable humility. He took upon Himself our human nature, except for sin, and became perfect God and perfect Man.

👉🏾 “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given; and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.”
(Isaiah 9:6)

👉🏾“What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You visit him? You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor, You set him over the works of Your hands, and You put all things in subjection under his feet.”(Hebrews 2:6–8)

✍🏾“Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus, who, being in the form of God, did not consider equality with God something to be grasped, but emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, and being made in the likeness of men.”
(Philippians 2:5–7)

(1 Corinthians 1:10)

text: Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾The Almighty God, our Creator, is compassionate and merciful toward His creation. Because of His great love for humanity, He willed to save us. For this reason, He was born of the Holy Virgin Mary and became a perfect man, without ceasing to be perfect God.

✍🏾After the fulfillment of the Sabbath count, after the prophecies were spoken, and after the holy prophets foretold that He would come and be born of a Virgin, the Archangel Gabriel announced to Saint Mary that God the Word would be born from her.

✍🏾When the appointed time came, 5,500 years after the creation of Adam, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ was born of the Holy Virgin Mary in Bethlehem.

👉🏾Through His birth:

✍🏾The curse was destroyed
Redemption was granted
Sorrow and sin were defeated Unity, harmony, compassion, peace, and love were restored.

Therefore, when we celebrate His Nativity, we celebrate the great victory of salvation.

2. The Meaning of Birth

Birth means coming forth from the womb into the light, becoming visible, present, and revealed.

In the Christian faith(be Anqetse Haymanot), “He became fully human”.
First, He dwelt hidden in the womb Later, He was revealed through His birth While He was in the womb of the Virgin, only a few righteous people knew Him.

After His birth, He was revealed to the whole world.

He was seen and touched by people and nations. He took a true human body and was revealed as a man.His present revelation was in the flesh.His eternal origin was divine fire, unapproachable to creation.

3.

text.text: The Burning Bush and the Virgin Mary

text:
✍🏾In the Old Testament, God appeared to Moses in the burning bush, a visible flame that did not consume the bush (Exodus 3:1–15).

✍🏾 Moses removed his sandals and approached with fear and reverence, learning the eternal name of God:“The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”This was the revelation of God in the Old Testament.

✍🏾In the New Testament, God was revealed in a greater way: in the flesh, dwelling in the womb of the Holy Virgin Mary.
Therefore:

👉🏾The Virgin Mary is like the green bush

👉🏾The divine fire is the divinity of the Word

✍🏾Just as the bush was not burned by the fire, the Virgin’s flesh was not harmed by the divinity dwelling within her.She is rightly called “Mahidere Melekot"),where God descended in humility and spoke to humanity.

👉🏾This revelation in the flesh is greater than the revelation on Mount Sinai.

✍🏾Anyone who approaches the bush of the New Covenant, in which God was revealed in the flesh, removes the sandals and beholds it with reverence and holy fear. The first to be granted this opportunity were Saint Elizabeth and Saint Joseph.

✍🏾When Saint Elizabeth heard the voice of the Holy Virgin Mary, the child in her womb leaped for joy and bowed in reverence. This was a great and holy miracle. Filled with the Holy Spirit, she cried out and said:

👉🏾“How is it granted to me that the mother of my Lord should come to me?”(Luke 1:39–43)
Saint Joseph also, with fear of God and deep reverence, protected and served the Holy Virgin and the divine mystery entrusted to her.


The great revelation of God in the Torah took place on Mount Sinai. 

When the living Word of the Father descended upon the mountain, He appeared in the midst of burning and terrifying fire. There were thunder and lightning, the earth shook, and thick darkness covered the mountain. All the people of Israel who stood below were filled with fear, as it is written:

“There were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of the trumpet was very loud; so all the people who were in the camp trembled.”(Exodus 19:16)

The Birth of the Lord in a Manger

text:

This event reveals:

👉🏾The first coming of our Lord

👉🏾His manifestation in the flesh

👉🏾The astonishing humility of His birth

👉🏾How marvelous it is that the Lord of lords was born not in a palace, but in a manger. He came from a poor household and found no place to stay. As He Himself later said:

👉🏾“Birds have nests and foxes have dens, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay His head.”
(Matthew 8:20)

✍🏾He came into the world in the likeness of fallen and humiliated Adam, in order to save Adam and all his children. After Adam departed from Paradise, his heart was filled with sorrow and rejection. Desiring to restore Adam to his former glory, the Son of God descended from heaven, took human flesh, and was born in a cave, bearing our humiliation and our sins.

👉🏾He gives us a new heart

👉🏾He grants us a resurrection heart

👉🏾He took our flesh so that we might receive His Spirit

👉🏾He bore our death so that we might inherit His glory and eternal lifeIn this way, He made us a new creation.

✍🏾For this reason, Scripture says that before the Lord accomplished all His saving work, He “created wisdom” (Proverbs 8:22), which the Church understands as the mystery of His birth in the flesh, prepared from the beginning for the salvation of mankind.

text.text: 2.The Revelation of the Lord’s Birth to the Shepherds

text:
✍🏾In the quiet of the night, while the shepherds were keeping watch over their flocks in the fields, a light descended from heaven and dispelled the darkness. This divine light revealed the glory and majesty of the Lord. Then the angel of the Lord appeared to them and became both a messenger and a preacher, announcing great joy that would come to all people.

✍🏾The angel declared to them that Christ the Lord, who had come for their salvation, was born in the city of David. He gave them a sign so that they might recognize Him, saying:

👉🏾“You will find a baby wrapped in swaddling cloths and lying in a manger.”

Suddenly, a multitude of angels appeared, beholding at the same time the majesty and humility of the Lord. 

They saw Him in heaven, enthroned with the Father and the Holy Spirit, and they also beheld Him on earth, lying humbly in a manger.

Therefore, they glorified God, saying:

“Glory to God in the highest.”

And as they beheld Him on earth in humility, they offered fitting thanksgiving and praise, proclaiming:

“Peace on earth, good will toward men.”

After witnessing these great wonders, the shepherds did not remain silent. They hurried to Bethlehem according to the sign given to them, as it is written:

👉🏾“They found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in the manger. When they had seen Him, they made known what had been told them concerning this Child. And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, just as it had been told them.”
(Luke 2:16–20)

The shepherds were the first believers to whom the good news was preached by the angel of the Lord. They became witnesses to the birth of Christ by proclaiming to others all that they had seen and heard.

Likewise, we too must go to Bethlehem, that is, to the Church, to seek the Lord who performed this great mystery in flesh and blood for the salvation of humanity. Let us come to know Him by receiving His holy Body and precious Blood, by believing in Him, and by honoring Him.

Therefore, let us continually give thanks in the Holy Liturgy, proclaiming:

“Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will.”

3.The Magi and the Star

When our Lord was born, the miracle of His Nativity was revealed not only on earth but also in heaven. A new star appeared, visible to the whole world. Just as the angel announced the Lord’s birth to the shepherds, so the star alone proclaimed His birth to all nations.

Guided by this star, the wise men from the East, called the Magi, came to Jerusalem. King Herod and all the city were troubled by the news they heard, asking where the King of the Jews had been born.

According to the prophecy, the Magi proceeded to Bethlehem. The star they had seen went before them and stood over the place where the Child was. As the Gospel says:

“When they had come into the house, they saw the young Child with Mary His mother, and fell down and worshiped Him. And when they had opened their treasures, they presented gifts to Him: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.”
(Matthew 2:11)

The holy Fathers of the Church teach us the meaning of these gifts:

👉🏾Gold signifies the kingship of our Lord

👉🏾Frankincense signifies His priesthood

👉🏾Myrrh signifies His saving death

Through these gifts, the Magi confessed Christ as King, Priest, and Savior.

text: Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

The Divine Liturgy is a communal prayer offered in unity, according to the order of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. It is the highest and most complete form of prayer, because in it the faithful unite with heaven, the angels, and the saints.

During the Divine Liturgy, five sacrifices are offered. Every Christian who participates offers these sacrifices to God.

text.text:
The Five Sacrifices Offered During the Liturgy

1. The Eucharistic Sacrifice

text:
During the Divine Liturgy, the bread is transformed into the Body of Christ, and the wine is transformed into His Blood by the power of the Holy Spirit.
This holy sacrifice is offered only during the Liturgy. Outside the Liturgy, there is no Eucharistic sacrifice.

The holy sacrifice prepared in Bethlehem and is offered in the church, which represents Calvary. Our Lord was born in Bethlehem, where the sacrifice was prepared, and through His crucifixion on Calvary the sacrifice was completed for the salvation of the whole world. Therefore, the holy sacrifice is continually offered to the faithful in the church, which is spiritually called Calvary.

This is the sacrifice of thanksgiving, praise, and prayer, offered by the priest, the deacon, and the people together.
As Scripture says, it is the fruit of our lips, offered in unity to our Creator.

The lamps lit during the Liturgy are an offering to God.

They symbolize Our Lord Jesus Christ, who came as the Light of the world, illuminating those who sit in darkness.

Incense is offered only by the priest. He incenses the altar, the sanctuary, and the congregation.

This symbolizes the prayers of the faithful ascending to the throne of the Holy Trinity.

Just as the angels in heaven offer incense before God while proclaiming, “Holy, Holy, Holy,” so the priest on earth represents the heavenly ministry and offers incense to God.

During the Liturgy, the faithful stand for most of the service.

At specific moments, they bow down and humble themselves before God.

Standing, bowing, and physical reverence are all forms of bodily sacrifice, offered in obedience and humility to the Creator.

✍🏾

text.text: The Three Main Parts of the Divine Liturgy

text:
The Divine Liturgy is divided into three major sections:

1.The Preparation

2.The Reading and Teaching

3.fre kidase (main holy liturgy )

The Holy Liturgy here vary according to the feast day, and there are fourteen in total. These are:

1.The Holy Liturgy

2.Kidase of the Apostles

3.Kidase of Our Lord

4.Kidase of the Virgin Mary

5.Kidase of Yohannes Welde Negodgwad

6.Kidase of the Three Saints

7.Kidase of Saint Athanasius

8.Kidase of Saint Basil

9.Kidase of Saint Gregory

10.Kidase of Saint Epiphanius

11.Kidase of Saint John Afewerk

12.Kidase of Saint Cyril (Zekerlos / Qerellos)

13.Kidase of Saint Jacob the Apostle

14.Kidase of Saint Dioscorus

Each holy liturgy is chosen according to the feast, season, or saint commemorated.

👉🏾 If it is the feast of Our Lord, the Holy Liturgy is Kidase Egzi

👉🏾 During the Advent of Our Lord and if pagume is on sunday, the Holy Liturgy of Saint Athanasius is celebrated.

👉🏾If it is the feast of Our Lady, the Holy Liturgy of the Virgin Mary is celebrated
(Gosa Labye Qale Senaye).

👉🏾 If it is the feast of the angels or the apostles, the Holy Liturgy of Saint Jacob of Serugh (Jacob Zesrug) is celebrated.

👉🏾 From the Feast of the Nativity until the Feast of the Circumcision, the Holy Liturgy of Saint Gregory the Theologian is celebrated.

text.text: Number of servants in the Holy Liturgy

text:
✍🏾The Holy Liturgy is often celebrated with five servants , symbolizing the five pillars of the holy mysteries.

However, it may also be celebrated with other numbers, each carrying spiritual meaning:

I was wondering during liturgy when we kiss the Bible I noticed at last night’s liturgy some people have the Bible placed on their back- and made a cross and also a circular motion. What is happening? And what do they do or how do they ask for that?

✍🏾 Answer :- During the Holy Liturgy, when we kiss the Gospel, we are showing reverence for the Holy Scriptures. As outlined in the Book of

the liturgical guide used in our Church every part of the liturgy is done according to a set order, including which Gospel reading, Epistles, and chapters to follow.

✍🏾The priest reads the Gospel during the service, and we are instructed to kiss it, bow, and blessed by it. a sign of respect. While the liturgical book does not specify exactly how to perform these actions, they are meant to express reverence for God’s Word.

✍🏾The specific gesture you noticed, where some people place the Gospel on their back and make the sign of the Cross with a circular motion, is a form of personal or traditional devotion. the form of these actions may vary, but their purpose is the same: to show our faith and belief in the Gospel and the Cross, as these are the means of our salvation.

text: So I have a question involving Qidase. Could someone please explain the priest walking around the Church with the incense. I understand in the Coptic Church the priest circle the Church to show how St. Paul went around the world preaching the Gospel. Also the Priest only circles halfway around the Church to symbolize the 12 who preached locally at the beginning of their mission. Can someone point me to when or if this is done in our Liturgy and point me to when it is happening so I can look for it. A bonus will be the actual words that are being said by the Church. Thank yall and Enkwan Abero Aderechu.

I’m happy you are asking such insightful questions about the Qidase and the role of incense during the service.

👉🏾During the Qidase, the priest burns incense inside a censer. The incense is a symbol of divinity, representing the prayers of the faithful rising to God. The censer is covered with a lid, symbolizing the Virgin Mary, who gave birth to Christ while remaining a virgin. The rod or chain that holds the censer also represents the Holy Spirit, who guides and sanctifies all things.

✍🏾As the priest walks around with the incense, he does so in imitation of Saint Paul, who traveled the world preaching the Gospel. The priest’s movement around the Church symbolizes how the Gospel spread throughout the world through the apostles’ travels and teachings.
The Qidase is divided into three parts:

1.
: Here, the Scriptures are read and the priest teaches the faithful.

This is the moment when the bread and wine are consecrated and become the Body and Blood of Christ.

Although it would be difficult to describe in exact numbers when the priest leaves the sanctuary to burn incense, but it happens when the Qidase begins,priest starts by saying the prayers of blessing (such as "Serawite" and invoking the name of God, "Egzio"). First, the main priest performs the ritual, followed by the assistant priest. The incense is burned while the priest moves around, and the names of the faithful are mentioned as prayers are offered.

✍🏾In general, the walking around with the incense is symbolic of the apostolic journeys. It also serves to purify the space and invite the presence of the Holy Spirit, as the priest walks and offers prayers for the faithful. This act represents the spread of the Gospel and the sanctification of the gathered community.

✍🏾I hope this helps you understand the deeper meaning behind the incense procession during the Qidase. It is a powerful moment that connects us to the apostles and the presence of God.

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today we reflect on the Ascension of the Prophet Elijah, the righteous man of God, who was taken alive into heaven by the power of the Lord. His life is a testimony to obedience, zeal for truth, victory over idolatry, and complete trust in God.

This lesson is drawn from Holy Scripture, the tradition of the Church, and the spiritual writings attributed to the Prophet Elijah.

Tir 6

✍🏾 This is the account of the ascension of Elijah, the Man of Thessalonica. He was endowed with an immortal conscience. He bore the burden of mankind and passed from death to life. While Elijah was praying, Saint Raguel appeared to him and said:

👉🏾“O warrior who has conquered lost consciences, who has conquered death, rejoice greatly, for the time has come for you to ascend to heaven. You shall live in a land of perfect joy, laughter, and happiness.”

✍🏾And it came to pass, when the Lord was about to take Elijah up into heaven, that Elijah and Elisha departed from Gilgal. Elijah said to Elisha, “Remain here, for the Lord has sent me to Bethel.” But Elisha replied, “As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you.” So they went to Bethel together.

✍🏾Again Elijah said, “Remain here, for the Lord has sent me to the Jordan.” Elisha answered, “As the Lord lives, I will not leave you.” Thus the two of them went on together. Fifty men of the sons of the prophets followed and stood at a distance, while Elijah and Elisha stood by the Jordan.

✍🏾Elijah took his mantle, rolled it up, and struck the waters of the Jordan. The waters were divided to the right and to the left, and both of them crossed over on dry ground. After they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, “Ask what I shall do for you before I am taken away from you.”

✍🏾Elisha said, “Let a double portion of the Holy Spirit that is upon you be upon me.” Elijah replied, “You have asked a good thing; nevertheless, if you see me when I am taken from you, it shall be so for you; but if you do not see me, it shall not be so.”

✍🏾 As they continued walking and talking, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared and separated the two of them. Elijah was taken up into heaven in a whirlwind. Elisha saw it and cried out, “My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and its horsemen!” And he saw him no more.

✍🏾 Then Elijah tore his clothes into two pieces. Elisha , picked up the mantle of Elijah that had fallen from him, returned, and stood by the bank of the Jordan. He took the mantle of Elijah and struck the water, saying, “Where is the God of Elijah?” When he struck the water, it was divided to the right and to the left, and Elisha crossed over.

✍🏾When the sons of the prophets who were watching saw this, they said, “The Holy Spirit that rested upon Elijah now rests upon Elisha.” They came to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.

👉🏾 Greetings to you, our father and friend Elijah.

👉🏾 Greetings to you, Elijah, who rebuked Ahab for his wicked deeds.

👉🏾 Greetings to you, Elijah, who destroyed the house of idols and shattered false worship.

👉🏾 The Lord has promised mercy to whoever writes, reads, hears, or commemorates your holy story.

👉🏾 May the God of the Prophet Elijah have mercy upon us all.

text:
My beloved child, may God's abundant grace always illuminate your path. This is a question of immense practical and spiritual importance, touching upon the very foundation of family life and our journey towards salvation. It speaks to the wisdom of the Church, which, like a loving mother, guides her children in all aspects of their lives, especially in matters as weighty as marriage and the formation of a household.

As we discussed earlier, the Orthodox Church, in her profound wisdom and experience of millennia, holds a clear and consistent teaching on marriage, which naturally extends to the dating relationships that lead to it.

The ideal, the blessed path that the Church always encourages, is for Orthodox Christians to marry within the Orthodox faith. This is not a matter of exclusivity or judgment towards those outside our fold, but rather a deep understanding of what constitutes a truly unified spiritual life for a couple and their future family.

Let us ponder this through the lens of Holy Scripture and the teachings of our Fathers:

✍🏾

The foundational principle is found in the Apostle Paul's admonition: "Do not be unequally yoked together with unbelievers. For what fellowship has righteousness with lawlessness? And what communion has light with darkness? And what accord has Christ with Belial? Or what part has a believer with an unbeliever?" (2 Corinthians 6:14-15, )

While this passage speaks broadly to various associations, its application to marriage, the most intimate and foundational of human unions, is profound and undeniable. When a farmer yokes two animals together, they must be of the same strength and nature to plow a straight furrow effectively. If they are unequal, the plow will veer off course, and the burden will fall unevenly, causing stress and imbalance.

✍🏾

text.text: Why is this Unity So Crucial in Marriage?

text: In the Orthodox understanding, the Christian home is not merely a secular dwelling; it is meant to be a "domestic church," a living cell of the Body of Christ. The husband and wife, united in the Mystery of Holy Matrimony, are called to grow together in holiness, to pray together, to fast together, to partake of the Holy Sacraments together, and to raise their children in the fear and love of God. This shared spiritual vision and practice are exceedingly difficult, if not impossible, when spouses come from different spiritual traditions or lack a shared faith in Christ.

For the Orthodox Christian, the ultimate goal of life is theosis – deification, union with God. Marriage is a path to salvation, a means by which two souls help each other to attain this blessed end. If one spouse is striving towards this through the Orthodox Sacraments, ascetical life, and theological understanding, while the other holds a different path, their ultimate spiritual destinations, and the means to reach them, will inevitably diverge. How can one truly support the other in fasting, confession, frequent Communion, or the rigorous spiritual life if they do not share the conviction of their efficacy and necessity?

text: This is perhaps the most acute challenge in religiously mixed marriages. Parents have the sacred duty to nurture their children's souls in the Orthodox faith, to bring them to baptism, chrismation, and the Holy Eucharist, and to educate them in the traditions and teachings of the Church. When parents adhere to different faiths, children can experience confusion, internal conflict, and a weakening of their own spiritual identity. Often, one parent's faith is implicitly or explicitly undermined by the other, or compromises are made that dilute the children's spiritual formation. St. John Chrysostom himself, in speaking on family life, emphasized the crucial role of parents in transmitting the faith to their children, a task made immensely easier and more powerful when both parents are in agreement and actively participating.

Our life as Orthodox Christians is deeply sacramental. Holy Communion is the "medicine of immortality." Confession is the pathway to healing and reconciliation. Chrismation seals us with the gift of the Holy Spirit. These are not mere rituals; they are the very lifeblood of our spiritual existence. A spouse who cannot partake in these mysteries with their partner creates a fundamental separation in the most intimate aspects of their spiritual lives.

✍🏾

While dating might seem a less serious commitment than marriage, in the Orthodox Christian understanding, any serious dating relationship should be entered into with the potential for marriage in mind. Therefore, the same principles that apply to marriage apply strongly to dating. To pursue a relationship with someone of a different faith, knowing the Church's teaching and the inherent difficulties, is to set oneself on a path that is likely to lead to spiritual compromises or significant challenges.

✍🏾

text.text: What if a relationship already exists?

text:
If an Orthodox Christian finds themselves in a serious relationship with a non-Orthodox individual, the Church, with compassion, urges a path of prayer, discernment, and often, conversion of the non-Orthodox partner.

👉🏾

: The hope is always that, through witnessing the beauty and truth of Orthodoxy, the non-Orthodox partner might, by God's grace and their own free will, choose to embrace the Orthodox Faith. This must be a genuine conversion of the heart, not merely a superficial agreement for the sake of marriage, as true faith cannot be coerced.

: It is absolutely essential to seek the counsel of a spiritual father, a confessor, in such situations. He, with prayer and wisdom, can offer specific guidance tailored to the unique circumstances of the couple, helping them to discern God's will and navigate the challenges ahead. He can explain the implications more deeply and guide them in prayer and reflection.

My beloved child, the Church's guidance in this matter is born not out of rigidity, but out of a profound love for her children and a desire for their deepest joy and salvation. True joy and lasting peace in marriage are found when both spouses are striving together, hand in hand, towards the Kingdom of Heaven, supported by the same Sacraments, nourished by the same spiritual food, and guided by the same holy traditions.

"The Lord will give strength to His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace." (Psalm 28:11) May this peace, which surpasses all understanding, dwell in your heart as you ponder these sacred teachings.

text.text: The Four Main Purposes Found in the Consecration of the Liturgy

text: During the celebration of the Holy Liturgy, four essential spiritual elements are revealed:

The Divine Liturgy contains the dogma and doctrine of the Church. The mysteries of the Holy Trinity, the Incarnation, the Body and Blood of Christ, and the honor of the Holy Virgin Mary are all proclaimed through the prayers of the Liturgy.

For example, when Abba Hiryakos composed the Liturgy of St. Mary, he clearly expressed the mystery of the Trinity and the divine role of the Theotokos.
Through the celebration of the fourteen liturgy, the faithful learn the history of the Church, the lives of the saints, the apostles, and the work of God throughout salvation history.

The Liturgy teaches believers to love one another, to be patient, to live in unity, to fast, to pray, and to walk in holiness. These teachings are not given briefly, but deeply and repeatedly throughout the Liturgy.

The Liturgy also exhorts the faithful to examine themselves. For example, it teaches that if someone has a quarrel with a brother or sister, reconciliation must come before Communion. It reminds us of our relationship with others and our 
submission to God the Creator.

These four elements show that the holy Liturgy is a complete spiritual school for humanity.

✍🏾

The Divine Liturgy is a communal prayer where readings, hymns, and sacrifices are offered by the priest, the deacon, and the faithful together.

The Church teaches:
“Do not stand naked before the prophet of God.”

✍🏾This means that no one should come before God without an offering. Even if a person has little, they should offer what they are able without shame. Offerings may include incense, raisins, bread, or other gifts.

✍🏾During the Liturgy, the priest prays specifically over the offerings of the faithful. If no one brings an offering, we must ask: for whom is this prayer said? Therefore, preparation for the Liturgy includes preparing an offering, according to one’s ability.

✍🏾

When we come to church to participate in the Holy Liturgy, we must prepare ourselves in the following ways:

👉🏾To stand reverently and participate fully

👉🏾To listen attentively to the readings and apply them to our lives

👉🏾To receive Holy Communion for eternal life The Church teaches through hymnody that anyone who does not remain until the end of the Liturgy, who does not listen to the Holy Scriptures, and who does not receive Holy Communion without reason, separates themselves from the communion of the Church. Therefore, preparation is essential.

✍🏾

text.text: Sanctification of the Five Senses in the Liturgy

text: During the Divine Liturgy, all five human senses are consecrate :

The faithful observe the priest’s movements at the altar.

These movements are not random; each has deep spiritual and mystical meaning. By seeing them, the eyes are sanctified.
Through hymns, prayers, Scripture readings, and proclamations by the priest and deacon, the ears are sanctified.
The fragrance of incense sanctifies the sense of smell and symbolizes the prayers of the faithful rising to God.
By receiving the Holy Communion, the Body and Blood of Christ, the sense of taste is sanctified.
Touch is sanctified through bowing, prostration, kissing the Gospel, and receiving the priest’s blessing.

4. Taste (Tongue)

By receiving the Holy Communion, the Body and Blood of Christ, the sense of taste is sanctified.

5. Touch (Hands and Body)

Touch is sanctified through bowing, prostration, kissing the Gospel, and receiving the priest’s blessing.

text:
✍🏾When all five senses are united in worship, the believer experiences full communion with God. This is the Divine Liturgy.

✍🏾The education received in the Liturgy is different from ordinary teaching. It is revealed by the Holy Spirit through generations of scholars and saints. The Gospel, Epistles, Acts, Psalms, and hymns are read melodiously, especially from the Psalms of David (Misbak).

Through continual participation in the Liturgy, a person spiritually learns the entire Bible from the Old Testament to the New Testament and lives the life of the angels on earth.

✍🏾

The Divine Liturgy is the greatest mystery of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. Therefore, it is our responsibility to teach our children:

👉🏾To participate in the Liturgy

👉🏾To bring offerings

👉🏾To prepare themselves spiritually

👉🏾To receive Holy Communion

If we fail to pass this sacred tradition to the next generation, we risk losing what has been entrusted to us by the Fathers of the Church.

May this heavenly mystery, in which we unite with the angels and glorify our Creator, bring peace and strength to our homes and preserve the Holy Church without wavering.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾The word Ketera is derived from the Geʿez verb መከተር (meketer), which means to gather water, to restrain it, or to block its flow.

✍🏾On the eve of the Feast of Baptism, the Ark of the Covenant (Tabot) is taken out of the church and brought to a place where water is found, such as a river, spring, or prepared pool. The faithful of the area gather at that place and erect a tent (dass) near the water for the Ark to remain overnight. When no natural shelter exists, a tent is deliberately set up for this sacred purpose.

👉🏾Because spring water is often weak or limited, a well or pit is dug to collect the water. The water is then restricted and prevented from flowing away, so that it may be prepared and preserved for the baptismal celebration on the following day.

👉🏾Regarding the meaning of the word Ketera, Wazemaw Sergew (1981, p. 8) explains that Ketera comes from the Geʿez verb ketera, which carries the meaning of gathering, restraining, or enclosing, and is closely related to the sense of kebebe (to surround or enclose).

✍🏾Similarly, Kidane Wold Kifle (1948, p. 555) interprets the root “ketere” as meaning to block, stop, restrain, or forbid. Since the primary activity of the faithful on Tir 10 each year is the gathering and restriction of water for baptism, this day is appropriately named Ketera.

✍🏾The water is collected and prepared to be used as the baptismal font for the faithful, since the Feast of Baptism (Timket) is celebrated on Tir 11.

✍🏾The place where the Ark of the Covenant (Tabot) is kept overnight in a tent or temporary shelter, and where natural or gathered water is cleansed, preserved, or collected, whether from springs, rivers, or artificially prepared pools, is called the Bahire Tmket,Ark shelter .

✍🏾

The Sea (Bahir) refers to a place where water is gathered, such as a reservoir or collected body of water prepared for baptism. In this sense, it is a “land of water”, a sacred space set apart for worship, prayer, and the mystery of baptism. It represents a sanctified world of water(mekane may, aleme may), prepared for holy use.

👉🏾During the reign of Saint Lalibela, the righteous Abune Tekle Haymanot, who traveled widely throughout Ethiopia preaching salvation and evangelism, blessed and sanctified the baptismal fonts in places such as Aksum, Mekelle, and Melrtule Maryam, strengthening the tradition of Ketera and Timket.

✍🏾Later, during the reign of Emperor Yekuno Amlak (1260–1275 AD), the righteous Abune Tekle Haymanot (1203–1204 AD) formally affirmed and ordered the continuation of the celebration that had already been practiced by the faithful under their spiritual care.

✍🏾The Tabots (Arks of the Covenant) were placed under the protection and care of the community and were brought to the baptismal sites for the celebration. Over time, the observance of the Feast of Baptism expanded, growing from a local religious practice into a national spiritual celebration.

✍🏾Although the Feast of the Baptism of the Lord had been observed as a public celebration since the time of Emperor Gebre Meskel, it was firmly established and systematized in the 15th century by Emperor Zara Yaqob (1426–1460 AD).

✍🏾

✍🏾The Tabot should descend to the baptismal site on the afternoon of Tir 10, the eve of the Feast.It should remain there overnight.It should not return by the same route, so that the land would be blessed by its passage.

👉🏾Following this decree, Emperor Naod (1486–1500 AD) further commanded that all Orthodox Tewahedo believers should accompany the Ark of the Covenant both during its descent to the baptismal site and its return to the church.

text:
👇🏾

✍🏾The faithfuls carrying the Ark of the Law (Tabot) out of the church with loud voices, ululation, and joyful proclamation, the faithful escort it to the Jordan of Baptism, where they remain overnight in vigil, prayer, and praise.

✍🏾Because more than one Tabot descends to the Jordan, this fulfills the word of God spoken to the prophet Moses:

“The Ark shall be a sign that I am with you.” (Exodus 25)
Just as the priests of the Old Covenant crossed the Jordan River carrying the Ark of the Law, so too the priests of the New Covenant, carrying the unchanging Ark, unite the Old Testament with the New Testament. 

👉🏾Remembering Jesus Christ as the foundation of the New Testament, the priests of the Church also journey to the Jordan, following His path.

✍🏾According to the great scholar Haregewein Ageze, the learned clergy spend the night teaching and proclaiming the Word of God appropriate to the feast. Likewise, ketera commemorates Tir 10 as the day on which our Lord Jesus Christ went from Galilee to the Jordan River to be baptized by Saint John the Baptist.

✍🏾

text.text: Liturgical Order of the Eve of Baptism

text:
✍🏾On the eve of the feast, Vespers begin at four o’clock in the morning in all local churches. The service continues with prayers proper to the feast, and the Holy Liturgy is celebrated. The priests who carry the Tabot abstain from Food, observe spiritual discipline, and offer prayers fitting to the sacred occasion.

✍🏾

On the Ketera day, after the tent has been prepared, the water gathered, and everything arranged properly, the time comes for the movement of the Ark of the Covenant from the Church .

✍🏾

👉🏾Covered with gold and silver cloths

👉🏾Adorned with beautifully embroidered priestly vestments
Priests and deacons, shining in their sacred garments, carry crosses (Metsor Meskel )and censers, and as they depart from the church toward the Abhirt (sanctuary or baptismal site), church bells ring everywhere, announcing the holy procession.

✍🏾

The faithful, young and old, walk along the paths through which the Ark passes, wearing their festive garments, rejoicing and celebrating the feast. 

👉🏾When the Ark is lifted from its throne, the chant “Yom Fisiha Kone” is sung. As the Ark is raised, the hymn proclaiming “werede weld emsemayat ...” is chanted, and the priests carry the Ark with reverence and praise.

✍🏾The priests, clothed in golden vestments and turbans, and the monks, carrying the cross and prayer beads, walk in front of the Ark of the Covenant. The deacons, wearing sacred vestments similar to those of the priests, follow, carrying crosses and prayer beads, and leading the orderly movement of the procession.

✍🏾In front of the deacons walk the church singers (debatra), dressed in robes and turbans, carrying silver and bronze cymbals. As they move, they chant hymns such as “The Son has descended”, proclaiming the mystery of the Incarnation and Baptism of Christ.

✍🏾The parish priests and abbots follow the Ark. Behind them, Sunday school students, dressed in colorful garments, participate joyfully, singing hymns such as “Werede Wold,” “EzgiʾO Merha,” “Hore Eyesus,” and other traditional Amharic praises. The mothers of the faithful raise voices of thanksgiving, chanting “Ney Ney Emye Maryam” and similar praises to the Holy Virgin. Thus, the procession advances slowly and reverently toward the baptismal pool.

✍🏾Upon reaching the baptismal site, the Ark is positioned near the prepared tent. After the hymn “Werede Wold” is properly led and sung, a prayer is offered. The Gospel reading and the hymn appointed for the day are then proclaimed. Finally, the Ark of the Covenant is solemnly led into the tent prepared for it, where it is placed with reverence and honor.
(Sergiw, 1981, p. 9)
