text.text: The Night Liturgy and the Symbolism of the Descent of the Ark

text:
✍🏾In the second part of the service, the priests remain throughout the night, offering prayers and preparing for the Divine Liturgy. The liturgy begins at midnight, and by early morning the faithful are gathered in readiness. The baptismal celebration continues on the following day, completing the mystery of the feast.

✍🏾

text.text: Symbolism of the Feast and the Descent of the Ark

text:
✍🏾The descent of the Ark of the Covenant into the water on the eve of the Feast of Baptism, and the preparation of the Sea (baptismal pool), are not symbolic inventions. They are rooted in biblical history and divine typology.

👉🏾This sacred journey with the Ark began in the time of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, and was fully revealed during the leadership of Joshua, the successor of Moses.

👉🏾Crossing of the Jordan as a Type of Baptism

When Joshua led the people of Israel to the Jordan River, the waters of the river were divided, and the flow of the river was stopped by the power of God.

“When you come to the edge of the waters of the Jordan, you shall stand still in the Jordan.”
(Joshua 3:8–9)

✍🏾

text.text: As the Israelites prepared to cross into the Promised Land:

text:

👉🏾The Ark of the Covenant was placed inside

“When you see the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord your God, and the Levitical priests carrying it, then you shall set out from your camps and follow it.” (Joshua 3:3)

✍🏾The Ark of the Covenant being taken down from its place and carried to the Jordan River on the eve of the Feast of Baptism symbolizes our Lord Jesus Christ descending to the Jordan River under the ministry of Saint John the Baptist. Just as the Ark waited in the river The whole night , Christ, in humility, waited His turn to be baptized, showing His obedience and solidarity with humanity.

👉🏾Baptism is a symbol of Christ’s death and resurrection. Though sinless, He was counted among sinners and baptized at the hands of John, prefiguring His crucifixion and the salvation of mankind.
“He was baptized in the Jordan River by John, as if He were a perfect sinner, and received baptism at the feet of John.” (KJV; 517)

The month in which Christ was baptized was a rainy and snowy season for the Israelites. It was impossible to remain by the river overnight without shelter. Therefore, those who came to be baptized pitched tents around the Jordan River for protection and worship.

Today, the Church continues this tradition: 
during the Feast of Baptism, the Ark of the Covenant is carried to the water, tents and booths are erected around the baptismal site, and the faithful participate in the sacred commemoration, re-living the mystery of Christ’s humility and our own baptismal renewal.

May our God grant us the blessings of the Lord!

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

Baptism is one of the nine great feasts of our Lord Jesus Christ, foretold by the prophets and revealed in the Holy Gospel. The word baptism comes from the verb meaning to "Tetemke". Its meaning is to be fully immersed in water, usually in flowing water such as a river, spring, or lake. The baptism performed by the priests of the Church is a holy sacrament, distinct from all other forms of symbolic baptisms.

✍🏾

text.text: Baptism in the Old and New Testaments

text:
✍🏾 In the Old Testament, baptism was a baptism of repentance. In the New Testament, baptism is the baptism of rebirth and adoption as children of God, beginning from infancy. However, the baptism of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ is unique and unlike any other. Though He is God by nature, He humbled Himself, not seeking honor from humanity, but honoring humanity.

✍🏾 To be an example and a spiritual Father to us, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ was baptized in the Jordan River by John the Baptist. Through His baptism, He revealed His natural Sonship and His divinity, testified by God the Father and the Holy Spirit. On that day, He sanctified the waters, and afterward He withdrew and began His fast .

✍🏾 The Law and the order that our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ fulfilled were not fulfilled as something foreign or strange, like a guest who arrives unexpectedly.  He fulfilled the prophecies that were spoken beforehand, the examples that were foreshadowed, the appointed times that were counted, and the hope of salvation that was given to Adam from the beginning. The Holy Scriptures testify to this fulfillment and example as follows:

👉🏾“Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to John, to be baptized by him.”(Matthew 3:13; Mark 1:9; Luke 3:21; John 1:32)

👉🏾But John objected and said, “Does the Lord receive baptism from His servant? Should the servant baptize the Lord? Does the servant go to the Lord, or does the Lord come to the servant?”

✍🏾 When our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, came from Nazareth to visit Elizabeth, the mother of John the Baptist, Holy Elizabeth said, “Why is this granted to me, that the Mother of my Lord should come to me?” Likewise, John expressed humility before Christ. But our Lord said to him, “This is our joy and our gladness:
 
✍🏾that you are proclaimed in the ministry of baptism and your honor is spoken of, and that I am baptized by the hand of a servant and My humility is proclaimed. Allow it for a time, for it is fitting for us to fulfill the prophecies of the prophets.”

✍🏾He was baptized once, not twice; willingly, not by force; in His human nature, not in His divinity. For He who is pure God had no need of cleansing, yet He accepted baptism to fulfill righteousness, to reveal humility, and to establish the sacrament for the salvation of humanity.

It was foretold by the prophets that John would baptize, and that the Lord Himself would be baptized by John. 

Therefore, our Lord said, “It is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness,” meaning that the prophecies spoken beforehand must be fulfilled.

This was done for the joy of the believers, so that when they are baptized, the Holy Spirit may come upon them. It was also for the joy of the Father, who testifies to His Son; for the joy of the Son, who reveals His obedience and humility; 

and for the joy of the Holy Spirit, who is manifested to the world.
When the Son was baptized in the Jordan River, God the Father bore witness from heaven, saying, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.” At the same time, the Holy Spirit descended in the form of a dove and rested upon Him. Through this divine manifestation, the unity and revelation of the Holy Trinity were made known.

text:
👇🏾

Then our Lord said to John, “We must complete the work of righteousness that has begun; allow it for a time.” And John consented and baptized Him willingly, according to the will of God.

👉🏾John the Baptist said, “The Father is in You through the Holy Spirit, and You are in the Father through the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit is in You and in the Father. I baptize others in Your name, but in whose name shall I baptize You?”

👉🏾Our Lord answered him, saying, “The Son is blessed, and you are a priest to the world, according to the order of Melchizedek.”

✍🏾After this, they went down together into the water. As the Gospel says, “When our Lord Jesus Christ was baptized, He came up from the water” (Matthew 3:16), and “the heavens were opened to Him.” This opening of the heavens does not mean that heaven was physically closed and then opened. Rather, just as when a sealed vessel is opened its contents become visible, so also at the baptism of our Lord a hidden mystery was revealed. That mystery is the manifestation of the unity of the Holy Trinity.

👉🏾From this arises the question: Why did the Lord go from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized? Does a servant go to his master, or does the Lord go to His servant? Does the servant receive baptism from his master, or does the Lord receive baptism from His servant?

Our Lord’s coming was not for His own glory, nor merely for humility. 

👉🏾Rather, it was to set an example. If our Lord had said to John, “Come and baptize Me,” then kings, nobles, and rulers would later say, “Come to our houses and baptize us.” Instead, our Lord Himself went to John and was baptized, teaching us by example to go to the Church, where the priests are, and to receive baptism according to the order established by God.

✍🏾 The baptism of our Lord was not to add glory to Him, for He is already full of glory. Rather, it was to make the Jordan River a radiant womb, so that we, the believers, might be reborn of water and the Holy Spirit and enter the Kingdom of Heaven. 

Through His baptism, the waters were sanctified, and the way of spiritual rebirth was opened for humanity.

Likewise, the sacrament of baptism was established to teach us and to serve as an example. As our Lord said:

“Unless one is born again of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.” (John 3:5)

And again:

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾The Feast of Cana of Galilee is one of the nine minor feasts of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. It is celebrated on Tir 12.

✍🏾Originally, this feast was to be celebrated on Yekatit 23. However, since Yekatit falls during a fasting season, the Fathers of the Church, guided by wisdom, named it “The Feast of Water with Water” and transferred its celebration to Tir 12.

The Holy Gospel according to Saint John says:

👉🏾“On the third day there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee.”(John 2:1)

It continues:

“The mother of Jesus was there. Jesus also was invited to the wedding with His disciples.”

✍🏾From this , we understand that the Holy Virgin Mary was present first at the wedding. After the Mother was present, the Son was invited, and after Him, His disciples were also invited with Him.During the wedding, when the wine ran out, the Holy Virgin Mary said to Him, “They have no wine.”

Our Lord Jesus Christ replied to her, saying:

👉🏾“What have I to do with you? My time has not yet come.”

👉🏾This exchange reveals a deep spiritual mystery, showing both the intercession of the Holy Virgin Mary and the divine wisdom of our Lord Jesus Christ, who would reveal His glory at the appointed time.

When We Enter into the Mystery

What Is Meant by “The Third Day”?

Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ was baptized on Tir 11. 

Immediately after His baptism, He went into the wilderness, where He fasted for forty days and forty nights. His fast ended on Yekatit 20, and on Yekatit 23, Scripture says:

“On the third day there was a wedding.”(John 2:1)This “third day” does not refer only to a number of days, but to a spiritual age.

✍🏾

text.text: The Meaning of the Three Days

text:
👉🏾The first day refers to the time of the Patriarchs, when Adam, Abraham, and Isaac were the fathers of God’s people(Zemene Abew).

👉🏾The second day refers to the time of the Law (Torah), when Moses was the father and guide of Israel.(zemene Orit)

👉🏾The third day refers to the time when our Lord Jesus Christ became man, fulfilling the Law and the Prophets.

✍🏾It was during this third time, the age of grace and incarnation, that the wedding at Cana of Galilee took place.

👉🏾“Our Lady Was Before”
When it is said, “Our Lady was before,” this means that the Holy Virgin Mary preceded our Lord Jesus Christ in His physical manifestation.
 
✍🏾Saint John the Baptist was born six months before Christ, and his mother Elizabeth conceived before the Virgin Mary gave birth. 

✍🏾For this reason, to speak of the Child without knowing the Mother becomes difficult and incomplete.

✍🏾If one speaks of Jesus Christ without knowing the Holy Virgin Mary, who was chosen and prepared before His incarnation, the understanding of salvation becomes weak and incomplete. Even today, before calling upon the name of Jesus, the Church teaches us to approach Him through His Mother as our intercessor.

👉🏾The Place of the Virgin Mary in SalvationWhen we reflect on salvation:

We must first bring the Holy Virgin Mary to our mind.The beginning of the mystery of the Incarnation through Mary is the foundation of the doctrine of salvation.

Our Lord was born, lived in exile, taught, was crucified, died, rose from the dead, ascended into heaven, and will come again in the flesh He took from the Virgin Mary.

From this, we understand why the Church honors her first, without separating her from her Son.

👉🏾When the wine ran out, the Holy Virgin Mary said,

👉🏾“They have no wine.”

✍🏾The Gospel does not say who informed her. It was not necessarily the bridegroom or the servants. Rather, the Holy Virgin Mary herself knew, because she is a prophetess, endowed with divine grace. She knows what has happened and what will happen.

✍🏾After Saint Zechariah and Saint Elizabeth praised her, she proclaimed:

👉🏾“From now on all generations will call me blessed.”
(Luke 1:48–49)

✍🏾This declaration reveals her prophetic nature and confirms the unique grace given to her by God.

✍🏾

text.text: The Grace and Knowledge of the Holy Virgin Mary

text:
Isaiah prophesies, saying,  And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. ” (Isaiah 8:1). 

✍🏾The Church understands this prophetess as a type pointing to Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, through whom the mystery of the Incarnation would be revealed.In 2 Kings 6:8–12, the king of Syria secretly planned to attack the king of Israel. Yet the prophet Elisha, though physically in Jerusalem, knew everything that was happening in Syria. 

✍🏾Through divine grace, he revealed the enemy’s plans and saved the king. This shows the extraordinary gift God granted to His prophets: knowledge of distant and hidden things.

✍🏾If the prophets of old were given such grace, what then of the Holy Virgin Mary, the Mother of God? Would it be strange that she perceived the problem in the house of Dokim (Cana) when the wine ran out? How much greater must her grace be, she who bore God the Word in her womb. Truly, none among the ancient generations was more blessed than she. Therefore the angel rightly proclaimed, “Rejoice, full of grace” (Luke 1:28).

✍🏾When our Lord said to her, “What have I to do with you?” (John 2:4), He did not speak with rejection or disrespect. He did not mean, “Go away.” Rather, His words indicate, “What is there that would prevent Me from doing what you have asked?” His response preserves both divine authority and perfect obedience.

👉🏾Scripture commands, “Honor your father and your mother” (Exodus 20:12), and the Gospel testifies that Christ “was subject to them” (Luke 2:51). It would be unthinkable and contrary to His nature to speak harshly to His mother. 

✍🏾He is the perfect Son, obedient in all things.When He said, “My hour has not yet come,” this refers not to refusal, but to divine timing. The wine had to be completely finished so that the miracle would be unmistakable. Had water been added earlier, people might have claimed the wine was merely diluted. But when all the wine was gone, and water was transformed into wine, the glory of God was clearly revealed.

Thus, after the wine was entirely exhausted, our Lord Jesus Christ transformed water into wine, and His miracle became known to all.

👉🏾 For this reason,
Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ performed His miracle at Cana of Galilee, through the intercession of His holy Mother.

May God enlighten our minds and establish us in understanding.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

Some people, either out of ignorance or jealousy, claim that wearing white garments when going to church is not a Christian practice. However, the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church (EOTC) explains this tradition clearly through both Holy Scripture and living practice, revealing its deep spiritual mystery.

✍🏾 It is appropriate and fitting to wear white clothing when we enter the church. The white garment is not worn without meaning. There are sacred mysteries we are meant to remember when we wear the white robe and stand in the holy temple bearing the sign of the Cross.

✍🏾

text.text: Why do we wear white robe like Cross sign ?

text:
We wear it to remember the suffering of our Lord Jesus Christ. The way the tunic or netela is folded from left to right forms the sign of the Cross, reminding us of His crucifixion.

✍🏾 At that moment, we remember the suffering of our Lord on Good Friday and His crucifixion on the Holy Cross at Golgotha. Whoever sees the Cross-shaped garment is reminded of accepting the suffering of Christ and walking in His footsteps.

✍🏾 The reason the garment we wear is white carries many spiritual meanings. Though these reasons are many, we summarize them as follows:

text.text: 1. We wear white as a reminder of the heavenly glory prepared for us

text:
👉🏾 “And they were given white robes…”(Revelation 6:9–11)

👉🏾 “After this I looked, and behold, a great multitude that no one could number, from every nation, tribe, people, and language, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands.”(Revelation 7:9)

White reminds us of the eternal glory awaiting the righteous in the Kingdom of Heaven.

text.text: 2. We remember that the holy angels are present with us

text:
👉🏾 “Mary stood outside the tomb weeping… and she saw two angels in white sitting where the body of Jesus had been.”
(John 20:11–12)

When we serve in the church, we serve together with the angels. Dressing in purity and humility reflects the heavenly worship. To serve carelessly or arrogantly in the house of God is shameful.

text.text: 3. We remember that we stand before our Lord Himself

text:
👉🏾 “And He was transfigured before them; His face shone like the sun, and His clothes became white as the light.”(Matthew 17:1–2)

(Netela )The single white garment reminds us of Christ’s glory and calls us to purity of body and soul.

✍🏾 Therefore, wearing a single garment has deep spiritual meaning.

Men should wear a single white garment during the Covenant, the Holy Liturgy, and the Feast of the Church . Likewise, it is fitting for women to wear a proper white garment that preserves order and modesty, while remembering these spiritual truths.

👉🏾 “Do not remove the ancient landmark which your fathers have set.”(Proverbs 22:28)

✍🏾 Let us be encouraged to preserve the order and tradition of the Church.

May God enlighten our minds so that we may live according to His will, not according to our personal desires. Many of us struggle with obedience to the Word because we have become accustomed to worldly thinking and self-centered freedom.

If we followed only our own opinions without dogma and canon, like the Protestant Reformers, we would have become countless divided groups. But the Orthodox Church, guided by the Holy Spirit, has preserved one faith, one dogma, and one path that leads us toward one goal: salvation.

text:
Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

The life of Our Lady in the Temple is taught by many holy Fathers and scholars, including:

👉🏾Saint Yared

👉🏾Abba Tsige Dengel

👉🏾Abba Hiriakos

👉🏾Saint Athanasius

👉🏾Saint Cyril of Alexandria

👉🏾Saint Demetrius

👉🏾Saint Cyril of Jerusalem

Before examining their teachings, let us first recall the account of her entrance into the Temple at the age of three.

text.text: The Entrance of the Holy Virgin into the Temple

text:
When the Holy Virgin Mary reached the age of three, her parents, Saint Joachim and Saint Hannah, fulfilled the vow they had made to God.

They called their relatives, friends, and their children, dressed the Holy Child in pure and special garments, and brought her to the Temple in Jerusalem. 

While praising God with spiritual hymns, they carried lamps in their hands and joyfully escorted her to the Temple.

The High Priest Zechariah, together with the priests and elders, came out of the Temple to receive her, singing hymns of thanksgiving. With great reverence and gratitude, Joachim and Hannah presented the Holy Virgin Mary to God.

At that moment, the Holy Spirit revealed to High Priest Zechariah that this Child was the one who would give birth to the Son of God, whom the prophets had foretold as the Savior who would restore humanity to Paradise.

By divine revelation, Zechariah placed her in the Holy of Holies, a place where only the high priest could enter once a year to offer sacrifice. This itself was a great mystery and sign of her unique holiness.

✍🏾

When Zechariah became concerned, saying:

“What shall we do with this Child?
What shall we feed her?
What shall we give her to drink?
How shall we care for her?”

God, in His mercy, sent Archangel Phanuel, the angel of fire.

The archangel descended from heaven, lifted the Holy Virgin with his wings, and fed her the Bread of Heaven and gave her the Cup of Light to drink. After nourishing her, the angel ascended again to heaven.

Seeing this great mystery, all glorified God.

Thus, Our Lady Mary, the Ark of the Incarnate Word, entered the Temple, which itself is the image of the heavenly Temple, on Tahsas 3/5488 BC, at the age of three years. After this, Joachim and Hannah returned to their home.

✍🏾

text.text: Teaching of Saint Yared on Her Entrance into the Temple

text:
👉🏾 Saint Yared teaches about the Holy Virgin in his hymns and prayers, saying:

1.The angels call Our Lady their sister and cover her with their wings.

The Word of God flows from her lips like honey.The Most High loves her, and King David praised her in his Psalms.She was received into the Temple by divine will.(Saint Yared_ Metshafe diguwa)

2. “O Mary, whom the Lord has chosen, pray for us.You were received by Zechariah in the Temple.All the saints call you the New Virgin.”

3. “Our Lady, daughter of David, clothed in wisdom and humility,who grew up in the Temple,called down the One who came from heaven.”

✍🏾

text.text: Teaching of Abba Tsige Dengel and Abba Gebre Mariam

text:
These scholars, in Mahlete Tsige, teach that the Holy Virgin Mary was fed by the hand of an angel.

They praise her life in the Temple, saying in meaning:

“O Mary, the solitude you endured when you entered the Temple while still nursing from Hannah saddens us;
yet the miracle of your growth in purity fills us with joy.

Phanuel, the angel of fire, who walks upon the clouds, fed you with heavenly manna together with the angels.”

They also describe her as:

“An Ark adorned with gold,pure in body and soul,filled with heavenly fragrance,shown to the world through the faith of Joachim and Hannah.”

text.text: Question : why don`t we recite other prayers in holy lituargy

text:
: My child, the Divine Liturgy is not an ordinary time of prayer. It is the highest and most perfect prayer of the Church, handed down to us by the Apostles and sealed by the Holy Spirit. When we stand in the Holy Liturgy, we are not standing alone as individuals, but together with the Church on earth and the Church in heaven.

For this reason, we do not recite personal or separate prayers during the Holy Liturgy. To do so would be to divide the heart and the attention. 

The Liturgy itself is a complete prayer: thanksgiving, repentance, supplication, praise, and sacrifice. In it, the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ are offered and received. There is no prayer higher than this on earth.
The fathers teach us that mixing other prayers into the Liturgy is like lighting a candle under the full sun. When the sun is shining, the candle adds nothing. The Holy Liturgy is that sun. If we participate in it with fear of God, faith, and love, our souls receive life itself.

This does not mean that personal prayer is unimportant. On the contrary, prayer is as necessary to our life as food and water. But every prayer has its proper time and order. Personal prayers belong before or after the Liturgy, at home, in the night, or in times of need. During the Liturgy, our prayer must be one with the prayer of the Church.

If there is a serious and compelling reason that prevents a person from offering private prayer on a certain day, this does not mean that God abandons them because they did not pray. God is merciful and knows our weakness. Nevertheless, we must never become careless, for prayer is the breath of the soul and without it the soul grows weak.

Therefore, my child, when you stand in the Holy Liturgy, stand fully present. Listen, respond, bow, repent, and receive grace. Do not add to it, and do not take from it. What the Church gives you there is more than enough for life and salvation.

text.text: Question :What the incense in holy litury symbolises to?

text:
My beloved child, may God bless you with abundant grace as you seek to understand the sacred symbols of our Holy Church. Your question about the meaning of incense in the Divine Liturgy is a profound one, for this blessed aroma and its rising smoke are truly an integral part of our worship, speaking to our senses and elevating our souls.

As we continue on this journey of understanding our faith, let us contemplate the rich symbolism of incense. It is not merely an aesthetic element, but a tangible representation of spiritual realities, drawing us closer to the heavenly Kingdom.

The use of incense in worship is deeply rooted in both the Old and New Testaments, flowing from a tradition that spans millennia:

This is perhaps the most fundamental and universally understood symbolism. When the fragrant smoke rises heavenward, it symbolizes our prayers ascending to the Most High. The Holy Scriptures eloquently capture this:

    👉🏾"Let my prayer be set forth as incense before thee; the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice." (Psalm 140:2, Septuagint, which is Psalm 141 in other numbering systems)
   
👉🏾 In the Book of Revelation, Saint John the Theologian describes the heavenly liturgy: "And another angel came and stood at the altar, having a golden censer; and there was given unto him much incense, that he should offer it with the prayers of all saints upon the golden altar which was before the throne. And the smoke of the incense, which came with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before God out of the angel’s hand." (Revelation 8:3-4)

    These passages clearly link incense with the petitions and supplications of the faithful, rising as a pleasing aroma before God.

text: The sweet-smelling aroma of the incense symbolizes the presence of God's grace, the Holy Spirit, and the virtues of the saints. Just as a pleasant fragrance permeates the air, so too does God's holiness sanctify the space and the faithful. It is a reminder that we are in the presence of the Divine, and that His grace is poured out upon us

text.text: What is the role of our mother Mary in our salvation?

text:
My beloved child, may God’s grace and the boundless mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ ever dwell within your heart. Your question regarding the role of our Most Holy Mother Mary in our salvation is of profound spiritual importance, touching upon one of the most cherished doctrines of our Orthodox Faith. It is a question that requires deep reverence and careful elucidation.

As we journey together in understanding the mysteries of our faith, let us turn our gaze to the Mother of God, the Theotokos, for her role is central and indispensable in God's divine plan for humanity's salvation, though always understood in relation to her Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.

The Ark of the New Covenant and the Gate of Incarnation

Firstly and most fundamentally, the Most Holy Theotokos is the Mother of God (Theotokos in Greek, which means "God-bearer" or "she who gave birth to God"). This is her most exalted title, affirmed by the Third Ecumenical Council in Ephesus (431 A.D.). She is not merely the mother of Christ's human nature, but the mother of the Person who is both fully God and fully Man.

Her role in our salvation begins with her "Fiat" (Let it be done), her humble and free acceptance of God's will at the Annunciation: "Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word." (Luke 1:38, Septuagint) Without her "yes," without her pure and obedient vessel, the Incarnation of God the Word would not have occurred in the manner God ordained. She became the living Ark of the New Covenant, carrying within her womb the very Creator of the Universe, who took flesh from her pure blood.

The Holy Fathers often refer to the Theotokos as the New Eve. Just as the first Eve, through disobedience, brought sin and death into the world, leading to our condemnation, so too did the New Eve, through her perfect obedience and purity, become instrumental in bringing forth the New Adam, Christ, who would conquer sin and death. Her purity of heart and mind, her absolute devotion to God, made her worthy to become the vessel for salvation. We believe that she was chosen and preserved by divine grace, and that through the indwelling of the Holy Spirit at the Annunciation, she was made perfectly pure and sinless, a fitting dwelling place for God.

text.text: 3. Her Participation in the Economy of Salvation

text: Our Mother Mary did not merely give birth to Christ and then disappear. She actively participated in the economy of salvation:
She brought God into the world.
She offered Him to God and heard the prophecy of Simeon concerning the sword that would pierce her soul (Luke 2:35), foreshadowing her suffering at the foot of the Cross.
She interceded on behalf of others, prompting Christ's first public miracle: "Whatever He says to you, do it." (John 2:5) This is a profound lesson for us on obedience to Christ.

She stood steadfast, enduring unimaginable pain, truly sharing in the suffering of her Son for our salvation (John 19:25-27). This co-suffering, not co-redemption, further highlights her intimate participation.

Having completed her earthly course, our Mother Mary was assumed into heaven, body and soul (her Dormition). From her exalted position, she continues her maternal care for all humanity, especially those who call upon her Son. She is a most powerful intercessor before the throne of God. We seek her prayers, not because she grants salvation, but because her prayers, as the Mother of God, are especially potent and efficacious. She is our advocate, our solace, and a fount of mercy, always pointing us towards Christ, her Son and our God.

✍🏾Answer : My beloved child, may God’s grace and the boundless mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ ever dwell within your heart. Your question regarding the role of our Most Holy Mother Mary in our salvation is of profound spiritual importance, touching upon one of the most cherished doctrines of our Orthodox Faith. It is a question that requires deep reverence and careful elucidation.

As we journey together in understanding the mysteries of our faith, let us turn our gaze to the Mother of God, the Theotokos, for her role is central and indispensable in God's divine plan for humanity's salvation, though always understood in relation to her Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.

1. The Theotokos: The Ark of the New Covenant and the Gate of Incarnation

Firstly and most fundamentally, the Most Holy Theotokos is the Mother of God (Theotokos in Greek, which means "God-bearer" or "she who gave birth to God"). This is her most exalted title, affirmed by the Third Ecumenical Council in Ephesus (431 A.D.). She is not merely the mother of Christ's human nature, but the mother of the Person who is both fully God and fully Man.

Her role in our salvation begins with her "Fiat" (Let it be done), her humble and free acceptance of God's will at the Annunciation: "Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word." (Luke 1:38, Septuagint) Without her "yes," without her pure and obedient vessel, the Incarnation of God the Word would not have occurred in the manner God ordained. She became the living Ark of the New Covenant, carrying within her womb the very Creator of the Universe, who took flesh from her pure blood.

2. The New Eve: Undoing Disobedience

The Holy Fathers often refer to the Theotokos as the New Eve. Just as the first Eve, through disobedience, brought sin and death into the world, leading to our condemnation, so too did the New Eve, through her perfect obedience and purity, become instrumental in bringing forth the New Adam, Christ, who would conquer sin and death. Her purity of heart and mind, her absolute devotion to God, made her worthy to become the vessel for salvation. We believe that she was chosen and preserved by divine grace, and that through the indwelling of the Holy Spirit at the Annunciation, she was made perfectly pure and sinless, a fitting dwelling place for God.

3. Her Participation in the Economy of Salvation

Our Mother Mary did not merely give birth to Christ and then disappear. She actively participated in the economy of salvation:

👉🏾At the Nativity: She brought God into the world.

👉🏾At the Presentation in the Temple: She offered Him to God and heard the prophecy of Simeon concerning the sword that would pierce her soul (Luke 2:35), foreshadowing her suffering at the foot of the Cross.

👉🏾At the Wedding at Cana: She interceded on behalf of others, prompting Christ's first public miracle: "Whatever He says to you, do it." (John 2:5) This is a profound lesson for us on obedience to Christ.

👉🏾At the Foot of the Cross: She stood steadfast, enduring unimaginable pain, truly sharing in the suffering of her Son for our salvation (John 19:25-27). This co-suffering, not co-redemption, further highlights her intimate participation.

4. Our Intercessor and Mother

Having completed her earthly course, our Mother Mary was assumed into heaven, body and soul (her Dormition). From her exalted position, she continues her maternal care for all humanity, especially those who call upon her Son. She is a most powerful intercessor before the throne of God. We seek her prayers, not because she grants salvation, but because her prayers, as the Mother of God, are especially potent and efficacious. She is our advocate, our solace, and a fount of mercy, always pointing us towards Christ, her Son and our God.

Continues 👇🏾

✍🏾Let us be clear, my child: Salvation comes only through our Lord Jesus Christ. He alone is the Redeemer, the Savior, the High Priest, and the Sacrifice. The Theotokos made the Incarnation of our Savior possible. She is the bridge between God and humanity, the scala coeli (ladder to heaven), through whom God descended to us and through whom we ascend to Him.

As our beloved St. John Chrysostom teaches us to honor the saints and especially the Theotokos: "Let us marvel at her, let us be astonished, let us adore her as the Mother of God; yet let us also imitate her virtuous life." She is the epitome of humility, purity, obedience, and self-sacrifice – a perfect model for every Christian soul striving for theosis.

Therefore, her role in our salvation is indispensable and glorious. She is "more honorable than the Cherubim and incomparably more glorious than the Seraphim," because she bore God Himself. Through her, Christ came into the world to redeem it.

May the prayers of our Holy Mother Mary ever uphold you.

text.text: What the incense and lights in the holy liturgy symbolises to?

text: My beloved child,  Your insightful questions about the symbolism in our Holy Liturgy are truly a testament to your fervent desire to draw closer to the mysteries of our faith. We have spoken of the incense, and now you turn to the lights – indeed, they too are rich with spiritual meaning, illuminating our path and elevating our hearts.

text.text: Here is the answer about incense that you asked earlier.

text:
✍🏾In the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, the use of light in the church is not decorative or optional. It is a sacred requirement rooted in Holy Scripture and deep spiritual symbolism. For this reason, the church is filled with light through candles, oil lamps, olive oil, and even modern lamps. These lights are used during regular prayers, the Divine Liturgy, the reading of the Holy Gospel, before holy icons, and on the pulpit.

Light holds profound spiritual meaning because it is a divine command. From the very beginning, God revealed Himself through light:

“And God said, ‘Let there be light,’ and there was light. And God saw that the light was good” (Genesis 1:3–4).

✍🏾The early Christians also prayed with light, as Scripture tells us:“There were many lamps in the upper room where they were gathered” (Acts 20:8).

✍🏾Above all, the church must be filled with light because it is the dwelling place of God, who is holy and luminous. Our Lord Jesus Christ said, “I am the light of the world” (John 8:12), and the Apostle John teaches, “God is light, and in Him is no darkness at all” (1 John 1:5). In the Book of Revelation, the Church itself is called a lampstand. Saint John saw Christ standing among the seven golden lampstands, which represent the seven churches (Revelation 1:20).

✍🏾The mystery of lamps lit with olive oil is especially deep. In the Old Testament, oil was used to anoint priests and kings, symbolizing the presence and power of the Holy Spirit. Scripture says, “Then Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers; and the Spirit of the Lord came mightily upon David from that day forward” (1 Samuel 16:13). For this reason, oil and light in the church remind us of our anointing by the Holy Spirit and His work within us.

✍🏾The candle and lamp burning in the church symbolize the mercy of the Holy Spirit working in our hearts and our continual remembrance of God. Their constant flame reminds us that God’s protection never leaves us. The light of the church also represents the righteous and the martyrs. Our Lord said, “You are the light of the world. Let your light so shine before men” (Matthew 5:14–16), and Scripture speaks of the righteous shining like stars (Daniel 12:3). They are described as lamps placed on a lampstand (Matthew 5:15).

✍🏾Therefore, lighting lamps before the icons of the saints and martyrs signifies that they were lights in their deeds and words. They burned with the fire of God’s love and became light to the world through their faith and sacrifice. This light reminds us of their suffering and their glory, as the Lord said, “The righteous will shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father” (Matthew 13:43), and John the Baptist was called “a burning and shining lamp” (John 5:35).

✍🏾Our Lord also commands spiritual vigilance, saying, “Let your waist be girded and your lamps burning” (Luke 12:35). Thus, when we see the lamps burning in the church, we are reminded to remain spiritually awake and prepared for the coming of Christ.

✍🏾When a candle is lit during the reading of the Holy Gospel, it symbolizes the guiding power of God’s Word in our spiritual journey:

👉🏾“Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path” (Psalm 119:105).

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

During the season of Asteryo , the Church celebrates the great revelation of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, through which the mystery of the Holy Trinity was made known. However, although the Virgin Mary is inseparably united with the mystery of Christ’s incarnation, the Church does celebrate her feast during this season as “Asteryo Mary.” Each feast in the Church is honored according to its own spiritual meaning and appointed time.

✍🏾

text.text: The Departure and Glory of the Holy Virgin Mary

text:
Our Mother of God, the Holy Virgin Mary, lived on this earth in holiness and obedience, bearing suffering and pain for the sake of humanity’s salvation. After completing her earthly life, she rested in glory according to the guidance of the Holy Spirit. Though she died in the flesh, she was honored by God, and like her Son, she was raised in glory. According to the tradition of the Church, this took place in the holy month of Nehase.

✍🏾

text.text: The Life of the Holy Virgin Mary

text:
The Holy Virgin Mary lived:

👉🏾3 years with her parents,

👉🏾12 years in the Temple,

👉🏾33 years and 3 months with her beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ,

👉🏾15 years under the care of the holy Evangelist Saint John after the Ascension of our Lord.
Thus, she lived a total of 64 years in this world in purity and holiness.

✍🏾

The Holy Virgin Mary passed away on Tir 21/ 49 A.D after completing her life in holiness and obedience to God.

✍🏾

text.text: Why the Church Celebrates This Feast

text:
All Christians are called to celebrate this holy feast, because our Holy Orthodox Tewahedo Church, guided by the Holy Spirit, has established an orderly and spiritual tradition for us. The Ascension (Repose) of the Holy Virgin Mary is a feast celebrated by the faithful, and in Ethiopia, as well as throughout the entire Orthodox Tewahedo world, it is observed with great reverence, joy, and devotion.

✍🏾

We do not celebrate this feast merely to remember the passing of our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary. Rather, we celebrate it with hope in her intercession, trusting in her prayers and motherly care. As we remember her holy repose, we ask that our Mother, the Holy Virgin Mary, may remember her country Ethiopia, and through her prayers may God grant peace, love, unity, and stability to her people.

May she also intercede for us before her Son, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, for the forgiveness of our sins and the salvation of our souls.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.
Amen.

During the season of Asteryo , the Church celebrates the great revelation of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, through which the mystery of the Holy Trinity was made known. However, although the Virgin Mary is inseparably united with the mystery of Christ’s incarnation, the Church does celebrate her feast during this season as “Asteryo Mary.” Each feast in the Church is honored according to its own spiritual meaning and appointed time.

✍🏾 The Departure and Glory of the Holy Virgin Mary

Our Mother of God, the Holy Virgin Mary, lived on this earth in holiness and obedience, bearing suffering and pain for the sake of humanity’s salvation. After completing her earthly life, she rested in glory according to the guidance of the Holy Spirit. Though she died in the flesh, she was honored by God, and like her Son, she was raised in glory. According to the tradition of the Church, this took place in the holy month of Nehase.

👉🏾12 years in the Temple,

👉🏾33 years and 3 months with her beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ,

👉🏾15 years under the care of the holy Evangelist Saint John after the Ascension of our Lord.

The Holy Virgin Mary passed away on Tir 21/ 49 A.D after completing her life in holiness and obedience to God.

text.text: Meaning and Role of Saint Ura'el

text:
The name Ura'el means “Light of God” or “Lord of Light.”

From the creation of the world, Saint Uriel was appointed over lightning and thunder, manifesting the power and judgment of God.

👉🏾Saint Ura'el is known as a helper in times of trouble, a guide in darkness, and a protector of God’s faithful people.

The Archangel Saint Ura'el, who is a helper in times of trouble, has shown great favor to the kings of our country throughout the centuries. During the reign of Emperor Constantine II, Saint Ura'el guided the nation through his prayers and did not depart from it until the end of the king’s reign.

The king was a pious ruler who deeply loved the Mother of God, the Holy Virgin Mary. Because of his faith and devotion, he was able to govern Ethiopia according to true Orthodox belief and righteousness.

✍🏾 This king brought holy icons of Our Lady, painted by Saint Luke the Evangelist, from Jerusalem.

👉🏾 One of these holy icons was placed by Saint Uriel in a place called Jebla in Gojjam, a land sanctified by the blood of our Lord.

👉🏾 The second icon was placed at Debre Werk.

👉🏾 The third icon was placed in a lake, preserved by divine protection.

👉🏾The icon of Saint Ura’el, painted by Saint John the Evangelist, was placed with great honor in a golden tabernacle within the city.

👉🏾The red robe of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ was placed in the royal chapel of the Ambasle region, a place that Saint Ura’el sanctified with the blood of our Lord. Because this chapel surpassed all others in holiness and glory, it was given the name Debre Kerbe.

✍🏾 During his reign, King Zera Yacob also built a church in the name of Saint Ura’el in Debre Birhan, in addition to the many churches he established in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and the Holy Virgin Mary. He did this so that the name of the Archangel might be proclaimed and his feasts properly celebrated in the Church.

✍🏾 When King Zera Yacob learned that Muslims attempted to seize sacred treasures, and that after failing they arrested Abba Michael, the Archbishop of Alexandria, and burned churches in Egypt, the king rose in defense of the faith. He went to Egypt and fought against the persecutors of the Church, standing firm for Orthodox belief through the intercession of Our Lady Mary and Saint Ura’el.

✍🏾With the help of Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, and through the intercession of Saint Ura’el, the king was strengthened and victorious over his enemies. The king of the Muslims, Ahmed, and the noble warrior of Adal and T‌ilt‌al, Bedlayn, were defeated. Through this victory, Abba Michael, the Archbishop of Alexandria, was released from imprisonment and brought safely to Ethiopia, by the will of our Lord Jesus Christ.

✍🏾The king also raised and placed the Holy Cross in the building at Debre Kerbe, which had been constructed earlier by his father, King David II, thus restoring its glory and sanctity.

✍🏾 After this, King Zera Yacob commanded Queen Eleni to build a church in the name of Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary. When the Divine Liturgy was completed, our Lord appeared to them and blessed the church with the blood that flowed from His side when He was crucified on Calvary. Through this divine revelation, Saint Ura’el consecrated the church, sealing it with holiness.

✍🏾After this, the king built two churches at Debre Bisrat, and he also built two additional churches on its right side.

👉🏾 He named the first church “Seyf Atra” . This name was given because, when the construction of the church began, the king saw Saint Ura’el, together with the angels of fire and Our Lady, the Holy Virgin Mary, purifying the place with fiery swords carried in their wings.

✍🏾 When Ede Mariam, the son of King Zera Yacob, became king, he also built a church in the name of Saint Ura’el. He granted forty acres of land to the church as a memorial for the annual feast of the Archangel.

✍🏾 The Church was named “Mis'ale Maryam.” This king followed in the righteous footsteps of his father and continued to build churches. The works of the Nine Holy Fathers, together with the deeds of the Orthodox kings from King Yekuno Amlak to King Iyasu, and the steadfastness of their true faith, are recorded in the Book of Ura’el.
All of us who are Christians should commemorate the feast of this guardian Archangel, Saint Ura’el, who protects us from all evil, from enemies who come openly and secretly, and who delivers us from this passing world, which fades like a shadow and a desert flower.

✍🏾Through the grace of the Father, and at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, born of the Holy Virgin Mary, we are saved from eternal death through the prayers and intercession of Saint Ura’el.

✍🏾 In these times, when the world is filled with distress, suffering, and confusion, those who live in it can endure only through the intercession of the saints.

✍🏾 Many people cannot move freely, cannot live in peace, and cannot rest securely. Because of this, the prayers of the saints become a support for us, helping us not to lose hope, not to stray from the true path, and not to fall into spiritual darkness.

✍🏾 To avoid evil and to keep from falling into sin, we must fight the enemy who tempts us. Since our spiritual weapons are prayer, fasting, and worship, we need the intercession of the saints in all these struggles, and we must call upon them with diligence and faith.

text.text: Question:Can someone explain what we should pray about during the seven prayers each day?

text:
My child, the Seven Times of Prayer were not given to burden the body, but to heal the soul and gather the scattered hours of our day back to God. The Church, like a wise and patient mother, divided time itself and placed prayer inside it, so that no hour would remain empty of remembrance.

Each prayer hour is not random. Each one is rooted in creation, salvation, suffering, love, repentance, hope, and rest. When we pray them, we walk through the life of Christ and the history of humanity in one single day.

text.text: 1.Yengeh (11:00–12:00) – Why We Pray at This Hour

text:
We remember our Savior Jesus Christ, who loved us to the point of death, standing silently before Pilate without judgment. At this hour, we ask the God who grants rest to also grant rest to our souls.
This is the time when our father Adam was created, reminding us of our own beginning and God’s original purpose for humanity.

Especially if we did not pray during the night, it is good to pray in the morning. These may include:

👉🏾The Psalms of David

👉🏾Wudase Maryam

👉🏾Arganon

👉🏾Bartos Prayer

👉🏾Seife Selassie

👉🏾Seife Melekot

Since morning is a time of renewal and alertness, and the hours are open to us, we should pray according to our strength and love for prayer.

2.

text.text: The Third Hour Prayer (3:00 AM) – Why We Pray

text:
At this hour:

👉🏾Our mother Eve was created.

👉🏾The Prophet Daniel prayed and was saved from the mouth of the serpent.

👉🏾Our Lord Jesus Christ was flogged without sin before Pilate.

👉🏾The Holy Apostles received the Holy Spirit on Mount Zion, and the 72 languages were revealed.

👉🏾The Virgin Mary received the Good News from the Archangel Gabriel.

Because of this, we pray especially to the Virgin Mary and the Archangel Gabriel at this hour, asking her Son to intercede for us.
These prayers should not exceed 30 minutes. If time or strength is limited, it is sufficient to pray:

👉🏾

three times

👉🏾One

This is the hour when we remember:

👉🏾Christ was stripped to clothe us with the robe of glory.

👉🏾He was crowned for our sake.

👉🏾He accepted bitter suffering and death.

👉🏾The Virgin Mary endured deep sorrow.

At this time, it is good to pray:

👉🏾Sene gologota

👉🏾seyfe melekot

As the Psalmist says:

text.text: “Evening and morning and at noon I will pray, and He shall hear my voice.” (Psalm 54:17)

text:
This hour is also dangerous spiritually, as demons are active, so we must strengthen ourselves through prayer.

4.

This is the hour when our Lord revealed His love for humanity by dying on the Cross.It is also the hour when the holy angels carry human prayers to the Creator.

Because it is the hour of Christ’s death, we pray with repentance, remembering our own death, asking forgiveness for our sins, and glorifying God.

5

This hour reflects rest after labor. Just as people receive their daily bread, the faithful await their eternal reward at the Second Coming of Christ.For this reason, the prayer of this hour reminds us of the Second Coming.

At this time, it is appropriate to pray:

👉🏾 wudase Maryam

👉🏾mihla tselot (ምህላ)

6.

This is the hour when God established the order of prayer through the saints and among the people.

It is a prayer to the God of peace, asking Him to grant us peace of soul and body.

Recommended prayers include:

👉🏾wudase maryam

👉🏾Anqetse birhan

👉🏾ywedswa

If one was unable to pray in the morning, this hour is especially suitable. It is also good to pray the Arganon used by our forefathers.

Question:Can someone explain what we should pray about during the seven prayers each day?

Answer:My child, the Seven Times of Prayer were not given to burden the body, but to heal the soul and gather the scattered hours of our day back to God. The Church, like a wise and patient mother, divided time itself and placed prayer inside it, so that no hour would remain empty of remembrance.

Each prayer hour is not random. Each one is rooted in creation, salvation, suffering, love, repentance, hope, and rest. When we pray them, we walk through the life of Christ and the history of humanity in one single day.

1.Yengeh (11:00–12:00) – Why We Pray at This Hour

We remember our Savior Jesus Christ, who loved us to the point of death, standing silently before Pilate without judgment. At this hour, we ask the God who grants rest to also grant rest to our souls.
This is the time when our father Adam was created, reminding us of our own beginning and God’s original purpose for humanity.

Morning Prayers 

Especially if we did not pray during the night, it is good to pray in the morning. These may include:

👉🏾The Psalms of David

👉🏾Wudase Maryam

👉🏾Arganon

👉🏾Bartos Prayer

👉🏾Seife Selassie

👉🏾Seife Melekot

Since morning is a time of renewal and alertness, and the hours are open to us, we should pray according to our strength and love for prayer.

2.The Third Hour Prayer (3:00 AM) – Why We Pray

At this hour:

👉🏾Our mother Eve was created.

👉🏾The Prophet Daniel prayed and was saved from the mouth of the serpent.

👉🏾Our Lord Jesus Christ was flogged without sin before Pilate.

👉🏾The Holy Apostles received the Holy Spirit on Mount Zion, and the 72 languages were revealed.

👉🏾The Virgin Mary received the Good News from the Archangel Gabriel.

Because of this, we pray especially to the Virgin Mary and the Archangel Gabriel at this hour, asking her Son to intercede for us.
These prayers should not exceed 30 minutes. If time or strength is limited, it is sufficient to pray:

👉🏾Selam Eleki three times

👉🏾One Abune Zebesemayat

3.The Sixth Hour Prayer (6:00 AM)

This is the hour when we remember:

👉🏾Christ was stripped to clothe us with the robe of glory.

👉🏾He was crowned for our sake.

👉🏾He accepted bitter suffering and death.

👉🏾The Virgin Mary endured deep sorrow.

At this time, it is good to pray:

👉🏾Sene gologota

👉🏾seyfe melekot

As the Psalmist says:
“Evening and morning and at noon I will pray, and He shall hear my voice.” (Psalm 54:17)

At this time, it is appropriate to pray:

👉🏾 wudase Maryam

👉🏾mihla tselot (ምህላ)

✍🏾According to the canon of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, there are seven major fasts observed by the faithful.

and the yearly

.

✍🏾Nineveh was a great and ancient city, founded by Nimrod, a mighty ruler, on the banks of the Tigris River, as recorded in Genesis 10:11–12.

Nineveh was known for its beauty, size, and strength.

The length of its city wall was approximately 12 kilometers, making it one of the largest cities of the ancient world.

👉🏾It served as the capital city of Assyria, just as Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia or other modern capitals serve their nations.

✍🏾Assyria traces its origin to Asshur, one of the sons of Shem, the son of Noah (Genesis 10:22).

👉🏾Asshur became the forefather of the Assyrian people, whose land was located in Upper Mesopotamia.

✍🏾Nineveh became the political and military center of the Assyrian Empire.

Nineveh served as the capital of the powerful Assyrian Empire. During its peak, it frequently challenged and attacked the Kingdom of Israel. 

✍🏾 This occurred after the reign of Solomon's son, Rehoboam, when the nation split into two weakened states: the Northern Kingdom (Israel) and the Southern Kingdom (Judah).

✍🏾 ​In 720 B.C., the Assyrian Empire—with Nineveh as its heart—conquered Samaria, the capital of the ten Northern tribes. They deported the population and scattered them across five unfamiliar foreign lands, where they eventually integrated and became known as the "Lost Tribes." In their place, the Assyrians resettled people from other regions in Samaria.

✍🏾 ​The Assyrian Empire also oppressed the Southern Kingdom of Judah, at one point even taking King Manasseh captive to Babylon. However, they were unable to destroy the capital city, Jerusalem. During the reign of King Hezekiah, the Assyrians insolently challenged God. As recorded in the Holy Scriptures:

✍🏾​"That night the angel of the Lord went out and put to death a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the Assyrian camp. When the people got up the next morning—there were all the dead bodies! So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there." (2 Kings 19:35-36)

​Until its fall to the Babylonian Empire in 612 B.C., Nineveh was renowned as "The Great City." It officially became the capital of Assyria around 700 B.C. during the reign of King Sennacherib.

text:
Question for those that Believe you have To be from certain Christina denomination to be saved. 

Through one man Adam, all humanity fell, everyone, everywhere, regardless of location, nationality, religion, belief, or morality. Death, suffering, and corruption spread through the devil’s use of one man.

Through one man, Jesus Christ, salvation was accomplished for all humanity, because He assumed human nature, healed it, and restored it.So here is the real question 

If the fall destroyed all humanity through Adam, does Christ’s redemptive power fall short of that destruction if only a few receive it through baptism, knowledge of the Gospel, or being part of a Christian denomination?

What about those who never heard it? 

If Christ healed human nature itself, shouldn’t that healing truly reach all, everywhere, without limitation?

If the devil could affect everyone through one man, can Christ’s victory be considered complete if  we teach it only saves some ?

✍🏾

My Child, At the beginning of your question, you said that this question is directed to those who believe that a person must belong to a specific Christian denomination in order to be saved. Therefore, we will answer you according to the teaching of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church.

✍🏾From your question, it is clear that you are a thoughtful reader. This is a good and deep question, not asked lightly. It comes from reflection and concern for the justice and completeness of God’s salvation.

✍🏾It is true that through Adam and Eve, death entered the entire human race. This affected all people, without distinction of religion, race, place, or morality. Because of Adam’s sin, Paradise was closed, and all humanity was destined to descend to Sheol. However, we must understand this correctly. The righteous did not suffer the torment of hell, nor were they separated from God’s care. As the Scripture says, “The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment shall touch them” (Wisdom 3:1). Yet, Paradise remained closed until Christ.

👉🏾 Just as Adam’s sin affected everyone, so Christ’s salvation also reached everyone.

✍🏾

We Orthodox believe that through the incarnation, suffering, death, and resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, the entire human race was saved from the sin of Adam and Eve and from the death that came through them. This salvation from Adam’s sin is universal. Every human being, regardless of religion, is freed from the condemnation of Adam through Christ. We are not judged for Adam’s sin, because Christ has already healed human nature.

👉🏾 The Church teaches that baptism, repentance, faith, learning the Gospel, and good works are necessary not to remove Adam’s sin, but for salvation from personal sins and from hell. This must be clearly understood. Christ has already saved all humanity from Adam’s sin. As the Scripture says, “He who believes and is baptized will be saved, but he who does not believe will be condemned.”

We do not believe that there is anyone today who has not, in some way, encountered the Gospel. Even before modern technology, the apostles preached throughout the world. Today, the Gospel is accessible everywhere. As our Lord said in the Gospel of Matthew, the Gospel would be preached to all nations, and the Gentiles would hear it. Hearing alone is not the way of Salivation . Acceptance remains a matter of the heart.
Yes, the Gospel has gone out into the world, and through Christ the whole world has been saved from Adam’s sin.

Therefore, we will answer you according to the teaching of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church.

✍🏾From your question, it is clear that you are a thoughtful reader. This is a good and deep question, not asked lightly. It comes from reflection and concern for the justice and completeness of God’s salvation.

✍🏾It is true that through Adam and Eve, death entered the entire human race. This affected all people, without distinction of religion, race, place, or morality. Because of Adam’s sin, Paradise was closed, and all humanity was destined to descend to Sheol. However, we must understand this correctly. The righteous did not suffer the torment of hell, nor were they separated from God’s care. As the Scripture says, “The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment shall touch them” (Wisdom 3:1). Yet, Paradise remained closed until Christ.

👉🏾 Just as Adam’s sin affected everyone, so Christ’s salvation also reached everyone.

✍🏾Answer 1

We Orthodox believe that through the incarnation, suffering, death, and resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, the entire human race was saved from the sin of Adam and Eve and from the death that came through them. This salvation from Adam’s sin is universal. Every human being, regardless of religion, is freed from the condemnation of Adam through Christ. We are not judged for Adam’s sin, because Christ has already healed human nature.

👉🏾 The Church teaches that baptism, repentance, faith, learning the Gospel, and good works are necessary not to remove Adam’s sin, but for salvation from personal sins and from hell. This must be clearly understood. Christ has already saved all humanity from Adam’s sin. As the Scripture says, “He who believes and is baptized will be saved, but he who does not believe will be condemned.”

Answer 2

We do not believe that there is anyone today who has not, in some way, encountered the Gospel. Even before modern technology, the apostles preached throughout the world. Today, the Gospel is accessible everywhere. As our Lord said in the Gospel of Matthew, the Gospel would be preached to all nations, and the Gentiles would hear it. Hearing alone is not the way of Salivation . Acceptance remains a matter of the heart.

Answer 3

Yes, the Gospel has gone out into the world, and through Christ the whole world has been saved from Adam’s sin.

Continues 👇🏾

text:
We do not teach that only a few are saved. We teach that Christ, by becoming man, saved the entire human race from the sin of Adam and Eve. However, after this universal healing, God gave us a law to guide our lives. While Christ cleansed us from Adam’s sin, He also calls us to obedience. Salvation is not automatic for the sins we personally commit. Whoever fulfills the law through faith and works will be saved, and whoever rejects it will be condemned.

As the Apostle James says, “As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead” (James 2:26). The Scriptures also teach us to pray, to fast, and to live a life of repentance. Our Lord Himself said, “Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life” (John 6:54). Eternal life means living in communion with God and being saved from hell.

This is the teaching of the Church, my child. It does not limit Christ’s victory, nor does it deny God’s mercy. It shows us the path by which healed humanity lives in the salvation Christ has already accomplished.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾The Fast of Nineveh was a fast of repentance observed by the people of the city of Nineveh. By the time of the holy Prophet Jonah, the wickedness and evil deeds of Nineveh had risen up to heaven before God.

✍🏾 Because of this, God sent the Prophet Jonah to Nineveh to warn its people, calling them to repentance so that they might be saved from the coming wrath.

✍🏾 Nineveh was located about 800 kilometers from Gath-Hepher, the place where the Prophet Jonah was born and raised. Although Jonah first withdrew from his mission, he later obeyed the command of God. As the Scripture says:

👉🏾“Jonah began to enter the city a day’s journey, and he cried out and said, ‘Yet three days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.’”(Jonah 3:4)
According to this verse, the Prophet Jonah went through the city of Nineveh, proclaiming the word of God.

✍🏾 The response of the people is written clearly in the Holy Scripture:“So the people of Nineveh believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least of them.”(Jonah 3:5)

👉🏾Through repentance, fasting, humility, and turning back to God, the people of Nineveh were reconciled with Him and were saved from destruction and divine wrath.For this reason, the Church remembers this repentance and calls it the Fast of Nineveh.

👉🏾 What Was the Sin of the People of Nineveh?

The sin of the people of Nineveh is not listed one by one in the prophecy of Jonah. Instead, it is described in a general but very serious way. God says:

“Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness has come up before Me.”(Jonah 1:2)

✍🏾 The Scripture does not specify their sins in detail in the Book of Jonah. However, the words “their wickedness has come up before Me” clearly reveal the greatness and severity of their sin. A sin that reaches heaven is not small, hidden, or accidental.

✍🏾 Although their sins are not listed in Jonah, they are described more clearly in other prophetic books.

👉🏾

text.text: The Witness of the Prophet Nahum

text:
✍🏾 The Prophet Nahum speaks openly about the sins of Nineveh. He begins his prophecy by saying:

“The burden against Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.”(Nahum 1:1)

One of the major sins of Nineveh described by Nahum is conspiring against God.

👉🏾“There is one who plots evil against the Lord, a wicked counselor.”(Nahum 1:11)

✍🏾

The kings of Nineveh during the time of Prophet Jonah humbled themselves, repented, and saved their city from destruction through fasting and prayer. But the rulers who lived before and after that generation became known for cruelty, arrogance, and rebellion against God.

✍🏾They trusted in idols, glorified violence, and opposed the will of the Most High. In their pride, they behaved as though God could be challenged, ignored, or replaced.
This is what it means to plot against God. Not only with words, but with actions, systems, and attitudes that deny His authority.

✍🏾

This lesson is not written for Nineveh alone.
Those who oppose God through injustice, pride, corruption, cruelty, or rebellion should take warning. Whether in leadership or among the people, no one escapes accountability before God.

✍🏾 Do not miss the opportunity to repent and be reconciled with God. The leaders of Nineveh became an example by humbling themselves first and leading their people in repentance. Through this, they saved both their city and their nation from the wrath of God.

✍🏾 No matter how great the sin, do not allow it to push you away from repentance. God does not hate the sinner, but the sin. What destroys us is not falling, but refusing to return.

Dear followers of the Orthodox teachings on John's Repentance website .we greet you with the peace of the Lord.Today , based on the topic mentioned above, we present to you the following important lesson.We encourage everyone to read it carefully and learn from it.

✍🏾

The people of Nineveh, especially their rulers and powerful officials, were known for their cruelty. Holy Scripture likens them to a lion, the king of beasts, symbolizing their savage and violent nature.

👉🏾 “The lion tears enough for his cubs and kills for his lionesses; he fills his caves with prey and his dens with flesh.”
(Nahum 2:12–13)

✍🏾The Assyrians, whose capital city was Nineveh, were infamous for their brutality. Their kings took pleasure in cruel punishments inflicted upon conquered nations.
It was their policy to deport entire populations and to destroy peoples they feared, committing acts of mass killing and terror.

✍🏾The leaders of conquered cities were tortured, mutilated, and publicly humiliated before being killed. Although the people of Nineveh repented at the preaching of the prophet Jonah, they did not persevere in repentance. Their wickedness once covered them completely. Although they repented for a time, they later returned to their former evil ways. Because they did not persevere in repentance, their city was ultimately overthrown.

✍🏾 The man of God, the prophet Nahum, speaks plainly about Nineveh, saying:

👉🏾 “Woe to the bloody city! It is all full of lies and robbery; its victims never depart… Your injury has no healing, your wound is severe. All who hear news of you will clap their hands over you. For upon whom has not your wickedness passed continually?”
(Nahum 3:1, 19)

👉🏾 In these verses, the prophet reveals the sins of Nineveh: bloodshed, deception, plunder, and unceasing injustice. He also declares that their punishment would be unavoidable, because their wickedness had become habitual and unrepented.

✍🏾 The Assyrian kings of Nineveh gloried in cruelty and violence, even boasting of piling human heads at the gates of their city as signs of victory. Such pride and bloodshed rose as a cry before God. Because they abandoned repentance and returned to wickedness, Nineveh was finally overthrown and destroyed in 612 BC, exactly as foretold by the holy prophets Jonah and Nahum.

✍🏾

✍🏾Without going further into detail, let us consider the burden pronounced against Nineveh in the book of the prophet Nahum, 

👉🏾 “Because of the multitude of the harlotries of the seductive harlot, who sells nations through her harlotries, and families through her sorceries.”
(Nahum 3:4)

✍🏾This verse reminds us that in the city of Nineveh, the so-called goddess of love was worshipped, and through this false worship the city was defiled by prostitution and witchcraft.

✍🏾The sins of Nineveh were not limited to these alone. The prophecy of Nahum also condemns fraud, deceit, and plundering in trade and daily dealings.

Which of the sins of Nineveh mentioned above is not practiced in our own time, in homes, cities, nations, and even in places of authority?

👉🏾 Have betrayal, bloodshed, hidden cruelty, rebellion against God, adultery, witchcraft, slander, and dishonesty in business not risen up to heaven?
Such abominations, if they are not removed through repentance,

👉🏾 and if they are not replaced by fasting and prayer, love and peace, understanding, true faith, and righteous conduct,

👉🏾 then poverty and persecution, war and judgment, bloodshed and destruction, disease and calamity will not be far from the earth.This means that God has entrusted life and death to our own actions.

(Nahum 3:1, 19)

👉🏾 In these verses, the prophet reveals the sins of Nineveh: bloodshed, deception, plunder, and unceasing injustice. He also declares that their punishment would be unavoidable, because their wickedness had become habitual and unrepented.

✍🏾 The Assyrian kings of Nineveh gloried in cruelty and violence, even boasting of piling human heads at the gates of their city as signs of victory. Such pride and bloodshed rose as a cry before God. Because they abandoned repentance and returned to wickedness, Nineveh was finally overthrown and destroyed in 612 BC, exactly as foretold by the holy prophets Jonah and Nahum.

✍🏾

✍🏾Without going further into detail, let us consider the burden pronounced against Nineveh in the book of the prophet Nahum, 

👉🏾 “Because of the multitude of the harlotries of the seductive harlot, who sells nations through her harlotries, and families through her sorceries.”
(Nahum 3:4)

✍🏾This verse reminds us that in the city of Nineveh, the so-called goddess of love was worshipped, and through this false worship the city was defiled by prostitution and witchcraft.

✍🏾The sins of Nineveh were not limited to these alone. The prophecy of Nahum also condemns fraud, deceit, and plundering in trade and daily dealings.

Which of the sins of Nineveh mentioned above is not practiced in our own time, in homes, cities, nations, and even in places of authority?

👉🏾 Have betrayal, bloodshed, hidden cruelty, rebellion against God, adultery, witchcraft, slander, and dishonesty in business not risen up to heaven?
Such abominations, if they are not removed through repentance,

👉🏾 and if they are not replaced by fasting and prayer, love and peace, understanding, true faith, and righteous conduct,

👉🏾 then poverty and persecution, war and judgment, bloodshed and destruction, disease and calamity will not be far from the earth.This means that God has entrusted life and death to our own actions.

May the name of the Holy God be praised forever and ever in every tongue that He has created, today and always.

May the blessings of God's mother, the virgin, and the cross be upon us.
Amen.

text.text: The Teaching of Saint Cyril of Jerusalem(315–386 AD)

text:
✍🏾Saint Cyril, Bishop of Jerusalem, taught about the life of Our Lady in the Temple in his sermons.

He explains that Joachim and Anna had the custom of visiting their daughter once each month. They would bring her what she needed, and the holy Virgin would serve in the Temple together with the older virgins, who taught her the work of the hands and the ways of service.When she reached the proper age, she would go to the Temple by herself.

✍🏾 No man would see her except the priests and her father. The Virgin Mary lived within the Temple, and the Archangel Gabriel would approach her with a sweet fragrance. Her beauty was beyond measure, and the Temple was filled with angels because of the fragrance of her purity. Saint Cyril describes her life in detail, saying that people would come only to hear her holy words.

✍🏾

text.text:
The Teaching of Saint Demetrius of Antioch
(256 AD)

text:
👉🏾Saint Demetrius, Archbishop of Antioch, also taught concerning the life of Our Lady in the Temple.

✍🏾When her mother Anna placed her at the door of the Temple before the priests, the child entered and went as far as the veil of the altar, where sacrifices were offered to the Lord. After entering, she did not turn back to go outside, nor did her mind dwell on her family or on earthly matters.

✍🏾As she grew and reached the age of eight or ten, she became an example to all the priests. They feared to gaze upon her, for her body was pure and her heart firmly established in the Lord.
She was pure in body and soul. She never turned her face toward the outside of the Temple, never saw a stranger, and never looked upon the face of a man. She lived in holiness, serving God continually in the Temple. Her garment reached her forehead, and her veil covered her eyes.

✍🏾She did not use eye makeup, nor did she adorn her face with ornaments or flowers. She did not wear sandals on her feet, nor bracelets or jewelry on her arms and hands. She did not seek rich food, did not walk in the marketplaces of the city, and had no interest in worldly affairs.

✍🏾She never exposed herself to defilement, nor examined her body with vanity, bearing witness to her perfect purity and holiness during her life in the Temple.

✍🏾

text.text: The Teaching of Saint Cyril of Alexandria(376–444 AD )

text:
Saint Cyril of Alexandria taught the women gathered in the Temple about the humble life of the Holy Virgin, saying:

👉🏾“All women who desire virginity should follow the example of Mary, the Mother of our Lord.”
He called attention to her simple way of eating and her habit of sleeping on the ground. She had no desire for the pleasures of this world, and her name was continually on the lips of the priests because of her holiness.
She never washed her body in public baths. She never adorned herself with makeup, eyeliner, ointments, or brightly colored clothing, as was common among women of her time.

👉🏾She never tasted wine and lived in constant expectation of her Creator, who created all worlds. She would sit facing the east in prayer. She did not meet or speak with anyone except her mother and father, and she became a teacher and example to the pure virgins.

✍🏾The prophet David says:

👉🏾 “The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree; he shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon. Those who are planted in the house of the Lord shall flourish in the courts of our God.”(Psalm 91:12–13)
